```tern
#                                   (TERN_WEB_DRAIN_SEC, 10)      s.stop()   closes and waits
#   Streamed bodies (a stream route): req.read_body(max) str, req.save_body(path) int,
#   req.next_part(&p) bool, req.read_part(max) str, req.save_part(path) int
#   http.file_response(path, req) Response     a file (ETag, 304, ranges, content types)
#   http.static_file(dir, rel, req) Response   rel under dir (".." and dot files are 404)
#   http.ws_upgrade(req) Response   accept a WebSocket (the route's ws handler runs next)
#   http.sse_open(req) Response     open an event stream (the route's sse handler runs next)
#
# WebSockets (Socket): ws.next(&msg) bool, ws.recv() str, ws.is_binary() bool, ws.send(text) bool,
#   ws.send_binary(data) bool, ws.ping(data) bool, ws.close(), ws.is_open() bool
#   http.ws_connect(url) Socket     a client ("ws://host/path", or "wss://" with `import tls`: verified,
#                                   SNI, port 443); ws.ok(), http.error()
#   http.ws_connect_with(url, headers) Socket
# Server-sent events (Stream): out.send(data) bool, out.event(name, data) bool,
#   out.comment(text) bool, out.forward(ch) bool (every message of a chan[str], until it closes)
#
# HTTP client (https:// needs `import tls`; certificates are verified; connections are pooled):
#   http.get(url) Response          http.post(url, body, content_type) Response
#   http.fetch(ClientRequest(method, url, headers, body, timeout_ms, redirects)) Response
#   http.request(method, url) ClientRequest   (30s timeout, follows 5 redirects)
#   http.try_get(url) / try_fetch(cr) Result[Response, str]   (Err: no response at all)
#   http.fetch_max(cr, max_body) Response   fails (status 0) past max_body bytes of body: for
#                                   untrusted URLs. "Connection: close" in cr.headers keeps the
#                                   connection out of the pool (one-off hosts, crawlers). Pooled
#                                   connections close after TERN_HTTP_POOL_IDLE (30) s idle; at most
#                                   TERN_HTTP_POOL_MAX (512) wait in all
#   http.header_line(name, value) str    http.failed(res) bool    http.url_encode(s) str
#
# For middleware:
#   http.now_us() int               a monotonic clock, microseconds
#   http.log(line)                  one line to stderr, buffered (the access log's writer)
#   http.limiter(per_second, burst) Limiter; lim.consume(key) float   token buckets by key,
#                                   shared by every thread: 0.0, or the seconds to wait
#   http.request_id() str           a random id          http.secure_equal(a, b) bool (constant time)
#   http.gzip(data) str             ("" if it can't)
#   http.enable_metrics(); http.metrics_text() str   Prometheus text: requests, latency by
#                                   route, connections, process stats, and metric_add / metric_set
#   http.metric_add(name, labels, v)  http.metric_set(name, labels, v)
#
# Environment: TERN_HTTP_THREADS, TERN_HTTP_MAX_BODY_MB (16), TERN_HTTP_IDLE_SEC (60),
# TERN_HTTP_HEADER_SEC (10) for serve; TERN_ASYNC_THREADS (worker threads), TERN_WEB_IDLE_SEC
# (60), TERN_WEB_HEADER_SEC (10), TERN_WEB_MAX_BODY_MB (16), TERN_WEB_WS_MAX_MB (16),
# TERN_WEB_MAX_CONNS for the engine. The servers and the client need sockets and threads, so
# not wasm; the request and response functions work everywhere.

struct Request:
    method: str                 # "GET", "POST", ...
    path: str                   # "/users/42" (without the query string)
    raw_query: str              # "page=2&sort=name" (see query)
    head: str                   # header lines as received, "Name: value\r\n" each (see header)
    body: str
    params: str                 # path parameters, packed (see param)
    ctx: {str: str}             # values middleware passes to inner handlers (see set_ctx)
    conn: int                   # the connection's socket (see peer and client_ip)

struct Response:
    status: int
    content_type: str
    body: str
    headers: str                # extra header lines, "Name: value\r\n" each (see set_header)
    upgrade: int                # 1: WebSocket, 2: event stream (see ws_upgrade / sse_open)

struct Socket:
    fd: int
    gen: int

struct Stream:
    fd: int
    gen: int

# multipart/form-data (HTML forms with <input type="file">): every part of the body
struct Part:
    name: str                   # the form field
    filename: str               # the uploaded file's name ("" for a plain field)
    content_type: str           # the part's Content-Type ("" if none was sent)
    data: str

struct Server:
    id: int
    port: int                   # the port it listens on, once listening

struct ClientRequest:
    method: str
    url: str
    headers: str                # "Name: value\r\n" lines (see header_line)
    body: str
    timeout_ms: int
    redirects: int              # how many redirects to follow

struct Limiter:                 # token buckets (see limiter)
    id: int

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- responses

fn text(body: str) Response:
    return Response(200, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", body, "", 0)

fn html(body: str) Response:
    return Response(200, "text/html; charset=utf-8", body, "", 0)

fn json(body: str) Response:
    return Response(200, "application/json", body, "", 0)

fn status(code: int, body: str) Response:
    return Response(code, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", body, "", 0)

fn not_found() Response:
    return Response(404, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "not found", "", 0)

fn no_content() Response:
    return Response(204, "", "", "", 0)

fn redirect(to: str) Response:
    return Response(302, "", "", "Location: " + to + "\r\n", 0)

fn redirect_permanent(to: str) Response:
    return Response(308, "", "", "Location: " + to + "\r\n", 0)

fn with_status(res: Response, code: int) Response:
    out = res
    out.status = code
    return out

fn set_header(res: mut Response, name: str, value: str):
    if name.lower() == "content-type":
        res.content_type = value
        return
    res.headers += name + ": " + value + "\r\n"

fn set_cookie(res: mut Response, name: str, value: str):
    res.headers += "Set-Cookie: " + name + "=" + value + "; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax\r\n"

fn set_cookie_with(res: mut Response, name: str, value: str, attrs: str):
    res.headers += "Set-Cookie: " + name + "=" + value + "; " + attrs + "\r\n"

fn get_header(res: Response, name: str) str:
    if name.lower() == "content-type":
        return res.content_type
    return _header(res.headers, name)

fn header_line(name: str, value: str) str:
    return name + ": " + value + "\r\n"

fn failed(res: Response) bool:
    return res.status == 0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- requests

# a request as the servers build it, for calling handlers in tests: target is the path with
# its query string ("/search?q=tern"); add headers with req.add_header(name, value)
fn new_request(method: str, target: str, body: str) Request:
    q = target.find("?")
    if q < 0:
        return Request(method, target, "", "", body, "", {}, -1)
    return Request(method, target[..q], target[q + 1..], "", body, "", {}, -1)

fn param(req: Request, name: str) str:
    return _param(req.params, name)

fn param_int(req: Request, name: str, default: int) int:
    return _param(req.params, name).to_int(default)

fn params(req: Request) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    for i in 0.._param_count(req.params):
        out[_param_at(req.params, i, false)] = _param_at(req.params, i, true)
    return out

fn query(req: Request, name: str) str:
    return _form(req.raw_query, name)

fn queries(req: Request) {str: str}:
    return _pairs(req.raw_query)

fn form(req: Request, name: str) str:
    return _form(req.body, name)

fn forms(req: Request) {str: str}:
    return _pairs(req.body)

fn _pairs(q: str) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    for i in 0.._form_count(q):
        k = _form_at(q, i, false)
        if k != "":
            out[k] = _form_at(q, i, true)
    return out

fn _param_of(h: str, key: str) str:
    for piece in h.split(";"):
        kv = piece.trim()
        if kv.lower().starts_with(key + "="):
            v = kv[len(key) + 1..]
            if v.starts_with("\"") and v.ends_with("\"") and len(v) >= 2:
                v = v[1..len(v) - 1]
            return v
    return ""

fn parts(req: Request) [Part]:
    out: [Part] = []
    ct = _header(req.head, "content-type")
    if not ct.lower().starts_with("multipart/"):
        return out
    boundary = _param_of(ct, "boundary")
    if boundary == "":
        return out
    body = req.body
    delim = "--" + boundary
    pos = _find_from(body, delim, 0)
    while pos >= 0:
        pos += len(delim)
        if body[pos..pos + 2] == "--":
            break
        head_end = _find_from(body, "\r\n\r\n", pos)
        if head_end < 0:
            break
        next = _find_from(body, "\r\n" + delim, head_end + 4)
        if next < 0:
            break
        p = Part("", "", "", body[head_end + 4..next])
        for line in body[pos..head_end].split("\r\n"):
            i = line.find(":")
            if i < 0:
                continue
            k = line[..i].trim().lower()
            v = line[i + 1..].trim()
            if k == "content-disposition":
                p.name = _param_of(v, "name")
                p.filename = _param_of(v, "filename")
            elif k == "content-type":
                p.content_type = v
        out.push(p)
        pos = next + 2
    return out

# the part for form field name (Part with name "" if there's none)
fn part(req: Request, name: str) Part:
    for p in parts(req):
        if p.name == name:
            return p
    return Part("", "", "", "")

fn header(req: Request, name: str) str:
    return _header(req.head, name)

fn headers(req: Request) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    for line in req.head.split("\r\n"):
        i = line.find(":")
        if i > 0:
            out[line[..i].lower()] = line[i + 1..].trim()
    return out

fn cookie(req: Request, name: str) str:
    return _cookie(_header(req.head, "cookie"), name)

fn add_header(req: mut Request, name: str, value: str):
    req.head += name + ": " + value + "\r\n"

fn set_ctx(req: mut Request, key: str, value: str):
    req.ctx[key] = value

fn ctx_value(req: Request, key: str) str:
    if key in req.ctx:
        return req.ctx[key]
    return ""

# match("/users/42", "/users/{id}", &params) true, params == {"id": "42"}: routing for
# serve's handlers (the engine routes by itself)
fn match(path: str, pattern: str, params: mut {str: str}) bool:
    a = path.split("/")
    b = pattern.split("/")
    if len(a) != len(b):
        return false
    found: {str: str} = {}
    for i in 0..len(b):
        if b[i].starts_with("{") and b[i].ends_with("}"):
            found[b[i][1..len(b[i]) - 1]] = url_decode(a[i])
        elif a[i] != b[i]:
            return false
    params = found
    return true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the connection behind a request

# the address the request came from, "1.2.3.4:5678" ("" if unknown)
fn peer(req: Request) str:
    return _peer(req.conn)

# the client's IP address: the connection's, or behind http.trust_proxies(n) proxies, the
# X-Forwarded-For entry those proxies vouch for (counting from the right: the entries left of
# it were written by the client and can say anything)
fn client_ip(req: Request) str:
    return _client_ip(req.conn, req.head)

# the pattern of the route that matched ("/users/{id}"; "" if none), for error trackers and
# logs; recorded once track_routes() was called (so servers that don't ask pay nothing)
fn matched_route(req: Request) str:
    return _route(req.conn)

fn track_routes():
    _track_routes()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the engine's server

fn new_server() Server:
    return Server(_server_new(), 0)

# the ws / sse arguments of add_route for a route that has none
fn no_ws(req: Request, ws: Socket):
    pass

fn no_sse(req: Request, out: Stream):
    pass

fn add_route(s: Server, method: str, pattern: str, h: fn(Request) Response, ws: fn(Request, Socket), sse: fn(Request, Stream), stream: bool):
    _server_route(s.id, method, pattern, h, ws, sse)
    if stream:
        _route_stream(s.id)

# At most n connections at once (0: no limit, the default; TERN_WEB_MAX_CONNS sets it too).
# Past the limit the server stops accepting until a connection closes; new clients wait in
# the kernel's queue rather than being refused.
fn limit_connections(s: Server, n: int):
    _server_limit(s.id, n)

fn listen(s: mut Server, host: str, port: int, fallback: fn(Request) Response):
    s.port = _server_listen(s.id, host, port, fallback)

fn listen_tls(s: mut Server, host: str, port: int, fallback: fn(Request) Response, cert: str, key: str):
    s.port = _server_listen_tls(s.id, host, port, fallback, cert, key)

fn wait(s: Server):
    _server_wait(s.id)

fn stop(s: Server):
    _server_stop(s.id)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- streamed bodies, files, upgrades

# the next piece of a streamed body, up to max bytes ("" at the end)
fn read_body(req: Request, max: int) str:
    return _body_read(max)

# the rest of a streamed body into a file: bytes written, or -1 (http.error() says why)
fn save_body(req: Request, path: str) int:
    return _body_save(path, false)

# a streamed multipart/form-data body, part by part: next_part fills p (its data is "") and
# is false after the last part; read_part / save_part then read that part's bytes
fn next_part(req: Request, p: mut Part) bool:
    np = _part_next()
    if np.name == "" and np.filename == "":
        return false
    p = np
    return true

fn read_part(req: Request, max: int) str:
    return _part_read(max)

fn save_part(req: Request, path: str) int:
    return _body_save(path, true)

# a file under dir: content type from the extension, ETag / Last-Modified with 304 answers,
# single byte ranges (206), big files streamed from disk; ".." or dot files (other than
# .well-known) are 404, and a directory serves its index.html
fn static_file(dir: str, rel: str, req: Request) Response:
    return _static(dir, rel, req.head)

# one file (relative to the working directory; ".." is refused), with the same headers
fn file_response(path: str, req: Request) Response:
    return _static("", path, req.head)

# accept a WebSocket handshake: the route's ws handler takes the connection from here
fn ws_upgrade(req: Request) Response:
    if _header(req.head, "upgrade").lower() != "websocket":
        return status(426, "this endpoint takes WebSocket connections")
    key = _header(req.head, "sec-websocket-key")
    if key == "" or _header(req.head, "sec-websocket-version") != "13":
        return status(400, "bad WebSocket handshake")
    return Response(101, "", "", "Upgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Accept: " + _ws_accept(key) + "\r\n", 1)

# open a server-sent event stream: the route's sse handler writes to it from here
fn sse_open(req: Request) Response:
    return Response(200, "text/event-stream", "", "Cache-Control: no-cache\r\n", 2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- WebSockets

fn next(ws: Socket, msg: mut str) bool:
    m = _ws_recv(ws.fd, ws.gen)
    if _ws_closed(ws.fd, ws.gen):
        return false
    msg = m
    return true

fn recv(ws: Socket) str:
    return _ws_recv(ws.fd, ws.gen)

fn is_binary(ws: Socket) bool:
    return _ws_binary(ws.fd, ws.gen)

fn send(ws: Socket, text: str) bool:
    return _ws_send(ws.fd, ws.gen, text, 1)

fn send_binary(ws: Socket, data: str) bool:
    return _ws_send(ws.fd, ws.gen, data, 2)

fn ping(ws: Socket, data: str) bool:
    return _ws_send(ws.fd, ws.gen, data, 9)

fn close(ws: Socket):
    _ws_close(ws.fd, ws.gen)

fn is_open(ws: Socket) bool:
    return not _ws_closed(ws.fd, ws.gen)

fn ok(ws: Socket) bool:
    return ws.fd >= 0

fn ws_connect(url: str) Socket:
    return _ws_connect(url, "")

fn ws_connect_with(url: str, headers: str) Socket:
    return _ws_connect(url, headers)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- server-sent events

# out.send(data) (the compiler maps `send` on a Stream here)
fn sse_send(out: Stream, data: str) bool:
    return _sse_send(out.fd, out.gen, "", data, false)

fn event(out: Stream, name: str, data: str) bool:
    return _sse_send(out.fd, out.gen, name, data, false)

fn comment(out: Stream, text: str) bool:
    return _sse_send(out.fd, out.gen, "", text, true)

# out.forward(ch) bool (a builtin): sends every message from ch as an event until ch is
# closed (true) or the client goes away (false; noticed within a second even when ch is
# quiet). Messages that are already waiting go out together in one write.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the client

fn request(method: str, url: str) ClientRequest:
    return ClientRequest(method.upper(), url, "", "", 30000, 5)

fn get(url: str) Response:
    return fetch(ClientRequest("GET", url, "", "", 30000, 5))

fn post(url: str, body: str, content_type: str) Response:
    return fetch(ClientRequest("POST", url, "Content-Type: " + content_type + "\r\n", body, 30000, 5))

fn _origin(url: str) str:
    skip = 7
    if url.starts_with("https://"):
        skip = 8
    rest = url[skip..]
    i = rest.find("/")
    if i < 0:
        return url
    return url[..skip + i]

fn _resolve(base: str, loc: str) str:
    if loc.starts_with("http://") or loc.starts_with("https://"):
        return loc
    if loc.starts_with("/"):
        return _origin(base) + loc
    cut = base
    q = cut.find("?")
    if q >= 0:
        cut = cut[..q]
    skip = len(_origin(cut)) - 1
    i = len(cut) - 1
    while i > skip and cut[i] != "/":
        i -= 1
    if i <= skip:
        return cut + "/" + loc
    return cut[..i + 1] + loc

fn fetch(cr: ClientRequest) Response:
    return fetch_max(cr, 0)

# fetch, failing (status 0) once a response body would pass max_body bytes (0: no limit), for
# URLs you don't control: memory stays bounded however big the page (a Content-Length over
# the limit fails before any of the body is read)
fn fetch_max(cr: ClientRequest, max_body: int) Response:
    method = cr.method
    url = cr.url
    body = cr.body
    headers = cr.headers
    hops = 0
    while true:
        res = _fetch_max(method, url, headers, body, cr.timeout_ms, max_body)
        if res.status < 300 or res.status >= 400 or res.status == 304 or hops >= cr.redirects:
            return res
        loc = _header(res.headers, "location")
        if loc == "":
            return res
        url = _resolve(url, loc)
        hops += 1
        if res.status == 303 or ((res.status == 301 or res.status == 302) and method == "POST"):
            method = "GET"
            body = ""
    return Response(0, "", "", "", 0)

# with Result: res = http.try_get(url)?   Err only when there's no response at all ("http:
# request failed: connect: Connection refused"); 4xx / 5xx responses are Ok
fn try_fetch(cr: ClientRequest) Result[Response, str]:
    res = fetch(cr)
    if res.status == 0:
        return Err("http: request failed: " + res.body)
    return Ok(res)

fn try_get(url: str) Result[Response, str]:
    return try_fetch(ClientRequest("GET", url, "", "", 30000, 5))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- for middleware

fn now_us() int:
    return _now_us()

fn log(line: str):
    _log(line)

# Token buckets by key (a client IP, an API key), refilled at per_second tokens a second up
# to burst, shared by every thread; idle ones are forgotten.
fn limiter(per_second: float, burst: int) Limiter:
    return Limiter(_rl_new(per_second, float(burst)))

# use a token from key's bucket: 0.0, or (none left) the seconds until one is there
fn consume(l: Limiter, key: str) float:
    return _rl_take(l.id, key)

fn request_id() str:
    return _request_id()

# a == b, in time that depends only on the lengths (for comparing secrets)
fn secure_equal(a: str, b: str) bool:
    return _ct_eq(a, b)

fn gzip(data: str) str:
    return _gzip(data)

# count requests from now on (every server in the program), for metrics_text
fn enable_metrics():
    _metrics_enable()

fn metrics_text() str:
    return _metrics_text()
```

## library/std/json.tn

```tern
# json: encode and decode any Tern value.
#
#   import json
#   text = json.encode(user)                 # structs, arrays, maps, str, int, float, bool
#   ok = json.decode(req.body, &user)        # fills user; false (and no change) if invalid
#   s = json.schema[User]()                  # User's JSON Schema (2020-12), as text
#
# Both are built into the compiler, which generates a dedicated encoder/decoder for
# each type (no reflection). Struct fields map to JSON object keys by name; missing
# keys keep their current value; unknown keys are ignored; null keeps the value.
# To tell a missing key from an empty value, make the field an Option and start it at None:
# a missing key (or null) leaves None, "" gives Some("").
#   struct LinkReq:  url: str   slug: Option[str]      ... if r.slug is Some(s): ...
# Map keys may be str or int (int keys are written as JSON strings).
#
# JSON whose shape isn't known ahead of time: parse it into a Value and look inside.
#
#   v = json.parse(text)?                    # Result[json.Value, str]
#   v.field("user").field("name").str_or("")     # a missing key or wrong kind gives Null,
#   v.field("tags").at(0).str_or("none")         # so lookups chain; the *_or default ends it
#   n = v.field("count").int_or(0)   x = v.field("ratio").float_or(0.0)   b = v.field("ok").bool_or(false)
#   for k in v.fields(): ...       for x in v.elems(): ...       v.size()
#   m = v.to_map()                           # {str: Value}: field() scans the keys, so for many
#                                            # lookups in a big object, index it once
#   match v: Obj(keys, vals) / Arr(items) / Str(s) / Num(x, text) / Bool(b) / Null
#   json.dump(v) str                         back to JSON text
#
# Objects keep their keys in order (and repeated keys, as written); numbers keep their text
# too, so int_or reads integers beyond float's 2^53 exactly.

enum Value:
    Null
    Bool(b: bool)
    Num(x: float, text: str)
    Str(s: str)
    Arr(items: [Value])
    Obj(keys: [str], vals: [Value])

fn _ws(s: str, pos: mut int):
    while pos < len(s):
        c = s.byte(pos)
        if c != 32 and c != 10 and c != 13 and c != 9:
            return
        pos += 1

fn _hexval(c: int) int:
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57:
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 102:
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 70:
        return c - 55
    return -1

fn _utf8(cp: int) str:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return chr(cp)
    if cp < 0x800:
        return chr(0xc0 | (cp >> 6)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))
    if cp < 0x10000:
        return chr(0xe0 | (cp >> 12)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))
    return chr(0xf0 | (cp >> 18)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3f)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))

fn _hex4(s: str, pos: int, err: mut str) int:
    if pos + 4 > len(s):
        err = "truncated \\u escape"
        return 0
    v = 0
    for i in 0..4:
        h = _hexval(s.byte(pos + i))
        if h < 0:
            err = "bad \\u escape"
            return 0
        v = v * 16 + h
    return v

fn _string(s: str, pos: mut int, err: mut str) str:
    pos += 1
    out = ""
    start = pos
    while pos < len(s):
        c = s.byte(pos)
        if c == 34:
            out += s[start..pos]
            pos += 1
            return out
        if c < 32:
            err = "control character in a string"
            return out
        if c == 92:
            out += s[start..pos]
            if pos + 1 >= len(s):
                break
            e = s.byte(pos + 1)
            pos += 2
            match e:
                110:
                    out += "\n"
                116:
                    out += "\t"
                114:
                    out += "\r"
                98:
                    out += chr(8)
                102:
                    out += chr(12)
                34:
                    out += "\""
                92:
                    out += "\\"
                47:
                    out += "/"
                117:
                    cp = _hex4(s, pos, &err)
                    pos += 4
                    if cp >= 0xd800 and cp < 0xdc00 and pos + 6 <= len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 92 and s.byte(pos + 1) == 117:
                        lo = _hex4(s, pos + 2, &err)
                        if lo >= 0xdc00 and lo < 0xe000:
                            cp = 0x10000 + ((cp - 0xd800) << 10) + (lo - 0xdc00)
                            pos += 6
                    out += _utf8(cp)
                _:
                    err = "bad escape \\" + chr(e)
                    return out
            start = pos
        else:
            pos += 1
    err = "unterminated string"
    return out

fn _value(s: str, pos: mut int, err: mut str, depth: int) Value:
    _ws(s, &pos)
    if pos >= len(s):
        err = "unexpected end"
        return Value.Null
    if depth > 512:
        err = "nested too deeply"
        return Value.Null
    c = s.byte(pos)
    if c == 34:
        return Value.Str(_string(s, &pos, &err))
    if c == 123:
        pos += 1
        keys: [str] = []
        vals: [Value] = []
        _ws(s, &pos)
        if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 125:
            pos += 1
            return Value.Obj(keys, vals)
        while err == "":
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos >= len(s) or s.byte(pos) != 34:
                err = "expected a key string"
                break
            keys.push(_string(s, &pos, &err))
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos >= len(s) or s.byte(pos) != 58:
                err = "expected `:` after a key"
                break
            pos += 1
            vals.push(_value(s, &pos, &err, depth + 1))
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 44:
                pos += 1
            elif pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 125:
                pos += 1
                break
            else:
                err = "expected `,` or `}`"
        return Value.Obj(keys, vals)
    if c == 91:
        pos += 1
        items: [Value] = []
        _ws(s, &pos)
        if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 93:
            pos += 1
            return Value.Arr(items)
        while err == "":
            items.push(_value(s, &pos, &err, depth + 1))
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 44:
                pos += 1
            elif pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 93:
                pos += 1
                break
            else:
                err = "expected `,` or `]`"
        return Value.Arr(items)
    if s[pos..pos + 4] == "true":
        pos += 4
        return Value.Bool(true)
    if s[pos..pos + 5] == "false":
        pos += 5
        return Value.Bool(false)
    if s[pos..pos + 4] == "null":
        pos += 4
        return Value.Null
    start = pos
    while pos < len(s):
        d = s.byte(pos)
        if (d >= 48 and d <= 57) or d == 45 or d == 43 or d == 46 or d == 101 or d == 69:
            pos += 1
        else:
            break
    text = s[start..pos]
    x = text.to_float(0.0)
    if pos == start or (x == 0.0 and not _zeroish(text)):
        err = "unexpected character"
        return Value.Null
    return Value.Num(x, text)

fn _zeroish(t: str) bool:
    for i in 0..len(t):
        c = t.byte(i)
        if c >= 49 and c <= 57:
            return false
    return len(t) > 0 and t != "-" and t != "."

# parse JSON text into a Value (Err says what's wrong and at which byte)
fn parse(text: str) Result[Value, str]:
    err = ""
    pos = 0
    v = _value(text, &pos, &err, 0)
    if err == "":
        _ws(text, &pos)
        if pos != len(text):
            err = "extra text after the value"
    if err != "":
        return Err(f"json: {err} at byte {pos}")
    return Ok(v)

# the value under key in an object (the last one, if repeated), or Null
fn field(v: Value, key: str) Value:
    match v:
        Obj(keys, vals):
            i = len(keys) - 1
            while i >= 0:
                if keys[i] == key:
                    return vals[i]
                i -= 1
        _:
            pass
    return Value.Null

# element i of an array, or Null
fn at(v: Value, i: int) Value:
    match v:
        Arr(items):
            if i >= 0 and i < len(items):
                return items[i]
        _:
            pass
    return Value.Null

fn str_or(v: Value, default: str) str:
    match v:
        Str(s):
            return s
        _:
            return default

fn float_or(v: Value, default: float) float:
    match v:
        Num(x, t):
            return x
        _:
            return default

fn int_or(v: Value, default: int) int:
    match v:
        Num(x, t):
            if not (t.contains(".") or t.contains("e") or t.contains("E")):
                return t.to_int(default)
            if x >= -9.2e18 and x <= 9.2e18:
                return int(x)
            return default
        _:
            return default

fn bool_or(v: Value, default: bool) bool:
    match v:
        Bool(b):
            return b
        _:
            return default

# an object's keys in order ([] for anything else)
fn fields(v: Value) [str]:
    match v:
        Obj(keys, vals):
            return keys
        _:
            return []

# an object as a map (a repeated key keeps its last value, as field() does; {} for anything else)
fn to_map(v: Value) {str: Value}:
    m: {str: Value} = {}
    match v:
        Obj(keys, vals):
            for i, k in keys:
                m[k] = vals[i]
        _:
            pass
    return m

# an array's elements ([] for anything else)
fn elems(v: Value) [Value]:
    match v:
        Arr(items):
            return items
        _:
            return []

# how many elements or keys (0 for anything else)
fn size(v: Value) int:
    match v:
        Arr(items):
            return len(items)
        Obj(keys, vals):
            return len(keys)
        _:
            return 0

# the value as compact JSON text
fn dump(v: Value) str:
    match v:
        Null:
            return "null"
        Bool(b):
            return "true" if b else "false"
        Num(x, t):
            return t
        Str(s):
            return json_quote(s)
        Arr(items):
            parts: [str] = []
            for x in items:
                parts.push(dump(x))
            return "[" + ",".join(parts) + "]"
        Obj(keys, vals):
            parts: [str] = []
            for i, k in keys:
                parts.push(json_quote(k) + ":" + dump(vals[i]))
            return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"
```

## library/std/log.tn

```tern
# log: leveled, structured logging to stderr, one line per call.
#
#   import log
#   log.info("server started")
#   log.info_with("user logged in", {"user": name, "id": str(id)})
#   log.warn("slow query")      log.error_with("payment failed", {"order": oid, "err": msg})
#   log.debug("cache miss")     (hidden unless the level is debug)
#
# Output (logfmt, the default):
#   time=2026-09-28T06:45:12.345Z level=info msg="user logged in" user=ada id=7
# log.set_format("json"):
#   {"time":"2026-09-28T06:45:12.345Z","level":"info","msg":"user logged in","user":"ada","id":"7"}
# log.set_format("text"), for people:
#   2026-09-28 06:45:12.345 INFO  user logged in user=ada id=7
#
#   log.debug(msg str)  log.info(msg str)  log.warn(msg str)  log.error(msg str)
#   log.debug_with(msg str, fields {str: str})  ... info_with, warn_with, error_with
#   log.set_level(name str) bool      "debug", "info" (default), "warn", "error", "off"
#   log.set_format(name str) bool     "logfmt" (default), "json", "text"
#   Or set them from the environment: TERN_LOG_LEVEL=debug, TERN_LOG_FORMAT=json.
#
# Times are UTC. Each line is one write(2), so lines from different threads never mix;
# a call below the level costs almost nothing (the fields aren't formatted).
#
# The last 100 records at warn and above are also kept in memory, whatever the level, for
# error reporters (Sentry breadcrumbs, a crash page):
#   log.recent(n int) [Record]        the newest n, oldest first (Record: time, level, msg, fields)
#   log.keep(name str) bool           keep records from this level up instead ("info", "off", ...)

import json

struct Record:
    time: float                 # seconds since 1970
    level: str
    msg: str
    fields: {str: str}

fn recent(n: int) [Record]:
    out: [Record] = []
    json.decode(_recent(n), &out)
    return out

fn _log(level: int, msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    if not _enabled(level):
        return
    kv: [str] = []
    for k, v in fields:
        kv.push(k)
        kv.push(v)
    _write(level, msg, kv)

fn debug(msg: str):
    _log(0, msg, {})

fn info(msg: str):
    _log(1, msg, {})

fn warn(msg: str):
    _log(2, msg, {})

fn error(msg: str):
    _log(3, msg, {})

fn debug_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(0, msg, fields)

fn info_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(1, msg, fields)

fn warn_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(2, msg, fields)

fn error_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(3, msg, fields)
```

## library/std/net.tn

```tern
# net: TCP connections for tasks. Reads and writes look blocking, but only the task
# waits (the other tasks keep running). Also works outside tasks (the thread waits).
#
#   import net
#   import task
#   fn serve_one(c: net.Conn):
#       line = c.read_line()                  # "hello\n"; "" when the peer closes
#       c.write("echo: " + line)
#       c.close()
#   fn main():
#       l = net.listen(9000)                  # every address; net.listen_on("127.0.0.1", 9000)
#       while true:
#           c = l.accept()
#           task.spawn(fn() serve_one(c))
#
#   c = net.connect("example.com", 80)        # check c.ok(); net.error() says why it failed
#
# net.listen(port int) Listener               net.listen_on(host str, port int) Listener
# net.port(l Listener) int  (after listen(0))  net.accept(l Listener) Conn   net.stop(l Listener)
# net.connect(host str, port int) Conn        net.ok(c Conn) bool           net.error() str
# net.read(c Conn, max int) str   ("" at end) net.read_line(c Conn) str  (with its "\n"; "" at end)
# net.read_exact(c Conn, n int) str           net.write(c Conn, data str) bool (false: peer gone)
# net.close(c Conn)                           net.peer(c Conn) str  ("1.2.3.4:5678")
# net.starttls(c Conn, host str, verify bool) bool   TLS on an open connection (needs `import tls`)
# net.pending(c Conn) bool                    a read wouldn't wait (data, or the end, is there)
# net.refill(c Conn, buf mut str, used int, max int) int    drop buf[..used], read onto buf's end
# net.connect_within(host str, port int, ms int) Conn   connect (resolving too) within ms
# net.wait_read(c Conn, ms int) bool          true once a read won't wait; false after ms
# net.read_line_within(c Conn, ms int) str    a whole line, or "" if none came within ms (or the end)
# net.dns_query(name str, qtype int, ms int) str   one DNS question's raw answer ("" if none)
# net.lookup_mx(domain str, ms int) Result[[Mx], str]   mail servers, most preferred first
#
# A Conn is its socket: copies refer to the same connection, and close() closes it for
# all of them (close it when you're done; the program's end closes the rest).
# Not available on wasm.

struct Conn:
    fd: int

struct Listener:
    fd: int

# with Result: c = net.dial("example.com", 80)?   (Err: "net: connect: Connection refused")
fn dial(host: str, port: int) Result[Conn, str]:
    c = connect(host, port)
    if not c.ok():
        return Err("net: " + error())
    return Ok(c)

# TLS on a connection that is already open, when the protocol says so first (PostgreSQL's
# SSLRequest, SMTP's STARTTLS). verify: check the certificate and the host name. Needs
# `import tls` in the program; without it (and when the handshake fails) false, and
# net.error() says why.
fn starttls(c: Conn, host: str, verify: bool) bool:
    return _starttls(c.fd, host, verify)

# Would a read return at once (data, or the end, is waiting)? A look without waiting: an idle
# connection the other side closed says so here (a connection pool's health check).
fn pending(c: Conn) bool:
    return _pending(c.fd)

# A buffered reader's step, for protocols: drops buf[..used] (what's been read), then reads up
# to max more bytes onto the end of buf, in place: no new string per read. Returns the bytes
# read (0: the end, or an error: net.error()).
#   n = c.refill(&buf, at, 65536)     # (then at = 0: what was at buf[at] is at buf[0])
fn refill(c: Conn, buf: mut str, used: int, max: int) int:
    return _refill(c.fd, &buf, used, max)

# connect, the whole attempt (resolving included) within ms milliseconds; check c.ok()
fn connect_within(host: str, port: int, ms: int) Conn:
    return Conn(_connect_ms(host, port, ms))

# Wait (only the task) until a read would return at once: data, or the end. false after ms
# milliseconds without either: a protocol's read timeout.
#   if not c.wait_read(10000): ...       # the server said nothing for 10 s
fn wait_read(c: Conn, ms: int) bool:
    return _readable(c.fd, ms)

# the next line (with its "\n"), or "" when no whole line came within ms or the peer closed
# (a part of one stays buffered for the next read)
fn read_line_within(c: Conn, ms: int) str:
    return _read_line_ms(c.fd, ms)

# One DNS question (qtype: 1 A, 15 MX, 16 TXT, 28 AAAA, ...) over UDP to the servers in
# TERN_DNS_SERVERS, else /etc/resolv.conf's: the answer's raw bytes (RFC 1035), "" if none
# came within ms. lookup_mx reads one; use this for the record types it doesn't.
fn dns_query(name: str, qtype: int, ms: int) str:
    return _dns(name, qtype, ms)

struct Mx:
    pref: int       # lower is preferred
    host: str

fn _u16(b: str, o: int) int:
    return b.byte(o) * 256 + b.byte(o + 1)

# the name at o in a DNS message (compression pointers followed) and where it ends
fn _dns_name(b: str, o0: int) (str, int):
    out = ""
    o = o0
    end = -1
    hops = 0
    while o < len(b) and hops < 64:
        c = b.byte(o)
        if c == 0:
            if end < 0:
                end = o + 1
            return (out, end)
        if c >= 192:
            if o + 1 >= len(b):
                return ("", -1)
            if end < 0:
                end = o + 2
            o = (c - 192) * 256 + b.byte(o + 1)
            hops += 1
            continue
        if o + 1 + c > len(b):
            return ("", -1)
        if out != "":
            out += "."
        out += b[o + 1..o + 1 + c]
        o += 1 + c
    return ("", -1)

# A domain's mail servers (MX records), most preferred first. Ok([]) when the domain exists
# but has none (mail then goes to its A record, RFC 5321); Err when it doesn't exist or no
# answer came within ms.
fn lookup_mx(domain: str, ms: int) Result[[Mx], str]:
    b = _dns(domain, 15, ms)
    if len(b) < 12:
        return Err("no answer for " + domain)
    rcode = b.byte(3) % 16
    if rcode == 3:
        return Err("no such domain: " + domain)
    if rcode != 0:
        return Err("name server failed for " + domain + " (rcode " + str(rcode) + ")")
    qd = _u16(b, 4)
    an = _u16(b, 6)
    o = 12
    for _ in 0..qd:
        o = _dns_name(b, o).1
        if o < 0:
            return Err("bad answer for " + domain)
        o += 4
    out: [Mx] = []
    for _ in 0..an:
        n = _dns_name(b, o)
        o = n.1
        if o < 0 or o + 10 > len(b):
            return Err("bad answer for " + domain)
        kind = _u16(b, o)
        size = _u16(b, o + 8)
        o += 10
        if o + size > len(b):
            return Err("bad answer for " + domain)
        if kind == 15 and size >= 3:
            h = _dns_name(b, o + 2)
            if h.1 >= 0:
                out.push(Mx(_u16(b, o), h.0.lower()))
        o += size
    return Ok(out.sort_by(fn(m) m.pref))
```

## library/std/os.tn

```tern
# os: the process: arguments, environment, exit, stderr, stdin, subprocesses, signals.
#   os.env(name str, default str) str       os.args() [str]  (args()[0] is the program)
#   os.exit(code int)                       (stdout is flushed first)
#   os.eprint(s str)                        a line to stderr
#   os.flush()                              write out buffered stdout now (print is buffered when
#                                           stdout isn't a terminal)
#   os.cpu_count() int                      the cores this process may use (Linux: its affinity mask)
#   os.load_avg() float                     the 1-minute load average (-1.0 where there's none)
#   os.read_line() str                      the next line of stdin, with its "\n" ("" at the end)
#   os.read_all() str                       the rest of stdin
#   os.run(cmd str, args [str]) Output      run a program (PATH is searched) and wait for it
#   os.run_input(cmd str, args [str], input str) Output     ... with input as its stdin
#       Output fields: status (exit code; 128+n if killed by signal n; -1 if it couldn't be
#       started, and then err says why), out (its stdout), err (its stderr)
#   os.wait_signal() str                    wait for SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGUSR1 or SIGUSR2 and
#                                           return its name; the first call makes those signals
#                                           events instead of ending the program. Each signal goes
#                                           to one waiter. (roost.serve drains and returns on
#                                           SIGINT / SIGTERM by itself.)
#   os.spawn(cmd str, args [str]) Process   start a program and keep going; its stdin and stdout
#                                           are pipes, its stderr is ours
#   os.spawn_with(cmd, args, ProcOpts) Process    ... with ProcOpts fields: dir (where it runs; ""
#       here), env (["NAME=value", ...] added to ours), out ("pipe", "inherit", "null", or a
#       file path), err ("inherit", "out" (into its stdout), "null", or a file path)
#   p.ok() bool                             false if it couldn't be started (os.error() says why)
#   p.write(text) bool   p.close_input()    to its stdin (false once it stopped reading)
#   p.out_line() str                        the next line of its stdout, with its "\n" ("" at the end)
#   p.out_bytes(n) str                      the next n bytes of its stdout (fewer at the end)
#   p.out_all() str                         the rest of its stdout (waits for it to close it)
#   p.wait() int                            its exit status (128+n if killed by signal n)
#   p.wait_ms(ms) int                       ... or -1 if it's still running after ms milliseconds
#   p.kill(sig) bool                        send signal sig (15 TERM, 9 KILL, 2 INT) to it and to
#                                           the processes it started (it has its own process group)
#   p.pid() int
#   os.cwd() str   os.chdir(dir) bool   os.setenv(name, value)  (value "" removes it)
#   os.error() str                          why the last spawn / chdir on this thread failed
#   os.on_error(f fn(ErrorReport))          call f with a report of every runtime error from now on,
#                                           caught ones too (a failed task, a web handler's 500):
#                                           message, file, line, function, frames [Frame{function,
#                                           pc}], image_base, slide, build_id, task_id, thread_id,
#                                           time (ns), locals (the failing task's task-locals).
#                                           f runs on a thread of its own, one report at a
#                                           time; its own errors are dropped. Stack overflows aren't
#                                           reported. (For error trackers like Sentry.)
#   os.last_error_report() ErrorReport      the most recent report (message "" if none); recording
#                                           starts with the first on_error or last_error_report call
# Reading stdin or waiting for a subprocess or a signal parks only the task (in a task).
#
#   r = os.run("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"])
#   if r.status == 0:
#       print(r.out.trim())
#   else:
#       os.eprint("git failed: " + r.err)
#
#   server = os.spawn("./server", ["--port", "8080"])
#   line = server.out_line()                 # e.g. wait until it says it's listening
#   ...
#   server.kill(15)
#   server.wait()

struct Output:
    status: int
    out: str
    err: str

fn run(cmd: str, args: [str]) Output:
    return run_input(cmd, args, "")

struct Process:
    h: int

struct ProcOpts:
    dir: str
    env: [str]
    out: str
    err: str

fn spawn(cmd: str, args: [str]) Process:
    return spawn_with(cmd, args, ProcOpts("", [], "pipe", "inherit"))

fn spawn_with(cmd: str, args: [str], o: ProcOpts) Process:
    return Process(_spawn(cmd, args, o.dir, o.env, o.out, o.err))

fn ok(p: Process) bool:
    return p.h >= 0

fn pid(p: Process) int:
    return _pid(p.h)

fn write(p: Process, text: str) bool:
    return _write(p.h, text)

fn close_input(p: Process):
    _close_input(p.h)

fn out_line(p: Process) str:
    return _out_line(p.h)

fn out_bytes(p: Process, n: int) str:
    return _out_bytes(p.h, n)

fn out_all(p: Process) str:
    return _out_all(p.h)

fn wait(p: Process) int:
    return _wait_ms(p.h, -1)

fn wait_ms(p: Process, ms: int) int:
    return _wait_ms(p.h, ms)

fn kill(p: Process, sig: int) bool:
    return _kill(p.h, sig)

# ---- error reports
struct Frame:
    function: str          # the Tern function (or the C symbol; "" if unknown)
    pc: int

struct ErrorReport:
    message: str           # "runtime error (...): ..." as printed
    file: str              # the source file ("" if unknown)
    line: int
    function: str          # the Tern function the error happened in ("" if unknown)
    frames: [Frame]        # innermost first
    image_base: int        # where the executable is loaded, and its ASLR slide
    slide: int
    build_id: str          # Mach-O LC_UUID / ELF GNU build id, in hex (for symbolicating)
    task_id: int           # 0 outside tasks
    thread_id: int
    time: int              # nanoseconds since the Unix epoch
    locals: {str: str}     # the failing task's task-locals (task.local_set), up to about 4KB

fn on_error(f: fn(ErrorReport)):
    _on_error(fn(s: str) f(_decode_report(s)))

fn last_error_report() ErrorReport:
    return _decode_report(_last_report())

fn _decode_report(s: str) ErrorReport:
    p = s.split(chr(31))
    locals: {str: str} = {}
    if len(p) < 11:
        return ErrorReport("", "", 0, "", [], 0, 0, "", 0, 0, 0, locals)
    kv = p[10].split(chr(30))
    j = 0
    while j + 1 < len(kv):
        locals[kv[j]] = kv[j + 1]
        j += 2
    frames: [Frame] = []
    i = 11
    while i + 1 < len(p):
        frames.push(Frame(p[i + 1], p[i].to_int(0)))
        i += 2
    return ErrorReport(p[0], p[1], p[2].to_int(0), p[3], frames, p[4].to_int(0), p[5].to_int(0), p[6], p[7].to_int(0), p[8].to_int(0), p[9].to_int(0), locals)
```

## library/std/path/glob.tn

```tern
# path: shell-style patterns (matches) and finding the files that match them (glob).

import fs

fn matches(pattern: str, name: str) bool:
    return _match(pattern, 0, name, 0)

# Iterative * with one backtrack point (linear for patterns with a single *, and never
# exponential: a later * replaces the earlier backtrack point).
fn _match(pat: str, p0: int, s: str, s0: int) bool:
    p = p0
    i = s0
    star_p = -1
    star_i = 0
    np = len(pat)
    ns = len(s)
    while true:
        if p < np:
            c = pat.byte(p)
            if c == 42:
                star_p = p
                star_i = i
                p += 1
                continue
            if i < ns:
                ch = s.byte(i)
                if c == 63:
                    if ch != 47:
                        p += 1
                        i += 1
                        continue
                elif c == 91:
                    end = _class_end(pat, p)
                    if end < 0:
                        return false
                    if ch != 47 and _in_class(pat, p + 1, end, ch):
                        p = end + 1
                        i += 1
                        continue
                elif c == 92:
                    if p + 1 >= np:
                        return false
                    if pat.byte(p + 1) == ch:
                        p += 2
                        i += 1
                        continue
                elif c == ch:
                    p += 1
                    i += 1
                    continue
            elif c == 91 and _class_end(pat, p) < 0:
                return false
        elif i == ns:
            return true
        # mismatch: let the last * take one more byte (never a "/")
        if star_p < 0 or star_i >= ns or s.byte(star_i) == 47:
            return false
        star_i += 1
        p = star_p + 1
        i = star_i
    return false

# Index of the "]" closing the class that starts at pat[p] == "[", or -1.
fn _class_end(pat: str, p: int) int:
    j = p + 1
    n = len(pat)
    if j < n and (pat.byte(j) == 33 or pat.byte(j) == 94):
        j += 1
    if j < n and pat.byte(j) == 93:          # "]" first is a member
        j += 1
    while j < n:
        c = pat.byte(j)
        if c == 92:
            j += 2
            continue
        if c == 93:
            return j
        j += 1
    return -1

fn _in_class(pat: str, a: int, end: int, ch: int) bool:
    neg = false
    j = a
    if j < end and (pat.byte(j) == 33 or pat.byte(j) == 94):
        neg = true
        j += 1
    found = false
    first = true
    while j < end:
        lo = pat.byte(j)
        if lo == 92 and j + 1 < end:
            j += 1
            lo = pat.byte(j)
        elif lo == 93 and not first:
            break
        first = false
        j += 1
        hi = lo
        if j + 1 < end and pat.byte(j) == 45:
            j += 1
            hi = pat.byte(j)
            if hi == 92 and j + 1 < end:
                j += 1
                hi = pat.byte(j)
            j += 1
        if ch >= lo and ch <= hi:
            found = true
    return found != neg

fn _has_meta(s: str) bool:
    for i in 0..len(s):
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 42 or c == 63 or c == 91 or c == 92:
            return true
    return false

# The piece with its "\" escapes removed (a piece with no * ? [ is a plain name).
fn _unescape(s: str) str:
    if not s.contains("\\"):
        return s
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s.byte(i) == 92 and i + 1 < len(s):
            i += 1
        out += s[i]
        i += 1
    return out

fn glob(pattern: str) [str]:
    out: [str] = []
    if pattern == "":
        return out
    pieces: [str] = []
    for piece in pattern.split("/"):
        if piece != "" and piece != ".":
            pieces.push(piece)
    start = "."
    if pattern.starts_with("/"):
        start = "/"
    _glob(start, pieces, 0, &out)
    out = out.sort_by(fn(x) x)
    if pattern.find_from("**", pattern.find("**") + 2) < 0:
        return out
    # two ** can reach a path more than one way
    once: [str] = []
    for p in out:
        if len(once) == 0 or once[len(once) - 1] != p:
            once.push(p)
    return once

fn _child(d: str, name: str) str:
    if d == ".":
        return name
    if d == "/":
        return "/" + name
    return d + "/" + name

# names in list_marked(d) end in "/" for a directory
fn _glob(d: str, pieces: [str], k: int, out: mut [str]):
    if k == len(pieces):
        if d != "." and d != "/":
            out.push(d)
        return
    piece = pieces[k]
    last = k + 1 == len(pieces)
    if piece == "**":
        if k + 1 < len(pieces) and pieces[k + 1] != "**" and pieces[k + 1] != ".." and _has_meta(pieces[k + 1]):
            _glob_star_star(d, pieces, k, &out)
            return
        _glob(d, pieces, k + 1, &out)
        for name in fs.list_marked(d):
            if name.byte(len(name) - 1) == 47 and name.byte(0) != 46:
                _glob(_child(d, name[..len(name) - 1]), pieces, k, &out)
        return
    if piece == ".." or not _has_meta(piece):
        c = _child(d, _unescape(piece))
        info = fs.stat(c)
        if info.exists and (last or info.is_dir):
            _glob(c, pieces, k + 1, &out)
        return
    dot_ok = piece.byte(0) == 46
    for name in fs.list_marked(d):
        if name.byte(0) == 46 and not dot_ok:
            continue
        is_dir = name.byte(len(name) - 1) == 47
        if not last and not is_dir:
            continue
        nm = name
        if is_dir:
            nm = name[..len(name) - 1]
        if matches(piece, nm):
            _glob(_child(d, nm), pieces, k + 1, &out)

# "**" followed by a pattern piece: one listing of d serves both (the next piece matched here,
# and the directories ** goes down into)
fn _glob_star_star(d: str, pieces: [str], k: int, out: mut [str]):
    piece = pieces[k + 1]
    dot_ok = piece.byte(0) == 46
    last = k + 2 == len(pieces)
    for name in fs.list_marked(d):
        is_dir = name.byte(len(name) - 1) == 47
        nm = name
        if is_dir:
            nm = name[..len(name) - 1]
        hidden = name.byte(0) == 46
        if (last or is_dir) and (dot_ok or not hidden) and matches(piece, nm):
            _glob(_child(d, nm), pieces, k + 2, &out)
        if is_dir and not hidden:
            _glob_star_star(_child(d, nm), pieces, k, &out)
```

## library/std/path/path.tn

```tern
# path: file paths as text (joining, splitting, cleaning, extensions, relative paths, globs).
# Paths use "/" (as on Linux, macOS and WebAssembly); nothing here touches the disk except
# path.abs (the working directory) and path.glob (lists directories).
#
#   import path
#   p = path.join("assets", "img/logo.png")       # "assets/img/logo.png"
#   path.dir(p)  path.base(p)  path.ext(p)         # "assets/img"  "logo.png"  ".png"
#   path.stem(p)  path.with_ext(p, ".webp")        # "logo"  "assets/img/logo.webp"
#   path.clean("a//b/./c/../d/")                   # "a/b/d"
#   path.rel("/srv/app", "/srv/app/static/x.css")? # "static/x.css"
#   for f in path.glob("src/**/*.tn"): ...         # every .tn file below src, sorted
#
#   path.join(a, b) str          a and b with one "/" between, cleaned ("" parts are skipped);
#                                like Go's filepath.Join: join("/a", "/b") is "/a/b"
#   path.join_all(parts) str     the same for any number of parts
#   path.resolve(base, p) str    p if it's absolute, else join(base, p) (like Python's
#                                os.path.join and Node's path.resolve with two arguments)
#   path.clean(p) str            the shortest equal path: one "/" between names, no "." names,
#                                "a/.." removed, no trailing "/"; "" becomes "."; ".." that go
#                                above the start stay ("../x"), above "/" are dropped ("/x")
#   path.dir(p) str              everything before the last name, cleaned: "a/b" -> "a",
#                                "a" -> ".", "/a" -> "/"
#   path.base(p) str             the last name, trailing "/" ignored: "a/b/" -> "b", "" -> ".",
#                                "/" -> "/"
#   path.split(p) (str, str)     (everything up to and including the last "/", the rest):
#                                "a/b.txt" -> ("a/", "b.txt"); joined back they are p
#   path.ext(p) str              the extension of the last name, with its dot: ".gz" for
#                                "x.tar.gz"; "" when there is none (".bashrc" has none)
#   path.stem(p) str             the last name without its extension: "x.tar" for "x.tar.gz"
#   path.with_ext(p, ext) str    p with its extension replaced (or added): with_ext("a/b.md",
#                                ".html") == "a/b.html"; ext "" removes it
#   path.parts(p) [str]          the names in clean(p): "/a/b" -> ["/", "a", "b"], "." -> []
#   path.is_abs(p) bool          starts with "/"
#   path.abs(p) str              resolve(os.cwd(), p), cleaned
#   path.rel(base, target) Result[str, str]
#                                a path that is target when joined to base: rel("a/b", "a/c/d")
#                                == Ok("../c/d"); Err when one is absolute and the other isn't
#                                (or base climbs out with ".." where target doesn't)
#   path.matches(pattern, name) bool
#                                shell-style match of the whole name: * (any run of bytes but
#                                "/"), ? (one byte but "/"), [abc] [a-z] [!a-z] (one byte in /
#                                not in the set), \x (x itself); a malformed pattern is false
#   path.glob(pattern) [str]     the existing paths that match, sorted; each "/"-separated piece
#                                is a matches() pattern, and a piece that is just ** matches any
#                                number of directories (zero included). Names starting with "."
#                                match only a piece that starts with "." (so ** skips .git).
#                                "src/**/*.tn", "/etc/*.conf", "docs/[a-c]*.md"

import os

fn join(a: str, b: str) str:
    if a == "":
        return clean(b)
    if b == "":
        return clean(a)
    return clean(a + "/" + b)

fn join_all(parts: [str]) str:
    s = ""
    for p in parts:
        if p != "":
            if s == "":
                s = p
            else:
                s += "/" + p
    return clean(s)

fn resolve(base: str, p: str) str:
    if p.starts_with("/"):
        return clean(p)
    return join(base, p)

fn is_abs(p: str) bool:
    return p.starts_with("/")

fn abs(p: str) str:
    return resolve(os.cwd(), p)

# clean in C (runtime/strings.h): an already-clean p comes back as it is
fn clean(p: str) str:
    return _clean(p, len(p))

fn _last_slash(p: str) int:
    i = len(p) - 1
    while i >= 0 and p.byte(i) != 47:
        i -= 1
    return i

fn split(p: str) (str, str):
    i = _last_slash(p)
    return (p[..i + 1], p[i + 1..])

fn dir(p: str) str:
    return _dir(p)

fn base(p: str) str:
    return _name(p, false)

# Where the extension's dot is in p (-1 if none): after the last "/", not the name's first byte.
fn _ext_at(p: str) int:
    i = len(p) - 1
    while i >= 0:
        c = p.byte(i)
        if c == 47:
            return -1
        if c == 46:
            if i == 0 or p.byte(i - 1) == 47:
                return -1
            return i
        i -= 1
    return -1

fn ext(p: str) str:
    i = _ext_at(p)
    if i < 0:
        return ""
    return p[i..]

fn stem(p: str) str:
    return _name(p, true)

fn with_ext(p: str, e: str) str:
    i = _ext_at(p)
    if i < 0:
        return p + e
    return p[..i] + e

fn parts(p: str) [str]:
    c = clean(p)
    out: [str] = []
    if c == ".":
        return out
    if c.starts_with("/"):
        out.push("/")
        c = c[1..]
        if c == "":
            return out
    for name in c.split("/"):
        out.push(name)
    return out

fn rel(base_path: str, target: str) Result[str, str]:
    b = clean(base_path)
    t = clean(target)
    if b == t:
        return Ok(".")
    if is_abs(b) != is_abs(t):
        return Err(f"path: can't make {target} relative to {base_path}")
    if b == ".":
        b = ""
    if t == ".":
        t = ""
    # skip the names they share, one at a time (Go's filepath.Rel)
    bl = len(b)
    tl = len(t)
    b0 = 0
    bi = 0
    t0 = 0
    ti = 0
    while true:
        while bi < bl and b.byte(bi) != 47:
            bi += 1
        while ti < tl and t.byte(ti) != 47:
            ti += 1
        if not _same(b, b0, bi, t, t0, ti):
            break
        if bi < bl:
            bi += 1
        if ti < tl:
            ti += 1
        b0 = bi
        t0 = ti
        if b0 >= bl and t0 >= tl:
            break
    if bi - b0 == 2 and b.byte(b0) == 46 and b.byte(b0 + 1) == 46:
        return Err(f"path: can't make {target} relative to {base_path}")
    if b0 < bl:
        out = ".."
        for k in b0..bl:
            if b.byte(k) == 47:
                out += "/.."
        if t0 < tl:
            out += "/" + t[t0..]
        return Ok(out)
    return Ok(t[t0..])

fn _same(a: str, a0: int, a1: int, b: str, b0: int, b1: int) bool:
    if a1 - a0 != b1 - b0:
        return false
    for k in 0..a1 - a0:
        if a.byte(a0 + k) != b.byte(b0 + k):
            return false
    return true
```

## library/std/pqueue.tn

```tern
# pqueue: values of any type, taken out in order of a priority (an int, float or str) given
# with each: lowest first (queue) or highest first (queue_max). For Dijkstra, schedulers,
# event loops. The priority comes first, as in Python's heapq tuples. Values with the same
# priority come out in no particular order.
#
#   import pqueue
#   q = pqueue.queue[int, str]()             # priorities int, values str
#   q.push(3, "deploy")
#   q.push(1, "build")
#   q.pop()                                  # Some("build")
#
#   pqueue.queue[P, T]() PriorityQueue[P, T]    pqueue.queue_max[P, T]()
#   q.push(priority, value)    q.pop() Option[T]    q.peek() Option[T]
#   q.peek_priority() Option[P]    q.len()    q.is_empty()

struct PriorityQueue[P, T]:
    prios: [P]
    vals: [T]
    max: bool
    big: bool       # has held _BIG values: when it empties, its arrays are let go

fn queue[P: Ord, T]() PriorityQueue[P, T]:
    return PriorityQueue[P, T]([], [], false, false)

fn queue_max[P: Ord, T]() PriorityQueue[P, T]:
    return PriorityQueue[P, T]([], [], true, false)

fn push[P: Ord, T](q: mut PriorityQueue[P, T], priority: P, value: T):
    q.prios.push(priority)
    q.vals.push(value)
    if len(q.prios) == _BIG:
        q.big = true
    if q.max:
        _up_max(&q.prios, &q.vals, priority, value)
    else:
        _up_min(&q.prios, &q.vals, priority, value)

# A queue that has grown big gives its memory back when pop empties it, as heap does.
const _BIG = 4096

fn pop[P: Ord, T](q: mut PriorityQueue[P, T]) Option[T]:
    n = len(q.prios)
    if n == 0:
        return None
    top = q.vals[0]
    if n == 1 and q.big:
        q.prios = []
        q.vals = []
        q.big = false
        return Some(top)
    lp = q.prios.pop()
    lv = q.vals.pop()
    if n > 1:
        if q.max:
            _refill_max(&q.prios, &q.vals, lp, lv)
        else:
            _refill_min(&q.prios, &q.vals, lp, lv)
    return Some(top)

# The sifts work on the two arrays themselves, one loop for each order (decided once per
# call), moving a hole instead of swapping. The heap is 4-ary (children of i at 4i+1 .. 4i+4),
# as in heap.tn: half the levels of a binary heap. After a pop the hole at the root goes down
# to a leaf by the best child, then (p, v), the old last pair, rises from there.
fn _up_min[P: Ord, T](ps: mut [P], vs: mut [T], p: P, v: T):
    i = len(ps) - 1
    while i > 0:
        u = (i - 1) >> 2
        if p >= ps[u]:
            break
        ps[i] = ps[u]
        vs[i] = vs[u]
        i = u
    ps[i] = p
    vs[i] = v

fn _refill_min[P: Ord, T](ps: mut [P], vs: mut [T], p: P, v: T):
    n = len(ps)
    i = 0
    c = 1
    while c + 3 < n:
        m = c
        if ps[c + 1] < ps[c]:
            m = c + 1
        m2 = c + 2
        if ps[c + 3] < ps[c + 2]:
            m2 = c + 3
        if ps[m2] < ps[m]:
            m = m2
        ps[i] = ps[m]
        vs[i] = vs[m]
        i = m
        c = 4 * i + 1
    if c < n:
        m = c
        k = c + 1
        while k < n:
            if ps[k] < ps[m]:
                m = k
            k += 1
        ps[i] = ps[m]
        vs[i] = vs[m]
        i = m
    while i > 0:
        u = (i - 1) >> 2
        if p >= ps[u]:
            break
        ps[i] = ps[u]
        vs[i] = vs[u]
        i = u
    ps[i] = p
    vs[i] = v

fn _up_max[P: Ord, T](ps: mut [P], vs: mut [T], p: P, v: T):
    i = len(ps) - 1
    while i > 0:
        u = (i - 1) >> 2
        if p <= ps[u]:
            break
        ps[i] = ps[u]
        vs[i] = vs[u]
        i = u
    ps[i] = p
    vs[i] = v

fn _refill_max[P: Ord, T](ps: mut [P], vs: mut [T], p: P, v: T):
    n = len(ps)
    i = 0
    c = 1
    while c + 3 < n:
        m = c
        if ps[c + 1] > ps[c]:
            m = c + 1
        m2 = c + 2
        if ps[c + 3] > ps[c + 2]:
            m2 = c + 3
        if ps[m2] > ps[m]:
            m = m2
        ps[i] = ps[m]
        vs[i] = vs[m]
        i = m
        c = 4 * i + 1
    if c < n:
        m = c
        k = c + 1
        while k < n:
            if ps[k] > ps[m]:
                m = k
            k += 1
        ps[i] = ps[m]
        vs[i] = vs[m]
        i = m
    while i > 0:
        u = (i - 1) >> 2
        if p <= ps[u]:
            break
        ps[i] = ps[u]
        vs[i] = vs[u]
        i = u
    ps[i] = p
    vs[i] = v

fn peek[P, T](q: PriorityQueue[P, T]) Option[T]:
    if len(q.vals) == 0:
        return None
    return Some(q.vals[0])

fn peek_priority[P, T](q: PriorityQueue[P, T]) Option[P]:
    if len(q.prios) == 0:
        return None
    return Some(q.prios[0])

fn len[P, T](q: PriorityQueue[P, T]) int:
    return len(q.prios)

fn is_empty[P, T](q: PriorityQueue[P, T]) bool:
    return len(q.prios) == 0
```

## library/std/prelude.tn

```tern
# The prelude: imported by every module, so its names need no `import` (a module's own
# definitions of the same names win).
#
#   enum Option[T]: Some(value: T) / None           "maybe a value": no null
#   enum Result[T, E]: Ok(value: T) / Err(error: E)  success, or an error
#
# Build them bare: `Some(3)`, `None`, `Ok(v)`, `Err("bad input")`. Test with `match`, or
# with `if o is Some(v):` (v is bound inside the `if`). `x?` returns early from a function
# that itself returns an Option (on None) or a Result (on Err). Methods:
#   o.unwrap_or(default: T) T      o.unwrap() T (a runtime error on None)
#   o.expect(msg: str) T           o.is_some() bool      o.is_none() bool
#   r.unwrap_or(default: T) T      r.unwrap() T (a runtime error on Err)
#   r.expect(msg: str) T           r.is_ok() bool        r.is_err() bool
#   r.ok() Option[T]               r.err() Option[E]
#   r.context(msg: str) Result[T, str]    an Err becomes "msg: error" (for Result[T, str])
#   r.map_err(f: fn(E) F) Result[T, F]    the Err transformed by f
#   o.ok_or(err: E) Result[T, E]          Some(v) -> Ok(v), None -> Err(err)
#
# And for strings and arrays (called as methods):
#   s.strip_prefix(p: str) str            s without p at its start (s if it doesn't start with p)
#   s.strip_suffix(p: str) str            s without p at its end
#   xs.extend(ys: [T])                    every element of ys pushed onto xs
#   xs.sorted() [T]                       a sorted copy (ints, floats, strs; `sort_by` for other orders)

enum Option[T]:
    Some(value: T)
    None

enum Result[T, E]:
    Ok(value: T)
    Err(error: E)

fn option_unwrap_or[T](o: Option[T], default: T) T:
    match o:
        Some(v):
            return v
        None:
            return default

fn option_unwrap[T](o: Option[T]) T:
    match o:
        Some(v):
            return v
        None:
            panic("unwrap() on None")

fn option_expect[T](o: Option[T], msg: str) T:
    match o:
        Some(v):
            return v
        None:
            panic(msg)

fn option_is_some[T](o: Option[T]) bool:
    match o:
        Some(v):
            return true
        None:
            return false

fn option_is_none[T](o: Option[T]) bool:
    return not option_is_some(o)

fn result_unwrap_or[T, E](r: Result[T, E], default: T) T:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return v
        Err(e):
            return default

fn result_unwrap[T, E](r: Result[T, E]) T:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return v
        Err(e):
            panic("unwrap() on Err")

fn result_expect[T, E](r: Result[T, E], msg: str) T:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return v
        Err(e):
            panic(msg)

fn result_is_ok[T, E](r: Result[T, E]) bool:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return true
        Err(e):
            return false

fn result_is_err[T, E](r: Result[T, E]) bool:
    return not result_is_ok(r)

fn result_ok[T, E](r: Result[T, E]) Option[T]:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return Some(v)
        Err(e):
            return None

fn result_err[T, E](r: Result[T, E]) Option[E]:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return None
        Err(e):
            return Some(e)

fn result_context[T](r: Result[T, str], msg: str) Result[T, str]:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return Ok(v)
        Err(e):
            return Err(msg + ": " + e)

fn result_map_err[T, E, F](r: Result[T, E], f: fn(E) F) Result[T, F]:
    match r:
        Ok(v):
            return Ok(v)
        Err(e):
            return Err(f(e))

fn option_ok_or[T, E](o: Option[T], err: E) Result[T, E]:
    match o:
        Some(v):
            return Ok(v)
        None:
            return Err(err)

fn strip_prefix(s: str, p: str) str:
    return s[len(p)..] if s.starts_with(p) else s

fn strip_suffix(s: str, p: str) str:
    return s[..len(s) - len(p)] if s.ends_with(p) else s

fn extend[T](xs: mut [T], ys: [T]):
    for y in ys:
        xs.push(y)

fn sorted[T: Ord](xs: [T]) [T]:
    return xs.sort_by(fn(x) x)
```

## library/std/random.tn

```tern
# random: fast pseudo-random numbers (xoshiro256**, one generator per thread).
#   random.int(lo, hi) int      (lo..hi inclusive)
#   random.float() float        (0.0 <= x < 1.0)
# Not for cryptography.
```

## library/std/re/compile.tn

```tern
# re: compiling a tree (parse.tn) into what the matchers run:
#   - a program over characters for the Pike VM, the backtracker and the one-pass walk
#     (I_* instructions: SPLIT and JMP, SAVE for group bounds, ASSERT, and CHAR / ANY / CLASS
#     that read one character);
#   - the same pattern over bytes, forwards and reversed, for the lazy DFA (B_* instructions;
#     UTF-8 spelled out as byte ranges, the RE2 / Go way);
#   - what lets a search skip ahead: a literal prefix, the bytes a match can start with, an
#     inner literal (an email's @), or a few literal alternatives (Teddy, prefilter.tn).
# Loops are compiled as Go's regexp does (k+ is `L: k; split L, out`), which gives Perl's order
# of preference for empty iterations.

import simd

const I_CHAR = 0
const I_ANY = 1
const I_ANYNL = 2
const I_CLASS = 3
const I_SPLIT = 4
const I_JMP = 5
const I_SAVE = 6
const I_MATCH = 7
const I_ASSERT = 8

const B_BYTE = 0
const B_SPLIT = 1
const B_JMP = 2
const B_MATCH = 3
const B_ASSERT = 4

const MAX_CODE = 200000

# a program over characters: instruction i is (op[i], x[i], y[i], fold[i]); x: the character,
# class, first branch, slot or assertion; y: the second branch
struct Code:
    op: [int]
    x: [int]
    y: [int]
    fold: [bool]
    bad: bool

# a program over bytes: B_BYTE reads a byte in lo..hi
struct BCode:
    op: [int]
    lo: [int]
    hi: [int]
    x: [int]
    y: [int]
    bad: bool
    rev: bool

# a literal alternative for Teddy: bytes b, with a mask per byte (0x20: an ASCII letter in
# either case: text byte t matches when t | m == b), and whether it's all of what matched
struct Lit:
    b: str
    m: str
    exact: bool

struct Prog:
    pattern: str
    code: Code
    classes: [Class]
    ngroups: int
    names: [str]
    prefix: str               # a literal every match starts with (case-sensitive)
    rare: int                 # the index of its rarest byte
    rare2: int                # ... and of the next rarest (rare if it's one byte)
    literal: bool             # the whole pattern is that literal, no groups
    first: [bool]             # 256: bytes a match can start with (when has_first)
    has_first: bool
    skip: bool                # the prefilter is worth using
    rlo: [int]                # first as up to 6 byte ranges, for the 16-byte scan ([]: too many)
    rhi: [int]
    vlo: [bytes16]            # ... as vectors: each range's start, and its length - 1
    vspan: [bytes16]
    anchored: bool            # starts with \A (or ^ without m)
    nullable: bool
    fffd: bool                # can match U+FFFD (invalid UTF-8 must then go to the VM)
    dfa: bool                 # the byte programs were built
    fwd: BCode                # (?s:.)*? then the pattern; bstart: the pattern alone
    bstart: int
    rev: BCode
    bcls: [int]               # 256: byte -> class (bytes that behave alike share one)
    nbcls: int
    inner: bool               # P L S, L a literal P can never contain
    lit: str
    lrare: int
    lrare2: int
    icode: BCode              # P, reversed
    lits: [Lit]
    tk: int                   # Teddy compares this many first bytes (1-3)
    teddy: bool
    lits_exact: bool          # the pattern is exactly those strings, no groups
    tb: [int]                 # 3 * 256: per position, byte -> buckets
    tlo: [int]                # 3 * 16: low nibble -> buckets
    thi: [int]
    vtlo: [bytes16]           # ... as 3 vector tables each (Teddy, simd.lookup)
    vthi: [bytes16]
    onepass: [int]            # 5 words a SPLIT (bits 0..255: next bytes that tk2 x; 256: end); []: no
    fixoff: [int]             # no SPLITs, ASCII only: each slot's offset in the match ([]: no)
    fixlen: int
    am0: [int]                # per instruction that reads a character: the ASCII characters
    am1: [int]                # it takes, as bits (am0: 0..63, am1: 64..127), for the backtracker
    ahi: [bool]               # ... and whether it takes every character past ASCII
    poss: [bool]              # per SPLIT of a greedy one-character loop: what follows can't
                              # start with a character the loop takes (the backtracker then
                              # tries only the loop's end)

# one byte as a string (chr encodes 128..255 as UTF-8)
fn _byte_str(b: int) str:
    return [byte(b)].to_str()

# the index of s's rarest byte other than at r (r when s is one byte); a far one breaks ties
fn second_rare(s: str, r: int) int:
    b = r
    for i in 0..len(s):
        if i != r and (b == r or rank(s.byte(i)) < rank(s.byte(b)) or (rank(s.byte(i)) == rank(s.byte(b)) and _far(i, r) > _far(b, r))):
            b = i
    return b

fn _far(i: int, r: int) int:
    return i - r if i > r else r - i

fn _no_code() Code:
    return Code([], [], [], [], false)

fn _no_bcode(rev: bool) BCode:
    return BCode([], [], [], [], [], false, rev)

fn _op(m: mut Code, op: int, x: int, y: int) int:
    if len(m.op) >= MAX_CODE:
        m.bad = true
        return len(m.op)
    m.op.push(op)
    m.x.push(x)
    m.y.push(y)
    m.fold.push(false)
    return len(m.op) - 1

fn nullable(t: Tree, i: int) bool:
    n = t.nodes[i]
    k = n.kind
    if k == N_EMPTY or k == N_ASSERT:
        return true
    if k == N_CAT:
        for c in n.kids:
            if not nullable(t, c):
                return false
        return true
    if k == N_ALT:
        for c in n.kids:
            if nullable(t, c):
                return true
        return false
    if k == N_REP:
        return n.min == 0 or nullable(t, n.kids[0])
    if k == N_GROUP:
        return nullable(t, n.kids[0])
    return false

fn _prefer(m: mut Code, l: int, body: int, out: int, greedy: bool):
    if m.bad:
        return
    if greedy:
        m.x[l] = body
        m.y[l] = out
    else:
        m.x[l] = out
        m.y[l] = body

fn _plus(m: mut Code, t: Tree, k: int, greedy: bool):
    body = len(m.op)
    _gen(&m, t, k)
    l = _op(&m, I_SPLIT, 0, 0)
    _prefer(&m, l, body, l + 1, greedy)

fn _star(m: mut Code, t: Tree, k: int, greedy: bool):
    if nullable(t, k):                              # (k+)?
        q = _op(&m, I_SPLIT, 0, 0)
        _plus(&m, t, k, greedy)
        _prefer(&m, q, q + 1, len(m.op), greedy)
        return
    l = _op(&m, I_SPLIT, 0, 0)
    _gen(&m, t, k)
    _op(&m, I_JMP, l, 0)
    _prefer(&m, l, l + 1, len(m.op), greedy)

fn _gen_rep(m: mut Code, t: Tree, n: Node):
    k = n.kids[0]
    if n.max < 0:                                   # k{min,}: k^(min-1) k+, or k*
        i = 0
        while i + 1 < n.min and not m.bad:
            _gen(&m, t, k)
            i += 1
        if n.min == 0:
            _star(&m, t, k, n.greedy)
        else:
            _plus(&m, t, k, n.greedy)
        return
    i = 0
    while i < n.min and not m.bad:
        _gen(&m, t, k)
        i += 1
    splits: [int] = []                              # then up to max-min more, nested: (k(k)?)?
    for j in 0..n.max - n.min:
        if m.bad:
            break
        splits.push(_op(&m, I_SPLIT, 0, 0))
        _gen(&m, t, k)
    if not m.bad:
        for s in splits:
            _prefer(&m, s, s + 1, len(m.op), n.greedy)

fn _gen(m: mut Code, t: Tree, i: int):
    if m.bad:
        return
    n = t.nodes[i]
    k = n.kind
    if k == N_CHAR:
        j = _op(&m, I_CHAR, lower(n.c) if n.fold else n.c, 0)
        if not m.bad:
            m.fold[j] = n.fold
    elif k == N_ANY:
        _op(&m, I_ANYNL if n.dotnl else I_ANY, 0, 0)
    elif k == N_CLASS:
        _op(&m, I_CLASS, n.cls, 0)
    elif k == N_ASSERT:
        _op(&m, I_ASSERT, n.at, 0)
    elif k == N_CAT:
        for c in n.kids:
            _gen(&m, t, c)
    elif k == N_GROUP:
        if n.group >= 0:
            _op(&m, I_SAVE, 2 * n.group, 0)
        _gen(&m, t, n.kids[0])
        if n.group >= 0:
            _op(&m, I_SAVE, 2 * n.group + 1, 0)
    elif k == N_REP:
        _gen_rep(&m, t, n)
    elif k == N_ALT:
        jmps: [int] = []
        last = len(n.kids) - 1
        for c, kid in n.kids:
            s = -1
            if c < last:
                s = _op(&m, I_SPLIT, 0, 0)
            if s >= 0 and not m.bad:
                m.x[s] = len(m.op)
            _gen(&m, t, kid)
            if c < last:
                jmps.push(_op(&m, I_JMP, 0, 0))
            if s >= 0 and not m.bad:
                m.y[s] = len(m.op)
        if not m.bad:
            for j in jmps:
                m.x[j] = len(m.op)

# roughly how often a byte occurs in typical text, per thousand bytes (English prose, code and
# logs): to pick a literal's rarest byte, and to judge whether stopping at every possible first
# byte of a match is worth it
fn rank(b: int) int:
    if b == 32:
        return 150
    if b == 10:
        return 20
    if b >= 97 and b <= 122:
        return _letter_rank(b - 97)
    if b >= 65 and b <= 90:
        return 1 + _letter_rank(b - 65) / 12
    if b >= 48 and b <= 57:
        return 4
    if b == 46 or b == 44 or b == 34 or b == 45 or b == 95 or b == 47 or b == 58 or b == 61 or b == 9:
        return 8
    if b >= 0x80:
        return 3
    return 1

# per letter a..z (from "etaoinshrdlcumwfgypbvkjxqz" with 100 70 65 60 57 57 50 50 48 34 32 22
# 22 20 19 18 16 16 15 12 8 6 2 2 1 1)
fn _letter_rank(i: int) int:
    t = [65, 12, 22, 34, 100, 18, 16, 50, 57, 2, 6, 32, 20, 57, 60, 15, 1, 48, 50, 70, 22, 8, 19, 2, 16, 1]
    return t[i]

# the literal every match starts with, from the tree (case-sensitive characters only); open
# stays true while the whole pattern so far is that literal
fn _prefix(t: Tree, i: int, buf: mut str, open: mut bool):
    if not open:
        return
    n = t.nodes[i]
    k = n.kind
    if k == N_CHAR:
        if n.fold or len(buf) + 4 > 64:
            open = false
            return
        buf += encode(n.c)
        return
    if k == N_CAT:
        for c in n.kids:
            if not open:
                return
            _prefix(t, c, &buf, &open)
```
