```tern
        return
    if k == N_GROUP:
        _prefix(t, n.kids[0], &buf, &open)
        return
    if k == N_EMPTY:
        return
    if k == N_REP:
        if n.min >= 1:
            _prefix(t, n.kids[0], &buf, &open)       # (its first copy)
        open = false
        return
    open = false

fn _set(set: mut [bool], b: int):
    set[b] = true

# the bytes a match can start with: follow the program from pc to the first characters
fn _first(p: Prog, pc0: int, set: mut [bool], seen: mut [bool]) bool:
    pc = pc0
    while true:
        if seen[pc]:
            return true
        seen[pc] = true
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_JMP:
            pc = p.code.x[pc]
            continue
        if op == I_SAVE or op == I_ASSERT:            # (an assertion only narrows where it starts)
            pc += 1
            continue
        if op == I_SPLIT:
            if not _first(p, p.code.x[pc], &set, &seen):
                return false
            pc = p.code.y[pc]
            continue
        if op == I_CHAR:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x == 0xFFFD:                          # (any invalid byte reads as U+FFFD)
                return false
            set[encode(x).byte(0)] = true
            if p.code.fold[pc]:
                set[encode(upper(x)).byte(0)] = true
            return true
        if op == I_CLASS:
            c = p.classes[p.code.x[pc]]
            if c.neg:
                return false
            for x in 0..128:
                if class_has(c, x):
                    set[x] = true
            # a character past ASCII starts with a byte >= 0xC2; U+FFFD also stands for any
            # invalid byte, 0x80 and up
            lead = 0x80 if class_has(c, 0xFFFD) else 0xC2
            if len(c.hi) > 0 and c.hi[len(c.hi) - 1] >= 128:
                for x in lead..256:
                    set[x] = true
            return true
        return false                                  # . or an empty match: any start
    return false

# ---- literal alternatives, from the tree
const LIT_LEN = 32
const LIT_MAX = 16

fn _lit_push(o: mut [Lit], l: Lit) bool:
    for x in o:                                       # (a repeat can never win: the first would)
        if x == l:
            return true
    if len(o) == LIT_MAX:
        return false
    o.push(l)
    return true

# the strings n's matches start with, in priority order (false: too many, or n can start with
# something that isn't a string, like a class). zw: an assertion was passed
fn _lits(t: Tree, i: int, o: mut [Lit], zw: mut bool) bool:
    o = []
    n = t.nodes[i]
    k = n.kind
    if k == N_EMPTY:
        o.push(Lit("", "", true))
        return true
    if k == N_ASSERT:
        zw = true
        o.push(Lit("", "", true))
        return true
    if k == N_GROUP:
        return _lits(t, n.kids[0], &o, &zw)
    if k == N_CHAR:
        if n.c == 0xFFFD:                             # (it also stands for any invalid byte)
            return false
        if not n.fold or n.c < 0x80:                  # (an ASCII letter folds with the mask)
            u = encode(lower(n.c) if n.fold else n.c)
            m = chr(0x20) + "\x00" * (len(u) - 1) if n.fold else "\x00" * len(u)
            o.push(Lit(u, m, true))
            return true
        a = lower(n.c)
        b = upper(a)
        o.push(Lit(encode(a), "\x00" * len(encode(a)), true))
        if b != a:
            o.push(Lit(encode(b), "\x00" * len(encode(b)), true))
        return true
    if k == N_REP:
        if n.min == 0 or not _lits(t, n.kids[0], &o, &zw):
            return false
        if n.min != 1 or n.max != 1:
            for j in 0..len(o):
                o[j].exact = false
        return true
    if k == N_ALT:
        for c in n.kids:
            sub: [Lit] = []
            if not _lits(t, c, &sub, &zw):
                return false
            for l in sub:
                if not _lit_push(&o, l):
                    return false
        return true
    if k == N_CAT:
        # the cross product, left to right, in priority order (the order a backtracker tries
        # them); where it can't go on, what it has so far starts every match
        o.push(Lit("", "", true))
        for c in n.kids:
            open = false
            for l in o:
                if l.exact:
                    open = true
            if not open:
                break
            sub: [Lit] = []
            ok = _lits(t, c, &sub, &zw)
            x: [Lit] = []
            for a in o:
                if not ok:
                    break
                if not a.exact:
                    ok = _lit_push(&x, a)
                    continue
                for b in sub:
                    if not ok:
                        break
                    tk2 = len(b.b) if len(b.b) < LIT_LEN - len(a.b) else LIT_LEN - len(a.b)
                    l = Lit(a.b + b.b[..tk2], a.m + b.m[..tk2], b.exact and tk2 == len(b.b))
                    ok = _lit_push(&x, l)
            if not ok:
                for j in 0..len(o):
                    o[j].exact = false
                break
            o = x
        return true
    return false

# the literal alternatives and their Teddy tables, if the pattern has a few that are rare
# enough to be worth looking for
fn _teddy_build(p: mut Prog, t: Tree):
    if p.anchored or len(p.prefix) > 0 or p.literal:
        return
    o: [Lit] = []
    zw = false
    if not _lits(t, t.root, &o, &zw) or len(o) == 0:
        return
    k = 3
    exact = not zw and p.ngroups == 1
    for l in o:
        if len(l.b) < k:
            k = len(l.b)
        exact = exact and l.exact
    # how often a place in the text starts one of them (per thousand bytes, roughly)
    often = 0.0
    if k > 0:
        for l in o:
            f = 1.0
            for j in 0..k:
                b = l.b.byte(j)
                r = rank(b)
                if l.m.byte(j) != 0:
                    r += rank(b & ~0x20)
                f *= float(r) / 1000.0
            often += f * 1000.0
    # with no automaton to run instead, even a common one pays; before the DFA, only a rare one
    # (a lone first byte is what the first-byte prefilter already does)
    if k == 0:
        return
    if exact:
        if often > 300.0:
            return
    elif k < 2 or often > 20.0:
        return
    p.lits = o
    p.tk = k
    p.tb = [0] * (3 * 256)
    p.tlo = [0] * (3 * 16)
    p.thi = [0] * (3 * 16)
    for i, l in o:
        bucket = 1 << (i & 7)
        for j in 0..k:
            b = l.b.byte(j)
            alt = b & ~l.m.byte(j)
            p.tb[j * 256 + b] |= bucket
            p.tb[j * 256 + alt] |= bucket
            p.tlo[j * 16 + (b & 15)] |= bucket
            p.thi[j * 16 + (b >> 4)] |= bucket
            p.tlo[j * 16 + (alt & 15)] |= bucket
            p.thi[j * 16 + (alt >> 4)] |= bucket
    for j in 0..3:
        lo = ""
        hi = ""
        for q in 0..16:
            lo += chr(p.tlo[j * 16 + q]) if p.tlo[j * 16 + q] < 128 else _byte_str(p.tlo[j * 16 + q])
            hi += chr(p.thi[j * 16 + q]) if p.thi[j * 16 + q] < 128 else _byte_str(p.thi[j * 16 + q])
        p.vtlo.push(simd.of(lo))
        p.vthi.push(simd.of(hi))
    if exact:
        p.lits_exact = true
    else:
        p.teddy = true
        p.skip = true
        p.rlo = []                                    # (instead of the first-byte scan)
        p.rhi = []
        p.vlo = []
        p.vspan = []

# ---- one-pass programs
# A program is one-pass if at every SPLIT the next byte (or the end of the match) says which
# branch to tk2: then a match's groups come from one walk down the program.
fn _bit(set: mut [int], at: int, b: int):
    set[at + (b >> 6)] |= 1 << (b & 63)

# the bytes that can be read next from pc into words at..at+5 of set (bit 256: the match can
# end); a character past ASCII counts as all its possible lead bytes
fn _next_bytes(p: Prog, pc0: int, set: mut [int], at: int, seen: mut [int], stamp: int):
    stack = [pc0]
    while len(stack) > 0:
        pc = stack.pop()
        if seen[pc] == stamp:
            continue
        seen[pc] = stamp
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_JMP:
            stack.push(p.code.x[pc])
        elif op == I_SPLIT:
            stack.push(p.code.y[pc])
            stack.push(p.code.x[pc])
        elif op == I_SAVE or op == I_ASSERT:
            stack.push(pc + 1)
        elif op == I_MATCH:
            _bit(&set, at, 256)
        elif op == I_ANY or op == I_ANYNL:
            for b in 0..256:
                if b != 10 or op == I_ANYNL:
                    _bit(&set, at, b)
        elif op == I_CHAR:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x < 0x80:
                _bit(&set, at, x)
                if p.code.fold[pc]:
                    _bit(&set, at, upper(x))
            else:
                for b in 0x80..256:                   # (U+FFFD: any invalid byte)
                    _bit(&set, at, b)
        elif op == I_CLASS:
            c = p.classes[p.code.x[pc]]
            for b in 0..128:
                if class_has(c, b):
                    _bit(&set, at, b)
            if c.neg or (len(c.hi) > 0 and c.hi[len(c.hi) - 1] >= 128):
                for b in 0x80..256:
                    _bit(&set, at, b)

fn _ascii_class(c: Class) bool:
    return not c.neg and (len(c.hi) == 0 or c.hi[len(c.hi) - 1] < 0x80)

fn _onepass_build(p: mut Prog):
    n = len(p.code.op)
    if p.ngroups == 1 or n > 2000:                    # (only groups need it)
        return
    # straight through, one byte per step (like (\d{4})-(\d{2})): the slots are at fixed offsets
    fix = [-1] * (2 * p.ngroups)                       # (a group repeated {0} times: never set)
    ok = true
    flen = 0
    for pc in 0..n:
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_SAVE:
            fix[p.code.x[pc]] = flen
        elif op == I_ASSERT:
            continue
        elif op == I_MATCH:
            break
        elif (op == I_CHAR and p.code.x[pc] < 0x80) or (op == I_CLASS and _ascii_class(p.classes[p.code.x[pc]])):
            flen += 1
        else:
            ok = false
            break
    if ok:
        p.fixoff = fix
        p.fixlen = flen
    sets = [0] * (5 * n)
    seen = [0] * n
    stamp = 0
    for pc in 0..n:
        if p.code.op[pc] != I_SPLIT:
            continue
        y = [0] * 5
        stamp += 1
        _next_bytes(p, p.code.x[pc], &sets, 5 * pc, &seen, stamp)
        stamp += 1
        _next_bytes(p, p.code.y[pc], &y, 0, &seen, stamp)
        for i in 0..5:
            if (sets[5 * pc + i] & y[i]) != 0:
                return
    p.onepass = sets

# ---- byte programs for the lazy DFA
fn _bop(m: mut BCode, op: int, lo: int, hi: int, x: int, y: int) int:
    if len(m.op) >= MAX_CODE:
        m.bad = true
        return len(m.op)
    m.op.push(op)
    m.lo.push(lo)
    m.hi.push(hi)
    m.x.push(x)
    m.y.push(y)
    return len(m.op) - 1

# a UTF-8 byte-range sequence: lo[k]..hi[k] for each of its bytes
struct Seq:
    lo: [int]
    hi: [int]

fn _seq_add(q: mut [Seq], lo: int, hi: int):
    a = encode(lo)
    b = encode(hi)
    s = Seq([], [])
    for j in 0..len(a):
        s.lo.push(a.byte(j))
        s.hi.push(b.byte(j))
    q.push(s)

# the code points lo..hi as UTF-8 byte-range sequences (the RE2 / Go algorithm)
fn _u8(q: mut [Seq], lo: int, hi: int):
    if lo > hi:
        return
    if lo <= 0xDFFF and hi >= 0xD800:                 # no surrogates
        if lo < 0xD800:
            _u8(&q, lo, 0xD7FF)
        if hi > 0xDFFF:
            _u8(&q, 0xE000, hi)
        return
    for mx in [0x7F, 0x7FF, 0xFFFF]:
        if lo <= mx and hi > mx:
            _u8(&q, lo, mx)
            _u8(&q, mx + 1, hi)
            return
    if hi <= 0x7F:
        _seq_add(&q, lo, hi)
        return
    n = 2 if hi <= 0x7FF else 3 if hi <= 0xFFFF else 4
    for i in 1..n:
        m = (1 << (6 * i)) - 1
        if (lo & ~m) != (hi & ~m):
            if (lo & m) != 0:
                _u8(&q, lo, lo | m)
                _u8(&q, (lo | m) + 1, hi)
                return
            if (hi & m) != m:
                _u8(&q, lo, (hi & ~m) - 1)
                _u8(&q, hi & ~m, hi)
                return
    _seq_add(&q, lo, hi)

# any one of the sequences (in reverse byte order for the reverse program)
fn _bseqs(m: mut BCode, q: [Seq]):
    if len(q) == 0:
        _bop(&m, B_BYTE, 1, 0, 0, 0)                  # matches nothing (lo > hi)
        return
    jmps: [int] = []
    for i, s in q:
        sp = -1
        if i < len(q) - 1:
            sp = _bop(&m, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0)
        if sp >= 0 and not m.bad:
            m.x[sp] = len(m.op)
        n = len(s.lo)
        for j in 0..n:
            k = n - 1 - j if m.rev else j
            _bop(&m, B_BYTE, s.lo[k], s.hi[k], 0, 0)
        if i < len(q) - 1:
            jmps.push(_bop(&m, B_JMP, 0, 0, 0, 0))
        if sp >= 0 and not m.bad:
            m.y[sp] = len(m.op)
    if not m.bad:
        for j in jmps:
            m.x[j] = len(m.op)

fn _bclass(m: mut BCode, c: Class):
    q: [Seq] = []
    if not c.neg:
        for i in 0..len(c.lo):
            _u8(&q, c.lo[i], c.hi[i])
    else:
        lo = 0
        for i in 0..len(c.lo):
            if c.lo[i] > lo:
                _u8(&q, lo, c.lo[i] - 1)
            lo = c.hi[i] + 1
        _u8(&q, lo, 0x10FFFF)
    _bseqs(&m, q)

fn _bprefer(m: mut BCode, l: int, body: int, out: int, greedy: bool):
    if m.bad:
        return
    if greedy:
        m.x[l] = body
        m.y[l] = out
    else:
        m.x[l] = out
        m.y[l] = body

fn _bplus(m: mut BCode, t: Tree, k: int, greedy: bool):
    body = len(m.op)
    _bgen(&m, t, k)
    l = _bop(&m, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    _bprefer(&m, l, body, l + 1, greedy)

fn _bstar(m: mut BCode, t: Tree, k: int, greedy: bool):
    if nullable(t, k):
        q = _bop(&m, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0)
        _bplus(&m, t, k, greedy)
        _bprefer(&m, q, q + 1, len(m.op), greedy)
        return
    l = _bop(&m, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    _bgen(&m, t, k)
    _bop(&m, B_JMP, 0, 0, l, 0)
    _bprefer(&m, l, l + 1, len(m.op), greedy)

fn _flip(k: int) int:
    if k == A_BOT:
        return A_EOT
    if k == A_EOT:
        return A_BOT
    if k == A_BOL:
        return A_EOL
    if k == A_EOL:
        return A_BOL
    return k

fn _bgen(m: mut BCode, t: Tree, i: int):
    if m.bad:
        return
    n = t.nodes[i]
    k = n.kind
    if k == N_CHAR:
        q: [Seq] = []
        cs = [n.c, lower(n.c) if n.fold else n.c, upper(n.c) if n.fold else n.c]
        for a in 0..3:
            dup = false
            for b in 0..a:
                if cs[b] == cs[a]:
                    dup = true
            if not dup:
                _u8(&q, cs[a], cs[a])
        _bseqs(&m, q)
    elif k == N_ANY:
        q: [Seq] = []
        if n.dotnl:
            _u8(&q, 0, 0x10FFFF)
        else:
            _u8(&q, 0, 9)
            _u8(&q, 11, 0x10FFFF)
        _bseqs(&m, q)
    elif k == N_CLASS:
        _bclass(&m, t.classes[n.cls])
    elif k == N_ASSERT:
        _bop(&m, B_ASSERT, 0, 0, _flip(n.at) if m.rev else n.at, 0)
    elif k == N_CAT:
        nk = len(n.kids)
        for j in 0..nk:
            _bgen(&m, t, n.kids[nk - 1 - j] if m.rev else n.kids[j])
    elif k == N_GROUP:
        _bgen(&m, t, n.kids[0])
    elif k == N_REP:
        kid = n.kids[0]
        if n.max < 0:
            j = 0
            while j + 1 < n.min and not m.bad:
                _bgen(&m, t, kid)
                j += 1
            if n.min == 0:
                _bstar(&m, t, kid, n.greedy)
            else:
                _bplus(&m, t, kid, n.greedy)
            return
        j = 0
        while j < n.min and not m.bad:
            _bgen(&m, t, kid)
            j += 1
        splits: [int] = []
        for r in 0..n.max - n.min:
            if m.bad:
                break
            splits.push(_bop(&m, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0))
            _bgen(&m, t, kid)
        if not m.bad:
            for s in splits:
                _bprefer(&m, s, s + 1, len(m.op), n.greedy)
    elif k == N_ALT:
        jmps: [int] = []
        last = len(n.kids) - 1
        for c, kid in n.kids:
            sp = -1
            if c < last:
                sp = _bop(&m, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0)
            if sp >= 0 and not m.bad:
                m.x[sp] = len(m.op)
            _bgen(&m, t, kid)
            if c < last:
                jmps.push(_bop(&m, B_JMP, 0, 0, 0, 0))
            if sp >= 0 and not m.bad:
                m.y[sp] = len(m.op)
        if not m.bad:
            for j in jmps:
                m.x[j] = len(m.op)

# can the pattern match U+FFFD (what the VM reads an invalid byte as)
fn _fffd(p: Prog) bool:
    for i in 0..len(p.code.op):
        op = p.code.op[i]
        if op == I_ANY or op == I_ANYNL:
            return true
        if op == I_CLASS and class_has(p.classes[p.code.x[i]], 0xFFFD):
            return true
        if op == I_CHAR and p.code.x[i] == 0xFFFD:
            return true
    return false

fn _is_plain_char(t: Tree, i: int) bool:
    n = t.nodes[i]
    return n.kind == N_CHAR and not n.fold

# P L S (see Prog.inner): only where the ordinary prefilter doesn't apply
fn _inner(p: mut Prog, t: Tree):
    root = t.nodes[t.root]
    if p.anchored or len(p.prefix) > 0 or root.kind != N_CAT:
        return
    kids = root.kids
    k = 1
    while k < len(kids) and not _is_plain_char(t, kids[k]):
        k += 1
    if k >= len(kids):
        return
    lit = ""
    j = k
    while j < len(kids) and _is_plain_char(t, kids[j]) and len(lit) + 4 <= 16:
        lit += encode(t.nodes[kids[j]].c)
        j += 1
    f = _no_bcode(false)                              # the bytes P can read: L's first mustn't be one
    for i in 0..k:
        _bgen(&f, t, kids[i])
    if f.bad:
        return
    l0 = lit.byte(0)
    for i in 0..len(f.op):
        if f.op[i] == B_BYTE and l0 >= f.lo[i] and l0 <= f.hi[i]:
            return
    if p.skip:              # a first-byte prefilter too: the literal only if it's much rarer
        often = 0           # (dates: `-` beats stopping at every digit)
        for b in 0..256:
            if p.first[b]:
                often += rank(b)
        lr = 0
        for i in 1..len(lit):
            if rank(lit.byte(i)) < rank(lit.byte(lr)):
                lr = i
        if rank(lit.byte(lr)) * 2 >= often:
            return
    r = _no_bcode(true)
    i = k - 1
    while i >= 0:
        _bgen(&r, t, kids[i])
        i -= 1
    _bop(&r, B_MATCH, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    if r.bad:
        return
    p.icode = r
    p.lit = lit
    p.inner = true
    p.lrare = 0
    for q in 0..len(lit):
        if rank(lit.byte(q)) < rank(lit.byte(p.lrare)):
            p.lrare = q
    p.lrare2 = second_rare(lit, p.lrare)

fn _bytes(p: mut Prog, t: Tree):
    f = _no_bcode(false)
    l0 = _bop(&f, B_SPLIT, 0, 0, 0, 0)                # (?s:.)*? over bytes, then the pattern
    _bop(&f, B_BYTE, 0, 255, 0, 0)
    _bop(&f, B_JMP, 0, 0, l0, 0)
    f.x[l0] = len(f.op)
    f.y[l0] = l0 + 1
    p.bstart = len(f.op)
    _bgen(&f, t, t.root)
    _bop(&f, B_MATCH, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    r = _no_bcode(true)
    _bgen(&r, t, t.root)
    _bop(&r, B_MATCH, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    if f.bad or r.bad:
        return
    p.fwd = f
    p.rev = r
    # byte classes: split 0..255 wherever an instruction's range starts or ends, and around the
    # bytes assertions look at (word characters, \n)
    cut = [false] * 257
    words = false
    lines = false
    for c in [f, r]:
        for i in 0..len(c.op):
            if c.op[i] == B_BYTE and c.lo[i] <= c.hi[i]:
                cut[c.lo[i]] = true
                cut[c.hi[i] + 1] = true
            if c.op[i] == B_ASSERT:
                if c.x[i] == A_WORD or c.x[i] == A_NWORD:
                    words = true
                if c.x[i] == A_BOL or c.x[i] == A_EOL:
                    lines = true
    if words:
        for pr in [(48, 57), (65, 90), (95, 95), (97, 122)]:
            cut[pr.0] = true
            cut[pr.1 + 1] = true
        cut[0x80] = true                              # (continuation bytes, for \B)
        cut[0xC0] = true
    if lines:
        cut[10] = true
        cut[11] = true
    p.bcls = [0] * 256
    c = 0
    for b in 0..256:
        if b > 0 and cut[b]:
            c += 1
        p.bcls[b] = c
    p.nbcls = c + 1
    p.fffd = _fffd(p)
    _inner(&p, t)
    for i in 0..len(f.op):
        if f.op[i] == B_ASSERT and f.x[i] == A_NWORD:
            p.fffd = true                             # \B's rule needs valid UTF-8
    p.dfa = true

fn _empty_prog(pattern: str, t: Tree) Prog:
    return Prog(pattern, _no_code(), t.classes, len(t.names), t.names, "", 0, 0, false, [false] * 256, false, false, [], [], [], [], false, false, false, false, _no_bcode(false), 0, _no_bcode(true), [], 0, false, "", 0, 0, _no_bcode(true), [], 0, false, false, [], [], [], [], [], [], [], 0, [], [], [], [])

# The program for pattern, or why it isn't one.
fn build(pattern: str) Result[Prog, str]:
    t = parse(pattern)?
    p = _empty_prog(pattern, t)
    m = _no_code()
    _op(&m, I_SAVE, 0, 0)
    _gen(&m, t, t.root)
    _op(&m, I_SAVE, 1, 0)
    _op(&m, I_MATCH, 0, 0)
    if m.bad:
        return Err(f"re: the pattern is too big (over {MAX_CODE} steps once repetitions are expanded)")
    p.code = m
    buf = ""
    open = true
    _prefix(t, t.root, &buf, &open)
    p.prefix = buf
    p.literal = open and len(buf) > 0 and p.ngroups == 1
    p.nullable = nullable(t, t.root)
    for i in 0..len(buf):
        if rank(buf.byte(i)) < rank(buf.byte(p.rare)):
            p.rare = i
    p.rare2 = second_rare(buf, p.rare)
    seen = [false] * len(m.op)
    first = [false] * 256
    p.has_first = _first(p, 0, &first, &seen)
    p.first = first
    # the prefilter pays when what it stops at is rare enough: a literal's first byte under
    # ~8% of text (memchr at each stop), or first bytes under ~25% (the 16-byte simd scan is
    # cheap to restart: \s+ replace 2x faster; any letter: no, leaving the DFA's loop at every
    # one costs more than reading on)
    often = 0
    for b in 0..256:
        if p.first[b]:
            often += rank(b)
    if len(p.prefix) > 1:
        p.skip = true
    elif len(p.prefix) == 1:
        p.skip = rank(p.prefix.byte(0)) < 80
    else:
        p.skip = p.has_first and often < 250
    if p.has_first:
        b = 0
        while b < 256:
            if not p.first[b]:
                b += 1
                continue
            e = b
            while e < 255 and p.first[e + 1]:
                e += 1
            if len(p.rlo) == 6:
                p.rlo = []
                p.rhi = []
                p.vlo = []
                p.vspan = []
                break
            p.rlo.push(b)
            p.rhi.push(e)
            p.vlo.push(simd.splat(b))
            p.vspan.push(simd.splat(e - b))
            b = e + 1
    # anchored: the first thing that can happen is \A
    pc = 0
    while pc < len(m.op) and m.op[pc] == I_SAVE:
        pc += 1
    p.anchored = pc < len(m.op) and m.op[pc] == I_ASSERT and m.x[pc] == A_BOT
    _bytes(&p, t)
    _teddy_build(&p, t)
    _onepass_build(&p)
    _ascii_masks(&p)
    return Ok(p)

# am0/am1: for each instruction that reads a character, the ASCII ones it takes
fn _ascii_masks(p: mut Prog):
    n = len(p.code.op)
    a0 = [0] * n
    a1 = [0] * n
    for pc in 0..n:
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op <= I_CLASS:
            for c in 0..128:
                if _char_ok(p, pc, c):
                    if c < 64:
                        a0[pc] = a0[pc] | (1 << c)
                    else:
                        a1[pc] = a1[pc] | (1 << (c - 64))
    p.am0 = a0
    p.am1 = a1
    hi = [false] * n
    poss = [false] * n
    for pc in 0..n:
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_ANY or op == I_ANYNL:
            hi[pc] = true
        elif op == I_CLASS:
            c = p.classes[p.code.x[pc]]
            hi[pc] = c.neg and (len(c.hi) == 0 or c.hi[len(c.hi) - 1] < 128)
    p.ahi = hi
    for pc in 0..n:
        if p.code.op[pc] != I_SPLIT:
            continue
        b = p.code.x[pc]
        if p.code.op[b] > I_CLASS or not (b == pc - 1 or (b == pc + 1 and pc + 2 < n and p.code.op[pc + 2] == I_JMP and p.code.x[pc + 2] == pc)):
            continue
        f0 = 0
        f1 = 0
        seen = [false] * n
        ok = _first_ascii(p, p.code.y[pc], &f0, &f1, &seen)
        poss[pc] = ok and (f0 & a0[b]) == 0 and (f1 & a1[b]) == 0
    p.poss = poss

# the ASCII characters a match from pc can start with (f0: 0..63, f1: 64..127); false when
# it could start with anything else, or match nothing at all (reach MATCH reading nothing)
fn _first_ascii(p: Prog, pc0: int, f0: mut int, f1: mut int, seen: mut [bool]) bool:
    pc = pc0
    while true:
        if seen[pc]:
            return true
        seen[pc] = true
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_JMP:
            pc = p.code.x[pc]
            continue
        if op == I_SAVE or op == I_ASSERT:
            pc += 1
            continue
        if op == I_SPLIT:
            if not _first_ascii(p, p.code.x[pc], &f0, &f1, &seen):
                return false
            pc = p.code.y[pc]
            continue
        if op == I_CHAR and not p.code.fold[pc] and p.code.x[pc] < 128:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x < 64:
                f0 = f0 | (1 << x)
            else:
                f1 = f1 | (1 << (x - 64))
            return true
        if op == I_CLASS:
            c = p.classes[p.code.x[pc]]
            if c.neg or (len(c.hi) > 0 and c.hi[len(c.hi) - 1] >= 128):
                return false
            f0 = f0 | p.am0[pc]
            f1 = f1 | p.am1[pc]
            return true
        return false
    return false
```

## library/std/re/dfa.tn

```tern
# re: the lazy DFA. A state is an ordered list of byte-program instructions waiting for the
# next byte, plus what the last byte was (a word character, a newline, a UTF-8 continuation
# byte, or none: the edge of the text). Following a byte first expands the list (jumps,
# splits and assertions, which can see the previous and next byte) in priority order, then
# keeps the instructions that accept the byte. A MATCH reached while expanding means a match
# ends before that byte; in leftmost-first mode (cut) everything of lower priority is dropped
# there. Transitions are computed the first time they're used and kept; a cache that grows past
# MAX_STATES is cleared, and a search that clears it too often finishes in the VM.
#
# A transition is the next state's id times the row width (so the hot loop just adds the
# byte's class), | MBIT if a match ends before the byte, | SBIT if the next state needs a look
# (dead, or idle: where the prefilter can jump ahead); -1: not computed yet.

import binary

const CTX_WORD = 1
const CTX_NL = 2
const CTX_EDGE = 4
const CTX_CONT = 8

const DEAD = 0
const MBIT = 1 << 30
const SBIT = 1 << 29
const IDMASK = (1 << 29) - 1
const MAX_STATES = 4096

struct Dfa:
    which: int                # its program: 0 the Prog's fwd, 1 its rev, 2 its icode (kept
                              # there: every thread's Dfa shares it, so it isn't copied here)
    cut: bool
    rev: bool
    mark_idle: bool           # flag entering the idle state
    stride: int               # byte classes + 1 (the end of the text), up to a power of two
    shift: int                # stride == 1 << shift: a row's state is off >> shift
    st_off: [int]             # state -> its instructions in pool, how many, its context
    st_n: [int]
    st_ctx: [int]
    pool: [int]
    trans: [int]              # state * stride + class -> transition
    ids: {str: int}           # (context, instructions) -> state
    starts: [int]             # 16: the start state for each context (0: not made)
    start_pc: [int]           # ... and the pc each was made for
    clears: int
    seen: [int]               # scratch for step: a stamp per instruction
    stamp: int
    dirty: bool               # states or transitions were added since it was copied

# forward first-match, forward longest (full), reverse, and the inner literal's prefix
struct Dfas:
    f: Dfa
    l: Dfa
    r: Dfa
    i: Dfa
    made: bool

fn _dfa(code: BCode, which: int, nclass: int, cut: bool, rev: bool) Dfa:
    sh = 0
    while (1 << sh) < nclass + 1:
        sh += 1
    d = Dfa(which, cut, rev, false, 1 << sh, sh, [], [], [], [], [], {}, [0] * 16, [0] * 16, 0, [0] * len(code.op), 0, true)
    _reset(&d)
    return d

# a Dfa with no tables: not made yet (or not needed)
fn _no_dfa() Dfa:
    return Dfa(0, false, false, false, 1, 0, [], [], [], [], [], {}, [], [], 0, [], 0, false)

fn no_dfas() Dfas:
    e = _no_dfa()
    return Dfas(e, e, e, e, false)

fn make_dfas(p: Prog) Dfas:
    f = _dfa(p.fwd, 0, p.nbcls, true, false)
    f.mark_idle = not p.anchored and p.skip           # (only worth a look with a prefilter)
    r = _dfa(p.rev, 1, p.nbcls, false, true)
    i = _dfa(p.icode, 2, p.nbcls, false, true) if p.inner else _no_dfa()
    # (l, for whole-text matches, is made when first used: most searches never need it)
    return Dfas(f, _no_dfa(), r, i, true)

# state 0: dead (no instructions)
fn _reset(d: mut Dfa):
    d.st_off = [0]
    d.st_n = [0]
    d.st_ctx = [0]
    d.pool = []
    d.ids = {}
    d.starts = [0] * 16
    d.start_pc = [0] * 16
    d.trans = [DEAD] * d.stride
    d.dirty = true

fn _key(ctx: int, pcs: [int]) str:
    w = binary.writer()
    w.put_u8(ctx)
    for pc in pcs:
        w.put_u32le(pc)
    return w.bytes()

fn _state(d: mut Dfa, ctx: int, pcs: [int]) int:
    if len(pcs) == 0:
        return DEAD
    k = _key(ctx, pcs)
    found = d.ids.get(k, -1)
    if found >= 0:
        return found
    id = len(d.st_n)
    d.st_off.push(len(d.pool))
    d.st_n.push(len(pcs))
    d.st_ctx.push(ctx)
    for pc in pcs:
        d.pool.push(pc)
    for c in 0..d.stride:
        d.trans.push(-1)
    d.ids[k] = id
    d.dirty = true
    return id

fn ctx_of(b: int) int:
    if b < 0:
        return CTX_EDGE
    c = 0
    if is_word(b):
        c = CTX_WORD
    if b == 10:
        c |= CTX_NL
    if b >= 0x80 and b < 0xC0:
        c |= CTX_CONT
    return c

# (rev: scanning backwards, so ctx is the byte after the position and next the one before)
fn _bassert(kind: int, ctx: int, next: int, rev: bool) bool:
    if kind == A_BOT:
        return (ctx & CTX_EDGE) != 0
    if kind == A_EOT:
        return next < 0
    if kind == A_BOL:
        return (ctx & (CTX_EDGE | CTX_NL)) != 0
    if kind == A_EOL:
        return next < 0 or next == 10
    a = (ctx & CTX_WORD) != 0
    b = next >= 0 and is_word(next)
    if kind == A_WORD:
        return a != b
    # \B holds between two non-word bytes, which includes the middle of a character: the VM
    # only stops at character boundaries, so neither may this
    if rev:
        if (ctx & CTX_CONT) != 0:
            return false
    elif next >= 0x80 and next < 0xC0:
        return false
    return a == b

# the transition from state id on byte b (-1: the end of the text): the next id, | MBIT if a
# match ends before b, | SBIT if the next state is special
fn _step(d: mut Dfa, c: BCode, id: int, b: int) int:
    d.stamp += 1
    stamp = d.stamp
    next: [int] = []
    matched = false
    stack: [int] = []
    off = d.st_off[id]
    ctx = d.st_ctx[id]
    for e in 0..d.st_n[id]:
        if matched and d.cut:
            break
        stack.push(d.pool[off + e])
        while len(stack) > 0:
            pc = stack.pop()
            if d.seen[pc] == stamp:
                continue
            d.seen[pc] = stamp
            op = c.op[pc]
            if op == B_JMP:
                stack.push(c.x[pc])
            elif op == B_SPLIT:
                stack.push(c.y[pc])
                stack.push(c.x[pc])
            elif op == B_ASSERT:
                if _bassert(c.x[pc], ctx, b, d.rev):
                    stack.push(pc + 1)
            elif op == B_MATCH:
                matched = true
                if d.cut:
                    stack = []                        # lower-priority threads lose
            elif b >= c.lo[pc] and b <= c.hi[pc]:
                next.push(pc + 1)
    nid = DEAD if b < 0 else _state(&d, ctx_of(b), next)
    special = nid == DEAD or (d.mark_idle and len(next) == 1 and next[0] == 2)
    return nid | (MBIT if matched else 0) | (SBIT if special else 0)

fn _fill(d: mut Dfa, c: BCode, id: int, b: int, k: int) int:
    t = _step(&d, c, id, b)
    t = ((t & IDMASK) << d.shift) | (t & (MBIT | SBIT))
    d.trans[id * d.stride + k] = t
    d.dirty = true
    return t

fn _trans(d: mut Dfa, p: Prog, id: int, b: int) int:
    k = d.stride - 1 if b < 0 else p.bcls[b]
    t = d.trans[id * d.stride + k]
    if t >= 0:
        return t
    if d.which == 0:
        return _fill(&d, p.fwd, id, b, k)
    if d.which == 1:
        return _fill(&d, p.rev, id, b, k)
    return _fill(&d, p.icode, id, b, k)

# (the forward DFA starts both unanchored searches, at pc 2, and anchored ones, at bstart: a
# start state is kept with the pc it was made for, or one would be taken for the other)
fn _start(d: mut Dfa, pc: int, ctx: int) int:
    slot = ctx & 15
    id = d.starts[slot]
    if id != 0 and d.start_pc[slot] == pc:
        return id
    return _start_new(&d, pc, ctx)

# (apart, so _start's common path is small enough to inline)
fn _start_new(d: mut Dfa, pc: int, ctx: int) int:
    slot = ctx & 15
    id = _state(&d, ctx, [pc])
    d.starts[slot] = id
    d.start_pc[slot] = pc
    return id

# room for another state: clears a cache that has grown too big (false if this search has
# cleared it too often), keeping state id (renumbered)
fn _room(d: mut Dfa, id: mut int) bool:
    if len(d.st_n) < MAX_STATES:
        return true
    d.clears += 1
    if d.clears > 3:
        return false
    off = d.st_off[id]
    pcs: [int] = []
    for e in 0..d.st_n[id]:
        pcs.push(d.pool[off + e])
    ctx = d.st_ctx[id]
    _reset(&d)
    id = _state(&d, ctx, pcs)
    return true

fn _idle(d: Dfa, id: int) bool:
    return d.st_n[id] == 1 and d.pool[d.st_off[id]] == 2

# The hot loops: known transitions from row `off` (state * stride), byte by byte, until one
# isn't known or is special: (where they stopped, the row there, the last position a match
# ended / started at, or -1). Plain parameters, so nothing is retained and the table can still
# be added to (copy-on-write) after they return.
fn _run(trans: [int], bcls: [int], s: str, i0: int, off0: int, quick: bool) (int, int, int):
    n = len(s)
    i = i0
    off = off0
    last = -1
    while i < n:
        t = trans[off + bcls[s.byte(i)]]
        if t < 0 or (t & (MBIT | SBIT)) != 0:         # (one test on the common path)
            if t < 0 or (t & SBIT) != 0 or quick:
                break
            last = i                                  # a match ends here: note it, go on
            t = t & IDMASK
        off = t
        i += 1
    return (i, off, last)

fn _run_full(trans: [int], bcls: [int], s: str, i0: int, off0: int) (int, int):
    n = len(s)
    i = i0
    off = off0
    while i < n:
        t = trans[off + bcls[s.byte(i)]]
        if t < 0 or (t & SBIT) != 0:
            break
        off = t & IDMASK
        i += 1
    return (i, off)

fn _run_back(trans: [int], bcls: [int], s: str, i0: int, at: int, off0: int) (int, int, int):
    i = i0
    off = off0
    best = -1
    while i > at:
        t = trans[off + bcls[s.byte(i - 1)]]
        if t < 0 or (t & (MBIT | SBIT)) != 0:
            if t < 0 or (t & SBIT) != 0:
                break
            best = i                                  # a match starts here: note it, go on
            t = t & IDMASK
        off = t
        i -= 1
    return (i, off, best)

# forward, leftmost-first: where the first match at or after `at` ends (-1: none; -2: the DFA
# gave up). quick: stop at the first match of any kind (for test). anchored: only a match
# starting at `at`
fn dfa_scan(p: Prog, x: mut Dfas, s: str, at: int, quick: bool, anchored: bool) int:
    x.f.clears = 0
    n = len(s)
    # unanchored: start at the JMP that closes the (?s:.)*? loop (pc 2), which is also the
    # state the loop returns to after a byte where nothing started: "idle"
    pc = p.bstart if anchored else 2
    id = _start(&x.f, pc, CTX_EDGE if at == 0 else ctx_of(s.byte(at - 1)))
    last = -1
    i = at
    stride = x.f.stride
    sh = x.f.shift
    skip = not anchored and p.skip
    while true:
        if skip and i < n and _idle(x.f, id):         # jump to where a match could begin
            j = prefilter(p, s, i)
            if j >= n:
                return last                           # (a match needs one of those bytes)
            if j > i:
                i = j
                id = _start(&x.f, pc, ctx_of(s.byte(i - 1)))
        r = _run(x.f.trans, p.bcls, s, i, id * stride, quick)
        i = r.0
        if r.2 >= 0:
            last = r.2
        id = r.1 >> sh
        b = s.byte(i) if i < n else -1
        t = _trans(&x.f, p, id, b)
        if (t & MBIT) != 0:
            last = i
            if quick:
                return i
        id = (t & IDMASK) >> sh
        if id == DEAD or b < 0:
            return last
        i += 1
        if not _room(&x.f, &id):
            return -2
    return -1

# anchored at `at`, longest: does the whole of s[at..] match (1), not (0), or gave up (-2)
fn dfa_full(p: Prog, x: mut Dfas, s: str, at: int) int:
    if len(x.l.starts) == 0:
        x.l = _dfa(p.fwd, 0, p.nbcls, false, false)
    x.l.clears = 0
    n = len(s)
    id = _start(&x.l, p.bstart, CTX_EDGE if at == 0 else ctx_of(s.byte(at - 1)))
    i = at
    stride = x.l.stride
    sh = x.l.shift
    while true:
        r = _run_full(x.l.trans, p.bcls, s, i, id * stride)
        i = r.0
        id = r.1 >> sh
        b = s.byte(i) if i < n else -1
        t = _trans(&x.l, p, id, b)
        if b < 0:
            return 1 if (t & MBIT) != 0 else 0
        id = (t & IDMASK) >> sh
        if id == DEAD:
            return 0
        i += 1
        if not _room(&x.l, &id):
            return -2
    return 0

# reverse from `end` with d (the reverse DFA, or the inner literal's prefix program), longest:
# the smallest start >= at of a match ending at end (-1: none; -2: gave up)
fn dfa_back(p: Prog, d: mut Dfa, s: str, at: int, end: int) int:
    d.clears = 0
    n = len(s)
    id = _start(&d, 0, CTX_EDGE if end == n else ctx_of(s.byte(end)))
    best = -1
    i = end
    stride = d.stride
    sh = d.shift
    while true:
        r = _run_back(d.trans, p.bcls, s, i, at, id * stride)
        i = r.0
        if r.2 >= 0:
            best = r.2
        id = r.1 >> sh
        b = s.byte(i - 1) if i > 0 else -1
        t = _trans(&d, p, id, b)
        if (t & MBIT) != 0:
            best = i
        if i <= at or b < 0:
            break
        id = (t & IDMASK) >> sh
        if id == DEAD:
            break
        i -= 1
        if not _room(&d, &id):
            best = -2
            break
    return best
```

## library/std/re/find.tn

```tern
# re: searching. A search runs the forward DFA to find where the first match ends, the
# reverse DFA to find where it starts, and fills in groups (vm.tn) only when asked; the Pike
# VM takes over where the DFA can't (invalid UTF-8 the pattern could match, or a DFA cache
# that keeps overflowing). Prefilters skip to where a match could begin: a literal prefix,
# the possible first bytes, Teddy for a few literal alternatives, an inner literal.
#
# A search's state (the DFAs' states, the VM's scratch) is kept in the Regex, shared by every
# copy, one per thread: a search takes its thread's state out of its cell, changes it in place
# (adding DFA states as it goes) and puts it back. A state another search holds (a task on
# the same thread slot, a find_all loop still running) is skipped for the next free one, and
# only when none is free does a search start from nothing. (With one state for all threads,
# each search copied it, and threads searching at once contended for it: 3x slower on 14.)

import binary
import simd
import task

const NCACHE = 16             # states a pattern keeps: one per thread (by scheduler slot)

# a compiled pattern: the program (one element: copying an Engine is one retain, not one per
# table) and its search states, shared by every copy
struct Engine:
    ps: [Prog]
    cache: [shared[[Search]]]

fn engine(pattern: str) Result[Engine, str]:
    p = build(pattern)?
    cs: [shared[[Search]]] = []
    for i in 0..NCACHE:
        cs.push(task.shared([_fresh()]))
    return Ok(Engine([p], cs))

# one search's state: the program's DFAs, scratch for the VM and the backtracker
struct Search:
    x: Dfas
    sc: Scratch
    has_sc: bool
    dfa: bool                 # the DFA may run on this text (once chk is false)
    chk: bool                 # whether the text is valid UTF-8 isn't known yet (and matters)
    slot: int                 # the cell it came from

fn _fresh() Search:
    return Search(no_dfas(), Scratch([], [], 0, [], [], 0, [], 0, [], [], [], [], [], 0), false, false, false, 0)

fn _take(c: mut [Search]) [Search]:
    t = c
    c = []
    return t

# the state for a search of s, taken from a cell (one element: changed in place, given back
# by _done)
fn _search(e: Engine, s: str) [Search]:
    k0 = task.thread_slot()
    xs: [Search] = []
    k = 0
    for j in 0..NCACHE:
        k = (k0 + j) & (NCACHE - 1)
        xs = e.cache[k].update(_take)
        if len(xs) > 0:
            break
    if len(xs) == 0:
        k = k0 & (NCACHE - 1)
        xs = [_fresh()]
    if e.ps[0].dfa and not xs[0].x.made:
        xs[0].x = make_dfas(e.ps[0])
    # (valid UTF-8 matters when the pattern can match U+FFFD: checked when the DFA would
    # first run, which an anchored search for groups doesn't)
    xs[0].dfa = e.ps[0].dfa
    xs[0].chk = e.ps[0].dfa and e.ps[0].fffd
    xs[0].slot = k
    return xs

# give the state back to the cell it came from
fn _done(e: Engine, sr: [Search]):
    e.cache[sr[0].slot].set(sr)

# whether the DFA may run on s (valid UTF-8 checked the first time it matters)
fn _dfa_ok(sr: mut Search, s: str) bool:
    if sr.chk:
        sr.chk = false
        sr.dfa = utf8_ok(s)
    return sr.dfa

fn _sc(p: Prog, sr: mut Search):
    if not sr.has_sc:
        sr.sc = scratch(p)
        sr.has_sc = true

# is s valid UTF-8 (8 ASCII bytes at a time)
fn utf8_ok(s: str) bool:
    n = len(s)
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        if i + 8 <= n and (binary.u64le(s, i) & 0x8080808080808080) == 0:
            i += 8
            continue
        if s.byte(i) < 0x80:
            i += 1
            continue
        d = decode(s, i)
        if d.0 == 0xFFFD and d.1 == 1:
            return false
        i += d.1
    return true

# ---- prefilters

# where needle occurs in s at or after i (-1: nowhere): 64 places at a time compared with the
# needle's rarest byte (at r1) where it would be, then the next rarest (r2) and the whole
# needle where it is
fn memmem_rare(s: str, i: int, needle: str, r1: int, r2: int) int:
    return _lit_scan(s, i, needle, r1, r2, false).0

# needle's occurrences from i: (the first, or -1), or with all, (-1, how many: not
# overlapping) counted in the one loop
fn _lit_scan(s: str, i: int, needle: str, r1: int, r2: int, all: bool) (int, int):
    m = len(needle)
    n = len(s)
    found = 0
    if m <= 1:
        if m == 0:
            return (i, 0)
        at = s.find_from(needle, i)
        while all and at >= 0:
            found += 1
            at = s.find_from(needle, at + 1)
        return (at, found)
    v1 = simd.splat(needle.byte(r1))
    b2 = needle.byte(r2)
    c = i
    while c + r1 + 64 <= n:                           # 64 places a step: one test when none
        x0 = simd.eq(simd.load(s, c + r1), v1)
        x1 = simd.eq(simd.load(s, c + r1 + 16), v1)
        x2 = simd.eq(simd.load(s, c + r1 + 32), v1)
        x3 = simd.eq(simd.load(s, c + r1 + 48), v1)
        if simd.any(x0 | x1 | x2 | x3):
            k = simd.bits(x0) | (simd.bits(x1) << 16) | (simd.bits(x2) << 32) | (simd.bits(x3) << 48)
            next = c + 64
            while k != 0:
                at = c + simd.first(k)
                k = k & (k - 1)
                if at + m <= n and s.byte(at + r2) == b2 and s[at..at + m] == needle:
                    if not all:
                        return (at, 0)
                    found += 1
                    if at + m > next:                 # (the rest of this step is inside it)
                        next = at + m
                        break
                    k = k & ~((1 << (at + m - c)) - 1) if at + m - c < 64 else 0
            c = next
            continue
        c += 64
    while c + m <= n:                                 # (the last few places)
        if s.byte(c + r1) == needle.byte(r1) and s[c..c + m] == needle:
            if not all:
                return (c, 0)
            found += 1
            c += m
            continue
        c += 1
    return (-1, found)

# is literal l at s[j..): its end, or -1
fn _lit_at(l: Lit, s: str, j: int) int:
    m = len(l.b)
    if m > len(s) - j:
        return -1
    for k in 0..m:
        if (s.byte(j + k) | l.m.byte(k)) != l.b.byte(k):
            return -1
    return j + m

# the first literal (in priority order) of the buckets in bits at s[j..): its end, or -1
fn _lits_at(p: Prog, s: str, j: int, bits: int) int:
    for i, l in p.lits:
        if ((bits >> (i & 7)) & 1) == 0:
            continue
        e = _lit_at(l, s, j)
        if e >= 0:
            return e
    return -1

# from i: the first place one of the literals may start (verify: the first where one does,
# its end in end). len(s): none. Each literal is in one of 8 buckets (a bit); for each of the
# first tk bytes, two 16-entry tables map a byte's low and high nibble to the buckets that
# allow it there: a lookup of each nibble of 16 text bytes, ANDed over the tk positions, leaves
# the buckets that may start at each byte. That over-approximates (the nibbles are checked
# apart), so each hit is then checked, or handed on as a place to look.
fn teddy(p: Prog, s: str, i0: int, verify: bool, end: mut int) int:
    n = len(s)
    k = p.tk
    i = i0
    f = simd.splat(15)
    while i + 16 + k - 1 <= n:
        x = simd.load(s, i)
        m = simd.lookup(p.vtlo[0], x & f) & simd.lookup(p.vthi[0], x >> 4)
        if k > 1:
            y = simd.load(s, i + 1)
            m = m & simd.lookup(p.vtlo[1], y & f) & simd.lookup(p.vthi[1], y >> 4)
        if k > 2:
            z = simd.load(s, i + 2)
            m = m & simd.lookup(p.vtlo[2], z & f) & simd.lookup(p.vthi[2], z >> 4)
        bits = simd.bits(m)
        while bits != 0:
            lane = simd.first(bits)
            if not verify:
                return i + lane
            e = _lits_at(p, s, i + lane, simd.lane(m, lane))
            if e >= 0:
                end = e
                return i + lane
            bits = bits & (bits - 1)
        i += 16
    while i + k <= n:                                 # (the last few bytes)
        b = p.tb[s.byte(i)]
        if k > 1:
            b &= p.tb[256 + s.byte(i + 1)]
        if k > 2:
            b &= p.tb[512 + s.byte(i + 2)]
        if b != 0:
            if not verify:
                return i
            e = _lits_at(p, s, i, b)
            if e >= 0:
                end = e
                return i
        i += 1
    return n

# where a match could begin at or after i (len(s): nowhere)
fn prefilter(p: Prog, s: str, i: int) int:
    n = len(s)
    if len(p.prefix) > 1:
        f = memmem_rare(s, i, p.prefix, p.rare, p.rare2)
        return n if f < 0 else f
    if len(p.prefix) == 1:
        f = s.find_from(p.prefix, i)
        return n if f < 0 else f
    j = i
    nr = len(p.vlo)
    if nr > 0:                                        # 16 bytes a step
        lo0 = p.vlo[0]
        sp0 = p.vspan[0]
        if nr == 1:
            while j + 16 <= n:
                k = simd.first_lane(simd.le(simd.load(s, j) - lo0, sp0))
                if k < 16:
                    return j + k
                j += 16
        while j + 16 <= n:
            x = simd.load(s, j)
            hit = simd.le(x - lo0, sp0)
            for r in 1..nr:
                hit = hit | simd.le(x - p.vlo[r], p.vspan[r])
            k = simd.first_lane(hit)
            if k < 16:
                return j + k
            j += 16
    if p.teddy:
        e = 0
        return teddy(p, s, j, false, &e)
    while j < n and not p.first[s.byte(j)]:
        j += 1
    return j

# ---- finding

# the first match at or after `at` into out[0..2*ngroups): the DFA finds where it ends, the
# reverse DFA where it starts, and groups() fills in groups (only if asked). end_only: just
# its end is needed, when the match can't be empty (out[0] may then be -1)
fn find_x(p: Prog, sr: mut Search, s: str, at: int, want_groups: bool, end_only: bool, out: mut [int]) bool:
    n = len(s)
    ns = 2 * p.ngroups
    if p.literal:                                     # just a string: no automaton
        f = memmem_rare(s, at, p.prefix, p.rare, p.rare2)
        if f < 0:
            return false
        out[0] = f
        out[1] = f + len(p.prefix)
        return true
    if p.lits_exact:                                  # a few strings: no automaton
        if at >= n:
            return false
        e = -1
        st = teddy(p, s, at, true, &e)
        if st >= n:
            return false
        out[0] = st
        out[1] = e
        return true
    if want_groups and at == 0 and _bt_only(p, n):
        # (anchored, groups wanted, a short text: the backtracker alone finds the match and
        # its groups, as RE2 does; a DFA pass first would only find where the match ends)
        _sc(p, &sr)
        return _backtrack(p, &sr.sc, s, 0, n, ns, &out)
    if p.inner and _dfa_ok(&sr, s):
        pos = at
        gave_up = false
        while pos < n:
            f = memmem_rare(s, pos, p.lit, p.lrare, p.lrare2)
            if f < 0:
                return false
            st = dfa_back(p, &sr.x.i, s, at, f)   # the earliest start of P before L
            if st == -2:
                gave_up = true
                break
            e = dfa_scan(p, &sr.x, s, st, false, true) if st >= 0 else -1
            if e == -2:
                gave_up = true
                break
            if e >= 0:
                if not want_groups or p.ngroups == 1:
                    out[0] = st
                    out[1] = e
                    for k in 2..ns:
                        out[k] = -1
                    return true
                _sc(p, &sr)
                if groups(p, &sr.sc, s, st, e, ns, &out):
                    return true
                gave_up = true
                break
            pos = f + 1                               # P or S failed around this L: the next one
        if not gave_up and at >= n:
            return false
    if _dfa_ok(&sr, s):
        e = -1
        if not (p.anchored and at > 0):
            e = dfa_scan(p, &sr.x, s, at, false, p.anchored)
        if e == -1:
            return false
        if e >= 0 and end_only and not p.nullable:
            out[0] = -1
            out[1] = e
            return true
        if e >= 0:
            # (an anchored match starts where the search did: at, which is 0)
            st = at if p.anchored else dfa_back(p, &sr.x.r, s, at, e)
            if st >= 0:
                if not want_groups or p.ngroups == 1:
                    out[0] = st
                    out[1] = e
                    for k in 2..ns:
                        out[k] = -1
                    return true
                _sc(p, &sr)
                if groups(p, &sr.sc, s, st, e, ns, &out):
                    return true
    _sc(p, &sr)
    if not run_vm(p, &sr.sc, s, at, 0, ns):
        return false
    for k in 0..ns:
        out[k] = sr.sc.best[k]
    return true

# whether a search from 0 for groups is the backtracker's alone: anchored, groups, not
# one-pass, a short text
fn _bt_only(p: Prog, n: int) bool:
    return p.anchored and p.ngroups > 1 and len(p.onepass) == 0 and len(p.code.op) * (n + 1) <= BT_MAX_BITS

# e_search from 0, and how much of s it read (see _backtrack): len(s) + 1 unless it was the
# backtracker's alone
fn e_search_reach(e: Engine, s: str) ([int], int):
    sr = _search(e, s)
    out = [0] * (2 * e.ps[0].ngroups)
    ok = find_x(e.ps[0], &sr[0], s, 0, true, false, &out)
    reach = len(s) + 1
    if _bt_only(e.ps[0], len(s)):
        reach = sr[0].sc.reach
    _done(e, sr)
    return (out if ok else []), reach

# the first match at or after `at`: its slots, or [] if there's none
fn e_search(e: Engine, s: str, at: int) [int]:
    if at < 0 or at > len(s):
        return []
    sr = _search(e, s)
    out = [0] * (2 * e.ps[0].ngroups)
    ok = find_x(e.ps[0], &sr[0], s, at, true, false, &out)
    _done(e, sr)
    return out if ok else []

# does the whole of s match
fn e_full(e: Engine, s: str) bool:
    sr = _search(e, s)
    if _dfa_ok(&sr[0], s):
        r = dfa_full(e.ps[0], &sr[0].x, s, 0)
        if r >= 0:
            _done(e, sr)
            return r == 1
    _sc(e.ps[0], &sr[0])
    ok = run_vm(e.ps[0], &sr[0].sc, s, 0, 1, 2 * e.ps[0].ngroups)
    _done(e, sr)
    return ok

# is there a match anywhere in s
fn e_test(e: Engine, s: str) bool:
    sr = _search(e, s)
    if _dfa_ok(&sr[0], s):
        r = dfa_scan(e.ps[0], &sr[0].x, s, 0, true, e.ps[0].anchored)
        if r != -2:
            _done(e, sr)
            return r >= 0
    _sc(e.ps[0], &sr[0])
    ok = run_vm(e.ps[0], &sr[0].sc, s, 0, 2, 0)
    _done(e, sr)
    return ok

fn _width(s: str, i: int) int:
    return decode(s, i).1 if i < len(s) else 1

# where a walk over every match is: where to search from, the last match's end
struct Walk:
    at: int
    last_end: int
    count: int

fn walk() Walk:
    return Walk(0, -1, 0)

# the next match of a walk (an empty match right after the previous match is skipped, and
# after an empty match the search moves on one character): true and its slots in out
fn walk_next(p: Prog, sr: mut Search, s: str, w: mut Walk, want_groups: bool, end_only: bool, out: mut [int]) bool:
    n = len(s)
    if p.literal:                                     # just a string (never empty): the next one
        f = memmem_rare(s, w.at, p.prefix, p.rare, p.rare2) if w.at <= n else -1
        if f < 0:
            w.at = n + 1
            return false
        out[0] = f
        out[1] = f + len(p.prefix)
        w.at = out[1]
        w.last_end = out[1]
        w.count += 1
        return true
    while w.at <= n:
        if not find_x(p, &sr, s, w.at, want_groups, end_only, &out):
            w.at = n + 1
            return false
        st = out[0]
        e = out[1]
        if st < 0:                                    # (counting a match that can't be empty)
            w.at = e
            w.last_end = e
            w.count += 1
            return true
        if e == st and st == w.last_end:
            if st >= n:
                w.at = n + 1
                return false
            w.at = st + _width(s, st)
            continue
        w.at = e
        if e == st:
            w.at = e + _width(s, e)
        w.last_end = e
        w.count += 1
        return true
    return false

fn e_count(e: Engine, s: str) int:
    if e.ps[0].literal:                               # one loop, not a search per match
        return _lit_scan(s, 0, e.ps[0].prefix, e.ps[0].rare, e.ps[0].rare2, true).1
    sr = _search(e, s)
    w = walk()
    out = [0] * (2 * e.ps[0].ngroups)
    while walk_next(e.ps[0], &sr[0], s, &w, false, true, &out):
        pass
    _done(e, sr)
    return w.count

# every match's slots, one after another (2 * ngroups each)
fn e_find_all(e: Engine, s: str) [int]:
    sr = _search(e, s)
    w = walk()
    ns = 2 * e.ps[0].ngroups
    out = [0] * ns
    all: [int] = []
    while walk_next(e.ps[0], &sr[0], s, &w, true, false, &out):
        for k in 0..ns:
            all.push(out[k])
    _done(e, sr)
    return all

# repl with $1 ${name} $0 $$ filled in from the match at slots m
fn expand(p: Prog, s: str, repl: str, m: [int], o: mut str):
    n = len(repl)
    run = 0
    c = 0
    while c < n:
        if repl.byte(c) != 36 or c + 1 >= n:
            c += 1
            continue
        o += repl[run..c]
        g = -1
        next = c + 1
        d = repl.byte(c + 1)
        if d == 36:
            o += "$"
            run = c + 2
            c += 2
            continue
        if d >= 48 and d <= 57:
            g = d - 48
            next = c + 2
        elif d == 123:
            close = repl.find_from("}", c + 2)
            if close < 0:
                run = c
                break
            name = repl[c + 2..close]
            digits = len(name) > 0
            for k in 0..len(name):
                if name.byte(k) < 48 or name.byte(k) > 57:
                    digits = false
            if digits:
                g = 0
                for k in 0..len(name):
                    if g < 100000:
                        g = g * 10 + name.byte(k) - 48
            else:
                for k in 1..p.ngroups:
                    if p.names[k] != "" and p.names[k] == name:
                        g = k
            if g < 0:
                g = 1 << 30                           # an unknown name: nothing
            next = close + 1
        else:
            o += "$"
            run = c + 1
            c += 1
            continue
        if g < p.ngroups and m[2 * g] >= 0 and m[2 * g + 1] >= m[2 * g]:
            o += s[m[2 * g]..m[2 * g + 1]]
        run = next
        c = next
    o += repl[run..]

# s with its matches (the first `limit`, or all if limit < 0) replaced by repl
fn e_replace(e: Engine, s: str, repl: str, limit: int) str:
    want = false                                      # $1 or ${...} need the groups
    for i in 0..len(repl) - 1:
        if repl.byte(i) == 36 and ((repl.byte(i + 1) >= 49 and repl.byte(i + 1) <= 57) or repl.byte(i + 1) == 123):
            want = true
    plain = repl.find("$") < 0
    sr = _search(e, s)
    w = walk()
    out = [0] * (2 * e.ps[0].ngroups)
    o = ""
    last = 0
    while (limit < 0 or w.count < limit) and walk_next(e.ps[0], &sr[0], s, &w, want, false, &out):
        if w.count == 1:
            o.reserve(len(s))                         # (like Rust's regex: one block, not doublings)
        o += s[last..out[0]]
        if plain:
            o += repl
        else:
            expand(e.ps[0], s, repl, out, &o)
        last = out[1]
    _done(e, sr)
    if w.count == 0:
        return s
    o += s[last..]
    return o
```

## library/std/re/literals.tn

```tern
# re: the literals every match of a pattern must contain, for searching an index (n-grams,
# a full-text index) before running the pattern: the codesearch analysis (Russ Cox, "Regular
# Expression Matching with a Trigram Index"), on the parsed tree.
#
# Each node gets: its exact set of matches when that's a few strings, else strings every
# match starts with (pre) and ends with (suf), plus clauses (cnf) every text holding a match
# satisfies: each clause is literals of which the text holds at least one. Literals compare
# ASCII letters without case (they're kept lowercase). Sets past LIT_SET strings are given
# up (a clause made from what's known, then the information dropped), so the answer is
# always right, just less precise for patterns that can match many different strings.

const LIT_SET = 32            # strings in an exact / prefix / suffix set at most
const LIT_OR = 64             # literals in one clause at most
const LIT_KEEP = 3            # clauses of each side kept when two are OR-ed (their product)

struct _LInfo:
    known: bool       # exact holds every string this matches
    exact: [str]
    pre: [str]
    suf: [str]
    cnf: [[str]]

fn _lany() _LInfo:
    return _LInfo(false, [], [""], [""], [])

fn _lexact(s: [str]) _LInfo:
    return _LInfo(true, s, [], [], [])

fn _lascii_lower(s: str) str:
    out = s
    for i in 0..len(s):
        b = s.byte(i)
        if b >= 65 and b <= 90:
            out = s.lower()
            break
    return out

fn _lhas(xs: [str], x: str) bool:
    for y in xs:
        if y == x:
            return true
    return false

# a and b as one set, or ([], false) past LIT_SET
fn _lunion(a: [str], b: [str]) ([str], bool):
    out = a
    for x in b:
        if not _lhas(out, x):
            if len(out) == LIT_SET:
                return ([], false)
            out.push(x)
    return (out, true)

# every x + y, or ([], false) past LIT_SET
fn _lcross(a: [str], b: [str]) ([str], bool):
    if len(a) * len(b) > LIT_SET * 4:
        return ([], false)
    out: [str] = []
    for x in a:
        for y in b:
            s = x + y
            if not _lhas(out, s):
                if len(out) == LIT_SET:
                    return ([], false)
                out.push(s)
    return (out, true)

# s as a clause: [] (says nothing) if one of its strings is shorter than min
fn _lclause(s: [str], min: int) [str]:
    if len(s) == 0 or len(s) > LIT_OR:
        return []
    for x in s:
        if len(x) < min or len(x) == 0:
            return []
    return s

fn _land(cnf: mut [[str]], c: [str]):
    if len(c) == 0:
        return
    for d in cnf:
        if d == c:
            return
    cnf.push(c)

fn _land_all(cnf: mut [[str]], cs: [[str]]):
    for c in cs:
        _land(&cnf, c)

# everything known about x, as clauses
fn _lfull(x: _LInfo, min: int) [[str]]:
    out = x.cnf
    if x.known:
        _land(&out, _lclause(x.exact, min))
    else:
        _land(&out, _lclause(x.pre, min))
        _land(&out, _lclause(x.suf, min))
    return out

# how much a clause narrows a search: its shortest literal (longer is rarer), then fewer
fn _lscore(c: [str]) int:
    m = 1 << 20
    for x in c:
        if len(x) < m:
            m = len(x)
    return m * 64 - len(c)

fn _lbest(cnf: [[str]], n: int) [[str]]:
    s = cnf.sort_by(fn(c) -_lscore(c))
    out: [[str]] = []
    for c in s:
        if len(out) < n:
            out.push(c)
    return out

# (a1 and a2 ...) or (b1 and b2 ...) = and of every (ai or bj)
fn _lor(a: [[str]], b: [[str]]) [[str]]:
    out: [[str]] = []
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return out
    for x in _lbest(a, LIT_KEEP):
        for y in _lbest(b, LIT_KEEP):
            u = x
            for s in y:
                if not _lhas(u, s):
                    u.push(s)
            if len(u) <= LIT_OR:
                _land(&out, u)
    return out

fn _lcat(x: _LInfo, y: _LInfo, min: int) _LInfo:
    if x.known and y.known:
        p = _lcross(x.exact, y.exact)
        if p.1:
            return _lexact(p.0)
        cnf = x.cnf
        _land_all(&cnf, y.cnf)
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(x.exact, min))
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(y.exact, min))
        return _LInfo(false, [], x.exact, y.exact, cnf)
    cnf = x.cnf
    _land_all(&cnf, y.cnf)
    xs = x.exact if x.known else x.suf
    yp = y.exact if y.known else y.pre
    j = _lcross(xs, yp)                               # across the join: "ab" then "cd" holds "abcd"
    if j.1:
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(j.0, min))
    else:
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(xs, min))
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(yp, min))
    pre = x.pre
    if x.known:
        p = _lcross(x.exact, y.pre)
        pre = p.0 if p.1 else x.exact
    suf = y.suf
    if y.known:
        p = _lcross(x.suf, y.exact)
        suf = p.0 if p.1 else y.exact
    return _LInfo(false, [], pre, suf, cnf)

fn _lalt(x: _LInfo, y: _LInfo, min: int) _LInfo:
    if x.known and y.known:
        u = _lunion(x.exact, y.exact)
        if u.1:
            return _lexact(u.0)
    xp = x.exact if x.known else x.pre
    yp = y.exact if y.known else y.pre
    xs = x.exact if x.known else x.suf
    ys = y.exact if y.known else y.suf
    p = _lunion(xp, yp)
    s = _lunion(xs, ys)
    return _LInfo(false, [], p.0 if p.1 else [""], s.0 if s.1 else [""], _lor(_lfull(x, min), _lfull(y, min)))

fn _linfo(t: Tree, i: int, min: int) _LInfo:
    n = t.nodes[i]
    if n.kind == N_EMPTY or n.kind == N_ASSERT:
        return _lexact([""])
    if n.kind == N_CHAR:
        if n.c == 0xFFFD or (n.fold and n.c >= 0x80):      # (U+FFFD also stands for a bad byte)
            return _lany()
        return _lexact([_lascii_lower(encode(n.c))])
    if n.kind == N_CLASS:
        c = t.classes[n.cls]
        if c.neg:
            return _lany()
        total = 0
        for k in 0..len(c.lo):
            if c.hi[k] >= 0x80:
                return _lany()
            total += c.hi[k] - c.lo[k] + 1
        if total > 2 * 10:
            return _lany()
        out: [str] = []
        for k in 0..len(c.lo):
            for x in c.lo[k]..c.hi[k] + 1:
                s = _lascii_lower(chr(x))
                if not _lhas(out, s):
                    out.push(s)
        return _lexact(out) if len(out) <= 10 else _lany()
    if n.kind == N_GROUP:
        return _linfo(t, n.kids[0], min)
    if n.kind == N_CAT:
        acc = _lexact([""])
        for k in n.kids:
            acc = _lcat(acc, _linfo(t, k, min), min)
        return acc
    if n.kind == N_ALT:
        acc = _linfo(t, n.kids[0], min)
        for k in 1..len(n.kids):
            acc = _lalt(acc, _linfo(t, n.kids[k], min), min)
        return acc
    if n.kind == N_REP:
        if n.max == 0:
            return _lexact([""])
        x = _linfo(t, n.kids[0], min)
        if n.min == 0:
            if n.max == 1 and x.known:
                u = _lunion(x.exact, [""])
                if u.1:
                    return _lexact(u.0)
            return _lany()
        if x.known and n.max == n.min:
            acc = _lexact([""])
            for k in 0..n.min:
                acc = _lcat(acc, x, min)
            return acc
        cnf = x.cnf
        if x.known:
            _land(&cnf, _lclause(x.exact, min))
            return _LInfo(false, [], x.exact, x.exact, cnf)
        return _LInfo(false, [], x.pre, x.suf, cnf)
    return _lany()                                       # N_ANY

# does every literal of a contain one of b's (then b says nothing a doesn't)
fn _limplies(a: [str], b: [str]) bool:
    for x in a:
        found = false
        for y in b:
            if x.contains(y):
                found = true
                break
        if not found:
            return false
    return true

# The clauses of tree t (see literals in re.tn).
fn tree_literals(t: Tree, min: int) [[str]]:
    all = _lfull(_linfo(t, t.root, min), min)
    out: [[str]] = []
    for i, c in all:
        implied = false
        for j, d in all:
            if j != i and _limplies(d, c) and (not _limplies(c, d) or j < i):
                implied = true
                break
        if not implied:
            out.push(c)
    return out.sort_by(fn(c) -_lscore(c))
```

## library/std/re/parse.tn

```tern
# re: the parser. A pattern becomes a tree of nodes in one array (Tree.nodes; a node's kids
# are indexes into it), and its character classes a table (Tree.classes). The syntax and the
# error messages are RE2's subset described in re.tn.

const N_EMPTY = 0
const N_CHAR = 1
const N_ANY = 2
const N_CLASS = 3
const N_CAT = 4
const N_ALT = 5
const N_REP = 6
const N_GROUP = 7
const N_ASSERT = 8

const A_BOT = 0       # \A, or ^ without (?m)
const A_EOT = 1       # \z, or $ without (?m)
const A_BOL = 2
const A_EOL = 3
const A_WORD = 4      # \b
const A_NWORD = 5     # \B

struct Node:
    kind: int
    c: int            # N_CHAR: the character (a code point)
    fold: bool        # N_CHAR: case-insensitive (and it has another case)
    dotnl: bool       # N_ANY: matches \n too
    cls: int          # N_CLASS: index into Tree.classes
    min: int          # N_REP
    max: int          # N_REP: -1 for no limit
    greedy: bool      # N_REP
    group: int        # N_GROUP: its index, or -1 (non-capturing)
    at: int           # N_ASSERT: A_*
    kids: [int]

# a set of characters: sorted, merged ranges [lo[i], hi[i]], and whether it's negated;
# ascii0/ascii1: the ranges' members below 64 and 64..127, as bits (before negation)
struct Class:
    lo: [int]
    hi: [int]
    neg: bool
    ascii0: int
    ascii1: int

struct Tree:
    nodes: [Node]
    classes: [Class]
    root: int
    names: [str]      # each group's name ("" if unnamed); [0] is the whole match

struct _P:
    s: str
    p: int
    fi: bool
    fm: bool
    fs: bool
    fx: bool
    depth: int
    err: str
    t: Tree

# one character of s at i: (code point, bytes). A byte that doesn't start a valid UTF-8
# sequence (overlong forms, surrogates and past U+10FFFF too) reads as U+FFFD, one byte wide.
fn decode(s: str, i: int) (int, int):
    c = s.byte(i)
    if c < 0x80:
        return (c, 1)
    n = 0
    lo = 0x80
    hi = 0xBF
    if c >= 0xC2 and c <= 0xDF:
        n = 2
    elif c >= 0xE0 and c <= 0xEF:
        n = 3
        if c == 0xE0:
            lo = 0xA0
        elif c == 0xED:
            hi = 0x9F
    elif c >= 0xF0 and c <= 0xF4:
        n = 4
        if c == 0xF0:
            lo = 0x90
        elif c == 0xF4:
            hi = 0x8F
    else:
        return (0xFFFD, 1)
    if i + n > len(s) or s.byte(i + 1) < lo or s.byte(i + 1) > hi:
        return (0xFFFD, 1)
    v = c & (0x3F >> (n - 1))
    for k in 1..n:
        b = s.byte(i + k)
        if k > 1 and (b & 0xC0) != 0x80:
            return (0xFFFD, 1)
        v = (v << 6) | (b & 0x3F)
    return (v, n)

fn encode(cp: int) str:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return chr(cp)
    out = ""
    if cp < 0x800:
        out += chr(0xC0 | cp >> 6)
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        out += chr(0xE0 | cp >> 12)
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp >> 6 & 63))
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))
        return out
    else:
        out += chr(0xF0 | cp >> 18)
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp >> 12 & 63))
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp >> 6 & 63))
    out += chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))
    return out

# simple case folding: ASCII, Latin-1, Greek, Cyrillic
fn lower(c: int) int:
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90:
        return c + 32
    if c < 0xC0:
        return c
    if (c >= 0xC0 and c <= 0xDE and c != 0xD7) or (c >= 0x391 and c <= 0x3A9 and c != 0x3A2) or (c >= 0x410 and c <= 0x42F):
        return c + 32
    if c >= 0x400 and c <= 0x40F:
        return c + 80
    return c

fn upper(c: int) int:
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122:
        return c - 32
    if c < 0xE0:
        return c
    if (c >= 0xE0 and c <= 0xFE and c != 0xF7) or (c >= 0x3B1 and c <= 0x3C9 and c != 0x3C2) or (c >= 0x430 and c <= 0x44F):
        return c - 32
    if c >= 0x450 and c <= 0x45F:
        return c - 80
    return c

fn is_word(c: int) bool:
    return (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or c == 95

fn _node(kind: int) Node:
    return Node(kind, 0, false, false, -1, 0, 0, true, -1, 0, [])

fn _add(ps: mut _P, n: Node) int:
    ps.t.nodes.push(n)
    return len(ps.t.nodes) - 1

fn _fail(ps: mut _P, msg: str) int:
    if ps.err == "":
        ps.err = f"re: {msg} (at byte {ps.p} of the pattern)"
    return -1

fn _more(ps: _P) bool:
    return ps.p < len(ps.s)

fn _at(ps: _P) int:
    return ps.s.byte(ps.p) if ps.p < len(ps.s) else -1

# classes
fn _class_add(c: mut Class, lo: int, hi: int):
    c.lo.push(lo)
    c.hi.push(hi)

fn _class_add_fold(c: mut Class, lo: int, hi: int, fold: bool):
    _class_add(&c, lo, hi)
    if not fold:
        return
    x = lo
    while x <= hi and x < 0x460:                 # the cased letters lower() knows
        l = lower(x)
        u = upper(x)
        if l != x:
            _class_add(&c, l, l)
        if u != x:
            _class_add(&c, u, u)
        x += 1

# sorts and merges the ranges, and fills the ASCII bitmaps
fn class_done(c: mut Class):
    if len(c.lo) > 1:
        idx: [int] = []
        for i in 0..len(c.lo):
            idx.push(i)
        los = c.lo
        order = idx.sort_by(fn(i) los[i])
        lo: [int] = []
        hi: [int] = []
        for i in order:
            if len(lo) > 0 and c.lo[i] <= hi[len(hi) - 1] + 1:
                if c.hi[i] > hi[len(hi) - 1]:
                    hi[len(hi) - 1] = c.hi[i]
            else:
                lo.push(c.lo[i])
                hi.push(c.hi[i])
        c.lo = lo
        c.hi = hi
    c.ascii0 = 0
    c.ascii1 = 0
    for i in 0..len(c.lo):
        x = c.lo[i]
        while x <= c.hi[i] and x < 128:
            if x < 64:
                c.ascii0 |= 1 << x
            else:
                c.ascii1 |= 1 << (x - 64)
            x += 1

fn class_has(c: Class, x: int) bool:
    inside = false
    if x < 64:
        inside = ((c.ascii0 >> x) & 1) != 0
    elif x < 128:
        inside = ((c.ascii1 >> (x - 64)) & 1) != 0
    else:
        lo = 0
        hi = len(c.lo) - 1
        while lo <= hi:
            m = (lo + hi) / 2
            if x < c.lo[m]:
                hi = m - 1
            elif x > c.hi[m]:
                lo = m + 1
            else:
                inside = true
                break
    return inside != c.neg

# \d \w \s and their negations (as ranges of the complement)
fn _perl(c: mut Class, k: int):
    r: [int] = [32, 32]
    if k == 100 or k == 68:
        r = [48, 57]
    elif k == 119 or k == 87:
        r = [48, 57, 65, 90, 95, 95, 97, 122]
    else:
        r = [9, 13, 32, 32]
    if k >= 97:
        for i in 0..len(r) / 2:
            _class_add(&c, r[2 * i], r[2 * i + 1])
        return
    lo = 0
    for i in 0..len(r) / 2:
        if r[2 * i] > lo:
            _class_add(&c, lo, r[2 * i] - 1)
        lo = r[2 * i + 1] + 1
    _class_add(&c, lo, 0x10FFFF)

fn _posix(c: mut Class, name: str, fold: bool) bool:
    t = [("alpha", "AZaz"), ("digit", "09"), ("alnum", "09AZaz"), ("upper", "AZ"), ("lower", "az"), ("space", "\t\r  "), ("xdigit", "09AFaf"), ("punct", "!/:@[`{~"), ("word", "09AZ__az"), ("blank", "\t\t  "), ("cntrl", "\x01\x1f\x7f\x7f"), ("print", " ~"), ("graph", "!~")]
    for e in t:
        if e.0 == name:
            for i in 0..len(e.1) / 2:
                _class_add_fold(&c, e.1.byte(2 * i), e.1.byte(2 * i + 1), fold)
            if name == "cntrl":
                _class_add(&c, 0, 0)
            return true
    return false

fn _hexval(b: int) int:
    if b >= 48 and b <= 57:
        return b - 48
    if b >= 97 and b <= 102:
        return b - 87
    if b >= 65 and b <= 70:
        return b - 55
    return -1

# after \x: HH or {H..}; -1 on an error
fn _hex(ps: mut _P) int:
    v = 0
    n = 0
    if _at(ps) == 123:
        ps.p += 1
        while _more(ps) and _at(ps) != 125:
            d = _hexval(_at(ps))
            n += 1
            if d < 0 or n > 6:
                return _fail(&ps, "bad \\x{...}: write 1 to 6 hex digits")
            v = v * 16 + d
            ps.p += 1
        if not _more(ps) or n == 0:
            return _fail(&ps, "bad \\x{...}: write 1 to 6 hex digits")
        ps.p += 1
    else:
        while n < 2:
            d = _hexval(_at(ps))
            if d < 0:
                return _fail(&ps, "bad \\x: write two hex digits (\\x41) or \\x{263a}")
            v = v * 16 + d
            ps.p += 1
            n += 1
    if v > 0x10FFFF:
        return _fail(&ps, "\\x{...} is past the last Unicode character")
    return v

# an escape after `\`: (kind, value): kind 0 a character, 1 a class (value: its index), 2 an
# assertion (value: A_*); kind -1 on an error
fn _escape(ps: mut _P, in_class: bool) (int, int):
    if not _more(ps):
        _fail(&ps, "the pattern ends with a lone \\")
        return (-1, 0)
    k = _at(ps)
    ps.p += 1
    if k == 110:
        return (0, 10)
    if k == 116:
        return (0, 9)
    if k == 114:
        return (0, 13)
    if k == 102:
        return (0, 12)
    if k == 118:
        return (0, 11)
    if k == 97:
        return (0, 7)
    if k == 120:
        v = _hex(&ps)
        return (-1, 0) if v < 0 else (0, v)
    if k == 100 or k == 68 or k == 119 or k == 87 or k == 115 or k == 83:
        c = Class([], [], false, 0, 0)
        _perl(&c, k)
        class_done(&c)
        ps.t.classes.push(c)
        return (1, len(ps.t.classes) - 1)
    if not in_class:
        if k == 98:
            return (2, A_WORD)
        if k == 66:
            return (2, A_NWORD)
        if k == 65:
            return (2, A_BOT)
        if k == 122:
            return (2, A_EOT)
    if k == 112 or k == 80:
        _fail(&ps, "\\p{...} Unicode classes aren't supported: use a class like [a-zA-Z\\x{c0}-\\x{24f}]")
        return (-1, 0)
    if k == 90:
        _fail(&ps, "\\Z isn't supported: use \\z (the end of the text)")
        return (-1, 0)
    if k >= 49 and k <= 57:
        _fail(&ps, "backreferences (\\1) aren't supported: they need backtracking, which can take exponential time")
        return (-1, 0)
    alnum = (k >= 48 and k <= 57) or (k >= 65 and k <= 90) or (k >= 97 and k <= 122)
    if k < 128 and not alnum:
        return (0, k)                               # \. \* \\ \( ...
    _fail(&ps, "unknown escape \\" + chr(k))
    return (-1, 0)

# after `[`
fn _class_node(ps: mut _P) int:
    c = Class([], [], false, 0, 0)
    if _at(ps) == 94:
        c.neg = true
        ps.p += 1
    first = true
    while _more(ps) and (_at(ps) != 93 or first):
        first = false
        lo = 0
        if _at(ps) == 91 and ps.p + 1 < len(ps.s) and ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) == 58:       # [:alpha:]
            nm = ps.p + 2
            e = nm
            while e + 1 < len(ps.s) and not (ps.s.byte(e) == 58 and ps.s.byte(e + 1) == 93):
                e += 1
            if e + 1 >= len(ps.s) or not _posix(&c, ps.s[nm..e], ps.fi):
                return _fail(&ps, "unknown [:class:] (alpha, digit, alnum, upper, lower, space, xdigit, punct, word, blank, cntrl, print, graph)")
            ps.p = e + 2
            continue
        if _at(ps) == 92:
            ps.p += 1
            esc = _escape(&ps, true)
            if esc.0 < 0:
                return -1
            if esc.0 == 1:                            # \d inside a class: its ranges
                sub = ps.t.classes[esc.1]
                for i in 0..len(sub.lo):
                    _class_add(&c, sub.lo[i], sub.hi[i])
                continue
            lo = esc.1
        else:
            d = decode(ps.s, ps.p)
            lo = d.0
            ps.p += d.1
        hi = lo
        if ps.p + 1 < len(ps.s) and _at(ps) == 45 and ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) != 93:
            ps.p += 1
            if _at(ps) == 92:
                ps.p += 1
                esc = _escape(&ps, true)
                if esc.0 < 0:
                    return -1
                if esc.0 == 1:
                    return _fail(&ps, "a class can't be the end of a range")
                hi = esc.1
            else:
                d = decode(ps.s, ps.p)
                hi = d.0
                ps.p += d.1
            if hi < lo:
                return _fail(&ps, "a range's end comes before its start (like z-a)")
        _class_add_fold(&c, lo, hi, ps.fi)
    if not _more(ps):
        return _fail(&ps, "missing ] to close a [class]")
    ps.p += 1
    class_done(&c)
    ps.t.classes.push(c)
    n = _node(N_CLASS)
    n.cls = len(ps.t.classes) - 1
    return _add(&ps, n)

fn _skip_x(ps: mut _P):
    if not ps.fx:
        return
    while _more(ps):
        b = _at(ps)
        if b == 32 or b == 9 or b == 10 or b == 13:
            ps.p += 1
        elif b == 35:
            while _more(ps) and _at(ps) != 10:
                ps.p += 1
        else:
            break

# (?flags) or (?flags:  -- 1 for a scoped group, 0 for flags alone, -1 on an error
fn _flags(ps: mut _P) int:
    on = true
    while _more(ps) and _at(ps) != 41 and _at(ps) != 58:
        b = _at(ps)
        if b == 45:
            on = false
        elif b == 105:
            ps.fi = on
        elif b == 109:
            ps.fm = on
        elif b == 115:
            ps.fs = on
        elif b == 120:
            ps.fx = on
        elif b == 85:
```
