```tern
            return _fail(&ps, "the U flag isn't supported: write lazy quantifiers (*?) where you want them")
        else:
            return _fail(&ps, "unknown flag in (?...): use i, m, s or x")
        ps.p += 1
    if not _more(ps):
        return _fail(&ps, "missing ) after (?flags")
    scoped = _at(ps) == 58
    ps.p += 1
    return 1 if scoped else 0

fn _char_node(ps: mut _P, ch: int) int:
    n = _node(N_CHAR)
    n.c = ch
    n.fold = ps.fi and lower(ch) != upper(ch)
    return _add(&ps, n)

fn _atom(ps: mut _P) int:
    c = _at(ps)
    if c == 40:                                         # (
        ps.p += 1
        ps.depth += 1
        if ps.depth > 500:
            return _fail(&ps, "groups nested too deeply")
        group = -1
        fi = ps.fi
        fm = ps.fm
        fs = ps.fs
        fx = ps.fx
        if _at(ps) == 63:
            ps.p += 1
            if _at(ps) == 61 or _at(ps) == 33:
                return _fail(&ps, "lookahead (?= ...) isn't supported (it needs backtracking)")
            if ps.p + 1 < len(ps.s) and _at(ps) == 60 and (ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) == 61 or ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) == 33):
                return _fail(&ps, "lookbehind (?<= ...) isn't supported (it needs backtracking)")
            if _at(ps) == 80 or _at(ps) == 60:              # a named group
                if _at(ps) == 80:
                    ps.p += 1
                if _at(ps) != 60:
                    return _fail(&ps, "a named group is (?P<name>...) or (?<name>...)")
                ps.p += 1
                nm = ps.p
                while _more(ps) and (is_word(_at(ps))):
                    ps.p += 1
                if _at(ps) != 62 or ps.p == nm:
                    return _fail(&ps, "a group name is letters, digits and _, then >")
                name = ps.s[nm..ps.p]
                for g in 1..len(ps.t.names):
                    if ps.t.names[g] == name:
                        return _fail(&ps, "two groups have the same name")
                ps.p += 1
                group = len(ps.t.names)
                ps.t.names.push(name)
            else:
                f = _flags(&ps)
                if f < 0:
                    return -1
                if f == 0:                                  # (?i): the rest of this group
                    ps.depth -= 1
                    return _add(&ps, _node(N_EMPTY))
        else:
            group = len(ps.t.names)
            ps.t.names.push("")
        sub = _alt(&ps)
        if sub < 0:
            return -1
        if _at(ps) != 41:
            return _fail(&ps, "missing ) to close a group")
        ps.p += 1
        ps.depth -= 1
        ps.fi = fi
        ps.fm = fm
        ps.fs = fs
        ps.fx = fx
        g = _node(N_GROUP)
        g.group = group
        g.kids.push(sub)
        return _add(&ps, g)
    if c == 91:
        ps.p += 1
        return _class_node(&ps)
    if c == 46:
        ps.p += 1
        n = _node(N_ANY)
        n.dotnl = ps.fs
        return _add(&ps, n)
    if c == 94 or c == 36:
        ps.p += 1
        n = _node(N_ASSERT)
        if c == 94:
            n.at = A_BOL if ps.fm else A_BOT
        else:
            n.at = A_EOL if ps.fm else A_EOT
        return _add(&ps, n)
    if c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63:
        return _fail(&ps, "a quantifier (* + ?) with nothing before it: write \\* for the character")
    if c == 92:
        ps.p += 1
        esc = _escape(&ps, false)
        if esc.0 < 0:
            return -1
        if esc.0 == 1:
            n = _node(N_CLASS)
            n.cls = esc.1
            return _add(&ps, n)
        if esc.0 == 2:
            n = _node(N_ASSERT)
            n.at = esc.1
            return _add(&ps, n)
        return _char_node(&ps, esc.1)
    d = decode(ps.s, ps.p)
    ps.p += d.1
    return _char_node(&ps, d.0)

# digits for {n,m}: the value, or -1 if there are none or more than 4
fn _pcount(ps: mut _P) int:
    v = 0
    n = 0
    while _more(ps) and _at(ps) >= 48 and _at(ps) <= 57:
        v = v * 10 + _at(ps) - 48
        ps.p += 1
        n += 1
        if n > 4:
            return -1
    return v if n > 0 else -1

fn _repeat(ps: mut _P) int:
    a = _atom(&ps)
    if a < 0:
        return -1
    while true:
        _skip_x(&ps)
        if not _more(ps):
            return a
        min = 0
        max = 0
        c = _at(ps)
        if c == 42:
            max = -1
            ps.p += 1
        elif c == 43:
            min = 1
            max = -1
            ps.p += 1
        elif c == 63:
            max = 1
            ps.p += 1
        elif c == 123:
            save = ps.p
            ps.p += 1
            min = _pcount(&ps)
            if min < 0:
                ps.p = save                                 # a literal {
                return a
            max = min
            if _at(ps) == 44:
                ps.p += 1
                if _at(ps) == 125:
                    max = -1
                else:
                    max = _pcount(&ps)
                    if max < 0:
                        return _fail(&ps, "bad {n,m}")
            if _at(ps) != 125:
                return _fail(&ps, "missing } in {n,m}")
            ps.p += 1
            if min > 1000 or max > 1000:
                return _fail(&ps, "a count in {n,m} is over 1000")
            if max >= 0 and max < min:
                return _fail(&ps, "{n,m} with m smaller than n")
        else:
            return a
        k = ps.t.nodes[a].kind
        if k == N_ASSERT or k == N_EMPTY:
            return _fail(&ps, "nothing to repeat before a quantifier")
        if k == N_REP:
            return _fail(&ps, "two quantifiers in a row (like a**): group the first one, (a*)*")
        r = _node(N_REP)
        r.min = min
        r.max = max
        if _at(ps) == 63:
            r.greedy = false
            ps.p += 1
        r.kids.push(a)
        a = _add(&ps, r)
    return a

fn _concat(ps: mut _P) int:
    kids: [int] = []
    while true:
        _skip_x(&ps)
        if not _more(ps) or _at(ps) == 124 or _at(ps) == 41:
            break
        k = _repeat(&ps)
        if k < 0:
            return -1
        kids.push(k)
    n = _node(N_CAT)
    n.kids = kids
    return _add(&ps, n)

fn _alt(ps: mut _P) int:
    first = _concat(&ps)
    if first < 0:
        return -1
    if _at(ps) != 124:
        return first
    kids = [first]
    while _at(ps) == 124:
        ps.p += 1
        k = _concat(&ps)
        if k < 0:
            return -1
        kids.push(k)
    n = _node(N_ALT)
    n.kids = kids
    return _add(&ps, n)

# The tree of pattern, or the reason it isn't a valid pattern.
fn parse(pattern: str) Result[Tree, str]:
    ps = _P(pattern, 0, false, false, false, false, 0, "", Tree([], [], -1, [""]))
    root = _alt(&ps)
    if root >= 0 and ps.p < len(pattern):
        _fail(&ps, "unmatched ) (write \\) for the character)")
    if ps.err != "":
        return Err(ps.err)
    ps.t.root = root
    return Ok(ps.t)
```

## library/std/re/re.tn

```tern
# re: regular expressions that run in linear time (no catastrophic backtracking).
#
#   import re
#   r = re.compile("(\\w+)@(\\w+)\\.com")?      # Result[re.Regex, str]; or re.must(pattern)
#   r.test(s) bool                              is there a match anywhere in s
#   r.full(s) bool                              does the whole of s match
#   r.search(s) Option[re.Match]                the first match
#   r.search_at(s, at) Option[re.Match]         the first match at or after byte `at`
#   r.find_all(s) [re.Match]                    every match, left to right, not overlapping
#                                               (`for m in r.find_all(s):` takes them one at a
#                                               time, without an array of all of them)
#   r.count(s) int                              how many matches
#   r.search_reach(s) ([int], int)              the first match as slots (each group's start
#                                               and end, -1 if it didn't take part; [] for no
#                                               match) and how many of s's first bytes the search
#                                               read: any text with those bytes first (and at
#                                               least as long) gets the same slots; len(s) + 1
#                                               when the rest mattered. For many texts sharing
#                                               prefixes (a sorted list), one search can stand
#                                               for the next
#   r.replace_all(s, repl) str                  every match replaced; repl may use $1, ${name},
#                                               $0 (the whole match), $$ (a dollar sign)
#   r.replace_first(s, repl) str                only the first match
#   r.replace_with(s, f) str                    each match replaced by f(m) (f: fn(re.Match) str)
#   r.split_all(s) [str]                        the text between matches
#   r.names() [str]                             each group's name ("" if unnamed; [0] is the match)
#   re.escape(s) str                            s with every special character escaped
#   re.error() str                              why the last compile failed
#   re.literals(pattern, min) Result[[[str]], str]   for searching an index before running the
#                                               pattern: groups of literals such that every match
#                                               contains at least one literal of each group
#                                               (literals are lowercase and compare ASCII letters
#                                               without case; none shorter than min bytes; [] if
#                                               nothing is certain, like for \w+). Sorted most
#                                               selective first. `cdn\.(shopify|wix)\.com` gives
#                                               [["cdn.shopify.com", "cdn.wix.com"]]
#
# A Match: start, end (byte offsets: s[m.start..m.end] is m.text), text, groups ([0] is the
# whole match, [i] group i, "" if it didn't take part), starts (each group's start, -1 if it
# didn't take part), and named ({name: text} for named groups). m.group("name") reads one.
#
# Syntax (RE2's, shared by Go, Rust, Python and JavaScript):
#   .  [abc]  [^a-z]  [[:alpha:]]  \d \w \s  \D \W \S       (\d \w \s are ASCII)
#   ^ $ (text start / end; with (?m) line start / end)  \A \z  \b \B (ASCII word boundary)
#   (x) (?:x) (?P<name>x) (?<name>x)   x|y   x* x+ x? x{n} x{n,} x{n,m}, and x*? etc. (lazy)
#   (?i) case-insensitive, (?m) multi-line, (?s) . matches \n, (?x) spaces and # comments
#   ignored; (?i:x) for part of a pattern. \x41 \x{1F600} \n \t, and \. \* \( ... for the
#   characters themselves.
# Not supported, because they need backtracking: backreferences (\1), lookahead and
# lookbehind ((?=x), (?<=x)). \p{...} Unicode classes aren't supported either.
#
# Matching is by character on UTF-8 text: `.` is one character, however many bytes. Offsets
# (start, end, starts) are in bytes, like everything else on str. Time is linear in the
# text's length. A pattern is compiled once per program (the last 1000 are kept, so
# re.must(p) in a loop is cheap) and shared by every thread; its DFA's states are kept per
# thread, so threads searching with one pattern at once don't wait on each other.
# The engine is in this directory: parse.tn (syntax), compile.tn (programs), vm.tn (Pike
# VM, backtracker, one-pass), dfa.tn (lazy DFA), find.tn (searching, prefilters with simd).

import task

struct Regex:
    pattern: str
    group_names: [str]      # each group's name ("" if unnamed); [0] is the whole match
    named_groups: bool      # any of them has a name
    e: Engine

struct Match:
    start: int
    end: int
    text: str
    groups: [str]
    starts: [int]
    named: {str: str}

# compiled patterns, by pattern (cleared when it holds CACHE_MAX)
struct _Cache:
    regs: {str: Regex}

const CACHE_MAX = 1000
const _CACHE = task.shared(_Cache({}))

fn _look(c: mut _Cache, pattern: str) Option[Regex]:
    if pattern in c.regs:
        return Some(c.regs[pattern])
    return None

fn _keep(c: mut _Cache, r: Regex) int:
    if len(c.regs) >= CACHE_MAX:
        c.regs = {}
    c.regs[r.pattern] = r
    return 0

fn _any_named(names: [str]) bool:
    for nm in names:
        if nm != "":
            return true
    return false

# with Result: r = re.compile("[0-9]+")?   (Err: "re: missing ) to close a group (at byte 3 of the pattern)")
fn compile(pattern: str) Result[Regex, str]:
    found = _CACHE.update(fn(c) _look(&c, pattern))
    match found:
        Some(r):
            return Ok(r)
        None:
            pass
    match engine(pattern):
        Ok(e):
            names = e.ps[0].names
            r = Regex(pattern, names, _any_named(names), e)
            _CACHE.update(fn(c) _keep(&c, r))
            task.local_set("re.error", "")
            return Ok(r)
        Err(msg):
            task.local_set("re.error", msg)
            return Err(msg)

# for a pattern written in the program: a bad one is a runtime error with the reason
fn must(pattern: str) Regex:
    match compile(pattern):
        Ok(r):
            return r
        Err(msg):
            panic(msg + ": " + pattern)
    return must(pattern)

# why the last compile on this task failed ("" if it didn't)
fn error() str:
    return task.local_get("re.error")

fn test(r: Regex, s: str) bool:
    return e_test(r.e, s)

fn full(r: Regex, s: str) bool:
    return e_full(r.e, s)

# the match of slots[base..base + 2 * groups]
fn _match_of(r: Regex, s: str, slots: [int], base: int) Match:
    n = len(r.group_names)
    groups: [str] = []
    starts: [int] = []
    named: {str: str} = {}
    for i in 0..n:
        a = slots[base + 2 * i]
        b = slots[base + 2 * i + 1]
        if a >= 0 and b >= a:
            groups.push(s[a..b])
            starts.push(a)
        else:
            groups.push("")
            starts.push(-1)
    if r.named_groups:
        for i, nm in r.group_names:
            if nm != "":
                named[nm] = groups[i]
    return Match(starts[0], starts[0] + len(groups[0]), groups[0], groups, starts, named)

fn search_at(r: Regex, s: str, at: int) Option[Match]:
    sl = e_search(r.e, s, at)
    if len(sl) == 0:
        return None
    return Some(_match_of(r, s, sl, 0))

fn search(r: Regex, s: str) Option[Match]:
    return search_at(r, s, 0)

fn search_reach(r: Regex, s: str) ([int], int):
    return e_search_reach(r.e, s)

# the matches one at a time (`for m in r.find_all(s)` runs on this: codegen find_all_foreach)
struct _Iter:
    sr: [Search]
    w: Walk
    out: [int]

fn _iter(r: Regex, s: str) _Iter:
    return _Iter(_search(r.e, s), walk(), [0] * (2 * len(r.group_names)))

fn _iter_next(r: Regex, s: str, it: mut _Iter) bool:
    if len(it.sr) == 0:
        return false
    if walk_next(r.e.ps[0], &it.sr[0], s, &it.w, true, false, &it.out):
        return true
    _done(r.e, it.sr)
    it.sr = []
    return false

fn _iter_match(r: Regex, s: str, it: _Iter) Match:
    return _match_of(r, s, it.out, 0)

fn find_all(r: Regex, s: str) [Match]:
    it = _iter(r, s)
    out: [Match] = []
    while _iter_next(r, s, &it):
        out.push(_iter_match(r, s, it))
    return out

fn count(r: Regex, s: str) int:
    return e_count(r.e, s)

fn replace_all(r: Regex, s: str, repl: str) str:
    return e_replace(r.e, s, repl, -1)

fn replace_first(r: Regex, s: str, repl: str) str:
    return e_replace(r.e, s, repl, 1)

fn replace_with(r: Regex, s: str, f: fn(Match) str) str:
    out = ""
    last = 0
    for m in find_all(r, s):
        out += s[last..m.start] + f(m)
        last = m.end
    return out + s[last..]

fn split_all(r: Regex, s: str) [str]:
    sl = e_find_all(r.e, s)
    per = 2 * len(r.group_names)
    out: [str] = []
    last = 0
    for i in 0..len(sl) / per:
        a = sl[i * per]
        b = sl[i * per + 1]
        if a == 0 and b == 0:
            continue
        out.push(s[last..a])
        last = b
    out.push(s[last..])
    return out

fn names(r: Regex) [str]:
    return copy(r.group_names)

# a named group's text ("" if the pattern has no such group or it didn't take part)
fn group(m: Match, name: str) str:
    return m.named.get(name, "")

fn escape(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    for i in 0..len(s):
        c = s[i..i + 1]
        if "\\.+*?()|[]{}^$#&-~ \t\n".contains(c):
            if c == "\n":
                out += "\\n"
            elif c == "\t":
                out += "\\t"
            else:
                out += "\\" + c
        else:
            out += c
    return out

fn literals(pattern: str, min: int) Result[[[str]], str]:
    t = parse(pattern)?
    return Ok(tree_literals(t, min))
```

## library/std/re/vm.tn

```tern
# re: the matchers that know groups. The Pike VM runs every possible match together, one
# character at a time (linear in the text); the bounded backtracker fills in the groups of a
# match already known to span s[st..e) by trying paths depth first without visiting an
# (instruction, position) twice; the one-pass walk does it with no choices at all when the
# next byte always says which branch to tk2.

# where to keep threads and captures (made once per search, sized for the program)
struct Scratch:
    apc: [int]
    acaps: [int]
    an: int
    bpc: [int]
    bcaps: [int]
    bn: int
    seen: [int]
    stamp: int
    stack: [int]
    best: [int]
    caps: [int]
    btseen: [int]
    jobs: [int]               # the backtracker's stack
    reach: int                # how much of the text the last backtrack read (see _backtrack)

# (the VM's thread lists are made when it first runs: most searches only backtrack)
fn scratch(p: Prog) Scratch:
    ns = 2 * p.ngroups
    return Scratch([], [], 0, [], [], 0, [], 0, [], [0] * ns, [0] * ns, [], [], 0)

fn _vm_scratch(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch):
    nc = len(p.code.op)
    ns = 2 * p.ngroups
    sc.apc = [0] * nc
    sc.acaps = [0] * (nc * ns)
    sc.bpc = [0] * nc
    sc.bcaps = [0] * (nc * ns)
    sc.seen = [0] * nc

fn _assert(kind: int, s: str, pos: int) bool:
    n = len(s)
    if kind == A_BOT:
        return pos == 0
    if kind == A_EOT:
        return pos == n
    if kind == A_BOL:
        return pos == 0 or s.byte(pos - 1) == 10
    if kind == A_EOL:
        return pos == n or s.byte(pos) == 10
    a = pos > 0 and is_word(s.byte(pos - 1))
    b = pos < n and is_word(s.byte(pos))
    return a != b if kind == A_WORD else a == b

fn _char_ok(p: Prog, pc: int, cp: int) bool:
    op = p.code.op[pc]
    if op == I_CHAR:
        return (lower(cp) if p.code.fold[pc] else cp) == p.code.x[pc]
    if op == I_ANY:
        return cp != 10
    if op == I_ANYNL:
        return true
    return class_has(p.classes[p.code.x[pc]], cp)

# _char_ok for instruction op at pc, with ASCII classes inline (the backtracker's hot path)
fn _cok(p: Prog, op: int, pc: int, cp: int) bool:
    if op == I_ANY:
        return cp != 10
    if op == I_CLASS:
        ci = p.code.x[pc]
        if cp < 64:
            return (((p.classes[ci].ascii0 >> cp) & 1) != 0) != p.classes[ci].neg
        if cp < 128:
            return (((p.classes[ci].ascii1 >> (cp - 64)) & 1) != 0) != p.classes[ci].neg
        return class_has(p.classes[ci], cp)
    if op == I_CHAR:
        return (lower(cp) if p.code.fold[pc] else cp) == p.code.x[pc]
    return true

# add the thread at pc (and everything it reaches without reading a character) to list b
# (into_b) or a; caps (the thread's slots) is scratch, restored on the way back
fn _addthread(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, into_b: bool, pc0: int, ns: int, s: str, pos: int):
    st = [pc0, -1]
    while len(st) > 0:
        b = st.pop()
        a = st.pop()
        if b >= 0:                                    # restore a capture slot
            sc.caps[a] = b
            continue
        if b == -2:                                   # (restore to "unset")
            sc.caps[a] = -1
            continue
        pc = a
        if sc.seen[pc] == sc.stamp:
            continue
        sc.seen[pc] = sc.stamp
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_JMP:
            st.push(p.code.x[pc])
            st.push(-1)
        elif op == I_SPLIT:
            st.push(p.code.y[pc])
            st.push(-1)
            st.push(p.code.x[pc])
            st.push(-1)
        elif op == I_SAVE:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x < ns:
                old = sc.caps[x]
                st.push(x)
                st.push(old if old >= 0 else -2)
                sc.caps[x] = pos
            st.push(pc + 1)
            st.push(-1)
        elif op == I_ASSERT:
            if _assert(p.code.x[pc], s, pos):
                st.push(pc + 1)
                st.push(-1)
        elif into_b:
            sc.bpc[sc.bn] = pc
            for k in 0..ns:
                sc.bcaps[sc.bn * ns + k] = sc.caps[k]
            sc.bn += 1
        else:
            sc.apc[sc.an] = pc
            for k in 0..ns:
                sc.acaps[sc.an * ns + k] = sc.caps[k]
            sc.an += 1

fn _swap(sc: mut Scratch):
    t = sc.apc
    sc.apc = sc.bpc
    sc.bpc = t
    tc = sc.acaps
    sc.acaps = sc.bcaps
    sc.bcaps = tc
    sc.an = sc.bn
    sc.bn = 0

# mode 0: the leftmost-first match at or after `at` (its slots in sc.best); 1: the same but
# only one that starts at `at` and ends at the end of the text (full); 2: just whether one
# exists; 3: only one that starts at `at`
fn run_vm(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, s: str, at: int, mode: int, ns: int) bool:
    if len(sc.seen) == 0:
        _vm_scratch(p, &sc)
    n = len(s)
    sc.an = 0
    sc.bn = 0
    matched = false
    only_start = mode == 1 or mode == 3 or p.anchored
    sc.stamp += 1
    pos = at
    while true:
        if not matched and (pos == at or not only_start):
            if sc.an == 0 and not only_start:         # nothing running: skip to a possible start
                if len(p.prefix) > 1 or (len(p.prefix) == 1 and p.has_first):
                    f = s.find_from(p.prefix, pos) if pos < n else -1
                    if f < 0:
                        return false
                    pos = f
                elif p.has_first:
                    while pos < n and not p.first[s.byte(pos)]:
                        pos += 1
                    if pos >= n:
                        return false
            if sc.an == 0:
                sc.stamp += 1
            for k in 0..ns:
                sc.caps[k] = -1
            _addthread(p, &sc, false, 0, ns, s, pos)
        if sc.an == 0:                                # nothing can match from here: the next start
            if matched or only_start or pos >= n:
                break
            pos += decode(s, pos).1
            continue
        cp = -1
        w = 0
        if pos < n:
            d = decode(s, pos)
            cp = d.0
            w = d.1
        sc.stamp += 1
        sc.bn = 0
        i = 0
        while i < sc.an:
            pc = sc.apc[i]
            op = p.code.op[pc]
            if op == I_MATCH:
                if mode == 1 and pos != n:
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if mode == 2:
                    return true
                for k in 0..ns:
                    sc.best[k] = sc.acaps[i * ns + k]
                matched = true
                break                                 # lower-priority threads lose
            if cp >= 0 and _char_ok(p, pc, cp):
                for k in 0..ns:
                    sc.caps[k] = sc.acaps[i * ns + k]
                _addthread(p, &sc, true, pc + 1, ns, s, pos + w)
            i += 1
        _swap(&sc)
        if pos >= n:                                  # (MATCHes at the end were seen this round)
            break
        pos += w
        if sc.an == 0 and (matched or only_start):
            break
    return matched

const BT_MAX_BITS = 256 * 1024

# (apart: the backtracker's stack doubles, rarely)
fn _more_jobs(js: mut [int]):
    n = [0] * (len(js) * 2 + 48)
    for i, x in js:
        n[i] = x
    js = n

# groups for a match known to span s[st..e), depth first in priority order (e: the end of
# the text when the match's end isn't known: the first MATCH reached is the match). Leaves in
# sc.reach how far it read: every text that starts with s[..reach] (and runs past it) gets
# the same answer; e + 1 when where the text ends mattered.
fn _backtrack(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, s: str, st: int, e: int, ns: int, out: mut [int]) bool:
    width = e - st + 1
    words = (len(p.code.op) * width + 63) / 64
    if len(sc.btseen) < words:
        sc.btseen = [0] * words
    else:
        for k in 0..words:
            sc.btseen[k] = 0
    for k in 0..ns:
        sc.caps[k] = -1
    # jobs: (pc, pos, -1): explore; (slot, value, -2): restore; kept in sc, `top` long
    if len(sc.jobs) < 3 * width + 48:                # (a job a position is the usual most)
        sc.jobs = [0] * (3 * width + 48)
    sc.jobs[0] = 0
    sc.jobs[1] = st
    sc.jobs[2] = -1
    top = 3
    reach = st
    while top > 0:
        top -= 3
        a = sc.jobs[top]
        b = sc.jobs[top + 1]
        kind = sc.jobs[top + 2]
        if kind == -2:
            sc.caps[a] = b
            continue
        pc = a
        pos = b
        while true:
            bit = pc * width + (pos - st)
            if ((sc.btseen[bit >> 6] >> (bit & 63)) & 1) != 0:
                break
            sc.btseen[bit >> 6] |= 1 << (bit & 63)
            op = p.code.op[pc]
            if op <= I_CLASS:                         # CHAR ANY ANYNL CLASS
                if pos >= e:
                    reach = e + 1
                    break
                cp = s.byte(pos)
                w = 1
                if pos >= reach:
                    reach = pos + 1
                if cp < 64:                           # (ASCII: the instruction's bits)
                    if ((p.am0[pc] >> cp) & 1) == 0:
                        break
                elif cp < 0x80:
                    if ((p.am1[pc] >> (cp - 64)) & 1) == 0:
                        break
                else:
                    reach = max(reach, e + 1 if pos + 4 > e else pos + 4)    # (decode reads up to 4)
                    d = decode(s, pos)
                    cp = d.0
                    w = d.1
                    if pos + w > e or not (p.ahi[pc] or _cok(p, op, pc, cp)):
                        break
                pc += 1
                pos += w
                continue
            if op == I_SPLIT:
                bpc = p.code.x[pc]
                bop = p.code.op[bpc]
                if bop <= I_CLASS and (bpc == pc - 1 or (bpc == pc + 1 and p.code.op[pc + 2] == I_JMP and p.code.x[pc + 2] == pc)):
                    # a greedy loop over one character (k+: k; SPLIT k,out. k*: SPLIT k,out; k;
                    # JMP): run it here, a job (leave the loop) and a visited bit at each
                    # position, not three instructions' worth. (The body and the JMP are only
                    # reached through this SPLIT, so they needn't be marked.)
                    # (possessive, when what follows the loop can't start with a character the
                    # loop takes: leaving it early can't match, so only its end is tried)
                    out_pc = p.code.y[pc]
                    poss = p.poss[pc]
                    last = pos
                    while true:
                        last = pos
                        if not poss:
                            if top + 3 > len(sc.jobs):
                                _more_jobs(&sc.jobs)
                            sc.jobs[top] = out_pc
                            sc.jobs[top + 1] = pos
                            sc.jobs[top + 2] = -1
                            top += 3
                        if pos >= e:
                            reach = e + 1
                            break
                        cp = s.byte(pos)
                        w = 1
                        if pos >= reach:
                            reach = pos + 1
                        if cp < 64:
                            if ((p.am0[bpc] >> cp) & 1) == 0:
                                break
                        elif cp < 0x80:
                            if ((p.am1[bpc] >> (cp - 64)) & 1) == 0:
                                break
                        else:
                            reach = max(reach, e + 1 if pos + 4 > e else pos + 4)
                            d = decode(s, pos)
                            cp = d.0
                            w = d.1
                            if pos + w > e or not (p.ahi[bpc] or _cok(p, bop, bpc, cp)):
                                break
                        pos += w
                        bit = pc * width + (pos - st)
                        if ((sc.btseen[bit >> 6] >> (bit & 63)) & 1) != 0:
                            break
                        sc.btseen[bit >> 6] |= 1 << (bit & 63)
                    if poss:
                        pc = out_pc
                        pos = last
                        continue
                    break
                if top + 3 > len(sc.jobs):
                    _more_jobs(&sc.jobs)
                sc.jobs[top] = p.code.y[pc]
                sc.jobs[top + 1] = pos
                sc.jobs[top + 2] = -1
                top += 3
                pc = p.code.x[pc]
                continue
            if op == I_JMP:
                pc = p.code.x[pc]
                continue
            if op == I_SAVE:
                x = p.code.x[pc]
                if x < ns:
                    if top + 3 > len(sc.jobs):
                        _more_jobs(&sc.jobs)
                    sc.jobs[top] = x
                    sc.jobs[top + 1] = sc.caps[x]
                    sc.jobs[top + 2] = -2
                    top += 3
                    sc.caps[x] = pos
                pc += 1
                continue
            if op == I_ASSERT:
                # (an assertion reads the bytes around pos, or that the text ends at pos)
                reach = max(reach, e + 1 if pos >= e else pos + 1)
                if not _assert(p.code.x[pc], s, pos):
                    break
                pc += 1
                continue
            for k in 0..ns:                           # MATCH: the first reached wins
                out[k] = sc.caps[k]
            sc.reach = reach
            return true
    sc.reach = reach
    return false

# groups for a match known to span s[st..e) when the program is one-pass; false: it didn't
# get there (the caller falls back to the backtracker)
fn _onepass(p: Prog, s: str, st: int, e: int, ns: int, out: mut [int]) bool:
    if len(p.fixoff) > 0:
        if e - st != p.fixlen:
            return false
        for k in 0..ns:
            out[k] = -1 if p.fixoff[k] < 0 else st + p.fixoff[k]
        return true
    for k in 0..ns:
        out[k] = -1
    pc = 0
    idle = 0                                          # steps since the last character
    pos = st
    n = len(s)
    nc = len(p.code.op)
    while true:
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_SAVE:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x < ns:
                out[x] = pos
            pc += 1
        elif op == I_JMP:
            pc = p.code.x[pc]
        elif op == I_SPLIT:
            b = s.byte(pos) if pos < e else 256
            tk2 = (p.onepass[5 * pc + (b >> 6)] >> (b & 63)) & 1
            pc = p.code.x[pc] if tk2 != 0 else p.code.y[pc]
        elif op == I_ASSERT:
            if not _assert(p.code.x[pc], s, pos):
                return false
            pc += 1
        elif op == I_MATCH:
            return pos == e
        else:
            if pos >= e:
                return false
            c = s.byte(pos)
            cp = c
            w = 1
            if c >= 0x80:
                d = decode(s, pos)
                cp = d.0
                w = d.1
            if pos + w > e or not _char_ok(p, pc, cp):
                return false
            pc += 1
            pos += w
            idle = -1
        idle += 1
        if idle > nc:                                 # (a loop that reads nothing)
            return false
    return false

# the groups of a match known to span s[st..e): one walk if the program is one-pass, else the
# backtracker if the match is short, else the VM
fn groups(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, s: str, st: int, e: int, ns: int, out: mut [int]) bool:
    if len(p.onepass) > 0 and _onepass(p, s, st, e, ns, &out):
        return true
    if len(p.code.op) * (e - st + 1) <= BT_MAX_BITS:
        if _backtrack(p, &sc, s, st, e, ns, &out):
            return true
    if run_vm(p, &sc, s, st, 3, ns):
        for k in 0..ns:
            out[k] = sc.best[k]
        return true
    return false
```

## library/std/simd.tn

```tern
# simd: 16 bytes worked on at once. A bytes16 is a value like an int (no allocation), and
# each operation is one instruction on ARM (NEON), x86 (SSE2/SSSE3) and wasm (SIMD128), or a
# short loop elsewhere: for scanning text, parsing, checksums, byte tables.
#
#   import simd
#   v = simd.load(s, i)            # bytes16: s[i..i+16] (a runtime error past the end)
#   simd.of(t) bytes16             # a 16-byte string as a bytes16 (a table for lookup)
#   simd.splat(b) bytes16          # every lane b (0 to 255)
#   simd.to_str(v) str             # the 16 bytes as a string
#   a & b, a | b, a ^ b, ~a        # lane by lane
#   a + b, a - b                   # lane by lane, wrapping (250 + 10 is 4)
#   a << n, a >> n                 # every lane shifted by n (0 to 7), zeros shifted in
#   a == b, a != b                 # all 16 lanes equal (bool)
#   simd.eq(a, b) bytes16          # 255 in the lanes where a == b, else 0
#   simd.lt(a, b), simd.le(a, b)   # ... where a < b / a <= b (as bytes: 0 to 255)
#   simd.min(a, b), simd.max(a, b) # lane by lane
#   simd.lookup(t, i) bytes16      # lane k is t's lane i[k] (0 if i[k] >= 16): a table lookup
#   simd.bits(v) int               # bit k set when lane k isn't 0 (16 bits)
#   simd.any(v) bool               # a lane isn't 0
#   simd.first_lane(v) int         # the first lane that isn't 0 (16 if none): cheaper than bits
#   simd.lane(v, k) int            # lane k (0 to 15)
#   simd.popcount(v) bytes16       # lane k is the number of bits set in lane k (0 to 8)
#   simd.sum(v) int                # the 16 lanes added up
#   simd.first(m) int              # the lowest set bit of m (64 if none): a bits mask's first lane
#
# f32x4: four f32s at once, a value like a bytes16 (dot products and distances over [f32]):
#   simd.load_f32(xs, i) f32x4     # xs[i..i+4] of an [f32]   simd.store_f32(&xs, i, v)
#   simd.splat_f32(x) f32x4        # every lane x             simd.f32x4(a, b, c, d) f32x4
#   a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b, -a # lane by lane (b may be an f32: every lane)
#   a == b, a != b                 # all four lanes equal (bool)
#   simd.fma(a, b, c) f32x4        # a * b + c, rounded once
#   simd.sum_f32(v) f32            # the four lanes added up
#   simd.min_f32(a, b), simd.max_f32(a, b), simd.abs_f32(v), simd.sqrt_f32(v)   # lane by lane
#   simd.lane_f32(v, k) f32        # lane k (0 to 3)
#
# Finding the first digit, 16 bytes a step:
#
#   fn first_digit(s: str) int:
#       zero = simd.splat(48)
#       nine = simd.splat(9)
#       i = 0
#       while i + 16 <= len(s):
#           k = simd.first_lane(simd.le(simd.load(s, i) - zero, nine))   # '0'..'9': 0..9 after - '0'
#           if k < 16:
#               return i + k
#           i += 16
#       ...                                                         # the last few bytes one at a time
```

## library/std/task.tn

```tern
# task: tasks (green threads), channels, and shared values. Like Go's goroutines, or
# tokio without async/await: code in a task looks blocking, but only the task waits.
#
#   import task
#   h = task.spawn(fn() fetch(url))      # h: task[str]; runs on any core
#   body = h.join()                      # waits; a runtime error in the task is raised here
#
#   ch: chan[int] = task.channel(100)    # holds up to 100 values (0: unbounded)
#   task.spawn(fn() produce(ch))
#   for x in ch:                         # until the channel is closed and empty
#       print(x)
#
#   hits = task.shared(0)                # shared[int]: one value many tasks change
#   fn bump(n: mut int):
#       n += 1
#   hits.update(bump)                    # runs under a lock; tasks (not threads) wait for it
#   print(hits.get())                    # a snapshot (O(1): values are copy-on-write)
#
# Channels:  ch.send(v)  ch.recv()  ch.next(&x) bool (false: closed)  ch.try_recv(&x) bool
#            ch.recv_timeout(&x, ms) bool  ch.close()  len(ch)
#            task.select(chans, &x, ms) int: receive from whichever of chans ([chan[T]]) has a
#            value first; returns its index, -1 after ms milliseconds (ms < 0: no limit), -2
#            when all are closed and empty. Like Go's select / tokio's select!.
# Tasks:     task.spawn(f) task[T]  h.join() T  h.done() bool  h.cancel()
#            task.sleep(ms)  task.yield_now()      (time.sleep(ms) also parks just the task)
#            task.blocking(f) T: run f (fn() T) on a pool of extra threads and wait for it;
#            for work that would stall this core (fsync, SQLite, big files), like tokio's
#            spawn_blocking. Only the calling task waits.
# Groups:    task.all(fs) [T]   task.try_all(fs) Result[[T], E]   task.try_all_limit(fs, n): run the
#            functions at once, results in order; the first Err cancels the rest (Go's errgroup;
#            see the end of this file)
# Shared:    task.shared(v) shared[T]  s.get() T  s.set(v)  s.update(f) (f: fn(mut T) R, returns R)
#            task.atomic(v) Atomic: a.load() a.store(v) a.add(n) int a.cas(old, new) bool
#            task.shared_map() SharedMap: m.put(k, v) m.get_or(k, default) str m.has(k) m.remove(k)
#              m.count() m.add_int(k, n) int m.get_int(k) int
#            (counters and caches without a task lock: far faster than shared under contention)
# Locals:    task.local_set(key, value)  task.local_get(key) str ("" if unset)  task.local_clear():
#            strings that belong to the running task (request ids, tracing context); a spawned
#            task starts with a copy of its spawner's, and they're freed with the task. Outside
#            tasks there's one set per thread.
# Id:        task.id() int: the running task's (0 outside tasks)
#            task.thread_slot() int: the running thread's slot in the scheduler (0 ... cores),
#            for a cache per thread that no other thread contends for
#            task.workers() int: the scheduler's threads (how many `parallel` iterations run
#            at once), for sizing batches of work
#
# Copying a chan / task / shared value shares it (they're handles). Values sent through
# a channel are copied (copy-on-write, so O(1)). One worker per core (TERN_ASYNC_THREADS
# to change); a task stays on the core that first runs it. Tasks share their core's
# 64MB stack, and a waiting task's frames are copied aside (usually well under 1KB), so
# deep recursion works in any task and a million waiting tasks are fine.
# Code inside `parallel:` may use channels; there it waits like a thread.
# Not available on wasm.

fn local_set(key: str, value: str):
    _local_set(key, value)

fn local_get(key: str) str:
    return _local_get(key)

fn local_clear():
    _local_clear()

# The running task's id: the same number for as long as the task runs (0 outside tasks).
# For keeping things per task, like the connection a task's database transaction is on.
fn id() int:
    return _id()

# The running thread's slot in the scheduler: a small number (0 ... cores) no other thread
# running at the same time has (threads outside the scheduler share 0). For keeping a cache
# per thread, as re does with its DFA states. A task may move to another thread when it
# waits, so read it again after a wait.
fn thread_slot() int:
    return _wid()

# The threads the scheduler runs tasks on (TERN_THREADS, or the cores this process may use):
# how many `parallel` iterations run at once. For sizing work batches to the machine.
fn workers() int:
    return _workers()

# ---- groups (like Go's errgroup)
#   task.all(fs) [T]                     run every f (fn() T) at once; their results in order.
#                                        A runtime error in one is raised here.
#   task.try_all(fs) Result[[T], E]      every f (fn() Result[T, E]) at once: Ok with the values in
#                                        order, or the first Err to arrive; the ones still
#                                        running are cancelled
#   task.try_all_limit(fs, n) Result[[T], E]     the same, at most n running at a time
#
#   pages = task.try_all([fn() fetch(a), fn() fetch(b), fn() fetch(c)])?

fn all[T](fs: [fn() T]) [T]:
    hs: [task[T]] = []
    for f in fs:
        hs.push(spawn(f))
    out: [T] = []
    for h in hs:
        out.push(h.join())
    return out

fn try_all[T, E](fs: [fn() Result[T, E]]) Result[[T], E]:
    return try_all_limit(fs, 0)

struct _Done[T, E]:
    i: int
    r: Option[Result[T, E]]

fn _run_one[T, E](ch: chan[_Done[T, E]], i: int, f: fn() Result[T, E]) int:
    ch.send(_Done(i, Some(f())))
    return i

fn try_all_limit[T, E](fs: [fn() Result[T, E]], limit: int) Result[[T], E]:
    n = len(fs)
    ch: chan[_Done[T, E]] = channel(0)
    hs: [task[int]] = []
    vals: [Option[T]] = []
    for k in 0..n:
        vals.push(None)
    started = 0
    got = 0
    while got < n:
        while started < n and (limit <= 0 or started - got < limit):
            i = started
            f = fs[i]
            hs.push(spawn(fn() _run_one(ch, i, f)))
            started += 1
        none: Option[Result[T, E]] = None
        d = _Done(0, none)
        if not ch.recv_timeout(&d, 10):
            for h in hs:                           # one that failed never sends: raise its error
                if h.done():
                    h.join()
            continue
        got += 1
        match d.r.unwrap():
            Ok(v):
                vals[d.i] = Some(v)
            Err(e):
                for h in hs:
                    if h.done():
                        h.join()
                    else:
                        h.cancel()
                while ch.try_recv(&d):             # (results that arrived meanwhile)
                    pass
                return Err(e)
    out: [T] = []
    for v in vals:
        out.push(v.unwrap())
    return Ok(out)

# ---- shared state without task locks (runtime/cells.h)
# shared[T] takes a lock that parks tasks on every get / update: right for a value that
# changes as a whole, slow for a counter or a cache that every request touches. These don't:
#   a = task.atomic(0)          task.Atomic: an int changed by atomic instructions
#   a.load() int   a.store(v)   a.add(n) int (the new value)   a.cas(old, new) bool (store if it was old)
#   m = task.shared_map()       task.SharedMap: str -> str, safe from any task or thread
#   m.put(k, v)   m.get_or(k, default) str   m.has(k) bool   m.remove(k) bool   m.count() int
#   m.add_int(k, n) int   m.get_int(k) int   a per-key int, for counting (0 until added to)
# Copies share the same one (like channels), and the last copy gone frees it: a cache may start
# again with a fresh map.

struct Atomic:
    _h: shared[int]

fn atomic(v: int) Atomic:
    return Atomic(_atomic_new(v))

fn load(a: Atomic) int:
    return _atomic_get(a._h)

fn store(a: Atomic, v: int):
    _atomic_set(a._h, v)

fn add(a: Atomic, n: int) int:
    return _atomic_add(a._h, n)

fn cas(a: Atomic, old: int, v: int) bool:
    return _atomic_cas(a._h, old, v)

struct SharedMap:
    _h: shared[int]

fn shared_map() SharedMap:
    return SharedMap(_smap_new())

fn put(m: SharedMap, k: str, v: str):
    _smap_put(m._h, k, v)

fn get_or(m: SharedMap, k: str, dflt: str) str:
    return _smap_get_or(m._h, k, dflt)

fn has(m: SharedMap, k: str) bool:
    return _smap_has(m._h, k)

fn remove(m: SharedMap, k: str) bool:
    return _smap_remove(m._h, k)

fn count(m: SharedMap) int:
    return _smap_len(m._h)

fn add_int(m: SharedMap, k: str, n: int) int:
    return _smap_add(m._h, k, n)

fn get_int(m: SharedMap, k: str) int:
    return _smap_get_int(m._h, k)
```

## library/std/term.tn

```tern
# term: the terminal: whether output goes to one, its size, colors that switch themselves off
# when they shouldn't show, aligned tables, a progress line, and reading a password.
#
#   import term
#   print(term.green("ok"), term.bold("3 files"))     # plain text when piped, NO_COLOR, ...
#   print(term.table([["NAME", "SIZE"], ["a.txt", "12"], ["notes.md", "3401"]]))
#   for i in 0..n:
#       term.progress(i + 1, n, "copying")             # one line on stderr, redrawn
#   pw = term.secret("password: ")                     # typed without echo
#
#   term.is_tty() bool          stdout is a terminal (stderr_is_tty, stdin_is_tty for the others)
#   term.width() int  term.height() int   the terminal's size ($COLUMNS / $LINES, else 80 x 24)
#   term.color() bool           whether the color functions add color: stdout is a terminal,
#                               NO_COLOR is unset and TERM isn't "dumb" (FORCE_COLOR=1 forces it)
#   term.set_color(on bool)     decide it yourself (a --color flag)
#   term.red(s) green yellow blue magenta cyan gray  bold dim italic underline  (s str) str
#   term.strip_ansi(s) str      s without escape sequences (colors, cursor moves, links)
#   term.display_width(s) int   the columns s takes: escapes take none, a character one
#   term.pad(s, width) str      s and spaces to width columns (escape sequences don't count)
#   term.table(rows [[str]]) str   columns lined up, two spaces apart, a line per row
#   term.progress(done, total, label)   "label [#####-----]  50% 5/10" on stderr, redrawn in
#                               place; a line end once done == total; nothing if stderr isn't
#                               a terminal
#   term.clear_line() str       goes to the start of the line and clears it ("\r\x1b[2K")
#   term.secret(prompt) str     prompt on stderr, then a line from stdin without echoing it
#   term.read_line(prompt) str  prompt on stderr, then a line from stdin with its "\n" ("" at the
#                               end of input), like os.read_line; on a terminal it can be edited
#                               (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl-A/E/K/U/W) and Up/Down bring back the lines
#                               read before. Ctrl-C returns "\x03"

import os

fn is_tty() bool:
    return _isatty(1)

fn stderr_is_tty() bool:
    return _isatty(2)

fn stdin_is_tty() bool:
    return _isatty(0)

fn width() int:
    s = _size()
    if s > 0:
        return s & 0xffff
    return max(os.env("COLUMNS", "").to_int(80), 1)

fn height() int:
    s = _size()
    if s > 0 and s >> 16 > 0:
        return s >> 16
    return max(os.env("LINES", "").to_int(24), 1)

fn color() bool:
    return _color_on()

fn _paint(s: str, code: str) str:
    if not _color_on():
        return s
    return "\x1b[" + code + "m" + s + "\x1b[0m"

fn red(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "31")

fn green(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "32")

fn yellow(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "33")

fn blue(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "34")

fn magenta(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "35")

fn cyan(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "36")

fn gray(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "90")

fn bold(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "1")

fn dim(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "2")

fn italic(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "3")

fn underline(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "4")

fn clear_line() str:
    return "\r\x1b[2K"

# columns: escape sequences take none, and each character (not byte) one
fn display_width(s: str) int:
    t = strip_ansi(s)
    n = 0
    for i in 0..len(t):
        if t.byte(i) & 0xc0 != 0x80:
            n += 1
    return n

fn pad(s: str, width: int) str:
    w = display_width(s)
    if w >= width:
        return s
    return s + " ".repeat(width - w)

fn table(rows: [[str]]) str:
    widths: [int] = []
    for row in rows:
        for k, cell in row:
            w = display_width(cell)
            if k >= len(widths):
                widths.push(w)
            elif w > widths[k]:
                widths[k] = w
    out = ""
    for row in rows:
        line = ""
        for k, cell in row:
            if k == len(row) - 1:
                line += cell
            else:
                line += pad(cell, widths[k]) + "  "
        e = len(line)
        while e > 0 and line.byte(e - 1) == 32:
            e -= 1
        out += line[..e] + "\n"
    return out

fn progress(done: int, total: int, label: str):
    if not _isatty(2):
        return
    t = max(total, 1)
    d = min(max(done, 0), t)
    bar = 30
    fill = d * bar / t
    pct = str(d * 100 / t)
    line = f"\r\x1b[2K{label} [" + "#".repeat(fill) + "-".repeat(bar - fill) + "] " + " ".repeat(3 - len(pct)) + f"{pct}% {d}/{t}"
    if d == t:
        line += "\n"
    _ewrite(line)

fn secret(prompt: str) str:
    return _secret(prompt)

fn read_line(prompt: str) str:
    return _read_line(prompt)
```

## library/std/testing.tn

```tern
# testing: checks for `tern test` (see docs/cli.md, "Testing").
#
#   import testing
#   fn test_add():
#       testing.eq_int(add(2, 2), 4)
#
# Each check that fails prints `FAIL: <what> <details>` and ends the test (exit
# status 1); `tern test` reports it with the test's output. A runtime error fails a test too.
#
#   testing.eq_int(got: int, want: int)         testing.eq_str(got: str, want: str)
#   testing.eq_float(got: float, want: float)   testing.eq_bool(got: bool, want: bool)
#   testing.near(got: float, want: float, tolerance: float)
#   testing.eq_ints(got: [int], want: [int])    testing.eq_strs(got: [str], want: [str])
#   testing.is_true(cond: bool, what: str)      testing.is_false(cond: bool, what: str)
#   testing.includes(s: str, sub: str)
#   testing.fail(msg: str)                      (always fails)
import os

fn fail(msg: str):
    print("FAIL: " + msg)
    os.exit(1)

fn eq_int(got: int, want: int):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_int: got {got}, want {want}")

fn eq_str(got: str, want: str):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_str: got {json_quote(got)}, want {json_quote(want)}")

fn eq_float(got: float, want: float):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_float: got {got}, want {want}")

fn near(got: float, want: float, tolerance: float):
    if abs(got - want) > tolerance:
        fail(f"near: got {got}, want {want} (within {tolerance})")

fn eq_bool(got: bool, want: bool):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_bool: got {got}, want {want}")

fn eq_ints(got: [int], want: [int]):
    if len(got) != len(want):
        fail(f"eq_ints: got {len(got)} values, want {len(want)}")
    for i, g in got:
        if g != want[i]:
            fail(f"eq_ints: [{i}] is {g}, want {want[i]}")

fn eq_strs(got: [str], want: [str]):
    if len(got) != len(want):
        fail(f"eq_strs: got {len(got)} values, want {len(want)}")
    for i, g in got:
        if g != want[i]:
            fail(f"eq_strs: [{i}] is {json_quote(g)}, want {json_quote(want[i])}")

fn is_true(cond: bool, what: str):
    if not cond:
        fail(f"is_true: {what}")

fn is_false(cond: bool, what: str):
    if cond:
        fail(f"is_false: {what}")

fn includes(s: str, sub: str):
    if not s.contains(sub):
        fail(f"includes: {json_quote(s)} doesn't contain {json_quote(sub)}")
```

## library/std/time.tn

```tern
# time: clocks, sleeping, formatting and parsing, calendar fields, durations.
# A time is a float: seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch), like time.now().
#
#   time.now() float                  wall clock        time.now_ms() int
#   time.mono_ns() int  time.mono_ms() int     a monotonic clock for measuring intervals
#                                     (never jumps when the wall clock is set)
#   time.sleep(ms)                    (in a task, only the task waits)
#
#   time.rfc3339(t) str               "2026-09-28T06:45:12Z" ("...12.345Z" when t has milliseconds)
#   time.rfc3339_local(t) str         "2026-09-28T08:45:12+02:00" (the system's time zone)
#   time.parse_rfc3339(s) float       accepts Z or +hh:mm offsets and any fraction of a second
#   time.format(t, layout) str        strftime layouts in UTC: "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", plus %L
#   time.format_local(t, layout) str  (milliseconds) and %f (microseconds)
#   time.parse(s, layout) float       strptime layouts, read as UTC   time.parse_local(s, layout) float
#   time.error() str                  why the last parse failed ("" after a success; a failed
#                                     parse returns 0.0)
#
#   time.utc(t) Date   time.local(t) Date    calendar fields (see struct Date)
#   time.date(year, month, day, hour, minute, second) float     a UTC time from fields
#                                     (months and days out of range carry over, like timegm)
#   time.offset(t) int                the local zone's offset from UTC at t, in seconds
#
#   time.duration(seconds float) str  "1h2m3.5s", "250ms", "12us" (Go's style)
#   time.parse_duration(s) float      "1h30m", "2.5s", "300ms", "-1m", "7d", "2w" -> seconds
#
#   start = time.mono_ns()
#   work()
#   print("took", time.duration(float(time.mono_ns() - start) / 1e9))
#   d = time.utc(time.parse_rfc3339("2026-02-28T23:30:00-05:00"))    # d.day == 1, d.month == 3

struct Date:
    year: int
    month: int                  # 1..12
    day: int                    # 1..31
    hour: int
    minute: int
    second: int
    nano: int                   # nanoseconds within the second
    weekday: int                # 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday
    yday: int                   # 1..366
    offset: int                 # seconds east of UTC (0 for utc())

fn utc(t: float) Date:
    return _fields(t, false)

fn local(t: float) Date:
    return _fields(t, true)

# with Result: t = time.try_parse_rfc3339(s)?   (Err: "time: not an RFC 3339 time: ...")
fn try_parse_rfc3339(s: str) Result[float, str]:
    t = parse_rfc3339(s)
    if error() != "":
        return Err("time: " + error())
    return Ok(t)

fn try_parse(s: str, layout: str) Result[float, str]:
    t = parse(s, layout)
    if error() != "":
        return Err("time: " + error())
    return Ok(t)

fn try_parse_duration(s: str) Result[float, str]:
    d = parse_duration(s)
    if error() != "":
        return Err("time: " + error())
    return Ok(d)
```

## library/std/tls.tn

```tern
# tls: encrypted connections (TLS 1.2 / 1.3, aws-lc linked statically into programs that
# import tls, built once per target by tern; nothing is linked otherwise; TERN_TLS=system
# uses the system's OpenSSL). Importing tls also turns on https:// in
# http.get / http.fetch and HTTPS serving (http.listen_tls, roost.serve_tls).
#
#   import net
#   import tls
#   c = tls.connect("example.com", 443)       # verifies the certificate and the host name
#   if not c.ok():
#       print(tls.error())                    # e.g. "tls handshake: certificate verify failed: ..."
#   c.write("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
#   print(c.read_line())                      # every net function works on a TLS connection
#
# The result is an ordinary net.Conn: c.read / read_line / read_exact / write / close all
# encrypt and decrypt. Reads and handshakes wait like any socket wait (only the task).
#
#   tls.connect(host str, port int) net.Conn          check c.ok(); tls.error() says why not
#   tls.connect_insecure(host str, port int) net.Conn  no certificate check (tests, self-signed)
#   tls.upgrade(c net.Conn, host str) bool              start TLS on a connected socket (STARTTLS,
#                                                       PostgreSQL's SSLRequest); false: see error()
#   tls.server(cert str, key str) Server                a certificate chain and key (PEM files);
#                                                       a runtime error if they can't be loaded
#   tls.accept(c net.Conn, s Server) bool               the server side of the handshake
#   tls.version(c net.Conn) str                         "TLSv1.3" ("" for a plain connection)
#   tls.trust(ca_file str) bool                         also trust the CAs in this PEM file, for
#                                                       every verified connection (a private CA)
#   tls.error() str                                     why the last connect / upgrade / accept failed
#
# ALPN (which protocol the connection speaks, agreed in the handshake: "h2" for HTTP/2 and gRPC,
# "http/1.1"):
#   tls.set_alpn(s Server, protocols [str])             the protocols s speaks, preferred first; a
#                                                       client offering only others fails the
#                                                       handshake; one offering none gets none
#   tls.connect_alpn(host str, port int, protocols [str]) net.Conn   connect (verified), offering these
#   tls.alpn(c net.Conn) str                            the protocol agreed ("" if none, or plain)
#
# Certificates are checked against $SSL_CERT_FILE / $SSL_CERT_DIR if set, else the system's
# CA bundle (/etc/ssl/cert.pem on macOS; /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt and the like on
# Linux). Not available on wasm.

import net

struct Server:
    ctx: int

fn upgrade(c: net.Conn, host: str) bool:
    return _client(c.fd, host, true, 30000)

fn _connect(host: str, port: int, verify: bool) net.Conn:
    c = net.connect(host, port)
    if c.ok() and not _client(c.fd, host, verify, 30000):
        c.close()
        return net.Conn(-1)
    return c

fn connect(host: str, port: int) net.Conn:
    return _connect(host, port, true)

fn connect_insecure(host: str, port: int) net.Conn:
    return _connect(host, port, false)

fn server(cert: str, key: str) Server:
    return Server(_server_ctx(cert, key))

fn accept(c: net.Conn, s: Server) bool:
    return _accept(c.fd, s.ctx, 10000)

fn version(c: net.Conn) str:
    return _version(c.fd)

# ALPN's wire form: each name after its length (names of 1 to 255 bytes; others are skipped)
fn _alpn_list(protocols: [str]) str:
    out = ""
    for p in protocols:
        if len(p) > 0 and len(p) < 256:
            out += chr(len(p)) + p
    return out

fn set_alpn(s: Server, protocols: [str]):
    _alpn_server(s.ctx, _alpn_list(protocols))

fn connect_alpn(host: str, port: int, protocols: [str]) net.Conn:
    c = net.connect(host, port)
    if c.ok() and not _client_alpn(c.fd, host, true, 30000, _alpn_list(protocols)):
        c.close()
        return net.Conn(-1)
    return c

fn alpn(c: net.Conn) str:
    return _alpn(c.fd)

fn error() str:
    return net.error()

# with Result: c = tls.dial("example.com", 443)?
#   (Err: "tls: handshake: certificate verify failed: hostname mismatch")
fn dial(host: str, port: int) Result[net.Conn, str]:
    c = connect(host, port)
    if not c.ok():
        why = error()
        if why.starts_with("tls "):
            why = why[4..]
        return Err("tls: " + why)
    return Ok(c)
```

## library/std/toml.tn

```tern
# toml: TOML 1.0 (config files) into a struct or a json.Value, and structs back to TOML.
#
#   import toml
#   struct Server:
#       host: str
#       port: int
#   struct Config:
#       name: str
#       server: Server
#       tags: [str]
#   cfg = Config("app", Server("localhost", 8080), [])    # defaults: keys the file leaves out keep them
#   toml.decode(fs.read("app.toml"), &cfg)?               # Err("toml: line 3: key defined twice")
#   v = toml.parse(text)?                                 # a json.Value: v.field("server").field("port").int_or(80)
#   text = toml.encode(cfg)?                              # a struct or map as TOML
#
#   toml.decode(text, out: mut T) Result[int, str]   fills out, as json.decode does (by field name;
#                                                    a key the struct lacks is ignored)
#   toml.parse(text) Result[json.Value, str]         the document as a json.Value (tables are Obj)
#   toml.encode(value: T) Result[str, str]           a struct or map as TOML: its plain keys, then
#                                                    [tables] and [[arrays of tables]]
#   toml.dump(v: json.Value) Result[str, str]        a json.Value (an Obj) as TOML
#
# Values: tables are objects (keys in the order written), arrays arrays, strings, integers
# (64-bit), floats and booleans as in JSON. Dates and times are strings in RFC 3339 form
# ("1979-05-27T07:32:00Z", "1979-05-27T07:32:00", "1979-05-27", "07:32:00"). inf comes out as
# a float too big for a double (inf when read as one), nan as null (a field keeps its value).
# TOML has no null: encode leaves out a None or null.
import json

fn parse(text: str) Result[json.Value, str]:
    return json.parse(_to_json(text)?)

fn decode[T](text: str, out: mut T) Result[int, str]:
    j = _to_json(text)?
    if not json.decode(j, &out):
        return Err("toml: a value doesn't fit its field (a string where a number goes, a table where a list goes...)")
    return Ok(0)

fn encode[T](value: T) Result[str, str]:
    return _from(json.encode(value))

fn dump(v: json.Value) Result[str, str]:
    return _from(json.dump(v))

fn _to_json(text: str) Result[str, str]:
    j = _json(text, false)
    if j != "" and j.byte(0) == 1:
        return Err("toml: " + j[1..])
    return Ok(j)

fn _from(j: str) Result[str, str]:
    t = _from_json(j)
    if t != "" and t.byte(0) == 1:
        return Err("toml: " + t[t.find(": ") + 2..])     # (no line: it is our own JSON)
    return Ok(t)
```

## library/std/url/escape.tn

```tern
# url: escaping (runtime/url.h, by Go's net/url rules).

const PATH = 1
const SEGMENT = 2
const HOST = 3
const ZONE = 4
const USER = 5
const QUERY = 6
const FRAGMENT = 7

fn query_escape(s: str) str:
    return _escape(s, QUERY)

fn path_escape(s: str) str:
    return _escape(s, SEGMENT)

fn query_unescape(s: str) Result[str, str]:
    return _unescape_as(s, QUERY)

fn path_unescape(s: str) Result[str, str]:
    return _unescape_as(s, SEGMENT)

fn _unescape_as(s: str, mode: int) Result[str, str]:
    b = _bad(s, mode)
    if b >= 0:
        return Err(_bad_message(s, b, mode))
    return Ok(_unescape(s, mode))

fn _bad_message(s: str, b: int, mode: int) str:
    if s.byte(b) == 37:
        return f"url: invalid escape \"{s[b..min(b + 3, len(s))]}\""
    return f"url: invalid character \"{s[b]}\" in host name"
```

## library/std/url/parts.tn

```tern
# url: the parts of a URL one by one (Parts), and the general parse into them: what
# url.parse falls back to when a URL isn't already written the way format writes it, and
# what url.build turns back into a Url.

struct Parts:
    scheme: str
    opaque: str
    user: str
    password: str
    host: str
    port: int
    path: str
    raw_path: str
    raw_query: str
    force_query: bool             # a "?" with nothing after it
    fragment: str
    raw_fragment: str             # the fragment as written, when format would write it otherwise
    omit_host: bool

fn _empty() Parts:
    return Parts("", "", "", "", "", 0, "", "", "", false, "", "", false)

# Positions in raw, and a slice only for each part kept (a slice is a copy).
fn _parse_parts(raw: str) Result[Parts, str]:
    sc = _scan(raw)               # control bytes, the "#", and whether any "%" comes before it
    if sc < 0:
        return Err("invalid control character")
    u = _empty()
    end = sc / 2 - 1
    pct = sc % 2 == 1
    if end < len(raw):
        f = raw[end + 1..]
        u.fragment = _part(f, FRAGMENT)?
        if _escape(u.fragment, FRAGMENT) != f:
            u.raw_fragment = f
    if end == 1 and raw.byte(0) == 42:
        u.path = "*"
        return Ok(u)
    k = _split(raw, end)
    if k < 0:
        _parse_rest(&u, raw, end, pct)?
        return Ok(u)
    # (the usual URL: _split found its parts in one pass)
    m = 4095
    se = k & m
    h0 = (k >> 12) & m
    h1 = (k >> 24) & m
    p0 = (k >> 36) & m
    pend = (k >> 48) & m
    pos = 0
    if se > 0:
        u.scheme = _scheme(raw, se)
        pos = se + 1
    if pend < end:
        if pend == end - 1:
            u.force_query = true
        else:
            u.raw_query = raw[pend + 1..end]
    if p0 >= pos + 2:
        if (k >> 60) & 1 == 1:
            info = raw[pos + 2..h0 - 1]
            c = info.find(":")
            if c < 0:
                u.user = info
            else:
                u.user = info[..c]
                u.password = info[c + 1..]
        u.host = raw[h0..h1]
        for i in h1 + 1..p0:
            u.port = u.port * 10 + raw.byte(i) - 48
    elif se > 0 and pos < pend and raw.byte(pos) == 47:
        u.omit_host = true
    rest = raw[p0..pend]
    u.path = rest
    if (k >> 61) & 1 == 0:
        if pct:
            u.path = _part(rest, PATH)?
        if _escape(u.path, PATH) != rest:
            u.raw_path = rest
    return Ok(u)

# _parse from the scheme on, for what _split leaves to it
fn _parse_rest(u: mut Parts, raw: str, end: int, pct: bool) Result[int, str]:
    # scheme: a letter, then letters, digits, + - . up to a ":"
    pos = 0
    for i in 0..end:
        c = raw.byte(i)
        if (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90):
            continue
        if (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 43 or c == 45 or c == 46:
            if i == 0:
                break
            continue
        if c == 58:
            if i == 0:
                return Err("missing scheme before \":\"")
            u.scheme = _scheme(raw, i)
            pos = i + 1
        break
    pend = end                    # where the path ends: the "?" or the end
    q = raw.find_from("?", pos)
    if q >= 0 and q < end:
        pend = q
        if q == end - 1:
            u.force_query = true
        else:
            u.raw_query = raw[q + 1..end]
    slash = pos < pend and raw.byte(pos) == 47
    if not slash:
        if u.scheme != "":
            u.opaque = raw[pos..pend]
            return Ok(0)
        seg = raw.find_from("/", pos)
        if seg < 0 or seg > pend:
            seg = pend
        c = raw.find_from(":", pos)
        if c >= 0 and c < seg:
            return Err("first path segment cannot contain a colon")
    p0 = pos
    two = slash and pos + 1 < pend and raw.byte(pos + 1) == 47
    if two and (u.scheme != "" or not (pos + 2 < pend and raw.byte(pos + 2) == 47)):
        a0 = pos + 2
        a1 = raw.find_from("/", a0)
        if a1 < 0 or a1 > pend:
            a1 = pend
        _authority(&u, raw, a0, a1)?
        p0 = a1
    elif u.scheme != "" and slash:
        u.omit_host = true
    rest = raw[p0..pend]
    u.path = rest
    if pct:
        u.path = _part(rest, PATH)?
    if _escape(u.path, PATH) != rest:
        u.raw_path = rest
    return Ok(0)

# raw[..i] lowered; "http" and "https" without a copy
fn _scheme(raw: str, i: int) str:
    if i == 5 and _lower_is(raw, "https"):
        return "https"
    if i == 4 and _lower_is(raw, "http"):
        return "http"
    return raw[..i].lower()

fn _lower_is(raw: str, lit: str) bool:
    for k in 0..len(lit):
        if raw.byte(k) | 32 != lit.byte(k):
            return false
    return true

fn _part(s: str, mode: int) Result[str, str]:
    if mode != HOST and mode != ZONE and not s.contains("%"):
        return Ok(s)
    b = _bad(s, mode)
    if b >= 0:
        return Err(_bad_message(s, b, mode).strip_prefix("url: "))
    return Ok(_unescape(s, mode))

# raw[a0..a1] is the authority: [user[:password]@]host[:port]
fn _authority(u: mut Parts, raw: str, a0: int, a1: int) Result[int, str]:
    h0 = a0
    at = raw.find_from("@", a0)
    if at >= 0 and at < a1:
        at = a1 - 1
        while raw.byte(at) != 64:
            at -= 1
        info = raw[a0..at]
        if not _valid_userinfo(info):
            return Err("invalid user or password")
        c = info.find(":")
        if c < 0:
            u.user = _part(info, USER)?
        else:
            u.user = _part(info[..c], USER)?
            u.password = _part(info[c + 1..], USER)?
        h0 = at + 1
    hp = _host(raw[h0..a1])?
    # host and port (Go's Hostname / Port)
    colon = hp.find(":")
    if colon >= 0:
        colon = _last(hp, 58)
    if colon >= 0 and _valid_port(hp[colon..]):
        port = 0
        for k in colon + 1..len(hp):
            port = port * 10 + hp.byte(k) - 48
            if port > 65535:
                return Err(f"invalid port \"{hp[colon + 1..]}\"")
        u.port = port
        hp = hp[..colon]
    if hp.starts_with("[") and hp.ends_with("]"):
        hp = hp[1..len(hp) - 1]
    elif hp.contains(":"):
        return Err(f"invalid host \"{hp}\" (an IPv6 address goes in brackets: [::1])")
    u.host = hp
    return Ok(0)

# index of the last byte c in s (-1 if none)
fn _last(s: str, c: int) int:
    i = len(s) - 1
    while i >= 0 and s.byte(i) != c:
        i -= 1
    return i

# ":" then digits (or nothing at all)
fn _valid_port(p: str) bool:
    if p == "":
        return true
    if p.byte(0) != 58:
        return false
    for i in 1..len(p):
        c = p.byte(i)
        if c < 48 or c > 57:
            return false
    return true

fn _host(h: str) Result[str, str]:
    if h.contains("["):
        # an IP literal: "[v6]" or "[v6%25zone]", then maybe ":port" (Go also takes text before
        # the "[" and drops it; that's an error here)
        e = -1
        for k in 0..len(h):
            if h.byte(k) == 93:
                e = k
        if e < 0:
            return Err("missing \"]\" in host")
        if not h.starts_with("[") or h[1..e].contains("["):
            return Err("\"[\" must start the host")
        if not _valid_port(h[e + 1..]):
            return Err(f"invalid port \"{h[e + 1..]}\" after host")
        name = h[1..e]
        z = name.find("%25")
        ip = ""
        if z >= 0:
            ip = _part(name[..z], HOST)? + _part(name[z..], ZONE)?
        else:
            ip = _part(name, HOST)?
        if not _ipv6(ip):
            return Err(f"invalid IPv6 address \"{ip}\" in host")
        return Ok("[" + ip + "]" + _part(h[e + 1..], HOST)?)
    i = h.find(":")
    if i >= 0:
        i = _last(h, 58)
    if i >= 0 and not _valid_port(h[i..]):
        return Err(f"invalid port \"{h[i..]}\" after host")
    return _part(h, HOST)

# An IPv6 address as Go's netip reads it (eight groups of hex, one "::", an IPv4 tail, a
# "%zone" that isn't empty); IPv4 alone isn't one.
fn _ipv6(s: str) bool:
    a = s
    z = s.find("%")
    if z >= 0:
        if z == len(s) - 1:
            return false
        a = s[..z]
    if not a.contains(":"):
        return false
    groups = 0
    gap = false
    i = 0
    n = len(a)
    if a.starts_with("::"):
        gap = true
        i = 2
        if n == 2:
            return true
    elif a.starts_with(":"):
        return false
    while i < n:
        # one group, or an IPv4 tail
        j = i
        while j < n and a.byte(j) != 58:
            j += 1
        g = a[i..j]
        if g.contains("."):
            if j != n or not _ipv4(g):
                return false
            groups += 2
            break
        if len(g) == 0 or len(g) > 4:
            return false
        for k in 0..len(g):
            c = g.byte(k) | 32
            if not ((c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 97 and c <= 102)):
                return false
        groups += 1
        if j == n:
            break
        if j + 1 < n and a.byte(j + 1) == 58:
            if gap:
                return false
            gap = true
            i = j + 2
            if i == n:
                break
        else:
            if j + 1 == n:
                return false
            i = j + 1
    if gap:
        return groups < 8
    return groups == 8

fn _ipv4(s: str) bool:
    parts = s.split(".")
    if len(parts) != 4:
        return false
    for p in parts:
        if p == "" or len(p) > 3 or (len(p) > 1 and p.byte(0) == 48):
            return false
        for k in 0..len(p):
            if p.byte(k) < 48 or p.byte(k) > 57:
                return false
        if p.to_int(256) > 255:
            return false
    return true

fn _valid_userinfo(s: str) bool:
    for i in 0..len(s):
        c = s.byte(i)
        if (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57):
            continue
        if not "-._:~!$&'()*+,;=%@".contains(s[i]):
            return false
    return true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- back to text

fn _esc_fragment(u: Parts) str:
    if u.raw_fragment != "" and _valid_encoded(u.raw_fragment, FRAGMENT) and _bad(u.raw_fragment, FRAGMENT) < 0 and _unescape(u.raw_fragment, FRAGMENT) == u.fragment:
        return u.raw_fragment
    return _escape(u.fragment, FRAGMENT)

fn _bracketed(host: str) str:
    if host.contains(":"):
        return "[" + host + "]"
    return host

# The path as it goes in the URL: raw_path when it says the same as path, else path escaped.
fn _esc_path(u: Parts) str:
    if u.raw_path != "" and _valid_encoded(u.raw_path, PATH) and _bad(u.raw_path, PATH) < 0 and _unescape(u.raw_path, PATH) == u.path:
        return u.raw_path
    if u.path == "*":
        return "*"
    return _escape(u.path, PATH)

fn _valid_encoded(s: str, mode: int) bool:
    for i in 0..len(s):
        if "!$&'()*+,;=:@[]%".contains(s[i]):
            continue
        if _escape(s[i], mode) != s[i]:
            return false
    return true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- references

fn _resolve_parts(base: Parts, ref: Parts) Parts:
    u = ref
    if ref.scheme == "":
        u.scheme = base.scheme
    if ref.scheme != "" or ref.host != "" or ref.port > 0 or ref.user != "" or ref.password != "":
        _set_path(&u, _resolve_path(_esc_path(ref), ""))
        return u
    if ref.opaque != "":
        u.user = ""
        u.password = ""
        u.host = ""
        u.port = 0
        u.path = ""
        u.raw_path = ""
        return u
    if ref.path == "" and not ref.force_query and ref.raw_query == "":
        u.raw_query = base.raw_query
        if ref.fragment == "":
            u.fragment = base.fragment
            u.raw_fragment = base.raw_fragment
    if ref.path == "" and base.opaque != "":
        u.opaque = base.opaque
        u.user = ""
        u.password = ""
        u.host = ""
        u.port = 0
        u.path = ""
        u.raw_path = ""
        return u
    u.host = base.host
    u.port = base.port
    u.user = base.user
    u.password = base.password
    if base.raw_path == "" and ref.raw_path == "" and base.path != "*" and ref.path != "*":
        # both written as escape() writes them, which never adds or drops a "/" or ".": the
        # decoded paths resolve to the decoded answer
        u.path = _resolve_path(base.path, ref.path)
        u.raw_path = ""
    else:
        _set_path(&u, _resolve_path(_esc_path(base), _esc_path(ref)))
    return u

fn _set_path(u: mut Parts, p: str):
    if _bad(p, PATH) >= 0:
        return
    u.path = _unescape(p, PATH)
    u.raw_path = ""
    if _escape(u.path, PATH) != p:
        u.raw_path = p

# RFC 3986 5.2: merge ref onto base's directory and drop "." and ".." (_resolve_path, in
# runtime/url.h, is Go's resolvePath step for step: where its slashes go is part of the answer)
```

## library/std/url/query.tn

```tern
# url: queries ("a=1&b=x+y"), as pairs in the order given (a key may repeat).

struct Query:
    keys: [str]
    vals: [str]

fn new_query() Query:
    return Query([], [])

# Go's ParseQuery: pairs split at "&", "=" between key and value, both query-unescaped; an
# empty piece is skipped, a ";" is an error (it was a separator once, and servers disagree).
fn parse_query(raw: str) Result[Query, str]:
    q = Query([], [])
    _pairs(raw, &q, true)?
    return Ok(q)

fn query(u: Url) Query:
    q = Query([], [])
    _pairs(raw_query(u), &q, false).unwrap_or(0)
    return q

fn _pairs(raw: str, q: mut Query, strict: bool) Result[int, str]:
    if raw == "":
        return Ok(0)
    for piece in raw.split("&"):
        if piece == "":
            continue
        if piece.contains(";"):
            if strict:
                return Err("url: invalid \";\" in query (use \"&\" between pairs)")
            continue
        k = piece
        v = ""
        e = piece.find("=")
        if e >= 0:
            k = piece[..e]
            v = piece[e + 1..]
        bk = _bad(k, QUERY)
        bv = _bad(v, QUERY)
        if bk >= 0 or bv >= 0:
            if strict:
                if bk >= 0:
                    return Err(_bad_message(k, bk, QUERY))
                return Err(_bad_message(v, bv, QUERY))
            continue
        q.keys.push(_unescape(k, QUERY))
        q.vals.push(_unescape(v, QUERY))
    return Ok(len(q.keys))

fn get(q: Query, key: str) str:
    for i, k in q.keys:
        if k == key:
            return q.vals[i]
    return ""

fn get_all(q: Query, key: str) [str]:
    out: [str] = []
    for i, k in q.keys:
        if k == key:
            out.push(q.vals[i])
    return out

fn has(q: Query, key: str) bool:
    for k in q.keys:
        if k == key:
            return true
    return false

fn add(q: mut Query, key: str, value: str):
    q.keys.push(key)
    q.vals.push(value)

fn set(q: mut Query, key: str, value: str):
    remove(&q, key)
    add(&q, key, value)

fn remove(q: mut Query, key: str):
    if not has(q, key):
        return
    ks: [str] = []
    vs: [str] = []
    for i, k in q.keys:
        if k != key:
            ks.push(k)
            vs.push(q.vals[i])
    q.keys = ks
    q.vals = vs

fn encode_query(q: Query) str:
    s = ""
    for i, k in q.keys:
        if i > 0:
            s += "&"
        s += _escape(k, QUERY)
        s += "="
        s += _escape(q.vals[i], QUERY)
    return s

# {key: value} as a query, keys sorted
fn query_string(pairs: {str: str}) str:
    q = Query([], [])
    for k in pairs.keys().sort_by(fn(x) x):
        add(&q, k, pairs[k])
    return encode_query(q)
```

## library/std/url/resolve.tn

```tern
# url: references (RFC 3986 section 5), as Go's ResolveReference.

fn resolve(base: Url, ref: Url) Url:
    bf = _hi(base._pf)
    rf = _hi(ref._pf)
    bp = escaped_path(base)
    # a link with no scheme, authority or opaque part (what pages hold), against a base with
    # a "//" or no scheme whose path starts at a "/" (nothing written before it): the base's
    # text up to its path, the merged path, then the query and fragment
    if _lo(ref._sp) == 0 and _lo(ref._host) == _hi(ref._host) and (rf & (_OPAQUE | _USER)) == 0 and _lo(ref._pf) == 0 and not ref._text.starts_with("//") and (bf & (_OPAQUE | _OMIT_HOST)) == 0 and (bp == "" or bp.byte(0) == 47) and (_lo(base._sp) == 0 or base._text[_after_scheme(base)..].starts_with("//")):
        rp = escaped_path(ref)
        ps = _hi(base._sp)
        p = _resolve_path(bp, rp)
        rest = ref._text[_lo(ref._qf)..]
        if rp == "" and _lo(ref._qf) == _hi(ref._qf):
            # no path and no "?": the base's query, and its fragment unless ref has one
            rq = raw_query(base)
            rest = ""
            if rq != "":
                rest = "?" + rq
            f = escaped_fragment(ref)
            if f == "":
                f = escaped_fragment(base)
            if f != "":
                rest += "#" + f
        t = base._text[..ps] + p + rest
        q = ps + len(p)
        h = rest.find("#")
        if h < 0:
            h = len(rest)
        return Url(t, base._sp, base._host, q | (q + h) << 32, base._ua, base._pf)
    return build(_resolve_parts(parts(base), parts(ref)))

fn join(base: str, ref: str) Result[str, str]:
    b = parse(base)?
    r = parse(ref)?
    return Ok(format(resolve(b, r)))
```
