```tern
# RFC 3986 5.2: merge ref onto base's directory and drop "." and ".." (_resolve_path, in
# runtime/url.h, is Go's resolvePath step for step: where its slashes go is part of the answer)
```

## library/std/url/url.tn

```tern
# url: parse, build and resolve URLs, and escape their parts, by the rules of Go's net/url
# (RFC 3986). A Url is its text, written the way format writes it, plus where each part is in
# it: format costs nothing, and parsing a URL that is already written that way (almost every
# one) keeps the text it was given. Parts come out decoded (path, user, fragment); the query
# stays as written until you ask for it with u.query().
#
#   import url
#   u = url.parse("https://ada:pw@example.com:8443/a%20b/c?q=1&tag=x&tag=y#top")?
#   u.scheme()  u.user()  u.password()  u.host()  u.port()  u.path()  # "https" "ada" "pw" "example.com" 8443 "/a b/c"
#   u.raw_query()  u.fragment()                                        # "q=1&tag=x&tag=y" "top"
#   q = u.query()                                           # q.get("tag") "x", q.get_all("tag") ["x", "y"]
#   url.format(u)                                           # its text, escaped where needed
#   u.set_path("/v2 docs")                                  # change one part (format escapes it)
#   url.join("https://x.dev/docs/a/", "../b?v=2")?          # "https://x.dev/docs/b?v=2"
#
#   url.parse(text) Result[Url, str]      Err for a bad escape, port, host or control byte
#   url.format(u) str                     u as text
#   url.resolve(base, ref: Url) Url       ref resolved against base (RFC 3986 section 5)
#   url.join(base, ref: str) Result[str, str]   the same for text: a link on a page
#   u.host_port() str                     "example.com:8443", "[::1]:80", "example.com"
#   u.request_uri() str                   what an HTTP request line asks for: "/a%20b/c?q=1"
#   u.query() Query                       the query's pairs (badly escaped ones are skipped)
#
# The parts of a Url: u.scheme() (lower case when parsed), u.opaque() (what follows "scheme:"
# when it isn't a path or "//": "mailto:ada@x" has opaque "ada@x"), u.user(), u.password(),
# u.host() (no brackets: "::1"), u.port() (0 when none), u.path() (decoded), u.raw_query(),
# u.fragment() (decoded), u.escaped_path() and u.escaped_fragment() (as the text has them),
# u.raw_path() and u.raw_fragment() (those, when that isn't how escaping the decoded part
# writes it: "/a%2Fb"; else ""), u.force_query() (a "?" with nothing after), u.omit_host()
# ("s:/p" had no "//"). To change one: u.set_scheme(s), set_user, set_password, set_host,
# set_port(n), set_path, set_raw_query, set_fragment. To change several at once or make one
# from nothing: p = u.parts() (or a url.Parts(...) of your own), set p's fields, url.build(p).
# Unlike Go: a port above 65535, a ":" in a host outside brackets, and text before a "[" are
# errors, and an empty or zero port ("x:/", "x:0"), user ("@x") or password ("u:@x") is dropped.
#
# Queries (keys in the order given; a key may repeat):
#   url.parse_query(raw) Result[Query, str]   "a=1&b=x+y" (Err for a bad escape or a ";")
#   q.get(key) str  ("" if absent)     q.get_all(key) [str]     q.has(key) bool
#   q.add(key, value)    q.set(key, value) (replaces every value)    q.remove(key)
#   url.encode_query(q) str            "a=1&b=x+y"; also url.query_string(pairs: {str: str}) str
#   q.keys [str]  q.vals [str]         the pairs, in order
# Escaping:
#   url.query_escape(s) str   url.query_unescape(s) Result[str, str]   (space is "+")
#   url.path_escape(s) str    url.path_unescape(s) Result[str, str]    (one path segment: "/" escaped)

# The text, and in it (two 32-bit positions an int): the scheme's length (0: none) and where
# the path starts; the host's start and end (inside any brackets); where the path ends (the
# "?", "#" or end) and where the fragment's "#" is (the end when none); the user's end and
# the "@" (both 0 without user info); the port and the flags.
struct Url:
    _text: str
    _sp: int
    _host: int
    _qf: int
    _ua: int
    _pf: int

const _OPAQUE = 1
const _OMIT_HOST = 2
const _USER = 4

fn parse(raw: str) Result[Url, str]:
    sc = _scan(raw)               # control bytes, the "#", and whether any "%" comes before it
    if sc >= 0:
        end = sc / 2 - 1
        k = _split(raw, end)
        if k >= 0 and (k >> 62) & 1 == 1:
            # already as format writes it: the Url keeps raw as its text
            m = 4095
            se = k & m
            h0 = (k >> 12) & m
            h1 = (k >> 24) & m
            p0 = (k >> 36) & m
            pend = (k >> 48) & m
            pos = 0
            if se > 0:
                pos = se + 1
            ua = 0
            port = 0
            flags = 0
            if p0 >= pos + 2:
                if (k >> 60) & 1 == 1:
                    at = h0 - 1
                    c = raw.find_from(":", pos + 2)
                    if c < 0 or c > at:
                        c = at
                    ua = c | at << 32
                    flags = _USER
                for i in h1 + 1..p0:
                    port = port * 10 + raw.byte(i) - 48
            elif se > 0 and pos < pend and raw.byte(pos) == 47:
                flags = _OMIT_HOST
            return Ok(Url(raw, se | p0 << 32, h0 | h1 << 32, pend | end << 32, ua, port | flags << 32))
    match _parse_parts(raw):
        Ok(p):
            return Ok(build(p))
        Err(why):
            return Err(f"url: {why} in {json_quote(raw)}")

fn format(u: Url) str:
    return u._text

fn _lo(x: int) int:
    return x & 0xffffffff

fn _hi(x: int) int:
    return x >> 32

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the parts

fn scheme(u: Url) str:
    n = _lo(u._sp)
    if n == 5 and u._text.starts_with("https"):
        return "https"
    if n == 4 and u._text.starts_with("http"):
        return "http"
    return u._text[..n]

fn _after_scheme(u: Url) int:
    n = _lo(u._sp)
    return n + 1 if n > 0 else 0

fn opaque(u: Url) str:
    if (_hi(u._pf) & _OPAQUE) == 0:
        return ""
    return u._text[_after_scheme(u).._lo(u._qf)]

fn omit_host(u: Url) bool:
    return (_hi(u._pf) & _OMIT_HOST) != 0

fn user(u: Url) str:
    if (_hi(u._pf) & _USER) == 0:
        return ""
    return _unescape(u._text[_after_scheme(u) + 2.._lo(u._ua)], USER)

fn password(u: Url) str:
    e = _lo(u._ua)
    at = _hi(u._ua)
    if (_hi(u._pf) & _USER) == 0 or e == at:
        return ""
    return _unescape(u._text[e + 1..at], USER)

fn host(u: Url) str:
    a = _lo(u._host)
    b = _hi(u._host)
    if a == b:
        return ""
    return _unescape(u._text[a..b], HOST)

fn port(u: Url) int:
    return _lo(u._pf)

fn escaped_path(u: Url) str:
    if (_hi(u._pf) & _OPAQUE) != 0:
        return ""
    return u._text[_hi(u._sp).._lo(u._qf)]

fn path(u: Url) str:
    return _unescape(escaped_path(u), PATH)

# the path as written when escaping path() would write it otherwise ("/a%2Fb"), else ""
fn raw_path(u: Url) str:
    e = escaped_path(u)
    if _escape(_unescape(e, PATH), PATH) == e or (e == "*" and _hi(u._sp) == 0 and _lo(u._qf) == _hi(u._qf)):
        return ""               # (a "*" alone, as OPTIONS asks for, is that path itself)
    return e

fn raw_query(u: Url) str:
    q = _lo(u._qf)
    f = _hi(u._qf)
    if q < f:
        return u._text[q + 1..f]
    return ""

fn force_query(u: Url) bool:
    q = _lo(u._qf)
    return q + 1 == _hi(u._qf) and q < len(u._text) and u._text.byte(q) == 63

fn escaped_fragment(u: Url) str:
    f = _hi(u._qf)
    if f < len(u._text):
        return u._text[f + 1..]
    return ""

fn fragment(u: Url) str:
    return _unescape(escaped_fragment(u), FRAGMENT)

fn raw_fragment(u: Url) str:
    e = escaped_fragment(u)
    if _escape(_unescape(e, FRAGMENT), FRAGMENT) == e:
        return ""
    return e

fn host_port(u: Url) str:
    if port(u) > 0:
        return _bracketed(host(u)) + ":" + str(port(u))
    return _bracketed(host(u))

fn request_uri(u: Url) str:
    r = opaque(u)
    if r == "":
        r = escaped_path(u)
        if r == "":
            r = "/"
    elif r.starts_with("//"):
        r = scheme(u) + ":" + r
    q = raw_query(u)
    if q != "":
        r += "?" + q
    return r

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- building and changing

# every part, decoded, in a struct you can change and give back to build
fn parts(u: Url) Parts:
    return Parts(scheme(u), opaque(u), user(u), password(u), host(u), port(u), path(u), raw_path(u), raw_query(u), force_query(u), fragment(u), raw_fragment(u), omit_host(u))

# p written out (escaped where needed: raw_path and raw_fragment when they say the same as
# path and fragment), as a Url
fn build(p: Parts) Url:
    t = ""
    sc = 0
    if p.scheme != "":
        t = p.scheme + ":"
        sc = len(p.scheme)
    frag = ""
    if p.fragment != "":
        frag = "#" + _esc_fragment(p)
    query = ""
    if p.force_query or p.raw_query != "":
        query = "?" + p.raw_query
    if p.opaque != "":
        ps = len(t)
        t += p.opaque
        q = len(t)
        t += query
        f = len(t)
        return Url(t + frag, sc | ps << 32, 0, q | f << 32, 0, _OPAQUE << 32)
    h0 = 0
    h1 = 0
    ua = 0
    port = 0
    flags = 0
    if p.omit_host:
        flags = _OMIT_HOST
    has_host = p.host != "" or p.port > 0
    has_user = p.user != "" or p.password != ""
    if p.scheme != "" or has_host or has_user:
        if not (p.omit_host and not has_host and not has_user):
            if has_host or p.path != "" or has_user:
                t += "//"
            if has_user:
                t += _escape(p.user, USER)
                e = len(t)
                if p.password != "":
                    t += ":" + _escape(p.password, USER)
                ua = e | len(t) << 32
                t += "@"
                flags = flags | _USER
            if has_host:
                b = p.host.contains(":")
                if b:
                    t += "["
                h0 = len(t)
                t += _escape(p.host, HOST)
                h1 = len(t)
                if b:
                    t += "]"
                if p.port > 0:
                    port = p.port
                    t += ":" + str(port)
    e = _esc_path(p)
    if e != "" and e.byte(0) != 47 and has_host:
        t += "/"
    elif p.scheme == "" and not t.starts_with("//") and e.contains(":"):
        # a first segment with ":" would read as a scheme
        k = e.find("/")
        if k < 0 or e[..k].contains(":"):
            t += "./"
    ps = len(t)
    t += e
    q = len(t)
    t += query
    f = len(t)
    return Url(t + frag, sc | ps << 32, h0 | h1 << 32, q | f << 32, ua, port | flags << 32)

fn set_scheme(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.scheme = s
    u = build(p)

fn set_user(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.user = s
    u = build(p)

fn set_password(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.password = s
    u = build(p)

fn set_host(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.host = s
    u = build(p)

fn set_port(u: mut Url, n: int):
    p = parts(u)
    p.port = n
    u = build(p)

# the decoded path ("/a b"), escaped as it goes into the text
fn set_path(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.path = s
    p.raw_path = ""
    u = build(p)

fn set_raw_query(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.raw_query = s
    p.force_query = false
    u = build(p)

fn set_fragment(u: mut Url, s: str):
    p = parts(u)
    p.fragment = s
    p.raw_fragment = ""
    u = build(p)
```

# First-party packages (library/)

Imported by name like the standard library (`import roost`).

## library/migrate/files.tn

```tern
# migrate: reading migration files (see migrate.tn)

struct Migration:
    version: int
    name: str
    up: str
    down: str                   # "" if the migration can't be rolled back
    transaction: bool           # false: `-- migrate:no-transaction`
    checksum: str               # sha256 of up, hex: an applied migration must not change

# One migration from its text. The text is the up SQL, optionally split by marker lines:
#   -- migrate:up                   (optional) the SQL that applies it
#   -- migrate:down                 the SQL that undoes it
#   -- migrate:no-transaction       run it outside a transaction (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY)
fn parse(version: int, name: str, text: str) Result[Migration, str]:
    up = ""
    down = ""
    in_down = false
    seen_up = false
    tx = true
    lines = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n")
    for line in lines:
        t = line.trim()
        if t.starts_with("-- migrate:"):
            what = t[11..].trim()
            if what == "up":
                if seen_up or in_down:
                    return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: `-- migrate:up` must come once, before `-- migrate:down`")
                seen_up = true
            elif what == "down":
                if in_down:
                    return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: `-- migrate:down` appears twice")
                in_down = true
            elif what == "no-transaction":
                tx = false
            else:
                return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: unknown marker `{t}` (use -- migrate:up, -- migrate:down, or -- migrate:no-transaction)")
            continue
        if in_down:
            down += line + "\n"
        else:
            up += line + "\n"
    if not _has_sql(up):
        return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: no SQL to apply (the up part is empty or only comments)")
    if not _has_sql(down):
        down = ""
    return Ok(Migration(version, name, up, down, tx, crypto.hex(crypto.sha256(up))))

# The migrations in a directory, oldest first. Files are named VERSION_NAME.sql
# (0001_create_users.sql, 20260928120000_add_email.sql), or VERSION_NAME.up.sql with an
# optional VERSION_NAME.down.sql beside it. Other files are ignored.
fn load(dir: str) Result[[Migration], str]:
    ups: {int: str} = {}
    downs: {int: str} = {}
    files = _files(dir)?
    for v in files.keys():
        for f in files[v]:
            text = fs.try_read(dir + "/" + f).context("migrate")?
            if f.ends_with(".down.sql"):
                downs[v] = text
            else:
                ups[v] = text
    out: [Migration] = []
    versions = files.keys().sort_by(fn(k) k)
    for v in versions:
        first = files[v][0]
        if not (v in ups):
            return Err(f"migrate: {first} has no {first[..len(first) - 9]}.up.sql")
        text = ups[v]
        if v in downs:
            if text.contains("-- migrate:down"):
                return Err(f"migrate: version {v} has a `-- migrate:down` section and a .down.sql file; keep one")
            text += "\n-- migrate:down\n" + downs[v]
        out.push(parse(v, _title(first), text)?)
    return Ok(out)

# the migration files in dir by version: [the .sql file] or [.down.sql, .up.sql]
fn _files(dir: str) Result[{int: [str]}, str]:
    names = fs.try_list(dir).context("migrate")?
    out: {int: [str]} = {}
    sorted = names.sort_by(fn(n) n)
    for f in sorted:
        if not f.ends_with(".sql"):
            continue
        base = f[..len(f) - 4]
        v = _version_of(base)
        if v < 0:
            return Err(f"migrate: {f}: name migration files VERSION_NAME.sql, like 0001_create_users.sql")
        if v in out:
            prev = out[v][0]
            # (sorted, so a .down.sql comes before its .up.sql)
            pair = len(out[v]) == 1 and prev.ends_with(".down.sql") and f.ends_with(".up.sql") and _title(prev) == _title(f)
            if not pair:
                return Err(f"migrate: {prev} and {f} have the same version, {v}; renumber one of them")
            out[v].push(f)
        else:
            out[v] = [f]
    return Ok(out)

# "0002_add_email.up.sql" -> "add_email"
fn _title(file: str) str:
    base = file[..len(file) - 4]
    if base.ends_with(".down"):
        base = base[..len(base) - 5]
    elif base.ends_with(".up"):
        base = base[..len(base) - 3]
    return base[_digits(base) + 1..]

# the next file name for `migrate new`: one more than the newest version, as wide as the
# existing names (0001_...), or a UTC timestamp if the versions are timestamps
fn next_file(versions: [int], name: str) str:
    last = 0
    for v in versions:
        last = max(last, v)
    if last >= 10000000000000:
        d = time.utc(time.now())
        return f"{d.year}{fmt.zero_pad(d.month, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.day, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.hour, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.minute, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.second, 2)}_{name}.sql"
    return f"{fmt.zero_pad(last + 1, 4)}_{name}.sql"

fn _digits(s: str) int:
    i = 0
    while i < len(s) and s.byte(i) >= 48 and s.byte(i) <= 57:
        i += 1
    return i

# "0001_create_users" -> 1; -1 if it doesn't start with digits, a _ or -, and a name
fn _version_of(base: str) int:
    n = _digits(base)
    if n == 0 or n > 18 or n + 1 >= len(base) or not (base[n] == "_" or base[n] == "-"):
        return -1
    return base[..n].to_int(-1)

# anything but whitespace and -- comments
fn _has_sql(s: str) bool:
    lines = s.split("\n")
    for line in lines:
        t = line.trim()
        if t != "" and not t.starts_with("--"):
            return true
    return false

# The statements in a script, split at the semicolons that end them (not ones in quotes,
# $$ bodies, or comments): PostgreSQL runs a multi-statement string in one transaction, so a
# no-transaction migration sends its statements one at a time.
fn split_statements(sql: str) [str]:
    out: [str] = []
    start = 0
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)
    while i < n:
        c = sql.byte(i)
        if c == 39 or c == 34:                              # '...' or "..." ('' and "" double up)
            i += 1
            while i < n and sql.byte(i) != c:
                i += 1
            i += 1
        elif c == 45 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 45:      # -- to the end of the line
            while i < n and sql.byte(i) != 10:
                i += 1
        elif c == 47 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 42:      # /* ... */, nested
            depth = 1
            i += 2
            while i < n and depth > 0:
                if sql.byte(i) == 47 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 42:
                    depth += 1
                    i += 1
                elif sql.byte(i) == 42 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 47:
                    depth -= 1
                    i += 1
                i += 1
        elif c == 36 and (i == 0 or not _ident_byte(sql.byte(i - 1))):     # $tag$ ... $tag$
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and _ident_byte(sql.byte(j)) and sql.byte(j) != 36:
                j += 1
            if j < n and sql.byte(j) == 36 and (j == i + 1 or not _is_digit(sql.byte(i + 1))):
                tag = sql[i..j + 1]
                end = sql[j + 1..].find(tag)
                i = n if end < 0 else j + 1 + end + len(tag)
            else:
                i += 1
        elif c == 59:                                       # ;
            _push_statement(&out, sql[start..i])
            i += 1
            start = i
        else:
            i += 1
    _push_statement(&out, sql[start..])
    return out

fn _push_statement(out: mut [str], s: str):
    if _has_sql(s):
        out.push(s.trim())

fn _is_digit(c: int) bool:
    return c >= 48 and c <= 57

fn _ident_byte(c: int) bool:
    return _is_digit(c) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or c == 95 or c == 36 or c >= 128
```

## library/migrate/migrate.tn

```tern
# migrate: database migrations for PostgreSQL and SQLite, from a directory of .sql files.
#
#   migrations/0001_create_users.sql:
#       -- migrate:up
#       CREATE TABLE users (id bigserial PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL);
#       -- migrate:down
#       DROP TABLE users;
#
#   import migrate
#   import pg
#
#   fn main() Result[int, str]:
#       p = pg.pool(os.env("DATABASE_URL", ""), 8)
#       done = migrate.postgres(p).up("migrations")?        # or migrate.sqlite(sqlite.open("app.db"))
#       print(f"applied {len(done)} migrations")
#       ...
#
# Or a migration command of its own (`tern run migrate.tn -- up | down [N] | status | new NAME`):
#
#   fn main() Result[int, str]:
#       return migrate.cli("migrations", os.env("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:app.db"))
#
# Databases:
#   migrate.postgres(p pg.Pool) Target     migrate.sqlite(d sqlite.Db) Target
#   migrate.open(url str) Result[Target, str]      postgres://... or sqlite:PATH
# Running (dir: the migrations directory; each returns the migrations it ran, in order):
#   t.up(dir) Result[[Migration], str]              every pending migration, oldest first
#   t.down(dir, n int) Result[[Migration], str]     undo the newest n applied migrations
#   t.status(dir) Result[[Status], str]             Status fields: version, name, state
#                                                   ("applied" "pending" "changed" "missing"), applied_at
#   t.apply(ms [Migration])  t.rollback(ms, n)  t.report(ms)     the same, for migrations you
#                                                   built in code (migrate.parse) instead of files
# Files:
#   migrate.load(dir) Result[[Migration], str]      Migration fields: version, name, up, down,
#                                                   transaction, checksum
#   migrate.parse(version int, name str, text str) Result[Migration, str]
#   migrate.create(dir, name) Result[str, str]      a new, empty migration file; its path
#   migrate.label(m) str                            "0001_create_users"
#   migrate.label_of(s Status) str                  the same, for a Status
#   migrate.cli(dir, url) Result[int, str]          up, down [N], status, new NAME (os.args())
#   migrate.command(dir, url, args) Result[int, str]    ... with the arguments given
#   migrate.split_statements(sql) [str]             a script's statements (quotes, $$ bodies and
#                                                   comments understood)
#
# Files are named VERSION_NAME.sql: 0001_create_users.sql, or a timestamp,
# 20260928120000_add_email.sql. The version is the number; they run in version order. A file
# holds the up SQL, and optionally `-- migrate:down` followed by the SQL that undoes it (or
# put that in VERSION_NAME.down.sql next to VERSION_NAME.up.sql). `-- migrate:no-transaction`
# runs it outside a transaction, for statements that refuse one (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY,
# ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE on old servers, VACUUM); keep those to one statement per file.
#
# How it runs:
# - Each migration runs in a transaction together with its row in the tern_migrations table,
#   so it is applied completely or not at all. (PostgreSQL rolls back DDL too; SQLite does,
#   except that some PRAGMAs do nothing inside a transaction.)
# - Only one run at a time: on PostgreSQL a run holds an advisory lock on a connection of its
#   own (so several instances of an app can all call up() as they start: one applies, the
#   others wait and then find nothing to do); on SQLite each migration takes the write lock.
# - An applied migration must not change: up() refuses to run if a file's up SQL differs
#   from what was applied (state "changed"). Put the change in a new migration.
# - A migration in the database but not in the directory ("missing": the code was rolled
#   back to an older version) is allowed, and reported by status.
# - A pending migration older than the newest applied one (merged from another branch) is
#   applied like any other.
# - Not available on wasm.

import crypto
import sqlite
import fmt
import fs
import os
import pg
import task
import time

struct Status:
    version: int
    name: str
    state: str                  # "applied", "pending", "changed", or "missing"
    applied_at: str             # "2026-09-28T12:00:00Z" ("" if pending)

fn up(t: Target, dir: str) Result[[Migration], str]:
    ms = load(dir)?
    return apply(t, ms)

fn down(t: Target, dir: str, n: int) Result[[Migration], str]:
    ms = load(dir)?
    return rollback(t, ms, n)

fn status(t: Target, dir: str) Result[[Status], str]:
    ms = load(dir)?
    return report(t, ms)

fn apply(t: Target, ms: [Migration]) Result[[Migration], str]:
    s = _begin(t)?
    r = _apply_all(s, ms)
    _end(s)
    return r

fn rollback(t: Target, ms: [Migration], n: int) Result[[Migration], str]:
    s = _begin(t)?
    r = _rollback_newest(s, ms, n)
    _end(s)
    return r

fn report(t: Target, ms: [Migration]) Result[[Status], str]:
    s = _begin(t)?
    r = _applied(s)
    _end(s)
    return Ok(_states(ms, r?))

fn label(m: Migration) str:
    return _label(m.version, m.name)

fn label_of(s: Status) str:
    return _label(s.version, s.name)

fn _label(version: int, name: str) str:
    return f"{fmt.zero_pad(version, 4)}_{name}"

# a new migration file in dir (created if needed), numbered after the newest one
fn create(dir: str, name: str) Result[str, str]:
    for ch in name:
        if not (_ident_byte(ch.byte(0)) and ch != "$"):
            return Err(f"migrate: name a migration with letters, digits and _ (like add_email), not `{name}`")
    if not fs.exists(dir) and not fs.mkdir(dir):
        return Err("migrate: " + fs.error())
    files = _files(dir)?
    path = dir + "/" + next_file(files.keys(), name)
    fs.try_write(path, "-- migrate:up\n\n\n-- migrate:down\n\n").context("migrate")?
    return Ok(path)

fn _apply_all(s: Target, ms: [Migration]) Result[[Migration], str]:
    done: {int: str} = {}
    applied = _applied(s)?
    for a in applied:
        done[a.version] = a.checksum
    todo: [Migration] = []
    sorted = ms.sort_by(fn(m) m.version)
    for m in sorted:
        if not (m.version in done):
            todo.push(m)
        elif done[m.version] != m.checksum:
            return Err(f"migrate: {label(m)} was changed after it was applied; undo the edit and put the change in a new migration")
    ran: [Migration] = []
    for m in todo:
        if _apply(s, m)?:
            ran.push(m)
    return Ok(ran)

fn _rollback_newest(s: Target, ms: [Migration], n: int) Result[[Migration], str]:
    by_version: {int: Migration} = {}
    for m in ms:
        by_version[m.version] = m
    applied = _applied(s)?
    undo: [Migration] = []
    i = len(applied) - 1
    while i >= 0 and len(undo) < n:
        a = applied[i]
        if not (a.version in by_version):
            return Err(f"migrate: can't roll back {_label(a.version, a.name)}: its file is gone")
        m = by_version[a.version]
        if m.down == "":
            return Err(f"migrate: can't roll back {label(m)}: it has no `-- migrate:down` section")
        undo.push(m)
        i -= 1
    for m in undo:
        _revert(s, m)?
    return Ok(undo)

fn _states(ms: [Migration], applied: [Applied]) [Status]:
    got: {int: Applied} = {}
    for a in applied:
        got[a.version] = a
    known: {int: bool} = {}
    out: [Status] = []
    for m in ms:
        known[m.version] = true
        if m.version in got:
            a = got[m.version]
            out.push(Status(m.version, m.name, "applied" if a.checksum == m.checksum else "changed", a.applied_at))
        else:
            out.push(Status(m.version, m.name, "pending", ""))
    for a in applied:
        if not (a.version in known):
            out.push(Status(a.version, a.name, "missing", a.applied_at))
    return out.sort_by(fn(s) s.version)

# A migration command: up, down [N], status, new NAME (from os.args()). url: see open().
fn cli(dir: str, url: str) Result[int, str]:
    return command(dir, url, os.args()[1..])

# the same, with the arguments given
fn command(dir: str, url: str, args: [str]) Result[int, str]:
    cmd = args[0] if len(args) > 0 else ""
    if cmd == "new":
        if len(args) != 2:
            return Err("usage: new NAME (like: new add_email)")
        print("created", create(dir, args[1])?)
        return Ok(0)
    if not (cmd in ["up", "down", "status"]) or len(args) > 2 or (len(args) == 2 and cmd != "down"):
        return Err("usage: up | down [N] | status | new NAME")
    t = open(url)?
    if cmd == "up":
        ran = up(t, dir)?
        for m in ran:
            print("applied", label(m))
        if len(ran) == 0:
            print("nothing to apply")
    elif cmd == "down":
        n = args[1].to_int(0) if len(args) == 2 else 1
        if n < 1:
            return Err(f"down: N is how many migrations to undo, not `{args[1]}`")
        for m in down(t, dir, n)?:
            print("rolled back", label(m))
    else:
        for st in status(t, dir)?:
            print(f"{fmt.pad_right(st.state, 8, " ")} {label_of(st)}  {st.applied_at}".trim())
    return Ok(0)
```

## library/migrate/store.tn

```tern
# migrate: the migrations table, locking, and running migrations, for PostgreSQL and SQLite

enum Target:
    Postgres(p: pg.Pool)
    Sqlite(d: sqlite.Db)

struct Applied:
    version: int
    name: str
    checksum: str
    applied_at: str

const TABLE = "tern_migrations"
const LOCK_KEY = 7271047361946082313            # pg advisory lock: one migration run at a time

fn postgres(p: pg.Pool) Target:
    return Target.Postgres(p)

fn sqlite(d: sqlite.Db) Target:
    return Target.Sqlite(d)

# postgres://... or postgresql://... (PostgreSQL), sqlite:PATH or a file path (SQLite)
fn open(url: str) Result[Target, str]:
    if url.starts_with("postgres://") or url.starts_with("postgresql://"):
        p = pg.connect(url)
        if not p.ok():
            return Err("migrate: can't connect: " + pg.error())
        return Ok(Target.Postgres(p))
    path = url
    if url.starts_with("sqlite://"):
        path = url[9..]
    elif url.starts_with("sqlite:"):
        path = url[7..]
    if path == "":
        return Err("migrate: no database given (postgres://user:pass@host/db, or sqlite:app.db)")
    return Ok(Target.Sqlite(sqlite.open(path)))

# A run starts here. PostgreSQL: a connection of its own that holds the advisory lock until
# _end (other runs wait for it); SQLite: each migration takes the write lock instead.
fn _begin(t: Target) Result[Target, str]:
    match t:
        Postgres(p):
            own = pg.connect(p.url)
            if not own.ok():
                return Err("migrate: can't connect: " + pg.error())
            r = _pg_setup(own)
            if r is Err(e):
                own.close()
                return Err(e)
            return Ok(Target.Postgres(own))
        Sqlite(d):
            d.run_script(f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {TABLE} (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, checksum TEXT NOT NULL, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')))").context("migrate")?
            return Ok(t)

fn _pg_setup(p: pg.Pool) Result[int, str]:
    # Waiting runs poll instead of blocking in pg_advisory_lock(): a session blocked there is
    # in the middle of a statement, holding a snapshot, and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in the
    # running migration waits for every snapshot: a deadlock that PostgreSQL breaks by
    # failing the index build.
    wait = 5
    while true:
        rows = p.query("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)::int AS ok", [str(LOCK_KEY)])
        if len(rows) == 0:
            return Err("migrate: taking the lock: " + pg.error())
        if rows[0]["ok"] == "1":
            break
        task.sleep(wait)
        wait = min(wait * 2, 250)
    p.run_script(f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {TABLE} (version bigint PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL, checksum text NOT NULL, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())").context("migrate")?
    return Ok(0)

fn _end(s: Target):
    if s is Postgres(p):
        p.close()                       # ending the session releases the lock

fn _applied(s: Target) Result[[Applied], str]:
    match s:
        Postgres(p):
            rows = p.fetch[Applied](f"SELECT version, name, checksum, to_char(applied_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"') AS applied_at FROM {TABLE} ORDER BY version", []).context("migrate")?
            return Ok(rows)
        Sqlite(d):
            rows: [Applied] = []
            d.query_into(f"SELECT version, name, checksum, applied_at FROM {TABLE} ORDER BY version", [], &rows)
            return Ok(rows)

# Applies m and records it, together. Ok(false): another process applied it first (SQLite).
fn _apply(s: Target, m: Migration) Result[bool, str]:
    record = f"INSERT INTO {TABLE} (version, name, checksum) VALUES ({m.version}, {_quote(m.name)}, {_quote(m.checksum)})"
    match s:
        Postgres(p):
            _pg_still_locked(p)?
            if m.transaction:
                _pg_tx(p, m, m.up, record)?
            else:
                statements = split_statements(m.up)
                for st in statements:
                    p.run_script(st).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                p.run_script(record).context("migrate")?
            return Ok(true)
        Sqlite(d):
            if not m.transaction:
                d.run_script(m.up).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                d.run_script(record).context("migrate")?
                return Ok(true)
            d.run_script("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").context("migrate")?
            if len(d.query(f"SELECT 1 AS x FROM {TABLE} WHERE version = ?", [str(m.version)])) > 0:
                d.run_script("COMMIT").context("migrate")?
                return Ok(false)
            _sqlite_tx(d, m, m.up, record)?
            return Ok(true)

# Undoes m (its down SQL) and forgets it, together.
fn _revert(s: Target, m: Migration) Result[bool, str]:
    forget = f"DELETE FROM {TABLE} WHERE version = {m.version}"
    match s:
        Postgres(p):
            _pg_still_locked(p)?
            if m.transaction:
                _pg_tx(p, m, m.down, forget)?
            else:
                statements = split_statements(m.down)
                for st in statements:
                    p.run_script(st).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                p.run_script(forget).context("migrate")?
            return Ok(true)
        Sqlite(d):
            if not m.transaction:
                d.run_script(m.down).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                d.run_script(forget).context("migrate")?
                return Ok(true)
            d.run_script("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").context("migrate")?
            _sqlite_tx(d, m, m.down, forget)?
            return Ok(true)

# one round trip: the migration's SQL and the bookkeeping commit or roll back together
fn _pg_tx(p: pg.Pool, m: Migration, sql: str, then: str) Result[int, str]:
    r = p.run_script("BEGIN;\n" + sql + "\n;\n" + then + ";\nCOMMIT;")
    if r is Err(e):
        p.run_script("ROLLBACK")                # the script stopped inside its transaction
        return Err(_failed(m, e))
    return Ok(0)

fn _sqlite_tx(d: sqlite.Db, m: Migration, sql: str, then: str) Result[int, str]:
    r = d.run_script(sql + "\n;\n" + then + ";\nCOMMIT;")
    if r is Err(e):
        d.run_script("ROLLBACK")
        return Err(_failed(m, e))
    return Ok(0)

# The run's connection holds the lock; if it was lost and replaced, a new one must get it
# back before anything else happens (pg_try_advisory_lock is re-entrant for its holder).
fn _pg_still_locked(p: pg.Pool) Result[int, str]:
    rows = p.query("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)::int AS ok", [str(LOCK_KEY)])
    if len(rows) == 0 or rows[0]["ok"] != "1":
        return Err("migrate: lost the migration lock (the connection dropped and another run holds it now); run again")
    return Ok(0)

fn _failed(m: Migration, e: str) str:
    why = e
    for prefix in ["pg: script failed: ", "sqlite: script failed: "]:
        if why.starts_with(prefix):
            why = why[len(prefix)..]
    return f"migrate: {label(m)} failed: {why}"

fn _quote(s: str) str:
    return "'" + s.replace("'", "''") + "'"
```

## library/pg/pg.tn

```tern
# pg: a PostgreSQL client for tasks: a connection pool, parameters bound safely, rows read
# into your structs, and transactions that belong to the task that started them.
#
#   import pg
#   import json
#
#   struct World:
#       id: int
#       randomNumber: int
#
#   db = pg.pool("postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/app", 16)   # 16 connections, shared by every task
#   if not db.ok():
#       print(pg.error())                          # why the first connection failed
#   n = db.exec("UPDATE world SET randomNumber = $1 WHERE id = $2", ["42", "7"])    # rows changed (-1: error)
#   rows = db.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1", ["7"])            # [{str: str}]
#   worlds: [World] = []
#   json.decode(db.query_json("SELECT id, randomNumber FROM world LIMIT 5", []), &worlds)
#   w = World(0, 0)
#   json.decode(db.query_row_json("SELECT * FROM world WHERE id = $1", ["7"]), &w)
#
#   db.begin()                                     # from here until commit/rollback, this task's
#   db.exec("INSERT INTO log (msg) VALUES ($1)", ["hi"])    # statements run on one connection,
#   db.commit()                                    # which no other task can use meanwhile
#
# Functions (a Pool is shared by copying it, like a channel):
#   pg.pool(url str, size int) Pool     at most size connections, opened as needed (the first
#                                       one right away, so p.ok() can report a bad url or password)
#   pg.connect(url str) Pool            pg.pool(url, 1)
#   p.ok() bool                         pg.error() str: why the last call failed ("" after a success)
#   p.exec(sql str, params [str]) int   rows affected, or -1 (pg.error() has the server's message,
#                                       e.g. "ERROR 23505: duplicate key value violates unique constraint ...")
#   p.query(sql str, params [str]) [{str: str}]     every value as text; NULL is ""
#   p.query_json(sql str, params [str]) str         the rows as a JSON array: numbers, booleans and
#                                                   null stay typed, so json.decode fills structs
#   p.query_row_json(sql str, params [str]) str     the first row as a JSON object ("null" if none)
#   p.begin() bool  p.commit() bool  p.rollback() bool
#   p.run_script(sql str) Result[int, str]   several statements (a schema, a migration): the
#                                       simple query protocol, no parameters
#   p.describe(sql str) Result[Statement, str]    the types of its parameters and columns,
#                                       without running it (see "describing a statement" below)
#   pg.array_int(xs) str  array_float  array_bool  array_str     a list as one parameter:
#                                       `WHERE id = ANY($1)` with [pg.array_int(ids)]
#   pg.NULL                             a parameter that is NULL
#   p.stats() PoolStats                 size open idle in_use waiting waits wait_ms timeouts opened closed
#   p.prune()                           closes the connections idle longer than max_idle (the
#                                       pool also does this by itself now and then)
#   p.close()                           closes the idle connections
#
# Parameters are $1, $2, ... and are sent separately from the SQL (no injection), as text;
# PostgreSQL converts them to the column types; pg.NULL is NULL. Statements are prepared on
# each connection the first time and reused after that.
#
# Transactions are bound to the task: any statement that leaves its connection inside a
# transaction (begin(), or exec("BEGIN")) keeps that connection for the task until the
# transaction ends, so other tasks never see or join it. A task that waits (a channel, a
# socket, a sleep) in the middle of a transaction keeps holding its connection.
#
# URL: postgres://user:password@host:port/dbname?sslmode=require (sslmode=require or
# verify-full need `import tls`; the default is no TLS); &application_name=app names the
# connections in pg_stat_activity (default: tern). Login: SCRAM-SHA-256 (PostgreSQL's
# default) or password. Not available on wasm.
# The pool: &pool_timeout=30s (how long a statement waits for a free connection, then fails),
# &max_lifetime=1h (a connection is replaced after this long), &max_idle=30m (an idle one is
# closed), &statement_cache=off (no prepared statements kept: PgBouncer); 0 turns a limit off.
# A connection the server closed is noticed and replaced before it is used.
#
# The protocol is Tern too: wire.tn.

import crypto
import json
import net
import task
import time

struct Pool:
    url: str
    size: int
    free: chan[Conn]            # idle connections; one not live is a slot not connected yet
    state: shared[_State]
    shards: [shared[_Shard]]    # transactions' connections and the waiting counts, by task (see _Shard)
    key: str                    # the task-local that marks a task holding one of its connections
    first_ok: bool
    timeout_ms: int             # ?pool_timeout: how long a task waits for a free connection (0: forever)
    lifetime_ms: int            # ?max_lifetime: a connection is replaced after this long (0: never)
    idle_ms: int                # ?max_idle: an idle connection is closed after this long (0: never)

# what p.stats() reports
struct PoolStats:
    size: int                   # the most connections it opens
    open: int                   # connections open now
    idle: int                   # ... of them not in use
    in_use: int                 # ... running a statement, or held by a task's transaction
    waiting: int                # tasks waiting for a connection now
    waits: int                  # times a task had to wait (every connection was in use)
    wait_ms: int                # ... and the milliseconds it waited, added up
    timeouts: int               # waits that gave up after pool_timeout
    opened: int                 # connections opened, ever
    closed: int                 # ... and closed (broken, too old, idle too long, p.close())

# What the tasks using a pool share, behind a lock. A statement that finds a free connection
# doesn't take it: only opening and closing connections do.
struct _State:
    stats: PoolStats            # (idle and in_use are worked out by stats(); the waiting counts
                                # are the shards')
    pruned: int                 # when idle connections were last closed (time.mono_ms)

# What transactions and waits touch, split by task.id() over _SHARDS locks. Each statement in
# a transaction takes its task's connection out and puts it back; with one lock for the pool,
# tasks queued on it, and a lock handed to a task that has to be woken first is held all the
# while it waits to run (a convoy: every statement of every transaction waited in it).
struct _Shard:
    bound: {int: Conn}          # connections held by a task's open transaction, by task.id()
    waiting: int                # (PoolStats' fields of the same names, for these tasks)
    waits: int
    wait_ms: int
    timeouts: int

const _SHARDS = 32

fn _shard(p: Pool, tid: int) shared[_Shard]:
    return p.shards[tid % len(p.shards)]

fn pool(url: str, size: int) Pool:
    n = max(size, 1)
    free: chan[Conn] = task.channel(0)
    first = _open(url)
    st = _State(PoolStats(n, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), time.mono_ms())
    if first.live:
        st.stats.open = 1
        st.stats.opened = 1
    ok = first.live
    free.send(first)
    for i in 1..n:
        free.send(_no_conn())
    key = "pg.tx." + crypto.hex(crypto.random_bytes(8))
    shards: [shared[_Shard]] = []
    for i in 0.._SHARDS:
        shards.push(task.shared(_Shard({}, 0, 0, 0, 0)))
    return Pool(url, n, free, task.shared(st), shards, key, ok, _ms(_param(url, "pool_timeout"), 30000),
                _ms(_param(url, "max_lifetime"), 3600000), _ms(_param(url, "max_idle"), 1800000))

fn connect(url: str) Pool:
    return pool(url, 1)

fn ok(p: Pool) bool:
    return p.first_ok

# the counters, and how many connections are idle and in use right now
fn stats(p: Pool) PoolStats:
    idle = 0
    for i in 0..len(p.free):
        c = _no_conn()
        if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
            break
        if c.live:
            idle += 1
        p.free.send(c)
    s = p.state.get().stats
    for sh in p.shards:
        w = sh.get()
        s.waiting += w.waiting
        s.waits += w.waits
        s.wait_ms += w.wait_ms
        s.timeouts += w.timeouts
    s.idle = idle
    s.in_use = max(s.open - idle, 0)
    return s

# why the last call on this task failed ("" after a success)
fn error() str:
    return task.local_get("pg.error")

fn _set_err(msg: str):
    if msg != "" or task.local_get("pg.error") != "":
        task.local_set("pg.error", msg)

# The connection for a statement: the task's own (in a transaction), or one from the pool
# that is still good (not broken, too old, idle too long, or closed by the server). Not
# live: none (pg.error() says why).
fn _take(p: Pool) Conn:
    if task.local_get(p.key) != "":             # this task holds one, in a transaction
        tid = task.id()
        mine = _shard(p, tid).update(fn(s) _held(&s, tid))
        if mine is Some(held):
            return held
    c = _no_conn()
    if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
        got = _wait(p)
        if got is Some(w):
            c = w
        else:
            return _no_conn()
    closed = 0
    if c.live and (c.broken or _stale(p, c)):
        _close_conn(c)
        closed = 1
        idled = p.idle_ms > 0 and time.mono_ms() - c.used_ms > p.idle_ms
        c = _no_conn()
        if idled:
            prune(p)                                 # (the others have likely idled too)
    if c.live:
        return c
    c = _open(p.url)
    opened = 1 if c.live else 0
    p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, opened - closed, opened, closed))
    if not c.live:
        p.free.send(_no_conn())
    return c

fn _held(s: mut _Shard, tid: int) Option[Conn]:
    if not (tid in s.bound):
        return None
    c = s.bound[tid]
    s.bound.remove(tid)
    return Some(c)

fn _count(s: mut _State, open: int, opened: int, closed: int) int:
    s.stats.open += open
    s.stats.opened += opened
    s.stats.closed += closed
    return 0

# every connection is in use: wait for one, up to pool_timeout
fn _wait(p: Pool) Option[Conn]:
    sh = _shard(p, task.id())
    sh.update(fn(s) _waiting(&s, 1, 0, false))
    t0 = time.mono_ms()
    c = _no_conn()
    got = true
    if p.timeout_ms > 0:
        got = p.free.recv_timeout(&c, p.timeout_ms)
    else:
        c = p.free.recv()
    waited = time.mono_ms() - t0
    sh.update(fn(s) _waiting(&s, -1, waited, not got))
    if not got:
        busy = "the pool's one connection is" if p.size == 1 else f"all {p.size} connections are"
        _set_err(f"pg: no connection free after {p.timeout_ms} ms: {busy} in use (a bigger pool, shorter transactions, or a longer ?pool_timeout=)")
        return None
    return Some(c)

fn _waiting(s: mut _Shard, now: int, waited: int, gave_up: bool) int:
    s.waiting += now
    if now < 0:
        s.waits += 1
        s.wait_ms += waited
    if gave_up:
        s.timeouts += 1
    return 0

fn _stale(p: Pool, c: Conn) bool:
    now = time.mono_ms()
    jitter = c.born_ms % 10 * (p.lifetime_ms / 100)     # (up to 9% early: not all at once)
    if p.lifetime_ms > 0 and now - c.born_ms > p.lifetime_ms - jitter:
        return true
    idle = now - c.used_ms
    if p.idle_ms > 0 and idle > p.idle_ms:
        return true
    return idle >= 100 and c.sock.pending()          # the server closed it (a restart, a kill)

# after a statement: keep the connection for the task while a transaction is open
fn _give_back(p: Pool, c: Conn):
    if not c.live:
        return
    if c.broken:
        _close_conn(c)
        p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, -1, 0, 1))
        p.free.send(_no_conn())
        _unmark(p)
        return
    if c.txs != 73:                                  # in a transaction ('T', or 'E': failed)
        tid = task.id()
        _shard(p, tid).update(fn(s) _hold(&s, tid, c))
        task.local_set(p.key, "1")
        return
    _unmark(p)
    back = c
    back.used_ms = time.mono_ms()
    back.uses += 1
    p.free.send(back)
    if p.idle_ms > 0 and back.uses % 256 == 0:       # now and then: close idle connections
        every = min(p.idle_ms / 2, 60000)
        now = back.used_ms
        if p.state.update(fn(s) _due(&s, now, every)):
            prune(p)

fn _unmark(p: Pool):
    if task.local_get(p.key) != "":
        task.local_set(p.key, "")

fn _hold(s: mut _Shard, tid: int, c: Conn) int:
    s.bound[tid] = c
    return 0

fn _due(s: mut _State, now: int, every: int) bool:
    if now - s.pruned < every:
        return false
    s.pruned = now
    return true

# Closes the connections idle longer than max_idle, so a pool shrinks after a busy spell.
# The pool does this by itself now and then, as connections come back.
fn prune(p: Pool):
    if p.idle_ms <= 0:
        return
    now = time.mono_ms()
    closed = 0
    for i in 0..len(p.free):
        c = _no_conn()
        if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
            break
        if c.live and now - c.used_ms > p.idle_ms:
            _close_conn(c)
            closed += 1
            c = _no_conn()
        p.free.send(c)
    if closed > 0:
        p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, -closed, 0, closed))

# closes the idle connections (the pool opens new ones when it needs them again)
fn close(p: Pool):
    closed = 0
    for i in 0..len(p.free):
        c = _no_conn()
        if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
            break
        if c.live:
            _close_conn(c)
            closed += 1
        p.free.send(_no_conn())
    if closed > 0:
        p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, -closed, 0, closed))

# a URL's ?name=value ("" if it has none)
fn _param(url: str, name: str) str:
    q = url.find("?")
    if q < 0:
        return ""
    for kv in url[q + 1..].split("&"):
        if kv.starts_with(name + "="):
            return kv[len(name) + 1..]
    return ""

# "5s", "500ms", "30m", "1h", "90" (seconds), "0" (off) -> milliseconds; dflt if empty or not one
fn _ms(text: str, dflt: int) int:
    units = [("ms", 1), ("s", 1000), ("m", 60000), ("h", 3600000)]
    for u in units:
        if text.ends_with(u.0) and len(text) > len(u.0):
            n = text[..len(text) - len(u.0)].to_float(-1.0)
            if n >= 0.0:
                return int(n * float(u.1))
    n = text.to_float(-1.0)
    if n >= 0.0 and text != "":
        return int(n * 1000.0)
    return dflt

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- statements

fn exec(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) int:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return -1
    r = _run(&c, sql, params, 0)
    _give_back(p, c)
    return r.affected if r.ok else -1

fn _rows(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str], mode: int) str:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return "null" if mode == 3 else ("" if mode == 4 else "[]")
    r = _run(&c, sql, params, mode)
    _give_back(p, c)
    if not r.ok:
        return "null" if mode == 3 else ("" if mode == 4 else "[]")
    return r.out

fn query_json(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) str:
    return _rows(p, sql, params, 1)

fn query_row_json(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) str:
    return _rows(p, sql, params, 3)

fn query(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) [{str: str}]:
    rows: [{str: str}] = []
    json.decode(_rows(p, sql, params, 2), &rows)
    return rows

fn begin(p: Pool) bool:
    return exec(p, "BEGIN", []) >= 0

fn commit(p: Pool) bool:
    return exec(p, "COMMIT", []) >= 0

fn rollback(p: Pool) bool:
    return exec(p, "ROLLBACK", []) >= 0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- with Result
# The same queries, returning Result: rows decoded straight into your struct type, and the
# server's message as the error ("pg: query failed: ERROR 42P01: relation \"x\" does not exist").
#   users: [User] = db.fetch("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE team = $1", [team])?
#   u = db.fetch_one[User]("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1", [id])?     # Option[User]
#   n = db.run("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires < now()", [])?                 # rows affected

fn _fail(what: str) str:
    return "pg: " + what + ": " + error()

fn fetch[T](p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) Result[[T], str]:
    raw = _rows(p, sql, params, 4)               # the rows as the server sent them
    if error() != "":
        return Err(_fail("query failed"))
    rows: [T] = []
    if not _decode_rows(raw, &rows):             # decoded by code made for T
        why = _decode_error()                    # (which value didn't fit which field)
        if why != "":
            return Err("pg: query failed: " + why)
        return Err("pg: query failed: the rows don't fit the type (check the column names and types)")
    return Ok(rows)

fn fetch_one[T](p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) Result[Option[T], str]:
    rows: [T] = fetch(p, sql, params)?
    none: Option[T] = None
    if len(rows) == 0:
        return Ok(none)
    return Ok(Some(rows[0]))

fn run(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) Result[int, str]:
    n = exec(p, sql, params)
    if n < 0:
        return Err(_fail("statement failed"))
    return Ok(n)

# several statements in one string (a schema file, a migration), run with the simple query
# protocol: in one implicit transaction unless the script has its own BEGIN / COMMIT, and
# with no $1 parameters. The rows affected, added up; the first error stops the script.
fn run_script(p: Pool, sql: str) Result[int, str]:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return Err(_fail("script failed"))
    r = _script(&c, sql)
    _give_back(p, c)
    if not r.ok:
        return Err(_fail("script failed"))
    return Ok(r.affected)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- describing a statement
# What the server knows about a statement, without running it: the types of its $1, $2, ...
# parameters and of the columns it returns (the base for generating typed query code).
#   s = db.describe("SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE id = $1")?
#   s.params                    ["int8"]
#   s.columns[1]                Column{name: "email", type_name: "text", table: "users", not_null: false, ...}

struct Column:
    name: str
    type_name: str              # pg_type.typname: "int8", "text", "timestamptz", "_int4" (int4[]), ...
    type_oid: int
    kind: str                   # pg_type.typtype: "b" base, "e" enum, "d" domain, "c" composite, ...
    base_type: str              # a domain's underlying type ("" otherwise)
    table: str                  # the table (or view) the column comes from; "" for an expression
    not_null: bool              # a table column declared NOT NULL (an outer join can still make it null)

struct Statement:
    params: [str]               # the type names of $1, $2, ...
    param_oids: [int]
    param_kinds: [str]          # ... and their pg_type.typtype ("e": an enum)
    columns: [Column]           # [] for a statement that returns no rows

struct _Type:
    oid: int
    name: str
    kind: str
    base: str

struct _Attr:
    rel: int
    num: int
    notnull: bool
    relname: str

fn describe(p: Pool, sql: str) Result[Statement, str]:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return Err(_fail("describe failed"))
    got = _describe_raw(&c, sql)
    _give_back(p, c)
    raw = got.map_err(fn(e) "pg: describe failed: " + e.replace("pg: ", ""))?
    oids: [int] = []
    rels: [int] = []
    for o in raw.params:
        oids.push(o)
    for c in raw.columns:
        oids.push(c.oid)
        if c.table != 0:
            rels.push(c.table)
    types: {int: _Type} = {}
    ts = fetch[_Type](p, "SELECT t.oid::int8 AS oid, t.typname::text AS name, t.typtype::text AS kind, coalesce(b.typname::text, '') AS base FROM pg_type t LEFT JOIN pg_type b ON b.oid = t.typbasetype AND t.typtype = 'd' WHERE t.oid = ANY($1::oid[])", [_oid_array(oids)])?
    for t in ts:
        types[t.oid] = t
    attrs: {str: _Attr} = {}
    if len(rels) > 0:
        as_ = fetch[_Attr](p, "SELECT a.attrelid::int8 AS rel, a.attnum::int8 AS num, a.attnotnull AS notnull, c.relname::text AS relname FROM pg_attribute a JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = a.attrelid WHERE a.attrelid = ANY($1::oid[]) AND a.attnum > 0", [_oid_array(rels)])?
        for a in as_:
            attrs[f"{a.rel}.{a.num}"] = a
    out = Statement([], [], [], [])
    for o in raw.params:
        out.params.push(_type_of(types, o).name)
        out.param_kinds.push(_type_of(types, o).kind)
        out.param_oids.push(o)
    for c in raw.columns:
        t = _type_of(types, c.oid)
        col = Column(c.name, t.name, c.oid, t.kind, t.base, "", false)
        key = f"{c.table}.{c.column}"
        if c.table != 0 and key in attrs:
            col.table = attrs[key].relname
            col.not_null = attrs[key].notnull
        out.columns.push(col)
    return Ok(out)

fn _type_of(types: {int: _Type}, oid: int) _Type:
    if oid in types:
        return types[oid]
    return _Type(oid, "unknown", "", "")

fn _oid_array(xs: [int]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) str(x))) + "}"

# A parameter that is SQL NULL: pass pg.NULL in params (["x", pg.NULL]). It is the one-byte
# string "\x00", which PostgreSQL text can never contain.
const NULL = "\x00"

# Arrays as parameters, in PostgreSQL's text form: `WHERE id = ANY($1)` with [pg.array_int(ids)].
# (Rows read arrays back into [int], [float], [bool] and [str] fields by themselves.)
fn array_int(xs: [int]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) str(x))) + "}"

fn array_float(xs: [float]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) str(x))) + "}"

fn array_bool(xs: [bool]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) "t" if x else "f")) + "}"

fn array_str(xs: [str]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) "\"" + x.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"")) + "}"
```

## library/pg/wire.tn

```tern
# pg: the PostgreSQL wire protocol (version 3), in Tern (pg.tn builds the API on it):
# connecting (TLS through SSLRequest; SCRAM-SHA-256 or password logins), statements through
# the extended protocol with each connection's prepared statements kept by their SQL, scripts
# through the simple protocol, and replies read into what the API returns.

# a statement prepared on a connection
struct Stmt:
    name: str                   # "t3" ("": unnamed, prepared again each time)
    cols: [str]                 # the columns it returns
    keys: [str]                 # ... as JSON keys: "\"id\":"
    types: [int]                # ... and their type OIDs
    head: str                   # Bind's constant start: portal, name, parameter formats ("": not prepared)
    fmts: str                   # ... and its result formats for pg.fetch (numbers in binary; "": all text)

struct Conn:
    sock: net.Conn
    live: bool                  # false: no connection (an empty slot in a pool)
    buf: str                    # bytes read and not used yet, from `at` on
    at: int
    ms: int                     # the message just read: where its body starts in buf,
    ml: int                     # ... its length,
    mt: int                     # ... and its type ('D', 'Z', ...)
    stmts: {str: Stmt}          # the statements prepared here, by their SQL
    txs: int                    # from ReadyForQuery: 'I' idle, 'T' in a transaction, 'E' a failed one
    broken: bool
    no_cache: bool              # ?statement_cache=off: unnamed statements only (PgBouncer)
    born_ms: int                # opened, and last used (time.mono_ms): for the pool
    used_ms: int
    uses: int                   # statements run (the pool looks at idle connections every so often)

# what a statement's reply comes to
struct Reply:
    ok: bool
    affected: int               # rows changed (or returned)
    out: str                    # the rows: JSON (modes 1-3) or raw (mode 4)

struct Url:
    user: str
    password: str
    host: str
    port: int
    db: str
    ssl: str
    app: str
    cache: str

fn _no_conn() Conn:
    return Conn(net.Conn(-1), false, "", 0, 0, 0, 0, {}, 73, true, false, 0, 0, 0)

fn _fail_reply(msg: str) Reply:
    _set_err(msg)
    return Reply(false, -1, "")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- bytes

fn _u32(n: int) str:
    return chr((n >> 24) & 255) + chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255)

fn _u16(n: int) str:
    return chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255)

fn _le32(n: int) str:                   # (the raw rows' header is read with memcpy: native order)
    return chr(n & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 24) & 255)

fn _msg(t: str, body: str) str:
    return t + _u32(len(body) + 4) + body

fn _be32(s: str, i: int) int:
    return (s.byte(i) << 24) | (s.byte(i + 1) << 16) | (s.byte(i + 2) << 8) | s.byte(i + 3)

fn _be16(s: str, i: int) int:
    return (s.byte(i) << 8) | s.byte(i + 1)

fn _i32(s: str, i: int) int:
    v = _be32(s, i)
    return v - 4294967296 if v >= 2147483648 else v

# the NUL-terminated string at s[i..] (before e)
fn _cstr(s: str, i: int, e: int) str:
    j = i
    while j < e and s.byte(j) != 0:
        j += 1
    return s[i..j]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reading and writing

# at least n bytes from c.at in c.buf
fn _read(c: mut Conn, n: int) bool:
    while len(c.buf) - c.at < n:
        got = c.sock.refill(&c.buf, c.at, 65536)       # (what was at c.at is now at 0)
        c.ms -= c.at
        c.at = 0
        if got == 0:
            c.broken = true
            why = net.error()
            _set_err("pg: connection lost" + (" (" + why + ")" if why != "" else ""))
            return false
    return true

# the next message (notices, parameter changes and notifications skipped): c.mt, c.ms, c.ml
fn _next(c: mut Conn) bool:
    while true:
        c.at = c.ms + c.ml
        if len(c.buf) - c.at < 5 and not _read(&c, 5):
            return false
        n = _be32(c.buf, c.at + 1)
        if n < 4 or n > 1073741824:
            c.broken = true
            _set_err("pg: protocol error (bad message length)")
            return false
        c.ms = c.at + 5
        c.ml = 0
        if len(c.buf) - c.at < n + 1 and not _read(&c, n + 1):
            return false
        c.mt = c.buf.byte(c.at)
        c.ms = c.at + 5
        c.ml = n - 4
        if not (c.mt == 78 or c.mt == 83 or c.mt == 65):
            return true
    return false

fn _send(c: mut Conn, out: str) bool:
    if c.sock.write(out):
        return true
    c.broken = true
    why = net.error()
    _set_err("pg: connection lost" + (" (" + why + ")" if why != "" else ""))
    return false

# an ErrorResponse: "ERROR 42P01: relation \"x\" does not exist (DETAIL) hint: HINT"
fn _server_error(c: Conn) str:
    sev = "ERROR"
    code = ""
    msg = ""
    detail = ""
    hint = ""
    i = c.ms
    e = c.ms + c.ml
    while i < e and c.buf.byte(i) != 0:
        f = c.buf.byte(i)
        v = _cstr(c.buf, i + 1, e)
        i += len(v) + 2
        if f == 83:
            sev = v
        elif f == 67:
            code = v
        elif f == 77:
            msg = v
        elif f == 68:
            detail = v
        elif f == 72:
            hint = v
    out = f"{sev} {code}: {msg}"
    if detail != "":
        out += f" ({detail})"
    if hint != "":
        out += " hint: " + hint
    return out

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- connecting

# postgres://user:password@host:port/dbname?sslmode=require&application_name=x&statement_cache=off
fn _parse_url(url: str) Result[Url, str]:
    rest = ""
    if url.starts_with("postgresql://"):
        rest = url[13..]
    elif url.starts_with("postgres://"):
        rest = url[11..]
    else:
        return Err("pg: not a postgres:// url")
    u = Url("postgres", "", "localhost", 5432, "", "prefer", "tern", "")
    query = ""
    q = rest.find("?")
    if q >= 0:
        query = rest[q + 1..]
        rest = rest[..q]
    hostpart = rest
    slash = rest.find("/")
    if slash >= 0:
        u.db = _unescape(rest[slash + 1..])
        hostpart = rest[..slash]
    at = _last(hostpart, "@")
    if at >= 0:
        cred = hostpart[..at]
        hostpart = hostpart[at + 1..]
        colon = cred.find(":")
        if colon >= 0:
            u.user = _unescape(cred[..colon])
            u.password = _unescape(cred[colon + 1..])
        else:
            u.user = _unescape(cred)
    if hostpart.starts_with("["):
        rb = hostpart.find("]")
        if rb < 0:
            return Err("pg: not a postgres:// url")
        u.host = hostpart[1..rb]
        if hostpart[rb + 1..].starts_with(":"):
            u.port = hostpart[rb + 2..].to_int(5432)
    else:
        colon = _last(hostpart, ":")
        if colon >= 0:
            u.port = hostpart[colon + 1..].to_int(5432)
            hostpart = hostpart[..colon]
        if hostpart != "":
            u.host = _unescape(hostpart)
    if u.db == "":
        u.db = u.user
    for kv in query.split("&"):
        eq = kv.find("=")
        if eq < 0:
            continue
        v = _unescape(kv[eq + 1..])
        k = kv[..eq]
        if k == "sslmode":
            u.ssl = v
        elif k == "application_name":
            u.app = v
        elif k == "statement_cache":
            u.cache = v
    return Ok(u)

fn _last(s: str, sub: str) int:        # (sub: one byte)
    b = sub.byte(0)
    i = len(s) - 1
    while i >= 0 and s.byte(i) != b:
        i -= 1
    return i

fn _unescape(s: str) str:             # %40 -> @
    if not s.contains("%"):
        return s
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == "%" and i + 2 < len(s) + 0 and _hex(s.byte(i + 1)) >= 0 and _hex(s.byte(i + 2)) >= 0:
            out += chr(_hex(s.byte(i + 1)) * 16 + _hex(s.byte(i + 2)))
            i += 3
        else:
            out += s[i]
            i += 1
    return out

fn _hex(c: int) int:
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57:
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 102:
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 70:
        return c - 55
    return -1

# a new connection, logged in and ready; or not live, and pg.error() says why
fn _open(url: str) Conn:
    r = _open_r(url)
    if r is Err(e):
        _set_err(e)
        return _no_conn()
    _set_err("")
    return r.unwrap()

fn _open_r(url: str) Result[Conn, str]:
    u = _parse_url(url)?
    sock = net.connect(u.host, u.port)
    if not sock.ok():
        return Err("pg: " + net.error())
    now = time.mono_ms()
    c = Conn(sock, true, "", 0, 0, 0, 0, {}, 73, false, u.cache == "off", now, now, 0)
    r = _login(&c, u)
    if r is Err(e):
        sock.close()
        return Err(e)
    return Ok(c)

fn _login(c: mut Conn, u: Url) Result[int, str]:
    if not (u.ssl in ["disable", "prefer", "allow"]):
        if not _send(&c, _u32(8) + _u32(80877103)):           # SSLRequest
            return Err(error())
        answer = c.sock.read_exact(1)
        if answer != "S":
            return Err("pg: the server doesn't accept TLS connections")
        if not c.sock.starttls(u.host, u.ssl == "verify-full"):
            return Err("pg: " + net.error())
    body = _u32(196608) + "user\x00" + u.user + "\x00database\x00" + u.db + "\x00application_name\x00" + u.app + "\x00client_encoding\x00UTF8\x00\x00"
    if not _send(&c, _u32(len(body) + 4) + body):
        return Err(error())
    while true:
        if not _next(&c):
            return Err(error())
        if c.mt == 69:
            return Err(_server_error(c))
        if c.mt == 90:
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            return Ok(0)
        if c.mt != 82 or c.ml < 4:
            continue                                          # BackendKeyData, ...
        kind = _be32(c.buf, c.ms)
        if kind == 0:
            continue                                          # AuthenticationOk
        if kind == 3:                                         # a password in clear (over TLS, one hopes)
            if not _send(&c, _msg("p", u.password + "\x00")):
                return Err(error())
        elif kind == 10:
            mechs = c.buf[c.ms + 4..c.ms + c.ml]
            if not mechs.contains("SCRAM-SHA-256\x00"):
                return Err("pg: the server wants a SASL mechanism other than SCRAM-SHA-256")
            _scram(&c, u.password)?
        else:
            return Err(f"pg: unsupported authentication method {kind} (use scram-sha-256 or password)")
    return Err("pg: login failed")

# SCRAM-SHA-256 (RFC 5802 / 7677), what PostgreSQL uses by default
fn _scram(c: mut Conn, password: str) Result[int, str]:
    nonce = crypto.base64(crypto.random_bytes(18))
    first_bare = "n=,r=" + nonce
    first = "n,," + first_bare
    if not _send(&c, _msg("p", "SCRAM-SHA-256\x00" + _u32(len(first)) + first)):
        return Err(error())
    server_first = _sasl_reply(&c, 11)?
    rnonce = ""
    salt64 = ""
    iters = 0
    for part in server_first.split(","):
        if part.starts_with("r="):
            rnonce = part[2..]
        elif part.starts_with("s="):
            salt64 = part[2..]
        elif part.starts_with("i="):
            iters = part[2..].to_int(0)
    if not rnonce.starts_with(nonce):
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: bad server message")
    salt = crypto.base64_decode(salt64)
    if salt == "" or iters < 1:
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: bad salt")
    salted = crypto.pbkdf2_sha256(password, salt, iters, 32)
    client_key = crypto.hmac_sha256(salted, "Client Key")
    final_bare = "c=biws,r=" + rnonce
    auth = first_bare + "," + server_first + "," + final_bare
    sig = crypto.hmac_sha256(crypto.sha256(client_key), auth)
    proof = ""
    for i in 0..32:
        proof += chr(client_key.byte(i) ^ sig.byte(i))
    if not _send(&c, _msg("p", final_bare + ",p=" + crypto.base64(proof))):
        return Err(error())
    server_final = _sasl_reply(&c, 12)?
    want = "v=" + crypto.base64(crypto.hmac_sha256(crypto.hmac_sha256(salted, "Server Key"), auth))
    if not server_final.starts_with(want):
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: the server's signature is wrong (not the real server?)")
    return Ok(0)

fn _sasl_reply(c: mut Conn, want: int) Result[str, str]:
    if not _next(&c):
        return Err(error())
    if c.mt == 69:
        return Err(_server_error(c))
    if c.mt != 82 or c.ml < 4 or _be32(c.buf, c.ms) != want:
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: unexpected reply")
    return Ok(c.buf[c.ms + 4..c.ms + c.ml])

fn _close_conn(c: Conn):
    if c.live and not c.broken:
        c.sock.write("X\x00\x00\x00\x04")                    # Terminate
    if c.live:
        c.sock.close()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- statements

# Types a prepared statement's rows bring back in binary, for pg.fetch (mode 4): numbers
# and booleans, which the server then needn't format nor the decoder parse.
fn _binary(oid: int) bool:
    return oid == 16 or oid == 20 or oid == 21 or oid == 23 or oid == 26 or oid == 700 or oid == 701

# Runs sql with params. mode 0: the rows affected; 1: the rows as JSON (typed); 2: as JSON,
# every value a string (NULL: ""); 3: like 1, only the first row, an object ("null": none);
# 4: raw, for the decoders the compiler writes (pg._decode_rows).
fn _run(c: mut Conn, sql: str, params: [str], mode: int) Reply:
    if c.broken:
        return _fail_reply("pg: the connection is broken")
    st = c.stmts.get(sql, Stmt("", [], [], [], "", ""))
    cached = st.head != ""
    pre = ""
    if not cached:
        name = "t" + str(len(c.stmts)) if not c.no_cache and len(c.stmts) < 256 else ""
        st = Stmt(name, [], [], [], "\x00" + name + "\x00\x00\x00", "")
        pre = _msg("P", name + "\x00" + sql + "\x00\x00\x00") + _msg("D", "S" + name + "\x00")
    binary = mode == 4 and cached and st.fmts != ""
    fm = st.fmts if binary else "\x00\x00"
    vals: [str] = []                                          # the parameters, as Bind has them
    size = 0
    for v in params:
        if v == "\x00":
            vals.push("\xff\xff\xff\xff")                     # pg.NULL
            size += 4
        else:
            vals.push(_u32(len(v)))
            vals.push(v)
            size += 4 + len(v)
    out = pre + "B" + _u32(6 + len(st.head) + size + len(fm)) + st.head + _u16(len(params)) + "".join(vals) + fm + "E\x00\x00\x00\x09\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00S\x00\x00\x00\x04"
    if not _send(&c, out):
        return Reply(false, -1, "")
    res = "[" if mode == 1 or mode == 2 else ""
    rows = 0
    affected = 0
    err = ""
    parsed = cached
    described = cached
    while _next(&c):
        t = c.mt
        if t == 90:                                           # ReadyForQuery
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            if not cached and parsed and st.name != "" and described:
                c.stmts[sql] = st                             # kept, even if running it failed
            if err != "":
                return _fail_reply(err)
            if mode == 1 or mode == 2:
                res += "]"
            elif mode == 3 and rows == 0:
                res = "null"
            elif mode == 4 and rows == 0:
                res = _raw_header(st, binary)
            _set_err("")
            return Reply(true, affected, res)
        if t == 69:
            if err == "":
                err = _server_error(c)
        elif err != "":
            pass
        elif t == 49:                                         # ParseComplete
            parsed = true
        elif t == 84 and not cached:                          # RowDescription
            st = _row_description(c, st.name, st.head)
            described = true
        elif t == 110 and not cached:                         # NoData
            described = true
        elif t == 68:                                         # DataRow
            if mode == 4:
                if rows == 0:
                    res = _raw_header(st, binary)
                # this row and the ones right after it in the buffer, copied as one block
                # (whole messages: the decoder steps over each one's type and length)
                end = c.ms + c.ml
                k = 1
                while end + 5 <= len(c.buf) and c.buf.byte(end) == 68:
                    m = _be32(c.buf, end + 1)
                    if end + 1 + m > len(c.buf):
                        break
                    end += 1 + m
                    k += 1
                res += c.buf[c.ms - 5..end]
                rows += k
                c.ml = end - c.ms                                 # (the next message is after the block)
                continue
            rows += 1
            if mode != 0 and not (mode == 3 and rows > 1):
                if rows > 1:
                    res += ","
                res += _json_row(c, st, mode)
        elif t == 67:                                         # CommandComplete: "UPDATE 2"
            affected = _tag_count(_cstr(c.buf, c.ms, c.ms + c.ml), rows)
    return Reply(false, -1, "")

fn _row_description(c: Conn, name: str, head: str) Stmt:
    st = Stmt(name, [], [], [], head, "")
    n = _be16(c.buf, c.ms)
    i = c.ms + 2
    e = c.ms + c.ml
    for k in 0..n:
        col = _cstr(c.buf, i, e)
        i += len(col) + 1
        st.cols.push(copy(col))
        st.keys.push(json_quote(col) + ":")
        st.types.push(_be32(c.buf, i + 6))
        i += 18
    fm = _u16(n)
    any = false
    for t in st.types:
        fm += "\x00\x01" if _binary(t) else "\x00\x00"
        any = any or _binary(t)
    if any:
        st.fmts = fm
    return st

fn _tag_count(tag: str, rows: int) int:
    sp = _last(tag, " ")
    return rows if sp < 0 else tag[sp + 1..].to_int(rows)

# a DataRow as a JSON object
fn _json_row(c: Conn, st: Stmt, mode: int) str:
    out = "{"
    n = min(_be16(c.buf, c.ms), len(st.keys))
    i = c.ms + 2
    for k in 0..n:
        vlen = _i32(c.buf, i)
        i += 4
        if k > 0:
            out += ","
        out += st.keys[k]
        if vlen < 0:
            out += "\"\"" if mode == 2 else "null"
            continue
        v = c.buf[i..i + vlen]
        i += vlen
        out += _json_value(v, st.types[k], mode)
    return out + "}"

fn _json_value(v: str, oid: int, mode: int) str:
    if mode != 2:
        if oid == 16:
            return "true" if v == "t" else "false"
        if oid == 20 or oid == 21 or oid == 23 or oid == 26:
            return v
        if (oid == 700 or oid == 701 or oid == 1700) and len(v) > 0 and not v.ends_with("y") and (v[0] == "-" or (v.byte(0) >= 48 and v.byte(0) <= 57)):
            return v
    return json_quote(v)

# the raw rows' header (runtime/pg.h, tern_pgd_*): the columns, their types and formats;
# after it come the DataRow messages, whole
fn _raw_header(st: Stmt, binary: bool) str:
    out = _le32(len(st.cols))
    for k, col in st.cols:
        out += _le32(st.types[k]) + _le32(1 if binary and _binary(st.types[k]) else 0) + _le32(len(col)) + col
    return out

# Several statements in one string, through the simple protocol: in one implicit transaction
# unless the script has its own BEGIN / COMMIT; the first error stops the rest. The rows
# affected, added up.
fn _script(c: mut Conn, sql: str) Reply:
    if c.broken:
        return _fail_reply("pg: the connection is broken")
    if not _send(&c, _msg("Q", sql + "\x00")):
        return Reply(false, -1, "")
    total = 0
    err = ""
    while _next(&c):
        t = c.mt
        if t == 90:
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            if err != "":
                return _fail_reply(err)
            _set_err("")
            return Reply(true, total, "")
        if t == 69 and err == "":
            err = _server_error(c)
        elif t == 67:
            tag = _cstr(c.buf, c.ms, c.ms + c.ml)
            sp = _last(tag, " ")
            if sp >= 0:
                total += tag[sp + 1..].to_int(0)
        elif t == 71:                                         # CopyInResponse: a script can't send data
            if not _send(&c, _msg("f", "COPY FROM STDIN is not supported in a script\x00")):
                return Reply(false, -1, "")
    return Reply(false, -1, "")

struct _RawCol:
    name: str
    oid: int
    table: int
    column: int

struct _Raw:
    params: [int]
    columns: [_RawCol]

# what the server knows about a statement, without running it (Parse and Describe, unnamed)
fn _describe_raw(c: mut Conn, sql: str) Result[_Raw, str]:
    if c.broken:
        return Err("pg: the connection is broken")
    out = _msg("P", "\x00" + sql + "\x00\x00\x00") + _msg("D", "S\x00") + "S\x00\x00\x00\x04"
    if not _send(&c, out):
        return Err(error())
    raw = _Raw([], [])
    err = ""
    while _next(&c):
        t = c.mt
        if t == 90:
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            if err != "":
                return Err(err)
            return Ok(raw)
        if t == 69 and err == "":
            err = _server_error(c)
        elif t == 116 and err == "":                          # ParameterDescription
            for k in 0.._be16(c.buf, c.ms):
                raw.params.push(_be32(c.buf, c.ms + 2 + 4 * k))
        elif t == 84 and err == "":
            i = c.ms + 2
            e = c.ms + c.ml
            for k in 0.._be16(c.buf, c.ms):
                col = _cstr(c.buf, i, e)
                i += len(col) + 1
                raw.columns.push(_RawCol(copy(col), _be32(c.buf, i + 6), _be32(c.buf, i), _be16(c.buf, i + 4)))
                i += 18
    return Err(error())
```

## library/redis/redis.tn

```tern
# redis: a Redis (or Valkey) client for tasks: a pool of connections shared by every task,
# the common commands as functions, any command through c.cmd, pipelines, and pub/sub.
#
#   import redis
#   r = redis.connect("redis://localhost:6379")        # redis://:password@host:port/db
#   if not r.ok():
#       print(redis.error())
#   r.set_str("greeting", "hello")
#   print(r.get_str("greeting"))                        # "hello" ("" if missing; see exists)
```
