```tern
#   r.set_ex("session:1", token, 3600)                  # expires in an hour
#   n = r.incr("hits")
#   reply = r.cmd(["HSET", "user:7", "name", "ada"])    # any command: a Reply
#   replies = r.pipeline([["INCR", "a"], ["INCR", "b"]])   # one round trip
#   msgs = r.subscribe(["news"])                        # chan[redis.Message]
#   for m in msgs:
#       print(m.channel, m.data)
#
# Functions (a Client is shared by copying it, like a channel):
#   redis.connect(url str) Client        a pool of 8 connections   redis.pool(url, size) Client
#   c.ok() bool                          redis.error() str: why the last call failed ("" if it didn't)
#   c.get_str(key) str   c.set_str(key, value) bool   c.set_ex(key, value, seconds) bool
#   c.set_nx(key, value) bool (only if absent)        c.del(key) int      c.exists(key) bool
#   c.incr(key) int   c.incr_by(key, n) int           c.expire(key, seconds) bool   c.ttl(key) int
#   c.mget(keys [str]) [str]                          c.publish(channel, message) int
#   c.cmd(args [str]) Reply              Reply fields: kind ("nil" "str" "int" "array" "error"),
#                                        text, num, items ([Reply] of an array)
#   c.pipeline(cmds [[str]]) [Reply]     several commands in one round trip
#   c.subscribe(channels [str]) Subscription     its own connection; patterns ("news.*") work too
#   sub.next(&m) bool                    the next Message (fields channel, data); false once closed
#   sub.unsubscribe()                    (sub.messages is the chan[Message] behind next)
#   c.close()                            closes the pool's connections (don't use c afterwards)
# (get and set are builtin names in Tern, hence get_str / set_str.) Errors: a failed call
# returns "" / false / 0 / -1 and redis.error() says why (set at the end of the call, so it
# is the calling task's own message); c.cmd returns them as a Reply with kind "error".
# URL: redis://[:password@]host[:port][/db], or rediss://... for TLS (needs `import tls`; the
# certificate is verified: tls.trust(ca_file) for a private CA). Not available on wasm.

import net
import random
import task

struct Reply:
    kind: str                   # "nil", "str", "int", "array", "error"
    text: str                   # a string reply, a status ("OK"), or the error message
    num: int                    # an integer reply
    items: [Reply]              # an array reply

struct Message:
    channel: str
    data: str

struct Client:
    host: str
    port: int
    password: str
    db: int
    muxes: [int]                # the pool's connections (shared, pipelined: runtime/net.h)
    first_ok: bool
    tls: bool                   # rediss://

struct Subscription:
    conn: net.Conn
    messages: chan[Message]

fn _parse_url(url: str, c: mut Client) bool:
    rest = url
    if rest.starts_with("redis://"):
        rest = rest[8..]
    elif rest.starts_with("rediss://"):
        rest = rest[9..]
        c.tls = true
    else:
        return false
    at = rest.find("@")
    if at >= 0:
        auth = rest[..at]
        colon = auth.find(":")
        if colon >= 0:
            c.password = auth[colon + 1..]
        else:
            c.password = auth
        rest = rest[at + 1..]
    slash = rest.find("/")
    hostport = rest
    if slash >= 0:
        hostport = rest[..slash]
        c.db = rest[slash + 1..].to_int(0)
    colon = hostport.find(":")
    if colon >= 0:
        c.host = hostport[..colon]
        c.port = hostport[colon + 1..].to_int(6379)
    elif hostport != "":
        c.host = hostport
    return true

fn _encode(args: [str]) str:
    out = "*" + str(len(args)) + "\r\n"
    for a in args:
        out += "$" + str(len(a)) + "\r\n" + a + "\r\n"
    return out

# one reply off the connection; kind "error" with text "connection lost" if it broke
fn _read_reply(conn: net.Conn) Reply:
    line = conn.read_line()
    if len(line) < 3:
        return Reply("error", "redis: connection lost", 0, [])
    kind = line[0]
    body = line[1..len(line) - 2]
    if kind == "+":
        return Reply("str", body, 0, [])
    if kind == "-":
        return Reply("error", body, 0, [])
    if kind == ":":
        return Reply("int", "", body.to_int(0), [])
    if kind == "$":
        n = body.to_int(-1)
        if n < 0:
            return Reply("nil", "", 0, [])
        data = conn.read_exact(n + 2)
        return Reply("str", data[..n], 0, [])
    if kind == "*":
        n = body.to_int(-1)
        if n < 0:
            return Reply("nil", "", 0, [])
        items: [Reply] = []
        for i in 0..n:
            items.push(_read_reply(conn))
        return Reply("array", "", 0, items)
    return Reply("error", "redis: protocol error", 0, [])

fn _dial(c: Client) int:
    conn = net.connect(c.host, c.port)
    if not conn.ok():
        _set_error("redis: " + net.error())
        return -1
    if c.tls and not _tls(conn.fd, c.host):
        why = net.error()
        conn.close()
        _set_error("redis: " + why)
        return -1
    if c.password != "":
        conn.write(_encode(["AUTH", c.password]))
        r = _read_reply(conn)
        if r.kind == "error":
            conn.close()
            _set_error("redis: " + r.text)
            return -1
    if c.db != 0:
        conn.write(_encode(["SELECT", str(c.db)]))
        r = _read_reply(conn)
        if r.kind == "error":
            conn.close()
            _set_error("redis: " + r.text)
            return -1
    return conn.fd

# Connections are multiplexed: every task's commands go to one of the pool's connections,
# queued commands go out together in one write (automatic pipelining), and replies are
# handed back to the tasks that asked, in order (runtime/net.h). A connection that breaks is
# redialed for the next call. Blocking commands (BLPOP ...) get a connection of their own.
fn pool(url: str, size: int) Client:
    c = Client("127.0.0.1", 6379, "", 0, [], false, false)
    if not _parse_url(url, &c):
        _set_error("redis: not a redis:// or rediss:// url")
        return c
    first = _dial(c)
    c.first_ok = first >= 0
    for i in 0..max(size, 1):
        fd = first
        if i > 0 and first >= 0:
            fd = _dial(c)
        c.muxes.push(_mux_new(fd))
    if c.first_ok:
        _set_error("")
    return c

fn connect(url: str) Client:
    return pool(url, 8)

fn ok(c: Client) bool:
    return c.first_ok

# close the pool's connections (calls made afterwards fail)
fn close(c: Client):
    for m in c.muxes:
        _mux_close(m)

fn _lost(n: int, why: str) [Reply]:
    out: [Reply] = []
    for i in 0..n:
        out.push(Reply("error", why, 0, []))
    return out

# a reply out of raw RESP bytes, from pos on (pos moves past it)
fn _parse(s: str, pos: mut int) Reply:
    e = _crlf(s, pos)
    if e < 0:
        return Reply("error", "redis: protocol error", 0, [])
    kind = s[pos]
    body = s[pos + 1..e]
    pos = e + 2
    if kind == "+":
        return Reply("str", body, 0, [])
    if kind == "-":
        return Reply("error", body, 0, [])
    if kind == ":":
        return Reply("int", "", body.to_int(0), [])
    if kind == "$":
        n = body.to_int(-1)
        if n < 0:
            return Reply("nil", "", 0, [])
        data = s[pos..pos + n]
        pos += n + 2
        return Reply("str", data, 0, [])
    if kind == "*":
        n = body.to_int(-1)
        if n < 0:
            return Reply("nil", "", 0, [])
        items: [Reply] = []
        for i in 0..n:
            items.push(_parse(s, &pos))
        return Reply("array", "", 0, items)
    return Reply("error", "redis: protocol error", 0, [])

# A task uses the pool's connection for the worker thread it runs on, so a connection's
# callers, the one of them reading its replies, and the tasks those replies wake all share
# one thread: no hand-offs between threads, and tasks woken by one batch of replies send
# their next commands together, in one write. (Connections beyond the number of workers
# stay idle; with more workers than connections, some workers share one.) Outside tasks,
# any connection.
fn _mux_for(c: Client) int:
    w = _worker()
    n = len(c.muxes)
    if w < 0:
        return c.muxes[random.int(0, n - 1)]
    return c.muxes[w % n]

# redial a connection that broke (another task may beat us to it)
fn _heal(c: Client, m: int):
    if _mux_broken(m):
        fd = _dial(c)
        if fd >= 0:
            _mux_reset(m, fd)

fn _blocking(args: [str]) bool:
    name = args[0].upper()
    if name == "BLPOP" or name == "BRPOP" or name == "BLMOVE" or name == "BRPOPLPUSH" or name == "BLMPOP":
        return true
    if name == "BZPOPMIN" or name == "BZPOPMAX" or name == "BZMPOP" or name == "WAIT" or name == "WAITAOF":
        return true
    if name == "XREAD" or name == "XREADGROUP":
        for a in args:
            if a.upper() == "BLOCK":
                return true
    return false

# a blocking command on a connection of its own (it would hold up a shared one)
fn _alone(c: Client, cmds: [[str]]) [Reply]:
    fd = _dial(c)
    if fd < 0:
        return _lost(len(cmds), error())
    conn = net.Conn(fd)
    out = ""
    for args in cmds:
        out += _encode(args)
    conn.write(out)
    replies: [Reply] = []
    for i in 0..len(cmds):
        replies.push(_read_reply(conn))
    conn.close()
    return replies

# run commands in one round trip: every reply, in order (the commands go out together, so a
# MULTI ... EXEC pipeline is a transaction)
fn pipeline(c: Client, cmds: [[str]]) [Reply]:
    replies: [Reply] = []
    if len(cmds) == 0:
        return replies
    if len(c.muxes) == 0:
        replies = _lost(len(cmds), "redis: not connected (check c.ok())")
    elif len(cmds) == 1 and _blocking(cmds[0]):
        replies = _alone(c, cmds)
    else:
        out = ""
        for args in cmds:
            out += _encode(args)
        m = _mux_for(c)
        if _mux_broken(m):
            _heal(c, m)
        if len(cmds) == 1:
            r = _call1(m, out)
            if r.kind == "raw":
                pos = 0
                r = _parse(r.text, &pos)
            replies.push(r)
        else:
            raw = _call(m, out, len(cmds))
            if raw == "":
                replies = _lost(len(cmds), error())
            else:
                pos = 0
                for i in 0..len(cmds):
                    replies.push(_parse(raw, &pos))
    msg = ""
    for r in replies:
        if r.kind == "error":
            msg = r.text
    _set_error(msg)                                     # (last, after every wait: see redis.error)
    return replies

fn cmd(c: Client, args: [str]) Reply:
    return pipeline(c, [args])[0]

fn get_str(c: Client, key: str) str:
    return cmd(c, ["GET", key]).text

fn set_str(c: Client, key: str, value: str) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["SET", key, value]).kind == "str"

fn set_ex(c: Client, key: str, value: str, seconds: int) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["SET", key, value, "EX", str(seconds)]).kind == "str"

fn set_nx(c: Client, key: str, value: str) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["SET", key, value, "NX"]).kind == "str"

fn del(c: Client, key: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["DEL", key]).num

fn exists(c: Client, key: str) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["EXISTS", key]).num > 0

fn incr(c: Client, key: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["INCR", key]).num

fn incr_by(c: Client, key: str, n: int) int:
    return cmd(c, ["INCRBY", key, str(n)]).num

fn expire(c: Client, key: str, seconds: int) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["EXPIRE", key, str(seconds)]).num == 1

fn ttl(c: Client, key: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["TTL", key]).num

fn mget(c: Client, keys: [str]) [str]:
    args = ["MGET"]
    for k in keys:
        args.push(k)
    out: [str] = []
    for it in cmd(c, args).items:
        out.push(it.text)
    return out

fn publish(c: Client, channel: str, message: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["PUBLISH", channel, message]).num

fn _pump(conn: net.Conn, ch: chan[Message]):
    while true:
        r = _read_reply(conn)
        if r.kind != "array":
            break
        if len(r.items) == 3 and r.items[0].text == "message":
            ch.send(Message(r.items[1].text, r.items[2].text))
        elif len(r.items) == 4 and r.items[0].text == "pmessage":
            ch.send(Message(r.items[2].text, r.items[3].text))
    ch.close()

# messages published to these channels (a pattern like "news.*" too), on a connection of
# its own; sub.messages closes if that connection drops or after sub.close()
fn subscribe(c: Client, channels: [str]) Subscription:
    ch: chan[Message] = task.channel(1024)
    fd = _dial(c)
    conn = net.Conn(fd)
    if fd < 0:
        ch.close()
        return Subscription(conn, ch)
    args = ["SUBSCRIBE"]
    pargs = ["PSUBSCRIBE"]
    for name in channels:
        if name.contains("*") or name.contains("?"):
            pargs.push(name)
        else:
            args.push(name)
    out = ""
    n = 0
    if len(args) > 1:
        out += _encode(args)
        n += len(args) - 1
    if len(pargs) > 1:
        out += _encode(pargs)
        n += len(pargs) - 1
    conn.write(out)
    for i in 0..n:
        _read_reply(conn)                              # the subscribe confirmations
    task.spawn(fn() _pump(conn, ch))
    return Subscription(conn, ch)

fn next(s: Subscription, m: mut Message) bool:
    return s.messages.next(&m)

fn unsubscribe(s: Subscription):
    s.conn.close()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- with Result
#   v = c.try_get(key)?          Option[str]: None when the key doesn't exist
#   r = c.try_cmd(["HGET", "user:7", "name"])?
# (Err: "redis: command failed: WRONGTYPE ...", or "redis: connection lost")
fn try_cmd(c: Client, args: [str]) Result[Reply, str]:
    r = cmd(c, args)
    if r.kind == "error":
        if r.text.starts_with("redis: "):
            return Err(r.text)
        return Err("redis: command failed: " + r.text)
    return Ok(r)

fn try_get(c: Client, key: str) Result[Option[str], str]:
    r = try_cmd(c, ["GET", key])?
    none: Option[str] = None
    if r.kind == "nil":
        return Ok(none)
    return Ok(Some(r.text))
```

## library/sqlgen/emit.tn

```tern
# sqlgen: from described queries to Tern code (see sqlgen.tn)

enum Database:
    Postgres(p: pg.Pool)
    Sqlite(d: sqlite.Db)

struct Col:
    name: str
    ty: str                     # the Tern type: int, float, bool, str, or Option of one
    db_type: str                # as the database calls it
    table: str                  # the table a column comes from ("" for an expression, a parameter)
    enum_oid: int               # a PostgreSQL enum type (0: not one): ty is the Tern enum made for it

struct Described:
    q: Query
    sql: str
    params: [Col]
    cols: [Col]
    model: str                  # the table whose struct the rows use ("": a struct of its own)

fn reserved() [str]:           # builtins a function can't be named
    return ["print", "len", "push", "pop", "chr", "copy", "float", "int", "sqrt", "abs", "min", "max", "str", "join", "split", "find", "contains", "starts_with", "ends_with", "replace", "trim", "upper", "lower", "to_int", "to_float", "byte", "repeat", "get", "remove", "keys", "values", "is_null", "string_at", "map", "filter", "sort_by", "url_decode", "json_quote", "panic", "assert", "main"]

fn keywords() [str]:
    return ["struct", "fn", "if", "elif", "else", "while", "for", "in", "return", "parallel", "do", "mut", "take", "true", "false", "and", "or", "not", "break", "continue", "pass", "import", "from", "extern", "export", "null", "enum", "const", "match", "is"]

# a PostgreSQL type name -> the Tern type its values are read as (text for the rest:
# timestamps, uuid, json, arrays, enums, ...)
fn pg_tern_type(pg_type: str) str:
    if pg_type.starts_with("_") and not is_time(pg_type[1..]) and pg_tern_type(pg_type[1..]) != "str":
        return "[" + pg_tern_type(pg_type[1..]) + "]"      # int8[] -> [int]
    if pg_type in ["_text", "_varchar", "_bpchar", "_name", "_uuid", "_citext"]:
        return "[str]"
    if is_time(pg_type):
        return "float"                                      # seconds since 1970, like time.now()
    if pg_type in ["int2", "int4", "int8", "oid"]:
        return "int"
    if pg_type in ["float4", "float8", "numeric"]:
        return "float"
    if pg_type == "bool":
        return "bool"
    return "str"

fn describe_query(dbase: Database, q: Query, cols_of: {str: str}) Result[Described, str]:
    where = f"{q.file}:{q.line}: {q.name}"
    match dbase:
        Postgres(p):
            pr = prepare(q, "$")?
            if len(pr.col_types) > 0:
                return Err(f"{where}: PostgreSQL gives the column types; to read one differently, cast it in the SQL (price::text AS price)")
            s = p.describe(pr.sql).map_err(fn(e) where + ": " + e.replace("pg: describe failed: ", ""))?
            params: [Col] = []
            for i, t in s.params:
                name = pr.params[i] if i < len(pr.params) else f"arg{i + 1}"
                eo = s.param_oids[i] if s.param_kinds[i] == "e" else 0
                ty = enum_name(t) if eo != 0 else pg_tern_type(t)
                if name in pr.param_types:
                    ty = pr.param_types[name]
                    eo = 0
                if name in pr.nullable:
                    ty = f"Option[{ty}]"
                params.push(Col(name, ty, t, "", eo))
            raw: [Col] = []
            nn: [bool] = []
            for c in s.columns:
                t = c.base_type if c.kind == "d" else c.type_name
                raw.push(Col(c.name, enum_name(t) if c.kind == "e" else pg_tern_type(t), t, c.table, c.type_oid if c.kind == "e" else 0))
                nn.push(c.not_null)
            return _finish(q, pr, params, raw, nn)
        Sqlite(d):
            pr = prepare(q, "?")?
            s = d.describe(pr.sql).map_err(fn(e) where + ": " + e.replace("sqlite: describe failed: ", ""))?
            guessed = infer_params(pr.sql, len(s.params), cols_of)
            params: [Col] = []
            for i, pn in s.params:
                name = f"arg{i + 1}"
                if i < len(pr.params):
                    name = pr.params[i]
                elif pn != "" and not pn.starts_with("?"):
                    name = pn[1..]
                ty = guessed[i] if guessed[i] != "" else "str"
                if name in pr.param_types:
                    ty = pr.param_types[name]
                if name in pr.nullable:
                    ty = f"Option[{ty}]"
                params.push(Col(name, ty, "", "", 0))
            raw: [Col] = []
            nn: [bool] = []
            for c in s.columns:
                ty = sqlite_type(c.decl_type)
                if c.name in pr.col_types:
                    ty = pr.col_types[c.name]
                raw.push(Col(c.name, ty, c.decl_type, c.table, 0))
                nn.push(c.not_null)
            return _finish(q, pr, params, raw, nn)

# names checked, nullability decided: a column is an Option unless it's a NOT NULL table
# column in a query without outer joins, or the query says otherwise ("col!" / "col?")
fn _finish(q: Query, pr: Prepared, params: [Col], raw: [Col], not_null: [bool]) Result[Described, str]:
    where = f"{q.file}:{q.line}: {q.name}"
    for p in params:
        if not is_ident(p.name) or p.name in keywords() or p.name in ["pool", "conn"]:
            return Err(f"{where}: `{p.name}` can't be a parameter name; use @name parameters")
    outer = has_outer_join(pr.sql)
    cols: [Col] = []
    names: {str: bool} = {}
    for i, c in raw:
        if not is_ident(c.name) or c.name in keywords():
            return Err(f"{where}: column `{c.name}` can't be a field name; name it with AS, like `count(*) AS n`")
        if c.name in names:
            return Err(f"{where}: two columns are named {c.name}; rename one with AS")
        names[c.name] = true
        nullable = not not_null[i] or outer
        if c.name in pr.forced:
            nullable = pr.forced[c.name]
        cols.push(Col(c.name, f"Option[{c.ty}]" if nullable else c.ty, c.db_type, "" if outer or c.name in pr.forced or c.name in pr.col_types else c.table, c.enum_oid))
    for f in pr.forced.keys():
        if not (f in names):
            return Err(f"{where}: \"{f}!\" / \"{f}?\" doesn't name a column it returns")
    if q.cmd != "exec" and len(cols) == 0:
        return Err(f"{where}: returns no rows; use :exec")
    return Ok(Described(q, pr.sql, params, cols, ""))

# LEFT / RIGHT / FULL joins can make any table's columns null
fn has_outer_join(sql: str) bool:
    words = sql.upper().replace("\n", " ").replace("\t", " ").split(" ").filter(fn(w) w != "")
    for i in 0..len(words) - 1:
        if words[i] in ["LEFT", "RIGHT", "FULL"] and words[i + 1] in ["JOIN", "OUTER"]:
            return true
    return false

fn emit(dbase: Database, ds: [Described], enums: [EnumType], sources: str) str:
    lite = dbase is Sqlite(_)
    module = "sqlite" if lite else "pg"
    out = f"# Code generated by sqlgen from {sources}. DO NOT EDIT.\n\nimport {module}\n"
    for e in enums:
        out += emit_enum(e)
    done: {str: bool} = {}
    for d in ds:                           # the tables' structs first
        if d.model != "" and not (d.model in done):
            done[d.model] = true
            out += f"\n# a row of {d.cols[0].table}\nstruct {d.model}:\n"
            for c in d.cols:
                out += f"    {c.name}: {c.ty}\n"
    helpers: {str: Col} = {}               # _text_or_null_ helpers, by name
    for d in ds:
        out += "\n" + emit_query(dbase, d)
        for c in d.params:
            if c.ty.starts_with("Option["):
                helpers[helper_suffix(c)] = Col("v", c.ty[7..len(c.ty) - 1], c.db_type, "", c.enum_oid)
    for k in helpers.keys().sort_by(fn(k) k):
        v = helpers[k]
        out += f"\nfn _text_or_null_{k}(x: Option[{v.ty}]) str:\n    if x is Some(v):\n        return {to_text(v, lite)}\n    return {module}.NULL\n"
    if out.contains("time.format("):
        out = out.replace(f"\nimport {module}\n", f"\nimport {module}\nimport time\n")
    return out

fn emit_query(dbase: Database, d: Described) str:
    q = d.q
    lite = dbase is Sqlite(_)
    single = q.cmd != "exec" and len(d.cols) == 1
    row = camel(q.name) + "Row"
    if single:
        row = "_" + row
    if d.model != "":
        row = d.model
    out = ""
    if q.cmd != "exec" and d.model == "":
        out += f"struct {row}:\n"
        for c in d.cols:
            out += f"    {c.name}: {c.ty}\n"
        out += "\n"
    args = ["conn: sqlite.Db" if lite else "pool: pg.Pool"]
    vals: [str] = []
    for c in d.params:
        args.push(f"{c.name}: {c.ty}")
        vals.push(to_text(c, lite))
    sql = quote(d.sql)
    ps = "[" + ", ".join(vals) + "]"
    item = d.cols[0].ty if single else row
    pick = f".{d.cols[0].name}" if single else ""
    for line in q.docs:
        out += ("# " + line).trim() + "\n"
    head = f"fn {q.name}(" + ", ".join(args) + ")"
    if lite:
        if q.cmd == "exec":
            return out + f"{head} int:\n    conn.exec({sql}, {ps})\n    return conn.query(\"SELECT changes() AS n\", [])[0][\"n\"].to_int(0)\n"
        body = f"    _rows: [{row}] = []\n    conn.query_into({sql}, {ps}, &_rows)\n"
        if q.cmd == "one":
            return out + f"{head} Option[{item}]:\n{body}    if len(_rows) == 0:\n        return None\n    return Some(_rows[0]{pick})\n"
        if single:
            return out + f"{head} [{item}]:\n{body}    return _rows.map(fn(_x) _x{pick})\n"
        return out + f"{head} [{item}]:\n{body}    return _rows\n"
    if q.cmd == "exec":
        return out + f"{head} Result[int, str]:\n    return pool.run({sql}, {ps})\n"
    if q.cmd == "one" and single:
        return out + f"{head} Result[Option[{item}], str]:\n    _r = pool.fetch_one[{row}]({sql}, {ps})?\n    if _r is Some(_row):\n        return Ok(Some(_row{pick}))\n    return Ok(Option[{item}].None)\n"
    if q.cmd == "one":
        return out + f"{head} Result[Option[{item}], str]:\n    return pool.fetch_one[{row}]({sql}, {ps})\n"
    if single:
        return out + f"{head} Result[[{item}], str]:\n    _rows = pool.fetch[{row}]({sql}, {ps})?\n    return Ok(_rows.map(fn(_x) _x{pick}))\n"
    return out + f"{head} Result[[{item}], str]:\n    return pool.fetch[{row}]({sql}, {ps})\n"

# a parameter as the text the database reads (SQLite keeps booleans as 1 / 0)
fn to_text(c: Col, lite: bool) str:
    if c.ty.starts_with("Option["):
        return f"_text_or_null_{helper_suffix(c)}({c.name})"
    if c.enum_oid != 0:                                  # its label
        return f"{label_fn(c.db_type)}({c.name})"
    if c.ty == "float" and is_time(c.db_type):          # microseconds, UTC
        return f"time.format({c.name}, \"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f+00\")"
    if c.ty.starts_with("["):
        return f"pg.array_{c.ty[1..len(c.ty) - 1]}({c.name})"
    if c.ty == "str":
        return c.name
    if c.ty == "bool":
        return f"\"1\" if {c.name} else \"0\"" if lite else f"\"true\" if {c.name} else \"false\""
    return f"str({c.name})"

fn camel(name: str) str:
    out = ""
    up = true
    for ch in name:
        if ch == "_":
            up = true
        elif up:
            out += ch.upper()
            up = false
        else:
            out += ch
    return out

# a Tern string literal
fn quote(s: str) str:
    return "\"" + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"").replace("\t", "\\t").replace("\n", "\\n") + "\""

# A query that returns a whole table's columns, in order (SELECT * FROM users), gets the
# table's struct (User), shared by every such query, instead of one of its own.
fn use_models(dbase: Database, ds: mut [Described]):
    table_cols: {str: [str]} = {}
    names: {str: str} = {}                 # struct name -> table
    for i in 0..len(ds):
        d = ds[i]
        if d.q.cmd == "exec" or len(d.cols) < 2:
            continue
        t = d.cols[0].table
        if t == "" or len(d.cols.filter(fn(c) c.table != t)) > 0:
            continue
        if not (t in table_cols):
            table_cols[t] = table_columns(dbase, t)
        if d.cols.map(fn(c) c.name) != table_cols[t]:
            continue
        name = model_name(t)
        if name in names and names[name] != t:
            name = camel(t) + "Table"
        names[name] = t
        ds[i].model = name

fn table_columns(dbase: Database, table: str) [str]:
    match dbase:
        Postgres(p):
            rows = p.query("SELECT attname::text AS n FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = $1::regclass AND attnum > 0 AND NOT attisdropped ORDER BY attnum", [table])
            return rows.map(fn(r) r["n"])
        Sqlite(d):
            rows = d.query("SELECT name AS n FROM pragma_table_info(?) ORDER BY cid", [table])
            return rows.map(fn(r) r["n"])

# users -> User, people -> Person, categories -> Category, addresses -> Address, user_roles -> UserRole
fn model_name(table: str) str:
    t = table
    if t == "people":
        t = "person"
    elif t.ends_with("ies") and len(t) > 3:
        t = t[..len(t) - 3] + "y"
    elif t.ends_with("sses") or t.ends_with("xes") or t.ends_with("ches") or t.ends_with("shes"):
        t = t[..len(t) - 2]
    elif t.ends_with("s") and not t.ends_with("ss") and not t.ends_with("us"):
        t = t[..len(t) - 1]
    return camel(t)

fn helper_suffix(c: Col) str:         # Option[[int]] -> list_int; a timestamp: float_time
    ty = c.ty[7..len(c.ty) - 1] if c.ty.starts_with("Option[") else c.ty
    return ty.replace("[", "list_").replace("]", "") + ("_time" if is_time(c.db_type) else "")

fn is_time(pg_type: str) bool:
    return pg_type == "timestamptz" or pg_type == "timestamp"
```

## library/sqlgen/enums.tn

```tern
# sqlgen: PostgreSQL enum types as Tern enums (see sqlgen.tn)
#
#   CREATE TYPE order_status AS ENUM ('pending', 'in_progress', 'shipped');
#
# becomes
#
#   enum OrderStatus:
#       Pending
#       InProgress
#       Shipped
#
#   fn order_status_label(v: OrderStatus) str       "in_progress" for InProgress
#
# Rows read the labels into the enum (pg.fetch matches a label to its variant); parameters
# of the type are sent as their label.

struct EnumType:
    oid: int
    pg_name: str                # order_status
    name: str                   # OrderStatus
    labels: [str]               # as PostgreSQL has them, in order
    variants: [str]             # the variant for each label

fn enum_name(pg_type: str) str:
    return camel(ident_of(pg_type))

fn label_fn(pg_type: str) str:
    return ident_of(pg_type) + "_label"

# anything but letters and digits -> _, lower case
fn ident_of(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    for ch in s.lower():
        c = ch.byte(0)
        out += ch if ident_byte(c) else "_"
    if out == "" or is_digit(out.byte(0)):
        out = "t_" + out
    return out

# "in_progress", "in progress", "In-Progress" -> InProgress (and it must read back: the
# decoder matches labels to variants ignoring case, _, - and spaces)
fn variant_name(label: str) Result[str, str]:
    out = ""
    up = true
    for ch in label:
        c = ch.byte(0)
        if ident_byte(c) and c != 95:
            out += ch.upper() if up else ch
            up = false
        else:
            up = true
    loose = label.lower().replace("_", "").replace("-", "").replace(" ", "")
    if out == "" or loose != out.lower():
        return Err(f"the label '{label}' can't be a variant name (use letters, digits, _, - and spaces)")
    if is_digit(out.byte(0)):
        return Err(f"the label '{label}' can't be a variant name (it starts with a digit)")
    return Ok(out)

# the enum types the queries use, with their labels
fn find_enums(dbase: Database, ds: [Described]) Result[[EnumType], str]:
    match dbase:
        Postgres(p):
            return _pg_enums(p, ds)
        Sqlite(d):
            none: [EnumType] = []
            return Ok(none)

fn _pg_enums(p: pg.Pool, ds: [Described]) Result[[EnumType], str]:
    out: [EnumType] = []
    seen: {int: bool} = {}
    for d in ds:
        cols = d.cols
        for c in d.params:
            cols.push(c)
        for c in cols:
            if c.enum_oid == 0 or c.enum_oid in seen:
                continue
            seen[c.enum_oid] = true
            rows = p.query("SELECT enumlabel::text AS l FROM pg_enum WHERE enumtypid = $1::oid ORDER BY enumsortorder", [str(c.enum_oid)])
            labels = rows.map(fn(r) r["l"])
            e = EnumType(c.enum_oid, c.db_type, enum_name(c.db_type), labels, [])
            taken: {str: str} = {}
            for l in labels:
                v = variant_name(l).map_err(fn(x) f"sqlgen: enum {c.db_type}: {x}")?
                if v in taken:
                    return Err(f"sqlgen: enum {c.db_type}: the labels '{taken[v]}' and '{l}' both become {v}")
                taken[v] = l
                e.variants.push(v)
            out.push(e)
    return Ok(out)

fn emit_enum(e: EnumType) str:
    out = f"\n# the PostgreSQL enum {e.pg_name}\nenum {e.name}:\n"
    for v in e.variants:
        out += f"    {v}\n"
    out += f"\n# the label PostgreSQL knows a {e.name} by\nfn {label_fn(e.pg_name)}(v: {e.name}) str:\n    match v:\n"
    for i, v in e.variants:
        out += f"        {v}:\n            return {quote(e.labels[i])}\n"
    return out
```

## library/sqlgen/infer.tn

```tern
# sqlgen: SQLite doesn't know its parameters' types, so they're read from where each one is
# used: `col = ?1` (and <, >, <=, >=, <>, !=, LIKE) takes col's type, INSERT INTO t (a, b)
# VALUES (?1, ?2) takes a's and b's, LIMIT / OFFSET take int. Anything else is str unless
# written @name:type.

# the table columns' declared types: "users.id" and (when no two tables disagree) "id"
fn column_types(d: sqlite.Db) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    clash: {str: bool} = {}
    rows = d.query("SELECT m.name AS tbl, p.name AS col, p.type AS type FROM sqlite_master m, pragma_table_info(m.name) p WHERE m.type IN ('table', 'view')", [])
    for r in rows:
        ty = sqlite_type(r["type"])
        out[r["tbl"] + "." + r["col"]] = ty
        c = r["col"]
        if c in out and out[c] != ty:
            clash[c] = true
        out[c] = ty
    for c in clash.keys():
        out.remove(c)
    return out

# a declared type -> a Tern type, by SQLite's affinity rules (plus BOOL)
fn sqlite_type(decl: str) str:
    d = decl.upper()
    if d.contains("INT"):
        return "int"
    if d.contains("BOOL"):
        return "bool"
    if d.contains("REAL") or d.contains("FLOA") or d.contains("DOUB") or d.contains("NUMERIC") or d.contains("DECIMAL"):
        return "float"
    return "str"

# the types of ?1 .. ?n ("" where nothing says)
fn infer_params(sql: str, n: int, cols: {str: str}) [str]:
    out = [""] * n
    ts = _tokens(sql)
    for i, t in ts:
        p = _param_index(t)
        if p < 0 or p >= n or out[p] != "":
            continue
        prev = ts[i - 1].upper() if i > 0 else ""
        if prev == "LIMIT" or prev == "OFFSET":
            out[p] = "int"
        elif i >= 2 and _is_compare(prev):
            out[p] = _type_of(cols, ts[i - 2])
        elif i + 2 < len(ts) and _is_compare(ts[i + 1].upper()):
            out[p] = _type_of(cols, ts[i + 2])
    _infer_insert(ts, cols, &out)
    return out

# INSERT INTO t (a, b, ...) VALUES (?1, ?2, ...), row by row
fn _infer_insert(ts: [str], cols: {str: str}, out: mut [str]):
    i = 0
    while i + 2 < len(ts):
        if ts[i].upper() == "INSERT":
            k = i + 1
            while k < len(ts) and ts[k].upper() != "INTO":
                k += 1
            table = ts[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(ts) else ""
            k += 2
            names: [str] = []
            if k < len(ts) and ts[k] == "(":
                k += 1
                while k < len(ts) and ts[k] != ")":
                    if ts[k] != ",":
                        names.push(copy(ts[k]))
                    k += 1
                k += 1
            if k < len(ts) and ts[k].upper() == "VALUES":
                k += 1
                while k < len(ts) and ts[k] == "(":
                    pos = 0
                    k += 1
                    depth = 0
                    while k < len(ts) and not (ts[k] == ")" and depth == 0):
                        if ts[k] == "(":
                            depth += 1
                        elif ts[k] == ")":
                            depth -= 1
                        elif ts[k] == "," and depth == 0:
                            pos += 1
                        elif depth == 0 and pos < len(names):
                            p = _param_index(ts[k])
                            if p >= 0 and p < len(out) and out[p] == "":
                                out[p] = _type_of(cols, table + "." + names[pos])
                        k += 1
                    k += 1
                    if k < len(ts) and ts[k] == ",":
                        k += 1
            i = k
        else:
            i += 1

fn _type_of(cols: {str: str}, ident: str) str:
    if ident in cols:
        return cols[ident]
    dot = ident.find(".")
    if dot >= 0 and ident[dot + 1..] in cols:
        return cols[ident[dot + 1..]]
    return ""

fn _is_compare(t: str) bool:
    return t in ["=", "==", "<>", "!=", "<", ">", "<=", ">=", "LIKE", "GLOB", "IS"]

# "?3" -> 2; anything else -> -1
fn _param_index(t: str) int:
    if len(t) < 2 or t[0] != "?":
        return -1
    return t[1..].to_int(0) - 1

# identifiers (a.b kept together), ?N parameters, operators and punctuation; strings,
# numbers and comments become "0"
fn _tokens(sql: str) [str]:
    out: [str] = []
    top = 0
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)
    while i < n:
        c = sql.byte(i)
        j = i + 1
        if c == 32 or c == 9 or c == 10 or c == 13:
            i = j
            continue
        if c == 39:
            while j < n and sql.byte(j) != 39:
                j += 1
            out.push("0")
            i = j + 1
            continue
        if c == 45 and j < n and sql.byte(j) == 45:
            while j < n and sql.byte(j) != 10:
                j += 1
            i = j
            continue
        if ident_start(c) or c == 34 or c == 96 or c == 91:            # names: a, "a", `a`, [a], a.b
            name = ""
            k = i
            while k < n:
                ch = sql.byte(k)
                if ch == 34 or ch == 96 or ch == 91:
                    close = 93 if ch == 91 else ch
                    e = k + 1
                    while e < n and sql.byte(e) != close:
                        e += 1
                    name += sql[k + 1..e]
                    k = e + 1
                elif ident_byte(ch):
                    s = k
                    while k < n and ident_byte(sql.byte(k)):
                        k += 1
                    name += sql[s..k]
                else:
                    break
                if k < n and sql.byte(k) == 46:
                    name += "."
                    k += 1
                else:
                    break
            out.push(name)
            i = k
            continue
        if c == 63:                                         # ?N, or ?: one more than the highest so far
            while j < n and is_digit(sql.byte(j)):
                j += 1
            num = sql[i + 1..j].to_int(0) if j > i + 1 else top + 1
            top = max(top, num)
            out.push("?" + str(num))
            i = j
            continue
        if is_digit(c):
            while j < n and (is_digit(sql.byte(j)) or sql.byte(j) == 46):
                j += 1
            out.push("0")
            i = j
            continue
        two = sql[i..i + 2]
        if two in ["<=", ">=", "<>", "!=", "=="]:
            out.push(two)
            i += 2
            continue
        out.push(sql[i])
        i = j
    return out
```

## library/sqlgen/queries.tn

```tern
# sqlgen: reading a queries file (see sqlgen.tn)

struct Query:
    name: str                   # the function to generate
    cmd: str                    # "one", "many", or "exec"
    raw: str                    # the SQL as written
    docs: [str]                 # the comment lines under `-- name:`
    file: str
    line: int

# a query made ready for one database
struct Prepared:
    sql: str                    # @name parameters turned into $1, $2 (PostgreSQL) or ?1, ?2 (SQLite)
    params: [str]               # the @names, in order ([] when the SQL numbers its own)
    param_types: {str: str}     # from @name:type
    nullable: {str: bool}       # from @name? (an Option, NULL when None)
    forced: {str: bool}         # column -> nullable, from "col!" (false) and "col?" (true)
    col_types: {str: str}       # column -> type, from "col: type"

# the queries in a file: each starts with `-- name: NAME :one|:many|:exec`
fn parse_queries(file: str, text: str) Result[[Query], str]:
    out: [Query] = []
    cur: [str] = []
    head = ""
    start = 0
    lines = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n")
    for i, line in lines:
        t = line.trim()
        if t.starts_with("-- name:"):
            if head != "":
                out.push(_query(file, start, head, cur)?)
            elif _has_sql(cur):
                return Err(f"{file}:{start + 1}: SQL before the first `-- name: NAME :one|:many|:exec` line")
            head = t
            start = i + 1
            cur = []
        else:
            cur.push(line)
    if head != "":
        out.push(_query(file, start, head, cur)?)
    seen: {str: int} = {}
    for q in out:
        if q.name in seen:
            return Err(f"{file}:{q.line}: a query named {q.name} is already on line {seen[q.name]}")
        seen[q.name] = q.line
    return Ok(out)

fn _query(file: str, line: int, head: str, body: [str]) Result[Query, str]:
    where = f"{file}:{line}"
    words = head[8..].trim().split(" ").filter(fn(w) w != "")
    if len(words) != 2 or not words[1].starts_with(":"):
        return Err(f"{where}: write `-- name: NAME :one` (or :many, :exec), not `{head}`")
    name = words[0]
    cmd = words[1][1..]
    if not (cmd in ["one", "many", "exec"]):
        return Err(f"{where}: {name}: `:{cmd}` should be :one (at most one row), :many (every row), or :exec (no rows)")
    if not is_ident(name) or name in reserved() or name in keywords():
        return Err(f"{where}: `{name}` can't name a function; use a name like get_user")
    docs: [str] = []
    k = 0
    while k < len(body) and body[k].trim().starts_with("--"):
        docs.push(body[k].trim()[2..].trim())
        k += 1
    sql = _code(body[k..]).trim()
    while sql.ends_with(";"):
        sql = sql[..len(sql) - 1].trim()
    if sql == "":
        return Err(f"{where}: {name} has no SQL")
    if len(migrate.split_statements(sql)) > 1:
        return Err(f"{where}: {name} has more than one statement; give each its own `-- name:`")
    return Ok(Query(name, cmd, sql, docs, file, line))

fn _code(lines: [str]) str:
    return "\n".join(lines)

fn _has_sql(lines: [str]) bool:          # anything but blank lines and -- comments
    for l in lines:
        t = l.trim()
        if t != "" and not t.starts_with("--"):
            return true
    return false

fn tern_types() [str]:
    return ["int", "float", "bool", "str"]

# @name[?][:type] parameters -> $N (mark "$") or ?N (mark "?"), the same name the same number;
# "col!" / "col?" / "col: type" column names -> "col", remembering what they said. Quotes,
# $$ bodies and comments are left alone.
fn prepare(q: Query, mark: str) Result[Prepared, str]:
    where = f"{q.file}:{q.line}: {q.name}"
    sql = q.raw
    pr = Prepared("", [], {}, {}, {}, {})
    out = ""
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)
    numbered = false
    while i < n:
        c = sql.byte(i)
        j = i + 1
        if c == 39:                                          # '...'
            while j < n and sql.byte(j) != 39:
                j += 1
            j += 1
        elif c == 34:                                        # "identifier", maybe with a note
            while j < n and sql.byte(j) != 34:
                j += 1
            col = _column_note(&pr, sql[i + 1..j], where)?
            out += "\"" + col + "\""
            i = j + 1
            continue
        elif c == 45 and j < n and sql.byte(j) == 45:        # -- comment
            while j < n and sql.byte(j) != 10:
                j += 1
        elif c == 47 and j < n and sql.byte(j) == 42:        # /* comment */
            end = sql[j..].find("*/")
            j = n if end < 0 else j + end + 2
        elif c == 36 and j < n and is_digit(sql.byte(j)):    # $1
            numbered = true
            while j < n and is_digit(sql.byte(j)):
                j += 1
        elif c == 63 and mark == "?":                        # ? or ?1 (SQLite; jsonb operators in PostgreSQL)
            numbered = true
        elif c == 36 and mark == "$":                        # $tag$ ... $tag$
            k = j
            while k < n and ident_byte(sql.byte(k)):
                k += 1
            if k < n and sql.byte(k) == 36:
                tag = sql[i..k + 1]
                end = sql[k + 1..].find(tag)
                j = n if end < 0 else k + 1 + end + len(tag)
        elif c == 64 and j < n and ident_start(sql.byte(j)) and not _operator_before(sql, i):     # @name
            while j < n and ident_byte(sql.byte(j)):
                j += 1
            pname = sql[i + 1..j]
            if pname in keywords() or pname in ["pool", "conn"]:
                return Err(f"{where}: rename the parameter @{pname}")
            if j < n and sql[j] == "?":                                        # @name?
                pr.nullable[pname] = true
                j += 1
            if j + 1 < n and sql[j] == ":" and sql[j + 1] != ":":               # @name:type
                k = j + 1
                while k < n and ident_byte(sql.byte(k)):
                    k += 1
                ty = sql[j + 1..k]
                if not (ty in tern_types()):
                    return Err(f"{where}: @{pname}:{ty}: the type is int, float, bool, or str")
                pr.param_types[pname] = ty
                j = k
            k = index_of(pr.params, pname)
            if k < 0:
                pr.params.push(copy(pname))
                k = len(pr.params) - 1
            out += mark + str(k + 1)
            i = j
            continue
        out += sql[i..j]
        i = j
    if numbered and len(pr.params) > 0:
        return Err(f"{where}: use @name parameters or numbered ones, not both")
    pr.sql = out
    return Ok(pr)

# "total!", "email?", "n: int", "n!: int" -> the column name, remembering the rest
fn _column_note(pr: mut Prepared, inner: str, where: str) Result[str, str]:
    col = inner
    ty = ""
    colon = inner.find(":")
    if colon > 0:
        ty = inner[colon + 1..].trim()
        if not (ty in tern_types()):
            return Err(f"{where}: \"{inner}\": the type after : is int, float, bool, or str")
        col = inner[..colon].trim()
    if len(col) > 1 and (col.ends_with("!") or col.ends_with("?")):
        pr.forced[col[..len(col) - 1]] = col.ends_with("?")
        col = col[..len(col) - 1]
    if ty != "":
        pr.col_types[col] = ty
    return Ok(col)

# `a <@ b`, `@@`, `x@y`: operators and other text, not parameters
fn _operator_before(sql: str, i: int) bool:
    return i > 0 and (ident_byte(sql.byte(i - 1)) or "<>@#~!=-+*/%^&|`?".contains(sql[i - 1]))

fn index_of(xs: [str], x: str) int:
    for i, y in xs:
        if y == x:
            return i
    return -1

fn is_digit(c: int) bool:
    return c >= 48 and c <= 57

fn ident_start(c: int) bool:
    return (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or c == 95

fn ident_byte(c: int) bool:
    return ident_start(c) or is_digit(c)

fn is_ident(s: str) bool:
    if s == "" or not ident_start(s.byte(0)):
        return false
    for i in 1..len(s):
        if not ident_byte(s.byte(i)):
            return false
    return true
```

## library/sqlgen/sqlgen.tn

```tern
# sqlgen: typed Tern functions from SQL queries, checked against a PostgreSQL or SQLite
# database (like Go's sqlc).
#
# You write the queries, in SQL, each under a `-- name:` line (queries.sql):
#
#   -- name: get_user :one
#   SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE id = @id;
#
#   -- name: list_users :many
#   -- Every user, newest first.
#   SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT @max;
#
#   -- name: rename_user :exec
#   UPDATE users SET name = @name WHERE id = @id;
#
# sqlgen asks the database for each query's parameter and column types, and writes a
# module (users_db.tn) with a struct per result and a function per query:
#
#   struct GetUserRow:
#       id: int
#       name: str
#       email: Option[str]          # the column can be NULL
#
#   PostgreSQL (import pg):
#   fn get_user(pool: pg.Pool, id: int) Result[Option[GetUserRow], str]
#   fn list_users(pool: pg.Pool, max: int) Result[[ListUsersRow], str]
#   fn rename_user(pool: pg.Pool, name: str, id: int) Result[int, str]       (rows changed)
#   SQLite (import sqlite; its errors are runtime errors, so no Result):
#   fn get_user(conn: sqlite.Db, id: int) Option[GetUserRow]
#   fn list_users(conn: sqlite.Db, max: int) [ListUsersRow]
#   fn rename_user(conn: sqlite.Db, name: str, id: int) int                     (rows changed)
#
# so a typo in a column, a missing parameter, or a nullable column read as if it weren't is
# an error when you generate (or `tern check`), not when the query runs.
#
# Running it: a program of your own (gen.tn),
#
#   import os
#   import sqlgen
#
#   fn main() Result[int, str]:
#       return sqlgen.cli(os.env("DATABASE_URL", "postgres://postgres@localhost/app"))   # or sqlite:app.db
#
#   tern run gen.tn -- queries.sql -o users_db.tn                   against the database as it is
#   tern run gen.tn -- queries.sql -o users_db.tn --migrations migrations
#                          in a scratch database made from your migrations (see migrate) and
#                          dropped afterwards: no schema needed anywhere, good for CI
#   tern run gen.tn -- ... --check    fail if users_db.tn isn't what sqlgen would write
#
# Functions:
#   sqlgen.cli(url str) Result[int, str]           the command above (arguments from os.args())
#   sqlgen.command(url str, args [str]) Result[int, str]   ... with the arguments given
#   sqlgen.postgres(p pg.Pool) Database            sqlgen.sqlite(d sqlite.Db) Database
#   sqlgen.generate(dbase Database, files [str]) Result[str, str]     the module's text
#   sqlgen.parse_queries(file str, text str) Result[[Query], str]
#
# Queries:
#   -- name: NAME :one      the first row, or None
#   -- name: NAME :many     every row
#   -- name: NAME :exec     the number of rows changed
#   Comment lines right under the name line become the function's comment. Parameters are
#   @name (the same name twice is one parameter), or numbered ($1 in PostgreSQL, ?1 or ?
#   in SQLite: named arg1, arg2, ...). A query returning one column gives that column's
#   values, not a Row.
#   A query returning every column of one table, in order (SELECT * FROM users), uses the
#   table's struct (User), shared by all such queries.
#
# Types: PostgreSQL's int2/int4/int8/oid -> int, float4/float8/numeric -> float, bool -> bool,
# timestamptz/timestamp -> float (seconds since 1970, UTC, like time.now()), arrays of those
# (and of text, varchar, uuid) -> [int], [float], [bool], [str], the rest (text, date, uuid,
# json, enums) -> str, as PostgreSQL writes them.
# SQLite goes by the declared type (INT... -> int, REAL/FLOAT/DOUBLE/NUMERIC -> float,
# BOOL... -> bool, else str); an expression is str unless its name says `"n: int"`. SQLite
# parameters take the type of the column they're compared with or inserted into (LIMIT and
# OFFSET: int), else str; `@id:int` says it outright.
# Enums: a PostgreSQL enum type becomes a Tern enum (order_status -> OrderStatus, labels
# in_progress -> InProgress) and a function order_status_label(v) str; columns and parameters
# of the type use it.
# Nulls: a column is an Option unless it is a table column declared NOT NULL (with a LEFT /
# RIGHT / FULL join, every column is). Say otherwise in its name: `count(*) AS "total!"`
# (never null), `u.name AS "name?"` (maybe null), `count(*) AS "n!: int"` (SQLite).
# A parameter that may be NULL is written @x? (Option[T] in the function; None is NULL).

import crypto
import sqlite
import fs
import migrate
import os
import pg

fn postgres(p: pg.Pool) Database:
    return Database.Postgres(p)

fn sqlite(d: sqlite.Db) Database:
    return Database.Sqlite(d)

fn generate(dbase: Database, files: [str]) Result[str, str]:
    cols_of: {str: str} = {}
    if dbase is Sqlite(d):
        cols_of = column_types(d)
    ds: [Described] = []
    names: {str: str} = {}
    for f in files:
        text = fs.try_read(f).context("sqlgen")?
        qs = parse_queries(f, text)?
        for q in qs:
            if q.name in names:
                return Err(f"{q.file}:{q.line}: {q.name} is also in {names[q.name]}")
            names[q.name] = q.file
            ds.push(describe_query(dbase, q, cols_of)?)
    use_models(dbase, &ds)
    enums = find_enums(dbase, ds)?
    return Ok(emit(dbase, ds, enums, ", ".join(files.map(fn(f) _base(f)))))

fn _base(path: str) str:
    parts = path.split("/")
    return parts[len(parts) - 1]

# QUERIES.sql ... -o OUT.tn [--migrations DIR] [--check]
fn cli(url: str) Result[int, str]:
    return command(url, os.args()[1..])

# the same, with the arguments given (`tern sqlgen` calls it)
fn command(url: str, args: [str]) Result[int, str]:
    usage = "usage: QUERIES.sql ... -o OUT.tn [--migrations DIR] [--check]"
    files: [str] = []
    out = ""
    migrations = ""
    check = false
    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        a = args[i]
        if a == "-o" and i + 1 < len(args):
            out = args[i + 1]
            i += 1
        elif a == "--migrations" and i + 1 < len(args):
            migrations = args[i + 1]
            i += 1
        elif a == "--check":
            check = true
        elif a.ends_with(".sql"):
            files.push(a)
        else:
            return Err(f"sqlgen: unexpected `{a}`; {usage}")
        i += 1
    if len(files) == 0 or out == "":
        return Err("sqlgen: " + usage)
    code = generate_at(url, files, migrations)?
    if check:
        if fs.read(out) != code:
            return Err(f"sqlgen: {out} is out of date: run sqlgen again")
        print(f"{out} is up to date")
        return Ok(0)
    fs.try_write(out, code).context("sqlgen")?
    print(f"wrote {out}")
    return Ok(0)

# generate() against the database at url (postgres://..., sqlite:PATH), or with migrations
# given, against a scratch database made from them
fn generate_at(url: str, files: [str], migrations: str) Result[str, str]:
    if not (url.starts_with("postgres://") or url.starts_with("postgresql://")):
        path = url[7..] if url.starts_with("sqlite:") else url
        if migrations == "":
            if not fs.exists(path):
                return Err(f"sqlgen: no database at {path}")
            return generate(Database.Sqlite(sqlite.open(path)), files)
        dir = fs.temp_dir("sqlgen")
        d = sqlite.open(dir + "/scratch.db")
        r = _generate_migrated(Database.Sqlite(d), migrate.sqlite(d), files, migrations)
        fs.remove_all(dir)
        return r
    p = pg.pool(url, 2)
    if not p.ok():
        return Err("sqlgen: can't connect: " + pg.error())
    if migrations == "":
        r = generate(Database.Postgres(p), files)
        p.close()
        return r
    name = "sqlgen_" + crypto.hex(crypto.random_bytes(6))
    made = p.run_script(f"CREATE DATABASE {name}").context("sqlgen: making a scratch database")
    if made is Err(e):
        p.close()
        return Err(e)
    scratch = pg.pool(with_database(url, name), 2)
    r: Result[str, str] = Err("sqlgen: can't connect to the scratch database: " + pg.error())
    if scratch.ok():
        r = _generate_migrated(Database.Postgres(scratch), migrate.postgres(scratch), files, migrations)
    scratch.close()
    p.run_script(f"DROP DATABASE {name} WITH (FORCE)")
    p.close()
    return r

fn _generate_migrated(dbase: Database, t: migrate.Target, files: [str], migrations: str) Result[str, str]:
    t.up(migrations)?
    return generate(dbase, files)

# the same server, another database: postgres://user:pass@host:port/NAME?options
fn with_database(url: str, name: str) str:
    at = url.find("//") + 2
    slash = url[at..].find("/")
    q = url[at..].find("?")
    if slash < 0:
        if q < 0:
            return url + "/" + name
        return url[..at + q] + "/" + name + url[at + q..]
    rest = url[at + slash + 1..]
    k = rest.find("?")
    return url[..at + slash + 1] + name + ("" if k < 0 else rest[k..])
```

## library/sqlite/sqlite.tn

```tern
# sqlite: SQLite databases (the system SQLite; linked only when you import sqlite).
#
#   import sqlite
#
#   d = sqlite.open("app.db")
#   d.exec("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT)", [])
#   id = d.exec("INSERT INTO todos (title) VALUES (?)", [title])     # returns the new row id
#   rows = d.query("SELECT id, title FROM todos WHERE id = ?", [str(id)])   # [{str: str}]
#
# Parameters are passed as strings and bound safely (no SQL injection); SQLite converts
# them by column type. A Db can be shared read-only by every server thread: each thread
# gets its own connection and prepared-statement cache, so queries run in parallel. A single
# INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE from a task shares its commit with the thread's other writes at that
# moment (it returns once committed; a write per web request stays fast). SQL errors are
# runtime errors (inside a web request they become a 500).
#   sqlite.open(path str) Db                 opens (creating) the database file
#   d.exec(sql str, params [str]) int        runs one statement; the new row id for an INSERT
#   d.query(sql str, params [str]) [{str: str}]   one map per row, column name -> text
#   d.query_into(sql, params, &out) int      rows read into a struct or [struct] (below)
#   d.run_script(sql) Result[int, str]   every statement in sql, errors returned (migrations)
#   d.exec_later(sql, params)            queue a write and return at once: a background thread commits
#                                        the queue in order every 50 ms (TERN_DB_LATER_MS) and at exit.
#                                        For writes a crash may lose (clicks, view counts); errors go to
#                                        stderr. The fastest way to write on a hot path.
#   d.flush()                            commit what exec_later queued, now (before a read that must
#                                        see it)
#   d.describe(sql) Result[Statement, str]   its parameters and columns, without running it
#   sqlite.NULL                              a parameter that is NULL (["x", sqlite.NULL])
#
# This was the standard library's `db` module; `import db` still works for now (with a
# warning) and means `import sqlite`.

import json

struct Db:
    handle: int

# Typed queries read rows straight into your structs (columns matched to fields by name;
# fields may be int, float, bool, or str). Returns the number of rows.
#   worlds: [World] = []
#   n = d.query_into("SELECT id, randomNumber FROM world", [], &worlds)
#   w = World(0, 0)
#   found = d.query_into("SELECT id, randomNumber FROM world WHERE id = ?", [str(id)], &w) > 0

# Every statement in sql, in order, with the error returned instead of being a runtime error
# (a migration, a schema file). The rows inserted, updated or deleted. No ? parameters.
#   d.run_script("CREATE TABLE a (x INT); CREATE INDEX a_x ON a (x);")?
fn run_script(d: Db, sql: str) Result[int, str]:
    e = _script(d, sql)
    if e != "":
        return Err("sqlite: script failed: " + e)
    return Ok(_script_rows())

# A statement's parameters and result columns, without running it (what sqlgen reads).
#   s = d.describe("SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE id = @id")?
#   s.params        ["@id"]
#   s.columns[1]    Column{name: "email", decl_type: "TEXT", table: "users", column: "email", not_null: false}
struct Column:
    name: str
    decl_type: str              # the declared type ("INTEGER", "TEXT", ...); "" for an expression
    table: str                  # the table the value comes from ("" for an expression)
    column: str                 # ... and its column there
    not_null: bool              # a table column declared NOT NULL (an outer join can still make it null)

struct Statement:
    params: [str]               # "@id", ":name", "$x", "?1"; "" for a plain ?
    columns: [Column]

struct _Described:
    error: str
    params: [str]
    columns: [_RawColumn]

struct _RawColumn:
    name: str
    decl: str
    table: str
    column: str
    not_null: bool

fn describe(d: Db, sql: str) Result[Statement, str]:
    raw = _Described("", [], [])
    if not json.decode(_describe(d, sql), &raw):
        return Err("sqlite: describe failed: unexpected reply")
    if raw.error != "":
        return Err("sqlite: describe failed: " + raw.error)
    out = Statement(raw.params, [])
    for c in raw.columns:
        out.columns.push(Column(c.name, c.decl, c.table, c.column, c.not_null))
    return Ok(out)

# A parameter that is SQL NULL: pass sqlite.NULL in params (["x", sqlite.NULL]). It is the one-byte
# string "\x00" (so that exact string can't be passed as text).
const NULL = "\x00"
```

# Packages (`tern add NAME`)

Imported by name once added (`import roost`).

## deps/auth/auth.tn

```tern
# auth: JSON Web Tokens (HS256) and signed-cookie sessions for web apps. A package of its
# own, so plain web programs don't carry crypto. Password hashing is crypto.hash_password.
#
#   import auth
#   import roost
#
#   token = auth.jwt_for("user-7", secret, 3600)          # {"sub":"user-7","iat":...,"exp":...}
#   t = auth.jwt_verify(token, secret)                    # t.ok, t.subject, t.payload, t.error
#
#   r.layer(auth.require_jwt(secret))                     # 401 unless "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>";
#                                                         #   (a JSON body: {"error":"unauthorized: why"})
#   ... req.ctx_value("jwt.sub")                          # handlers then find the subject here
#
#   s = auth.session(req, secret)                         # {str: str}; {} if none / tampered / expired
#   res = roost.text("hi")
#   auth.set_session(&res, secret, {"user": "7"})         # Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
#   auth.clear_session(&res)
#
# JWTs:
#   auth.jwt_encode(payload_json str, secret str) str     sign any JSON object
#   auth.jwt_for(subject str, secret str, ttl_seconds int) str
#   auth.jwt_verify(token str, secret str) Token          checks the signature (constant time),
#       that alg is HS256, and exp / nbf when present. Token fields: ok, payload (the JSON; decode
#       it into your struct with json.decode), subject ("sub"), error ("" when ok)
#   auth.require_jwt(secret str) middleware               sets ctx "jwt.sub" and "jwt" (the payload)
# Sessions: the data is in the cookie itself (JSON, base64url, HMAC-SHA256 signed; readable by
# the user but not changeable), so keep it small (cookies hold ~4 KB) and never put secrets in it.
#   auth.session(req http.Request, secret str) {str: str}
#   auth.set_session(res mut http.Response, secret str, data {str: str})      30 days
#   auth.set_session_for(res mut http.Response, secret str, data {str: str}, max_age_seconds int, attrs str)
#       attrs: extra cookie attributes, e.g. "Secure" behind HTTPS
#   auth.clear_session(res mut http.Response)
# (http.Request and http.Response are roost.Request and roost.Response: the same types.)
# Use a long random secret (crypto.base64url(crypto.random_bytes(32))), kept out of the code.

import crypto
import http
import json
import time

struct Token:
    ok: bool
    payload: str
    subject: str
    error: str

struct _Claims:
    sub: str
    exp: int
    nbf: int

struct _Header:
    alg: str
    typ: str

fn _sign(data: str, secret: str) str:
    return crypto.base64url(crypto.hmac_sha256(secret, data))

fn jwt_encode(payload_json: str, secret: str) str:
    head = crypto.base64url("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"typ\":\"JWT\"}") + "." + crypto.base64url(payload_json)
    return head + "." + _sign(head, secret)

fn jwt_for(subject: str, secret: str, ttl_seconds: int) str:
    now = int(time.now())
    return jwt_encode("{\"sub\":" + subject.json_quote() + ",\"iat\":" + str(now) + ",\"exp\":" + str(now + ttl_seconds) + "}", secret)

fn jwt_verify(token: str, secret: str) Token:
    parts = token.split(".")
    if len(parts) != 3:
        return Token(false, "", "", "malformed token")
    head = parts[0] + "." + parts[1]
    if not crypto.equal(_sign(head, secret), parts[2]):
        return Token(false, "", "", "bad signature")
    h = _Header("", "")
    if not json.decode(crypto.base64url_decode(parts[0]), &h) or h.alg != "HS256":
        return Token(false, "", "", "unsupported algorithm (only HS256)")
    payload = crypto.base64url_decode(parts[1])
    c = _Claims("", 0, 0)
    if not json.decode(payload, &c):
        return Token(false, "", "", "malformed payload")
    now = int(time.now())
    if c.exp != 0 and now >= c.exp:
        return Token(false, payload, c.sub, "expired")
    if c.nbf != 0 and now < c.nbf:
        return Token(false, payload, c.sub, "not valid yet")
    return Token(true, payload, c.sub, "")

fn _require(req: http.Request, inner: fn(http.Request) http.Response, secret: str) http.Response:
    h = req.header("authorization")
    if not h.starts_with("Bearer "):
        return _unauthorized("missing bearer token")
    t = jwt_verify(h[7..].trim(), secret)
    if not t.ok:
        return _unauthorized(t.error)
    r2 = req
    r2.set_ctx("jwt.sub", t.subject)
    r2.set_ctx("jwt", t.payload)
    return inner(r2)

fn _unauthorized(why: str) http.Response:              # JSON, like the rest of an API
    res = http.with_status(http.json("{\"error\":" + ("unauthorized: " + why).json_quote() + "}"), 401)
    res.set_header("WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer")
    return res

fn require_jwt(secret: str) fn(http.Request, fn(http.Request) http.Response) http.Response:
    return fn(req: http.Request, inner: fn(http.Request) http.Response) _require(req, inner, secret)

fn session(req: http.Request, secret: str) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    raw = req.cookie("session")
    dot = raw.find(".")
    if dot <= 0:
        return out
    body = raw[..dot]
    if not crypto.equal(_sign("session." + body, secret), raw[dot + 1..]):
        return out
    data: {str: str} = {}
    if not json.decode(crypto.base64url_decode(body), &data):
        return out
    if "_exp" in data:
        if int(time.now()) >= data["_exp"].to_int(0):
            return out
        data.remove("_exp")
    return data

fn set_session_for(res: mut http.Response, secret: str, data: {str: str}, max_age_seconds: int, attrs: str):
    d = data
    d["_exp"] = str(int(time.now()) + max_age_seconds)
    body = crypto.base64url(json.encode(d))
    extra = "Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=" + str(max_age_seconds)
    if attrs != "":
        extra += "; " + attrs
    res.set_cookie_with("session", body + "." + _sign("session." + body, secret), extra)

fn set_session(res: mut http.Response, secret: str, data: {str: str}):
    set_session_for(&res, secret, data, 30 * 86400, "")

fn clear_session(res: mut http.Response):
    res.set_cookie_with("session", "", "Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=0")

# with Result: user = auth.verify(token, secret)?   the subject ("sub");
#   Err: "auth: invalid token: expired"
fn verify(token: str, secret: str) Result[str, str]:
    t = jwt_verify(token, secret)
    if not t.ok:
        return Err("auth: invalid token: " + t.error)
    return Ok(t.subject)
```

## deps/grpc/client.tn

```tern
# Part of the grpc package (see grpc.tn): a small unary client, one connection per call
# (tests, tools, health checks; not a pooled, multiplexing client).

fn _read_frame(c: net.Conn, buf: mut str, at: mut int, typ: mut int, flags: mut int, sid: mut int, payload: mut str) bool:
    while len(buf) - at < 9:
        if c.refill(&buf, at, 65536) <= 0:
            return false
        at = 0
    n = (buf.byte(at) << 16) | (buf.byte(at + 1) << 8) | buf.byte(at + 2)
    while len(buf) - at < 9 + n:
        if c.refill(&buf, at, 65536 + n) <= 0:
            return false
        at = 0
    typ = buf.byte(at + 3)
    flags = buf.byte(at + 4)
    sid = _be32(buf, at + 5) & 0x7fffffff
    payload = buf[at + 9..at + 9 + n]
    at += 9 + n
    return true

# Calls method ("/pkg.Service/Method") on host:port (h2c) with one request message; the reply's
# status is UNAVAILABLE when the server can't be reached or the connection breaks.
fn call(host: str, port: int, method: str, metadata: {str: str}, message: str) Reply:
    c = net.connect(host, port)
    if not c.ok():
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, net.error())
    r = _call(c, host, port, method, metadata, message, "\x86")
    c.close()
    return r

# The same over TLS (ALPN "h2"), checking the server's certificate against host.
fn call_tls(host: str, port: int, method: str, metadata: {str: str}, message: str) Reply:
    c = tls.connect_alpn(host, port, ["h2"])
    if not c.ok():
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, tls.error())
    if tls.alpn(c) != "h2":
        c.close()
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "the server didn't agree to HTTP/2 (ALPN h2)")
    r = _call(c, host, port, method, metadata, message, "\x87")
    c.close()
    return r

fn _call(c: net.Conn, host: str, port: int, method: str, metadata: {str: str}, message: str, scheme: str) Reply:
    big = 1 << 30
    hello = PREFACE + frame(F_SETTINGS, 0, 0, _setting(2, 0) + _setting(4, big)) + _window(0, big)
    head = "\x83" + scheme + hpack_literal_idx(4, method) + hpack_literal_idx(1, host + ":" + str(port))
    head += hpack_literal_idx(31, "application/grpc") + hpack_literal("te", "trailers")
    for k, v in metadata:
        head += hpack_literal(k, v)
    if not c.write(hello + frame(F_HEADERS, END_HEADERS, 1, head)):
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, net.error())
    body = "\x00" + _u32(len(message)) + message
    sent = 0
    conn_win = 65535
    win = 65535
    max_frame = 16384
    hp = hpack_decoder(hpack_tables(), 4096)
    buf = ""
    at = 0
    typ = 0
    flags = 0
    sid = 0
    p = ""
    data = ""
    status = -1
    msg = ""
    http = ""
    while true:
        # send what the windows allow
        out = ""
        while sent < len(body):
            n = min(min(len(body) - sent, max_frame), min(conn_win, win))
            if n <= 0:
                break
            out += frame(F_DATA, END_STREAM if sent + n == len(body) else 0, 1, body[sent..sent + n])
            sent += n
            conn_win -= n
            win -= n
        if out != "" and not c.write(out):
            return fail(UNAVAILABLE, net.error())
        if not _read_frame(c, &buf, &at, &typ, &flags, &sid, &p):
            return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "the connection closed before the answer")
        match typ:
            4:
                if flags & ACK == 0:
                    for k in 0..len(p) / 6:
                        id = (p.byte(k * 6) << 8) | p.byte(k * 6 + 1)
                        v = _be32(p, k * 6 + 2)
                        if id == 4:
                            win += v - 65535
                        elif id == 5:
                            max_frame = v
                    c.write(frame(F_SETTINGS, ACK, 0, ""))
            8:
                inc = _be32(p, 0) & 0x7fffffff
                if sid == 0:
                    conn_win += inc
                elif sid == 1:
                    win += inc
            6:
                if flags & ACK == 0:
                    c.write(frame(F_PING, ACK, 0, p))
            7:
                if len(p) >= 8 and _be32(p, 4) != 0:
                    return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "GOAWAY: " + p[8..])
            3:
                if sid == 1:
                    return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "stream reset: code " + str(_be32(p, 0)))
            0:
                if sid == 1:
                    a = 0
                    b = len(p)
                    if flags & PADDED != 0:
                        a = 1
                        b -= p.byte(0)
                    data += p[a..b]
                    if len(p) > 0:
                        c.write(_window(0, len(p)) + _window(1, len(p)))
            1 | 9:
                blk = p
                if typ == 1 and flags & PADDED != 0:
                    blk = p[1..len(p) - p.byte(0)]
                if typ == 1 and flags & PRIORITY_FLAG != 0:
                    blk = blk[5..]
                hdrs: [str] = []
                size = 0
                if not hpack_decode(&hp, blk, &hdrs, &size):
                    return fail(INTERNAL, "hpack: " + hp.err)
                i = 0
                while i < len(hdrs):
                    if hdrs[i] == "grpc-status":
                        status = hdrs[i + 1].to_int(UNKNOWN)
                    elif hdrs[i] == "grpc-message":
                        msg = _unpct(hdrs[i + 1])
                    elif hdrs[i] == ":status":
                        http = hdrs[i + 1]
                    i += 2
            _:
                pass
        if (typ == 0 or typ == 1) and sid == 1 and flags & END_STREAM != 0:
            break
    if status < 0:
        return fail(UNKNOWN if http == "200" else INTERNAL, "no grpc-status (HTTP " + http + ")")
    if status != OK:
        return fail(status, msg)
    if len(data) < 5 or _be32(data, 1) != len(data) - 5:
        return fail(INTERNAL, "bad response framing")
    return ok(data[5..])

fn _unhex(b: int) int:
    if b >= 48 and b <= 57:
        return b - 48
    if b >= 65 and b <= 70:
        return b - 55
    if b >= 97 and b <= 102:
        return b - 87
    return -1

fn _unpct(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == "%" and i + 2 < len(s) and _unhex(s.byte(i + 1)) >= 0 and _unhex(s.byte(i + 2)) >= 0:
            out += chr(_unhex(s.byte(i + 1)) * 16 + _unhex(s.byte(i + 2)))
            i += 3
        else:
            out += s[i]
            i += 1
    return out
```

## deps/grpc/grpc.tn

```tern
# grpc: a gRPC server (unary calls) over HTTP/2, in Tern: what OTLP/gRPC exporters and most
# unary clients need. HTTP/2 over TLS (ALPN "h2", as gRPC clients do for https:// endpoints)
# or over cleartext with prior knowledge (h2c: the client starts with the HTTP/2 preface, as
# gRPC clients do for http:// endpoints), HPACK with Huffman, many concurrent streams per
# connection, flow control with generous windows, and gRPC's framing.
#
#   import grpc
#   fn handle(call: grpc.Call) grpc.Reply:
#       if call.method != "/helloworld.Greeter/SayHello":
#           return grpc.fail(grpc.UNIMPLEMENTED, "unknown method " + call.method)
#       if call.metadata.get("authorization", "") != "Bearer secret":
#           return grpc.fail(grpc.UNAUTHENTICATED, "bad key")
#       return grpc.ok(reply_bytes(call.message))       # call.message: the request (protobuf bytes)
#   fn main():
#       s = grpc.start("", 50051, handle, grpc.options())   # serves in tasks; returns at once
#       grpc.wait(s)                                     # until grpc.stop(s, ms) elsewhere
#
# grpc.start(host str, port int, h fn(Call) Reply, o Options) Server   ("" host: every address;
#     port 0: any free port, see grpc.port). A runtime error if the port can't be bound.
# grpc.start_tls(host str, port int, h fn(Call) Reply, o Options, cert str, key str) Server
#     the same over TLS: cert is the certificate chain, key its private key (PEM files; a runtime
#     error if they can't be loaded). The handshake must agree on "h2" by ALPN, as every gRPC
#     client offers; a client that doesn't offer it is refused. Clients check the certificate
#     against the name they dialed (a self-signed one: give the client it as its CA).
# grpc.port(s Server) int          grpc.wait(s Server)       grpc.serve(port, h): start + wait
# grpc.stop(s Server, drain_ms int)  stops accepting, sends GOAWAY to every connection, waits up
#     to drain_ms for the calls running to answer, then closes the connections.
# grpc.ok(body str) Reply          grpc.fail(status int, message str) Reply
# grpc.options() Options           the defaults below; change fields before start
#
# Call:     method ("/package.Service/Method"), metadata ({str: str}: the request's headers,
#           lowercase names, without the ":" pseudo-headers; repeated ones joined with ", "),
#           message (the request message's bytes), encoding ("" unless the message came
#           compressed: then its grpc-encoding, e.g. "gzip", one of Options.encodings, for the
#           handler to decompress), conn (the net.Conn it came on: conn.peer()).
# Reply:    status (grpc.OK ... grpc.UNAUTHENTICATED), message (grpc-message, for errors), body
#           (the response message's bytes, for OK).
# Options:  max_message (4 MiB: a bigger request gets RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), max_frame (1 MiB,
#           the largest frame a client may send), max_header_list (64 KiB of headers per call),
#           max_streams (256 calls at once per connection; more are refused, and clients retry),
#           stream_window (4 MiB) and conn_window (64 MiB): flow-control windows, credited back
#           as data arrives, so a big export never waits on them; header_table (4096, HPACK's),
#           encodings ([]: compressions the handler decompresses; a compressed message in
#           another gets UNIMPLEMENTED with grpc-accept-encoding, as gRPC says).
#
# Status codes: OK 0, CANCELLED 1, UNKNOWN 2, INVALID_ARGUMENT 3, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED 4,
# NOT_FOUND 5, ALREADY_EXISTS 6, PERMISSION_DENIED 7, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 8,
# FAILED_PRECONDITION 9, ABORTED 10, OUT_OF_RANGE 11, UNIMPLEMENTED 12, INTERNAL 13,
# UNAVAILABLE 14, DATA_LOSS 15, UNAUTHENTICATED 16.
#
# Each call's handler runs in its own task (calls on one connection run at once); a
# connection's frames are read by one task and written by another, which batches what is
# ready into one write. Malformed input ends the stream (RST_STREAM) or the connection
# (GOAWAY) with the error code RFC 9113 gives; it never ends the program.
# Not supported: streaming RPCs (a call is one request message, one response), server push,
# HTTP/1 upgrade to h2c, client certificates (mTLS), and response compression (responses go
# uncompressed, which every client accepts).
# Client (tests, tools; one connection per call): grpc.call(host, port, method, metadata, message)
# Reply over h2c, grpc.call_tls(...) the same over TLS (verified; tls.trust(ca) for a private CA).
# Parts: hpack.tn (header compression), wire.tn (frames, the connection's reader and writer),
# client.tn. The package imports tls, so programs using it link aws-lc (see the tls module).
# Not available on wasm.

import net
import task
import time
import tls

const OK = 0
const CANCELLED = 1
const UNKNOWN = 2
const INVALID_ARGUMENT = 3
const DEADLINE_EXCEEDED = 4
const NOT_FOUND = 5
const ALREADY_EXISTS = 6
const PERMISSION_DENIED = 7
const RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED = 8
const FAILED_PRECONDITION = 9
const ABORTED = 10
const OUT_OF_RANGE = 11
const UNIMPLEMENTED = 12
const INTERNAL = 13
const UNAVAILABLE = 14
const DATA_LOSS = 15
const UNAUTHENTICATED = 16

struct Call:
    method: str
    metadata: {str: str}
    message: str
    encoding: str
    conn: net.Conn

struct Reply:
    status: int
    message: str
    body: str

struct Options:
    max_message: int
    max_frame: int
    max_header_list: int
    max_streams: int
    stream_window: int
    conn_window: int
    header_table: int
    encodings: [str]

# a live connection, for stop: its socket and its writer's queue
struct _Live:
    sock: net.Conn
    out: chan[Out]

struct Server:
    listener: net.Listener
    host: str
    port: int
    stopping: shared[bool]
    inflight: shared[int]               # calls whose handler hasn't answered yet
    conns: shared[{int: _Live}]         # by socket
    done: chan[int]                     # closed by stop (wait returns)
    tls: tls.Server                     # (ctx 0: cleartext, h2c)

fn options() Options:
    return Options(4 << 20, 1 << 20, 65536, 256, 4 << 20, 64 << 20, 4096, [])

fn ok(body: str) Reply:
    return Reply(OK, "", body)

fn fail(status: int, message: str) Reply:
    return Reply(status, message, "")

fn _clamp(v: int, lo: int, hi: int) int:
    return max(lo, min(v, hi))

fn start(host: str, port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply, opts: Options) Server:
    return _start(host, port, handler, opts, tls.Server(0))

fn start_tls(host: str, port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply, opts: Options, cert: str, key: str) Server:
    t = tls.server(cert, key)
    tls.set_alpn(t, ["h2"])
    return _start(host, port, handler, opts, t)

fn _start(host: str, port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply, opts: Options, sec: tls.Server) Server:
    o = opts
    o.max_frame = _clamp(o.max_frame, 16384, 16777215)
    o.stream_window = _clamp(o.stream_window, 65535, 2147483647)
    o.conn_window = _clamp(o.conn_window, 65535, 2147483647)
    o.max_streams = max(o.max_streams, 1)
    o.header_table = _clamp(o.header_table, 0, 1 << 20)
    l = net.listen_on(host, port) if host != "" else net.listen(port)
    done: chan[int] = task.channel(1)
    s = Server(l, host, net.port(l), task.shared(false), task.shared(0), task.shared({0: _Live(net.Conn(-1), task.channel(1))}), done, sec)
    fn clear(m: mut {int: _Live}) int:
        m = {}
        return 0
    s.conns.update(clear)
    t = hpack_tables()
    task.spawn(fn() _accept_loop(s, handler, o, t))
    return s

fn port(s: Server) int:
    return s.port

fn wait(s: Server):
```
