```tern
    x = 0
    while s.done.next(&x):
        pass

fn serve(port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply):
    wait(start("", port, handler, options()))

fn _accept_loop(s: Server, handler: fn(Call) Reply, o: Options, t: Tables):
    while true:
        c = net.accept(s.listener)
        if s.stopping.get():
            c.close()
            break
        task.spawn(fn() _serve_conn(s, c, handler, o, t))

fn stop(s: Server, drain_ms: int):
    fn flag(b: mut bool) bool:
        was = b
        b = true
        return was
    if s.stopping.update(flag):
        return
    # wake the accept loop (it sees stopping and ends), then close the listener
    wake = net.connect("127.0.0.1" if s.host == "" or s.host == "0.0.0.0" else s.host, s.port)
    wake.close()
    task.sleep(10)
    net.stop(s.listener)
    live = s.conns.get()
    for fd, lv in live:
        lv.out.send(Out.Raw(_goaway(2147483647, NO_ERROR, "server stopping")))
    deadline = time.mono_ms() + drain_ms
    while s.inflight.get() > 0 and time.mono_ms() < deadline:
        task.sleep(5)
    task.sleep(20)                        # (the writers send the last answers)
    live = s.conns.get()
    for fd, lv in live:
        lv.sock.close()
    s.done.close()
```

## deps/grpc/hpack.tn

```tern
# Part of the grpc package (see grpc.tn): HPACK (RFC 7541), the header compression of HTTP/2.
# The decoder has the static table, a dynamic table (a ring of entries, evicted oldest first as
# the table's size says), integers and string literals, and Huffman-coded strings (a 4-bit
# state machine built at start from the code table below, like nghttp2's). The encoder writes
# literals without indexing and without Huffman: responses are small, and it keeps no state.

# the Huffman code (RFC 7541 appendix B): "code.bits" for bytes 0..255, then EOS
const HUFFMAN = "1ff8.13 7fffd8.23 fffffe2.28 fffffe3.28 fffffe4.28 fffffe5.28 fffffe6.28 fffffe7.28 fffffe8.28 ffffea.24 3ffffffc.30 fffffe9.28 fffffea.28 3ffffffd.30 fffffeb.28 fffffec.28 fffffed.28 fffffee.28 fffffef.28 ffffff0.28 ffffff1.28 ffffff2.28 3ffffffe.30 ffffff3.28 ffffff4.28 ffffff5.28 ffffff6.28 ffffff7.28 ffffff8.28 ffffff9.28 ffffffa.28 ffffffb.28 14.6 3f8.10 3f9.10 ffa.12 1ff9.13 15.6 f8.8 7fa.11 3fa.10 3fb.10 f9.8 7fb.11 fa.8 16.6 17.6 18.6 0.5 1.5 2.5 19.6 1a.6 1b.6 1c.6 1d.6 1e.6 1f.6 5c.7 fb.8 7ffc.15 20.6 ffb.12 3fc.10 1ffa.13 21.6 5d.7 5e.7 5f.7 60.7 61.7 62.7 63.7 64.7 65.7 66.7 67.7 68.7 69.7 6a.7 6b.7 6c.7 6d.7 6e.7 6f.7 70.7 71.7 72.7 fc.8 73.7 fd.8 1ffb.13 7fff0.19 1ffc.13 3ffc.14 22.6 7ffd.15 3.5 23.6 4.5 24.6 5.5 25.6 26.6 27.6 6.5 74.7 75.7 28.6 29.6 2a.6 7.5 2b.6 76.7 2c.6 8.5 9.5 2d.6 77.7 78.7 79.7 7a.7 7b.7 7ffe.15 7fc.11 3ffd.14 1ffd.13 ffffffc.28 fffe6.20 3fffd2.22 fffe7.20 fffe8.20 3fffd3.22 3fffd4.22 3fffd5.22 7fffd9.23 3fffd6.22 7fffda.23 7fffdb.23 7fffdc.23 7fffdd.23 7fffde.23 ffffeb.24 7fffdf.23 ffffec.24 ffffed.24 3fffd7.22 7fffe0.23 ffffee.24 7fffe1.23 7fffe2.23 7fffe3.23 7fffe4.23 1fffdc.21 3fffd8.22 7fffe5.23 3fffd9.22 7fffe6.23 7fffe7.23 ffffef.24 3fffda.22 1fffdd.21 fffe9.20 3fffdb.22 3fffdc.22 7fffe8.23 7fffe9.23 1fffde.21 7fffea.23 3fffdd.22 3fffde.22 fffff0.24 1fffdf.21 3fffdf.22 7fffeb.23 7fffec.23 1fffe0.21 1fffe1.21 3fffe0.22 1fffe2.21 7fffed.23 3fffe1.22 7fffee.23 7fffef.23 fffea.20 3fffe2.22 3fffe3.22 3fffe4.22 7ffff0.23 3fffe5.22 3fffe6.22 7ffff1.23 3ffffe0.26 3ffffe1.26 fffeb.20 7fff1.19 3fffe7.22 7ffff2.23 3fffe8.22 1ffffec.25 3ffffe2.26 3ffffe3.26 3ffffe4.26 7ffffde.27 7ffffdf.27 3ffffe5.26 fffff1.24 1ffffed.25 7fff2.19 1fffe3.21 3ffffe6.26 7ffffe0.27 7ffffe1.27 3ffffe7.26 7ffffe2.27 fffff2.24 1fffe4.21 1fffe5.21 3ffffe8.26 3ffffe9.26 ffffffd.28 7ffffe3.27 7ffffe4.27 7ffffe5.27 fffec.20 fffff3.24 fffed.20 1fffe6.21 3fffe9.22 1fffe7.21 1fffe8.21 7ffff3.23 3fffea.22 3fffeb.22 1ffffee.25 1ffffef.25 fffff4.24 fffff5.24 3ffffea.26 7ffff4.23 3ffffeb.26 7ffffe6.27 3ffffec.26 3ffffed.26 7ffffe7.27 7ffffe8.27 7ffffe9.27 7ffffea.27 7ffffeb.27 ffffffe.28 7ffffec.27 7ffffed.27 7ffffee.27 7ffffef.27 7fffff0.27 3ffffee.26 3fffffff.30"

# the static table (RFC 7541 appendix A): "name=value|..." for indexes 1..61
const STATIC = ":authority=|:method=GET|:method=POST|:path=/|:path=/index.html|:scheme=http|:scheme=https|:status=200|:status=204|:status=206|:status=304|:status=400|:status=404|:status=500|accept-charset=|accept-encoding=gzip, deflate|accept-language=|accept-ranges=|accept=|access-control-allow-origin=|age=|allow=|authorization=|cache-control=|content-disposition=|content-encoding=|content-language=|content-length=|content-location=|content-range=|content-type=|cookie=|date=|etag=|expect=|expires=|from=|host=|if-match=|if-modified-since=|if-none-match=|if-range=|if-unmodified-since=|last-modified=|link=|location=|max-forwards=|proxy-authenticate=|proxy-authorization=|range=|referer=|refresh=|retry-after=|server=|set-cookie=|strict-transport-security=|transfer-encoding=|user-agent=|vary=|via=|www-authenticate="

# The tables every decoder shares (built once by hpack_tables; copies are O(1)).
struct Tables:
    names: [str]                # the static table, index 1.. at [i - 1]
    values: [str]
    fsm: [int]                  # Huffman: state * 16 + nibble -> next | sym + 1 << 8 | flags
    accept: [bool]              # a state where the string may end (only EOS-prefix padding)

# An HPACK decoder: one per connection, fed every header block in order.
struct Hpack:
    t: Tables
    ring_names: [str]           # the dynamic table: a ring, newest at head
    ring_values: [str]
    head: int                   # where the next entry goes
    count: int                  # entries in the table
    size: int                   # their size (RFC 7541 4.1: name + value + 32 each)
    max_size: int               # the table's current limit (size updates)
    limit: int                  # the most a size update may ask for (SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE)
    err: str                    # why the last decode failed

const H_EMIT = 256              # (fsm entry flags)
const H_FAIL = 1 << 17

fn _hex(s: str) int:
    n = 0
    for c in s:
        b = c.byte(0)
        n = n * 16 + (b - 48 if b <= 57 else b - 87)
    return n

# Builds the static table and the Huffman state machine.
fn hpack_tables() Tables:
    names: [str] = []
    values: [str] = []
    for e in STATIC.split("|"):
        i = e.find("=")
        names.push(e[..i])
        values.push(e[i + 1..])
    # the code tree: internal nodes 0.. (0 the root); a child >= 0 is a node, < 0 a symbol (-sym - 1)
    left = [0]
    right = [0]
    left[0] = 1 << 40
    right[0] = 1 << 40
    unset = 1 << 40
    for sym, e in HUFFMAN.split(" "):
        dot = e.find(".")
        code = _hex(e[..dot])
        bits = e[dot + 1..].to_int(0)
        node = 0
        for k in 0..bits:
            bit = (code >> (bits - 1 - k)) & 1
            last = k == bits - 1
            nxt = left[node] if bit == 0 else right[node]
            if last:
                if bit == 0:
                    left[node] = -sym - 1
                else:
                    right[node] = -sym - 1
            else:
                if nxt == unset:
                    nxt = len(left)
                    left.push(unset)
                    right.push(unset)
                    if bit == 0:
                        left[node] = nxt
                    else:
                        right[node] = nxt
                node = nxt
    n = len(left)
    # the states that may end a string: the root, and up to 7 one-bits from it
    accept: [bool] = []
    for i in 0..n:
        accept.push(false)
    accept[0] = true
    node = 0
    for k in 0..7:
        node = right[node]
        if node < 0:
            break
        accept[node] = true
    fsm: [int] = []
    for s in 0..n:
        for v in 0..16:
            cur = s
            emit = -1
            fail = false
            for k in 0..4:
                bit = (v >> (3 - k)) & 1
                nxt = left[cur] if bit == 0 else right[cur]
                if nxt < 0:
                    sym = -nxt - 1
                    if sym == 256 or emit >= 0:
                        fail = true              # EOS in a string (or can't happen: two in 4 bits)
                        break
                    emit = sym
                    cur = 0
                elif nxt == unset:
                    fail = true
                    break
                else:
                    cur = nxt
            fsm.push(H_FAIL if fail else cur | ((emit + 1) << 8))
    return Tables(names, values, fsm, accept)

fn hpack_decoder(t: Tables, limit: int) Hpack:
    cap = limit / 32 + 1
    rn: [str] = []
    rv: [str] = []
    for i in 0..cap:
        rn.push("")
        rv.push("")
    return Hpack(t, rn, rv, 0, 0, 0, limit, limit, "")

# Decodes a Huffman-coded string; false when it's malformed.
fn huffman_decode(t: Tables, s: str, a: int, b: int, out: mut str) bool:
    st = 0
    for i in a..b:
        x = s.byte(i)
        e = t.fsm[st * 16 + (x >> 4)]
        if e == H_FAIL:
            return false
        if e >= H_EMIT:
            out += chr((e >> 8) - 1)
        st = e & 255
        e = t.fsm[st * 16 + (x & 15)]
        if e == H_FAIL:
            return false
        if e >= H_EMIT:
            out += chr((e >> 8) - 1)
        st = e & 255
    return t.accept[st]

# (the tree has 256 internal nodes, so a state fits the low 8 bits)

# An HPACK integer with an n-bit prefix at s[pos]; -1 when it's truncated or too big.
fn _int(s: str, pos: mut int, n: int) int:
    if pos >= len(s):
        return -1
    mask = (1 << n) - 1
    v = s.byte(pos) & mask
    pos += 1
    if v < mask:
        return v
    m = 0
    while true:
        if pos >= len(s) or m > 28:
            return -1
        b = s.byte(pos)
        pos += 1
        v += (b & 127) << m
        m += 7
        if b < 128:
            break
    return v if v < (1 << 32) else -1

fn _string(h: Hpack, s: str, pos: mut int, out: mut str) bool:
    if pos >= len(s):
        return false
    huff = s.byte(pos) >= 128
    n = _int(s, &pos, 7)
    if n < 0 or pos + n > len(s):
        return false
    if huff:
        out = ""
        ok = huffman_decode(h.t, s, pos, pos + n, &out)
        pos += n
        return ok
    out = s[pos..pos + n]
    pos += n
    return true

# entry i (1-based, 1..61 static, 62.. dynamic, newest first)
fn _entry(h: Hpack, i: int, name: mut str, value: mut str) bool:
    if i >= 1 and i <= 61:
        name = h.t.names[i - 1]
        value = h.t.values[i - 1]
        return true
    d = i - 62
    if i < 1 or d >= h.count:
        return false
    cap = len(h.ring_names)
    at = (h.head - 1 - d + cap * 2) % cap
    name = h.ring_names[at]
    value = h.ring_values[at]
    return true

fn _evict(h: mut Hpack, room: int):
    cap = len(h.ring_names)
    while h.count > 0 and h.size + room > h.max_size:
        at = (h.head - h.count + cap) % cap
        h.size -= len(h.ring_names[at]) + len(h.ring_values[at]) + 32
        h.ring_names[at] = ""
        h.ring_values[at] = ""
        h.count -= 1

fn _add(h: mut Hpack, name: str, value: str):
    sz = len(name) + len(value) + 32
    _evict(&h, sz)
    if sz > h.max_size:
        return                          # bigger than the table: it just empties it (4.4)
    cap = len(h.ring_names)
    h.ring_names[h.head] = name
    h.ring_values[h.head] = value
    h.head = (h.head + 1) % cap
    h.count += 1
    h.size += sz

fn _fail(h: mut Hpack, why: str) bool:
    h.err = why
    return false

# Decodes one header block onto out (name, value, name, value, ...). False: a compression error
# (h.err says what); the connection can't go on then, since the table is out of step.
# `size` gets the header list's size (RFC 7540 6.5.2: name + value + 32 each).
fn hpack_decode(h: mut Hpack, block: str, out: mut [str], size: mut int) bool:
    pos = 0
    n = len(block)
    first = true
    while pos < n:
        b = block.byte(pos)
        name = ""
        value = ""
        if b >= 128:                                    # indexed
            i = _int(block, &pos, 7)
            if i <= 0 or not _entry(h, i, &name, &value):
                return _fail(&h, "bad index")
        elif b >= 64 or b < 32:                         # a literal: with indexing (01), without (0000) or never (0001)
            idx = b >= 64
            i = _int(block, &pos, 6 if idx else 4)
            if i < 0:
                return _fail(&h, "bad literal")
            if i == 0:
                if not _string(h, block, &pos, &name):
                    return _fail(&h, "bad name")
            elif not _entry(h, i, &name, &value):
                return _fail(&h, "bad name index")
            if not _string(h, block, &pos, &value):
                return _fail(&h, "bad value")
            if idx:
                _add(&h, name, value)
        else:                                           # 001: dynamic table size update
            if not first:
                return _fail(&h, "size update after a header")
            m = _int(block, &pos, 5)
            if m < 0 or m > h.limit:
                return _fail(&h, "size update too big")
            h.max_size = m
            _evict(&h, 0)
            continue
        first = false
        size += len(name) + len(value) + 32
        out.push(name)
        out.push(value)
    return true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- encoding

fn hpack_int(prefix: int, n: int, value: int) str:
    v = value
    mask = (1 << n) - 1
    if v < mask:
        return chr(prefix | v)
    out = chr(prefix | mask)
    v -= mask
    while v >= 128:
        out += chr((v & 127) | 128)
        v >>= 7
    return out + chr(v)

# a header as a literal without indexing, new name (no Huffman)
fn hpack_literal(name: str, value: str) str:
    return "\x00" + hpack_int(0, 7, len(name)) + name + hpack_int(0, 7, len(value)) + value

# a header as a literal without indexing, its name from the static table
fn hpack_literal_idx(index: int, value: str) str:
    return hpack_int(0, 4, index) + hpack_int(0, 7, len(value)) + value
```

## deps/grpc/wire.tn

```tern
# Part of the grpc package (see grpc.tn): HTTP/2 frames (RFC 9113), a connection's reader (a
# Session: frames in, calls out) and its writer (the only task that writes to the socket).

const PREFACE = "PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n"

# frame types
const F_DATA = 0
const F_HEADERS = 1
const F_PRIORITY = 2
const F_RST = 3
const F_SETTINGS = 4
const F_PUSH = 5
const F_PING = 6
const F_GOAWAY = 7
const F_WINDOW = 8
const F_CONTINUATION = 9

# flags
const END_STREAM = 1
const ACK = 1
const END_HEADERS = 4
const PADDED = 8
const PRIORITY_FLAG = 32

# error codes
const NO_ERROR = 0
const PROTOCOL_ERROR = 1
const INTERNAL_ERROR = 2
const FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR = 3
const STREAM_CLOSED = 5
const FRAME_SIZE_ERROR = 6
const REFUSED_STREAM = 7
const CANCEL = 8
const COMPRESSION_ERROR = 9
const ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM = 11

# what the writer is asked to do
enum Out:
    Raw(bytes: str)                             # frames, ready to send
    Answer(sid: int, head: str, body: str, trailers: str)   # a call's answer ("" head: trailers only)
    Window(sid: int, inc: int)                  # the client's WINDOW_UPDATE
    Settings(window: int, frame: int)           # the client's SETTINGS (-1: not given); ack them
    Reset(sid: int)                             # the client reset the stream: drop its answer
    Close(answers: int)                         # the reader is done: close after this many answers

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- frames

fn _u32(n: int) str:
    return chr((n >> 24) & 255) + chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255)

fn _be32(s: str, i: int) int:
    return (s.byte(i) << 24) | (s.byte(i + 1) << 16) | (s.byte(i + 2) << 8) | s.byte(i + 3)

fn frame(typ: int, flags: int, sid: int, payload: str) str:
    n = len(payload)
    return chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255) + chr(typ) + chr(flags) + _u32(sid) + payload

fn _goaway(last: int, code: int, debug: str) str:
    return frame(F_GOAWAY, 0, 0, _u32(last) + _u32(code) + debug)

fn _rst(sid: int, code: int) str:
    return frame(F_RST, 0, sid, _u32(code))

fn _window(sid: int, inc: int) str:
    return frame(F_WINDOW, 0, sid, _u32(inc))

fn _setting(id: int, v: int) str:
    return chr(0) + chr(id) + _u32(v)

# grpc-message: percent-encoded (gRPC's HTTP/2 mapping)
fn _pct(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    hex = "0123456789ABCDEF"
    for c in s:
        b = c.byte(0)
        if b < 32 or b > 126 or b == 37:
            out += "%" + hex[b >> 4] + hex[b & 15]
        else:
            out += c
    return out

fn _grpc_head() str:
    return "\x88" + hpack_literal_idx(31, "application/grpc")     # :status 200, content-type

# the frames a call's answer turns into: head, body, trailers (encoded header blocks)
fn _answer(sid: int, r: Reply, encodings: str) Out:
    if r.status == OK:
        head = _grpc_head()
        if encodings != "":
            head += hpack_literal("grpc-accept-encoding", encodings)
        body = "\x00" + _u32(len(r.body)) + r.body
        return Out.Answer(sid, head, body, hpack_literal("grpc-status", "0"))
    t = _grpc_head() + hpack_literal("grpc-status", str(r.status))
    if r.message != "":
        t += hpack_literal("grpc-message", _pct(r.message))
    if encodings != "" and r.status == UNIMPLEMENTED:
        t += hpack_literal("grpc-accept-encoding", encodings)
    return Out.Answer(sid, "", "", t)

# a plain HTTP answer (not a gRPC request: wrong method or content type)
fn _http_answer(sid: int, status: int) Out:
    return Out.Answer(sid, "", "", hpack_literal_idx(8, str(status)) + hpack_literal("grpc-status", str(UNKNOWN if status != 415 else INTERNAL)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the reader

struct Stream:
    method: str
    meta: {str: str}
    data: str                   # the DATA received (gRPC-framed messages)
    window: int                 # what the client may still send on it
    unacked: int                # received, not yet credited back
    dead: bool                  # answered early (too big): what else arrives is dropped
    encoding: str

struct Session:
    sock: net.Conn
    out: chan[Out]
    o: Options
    accept_enc: str             # Options.encodings, joined (grpc-accept-encoding)
    hp: Hpack
    streams: {int: Stream}
    last: int                   # the highest stream id the client opened
    cont: int                   # a header block in progress (CONTINUATION expected on it), else 0
    block: str
    block_end: bool             # ... and whether its HEADERS had END_STREAM
    window: int                 # what the client may still send on the connection
    unacked: int
    ctl: str                    # control frames to send when the reader next waits
    started: int                # calls handed to handlers
    live: shared[int]           # this connection's calls running
    inflight: shared[int]       # the server's
    h: fn(Call) Reply
    buf: str
    at: int
    err: int                    # a connection error (GOAWAY sent): -1 while fine
    seen_settings: bool

fn _dec(n: mut int) int:
    n -= 1
    return n

fn _inc(n: mut int) int:
    n += 1
    return n

fn new_session(sock: net.Conn, out: chan[Out], o: Options, t: Tables, h: fn(Call) Reply, inflight: shared[int]) Session:
    return Session(sock, out, o, ", ".join(o.encodings), hpack_decoder(t, o.header_table), {}, 0, 0, "", false, o.conn_window, 0, "", 0, task.shared(0), inflight, h, "", 0, -1, false)

fn _conn_error(s: mut Session, code: int, why: str):
    if s.err < 0:
        s.err = code
        s.ctl += _goaway(s.last, code, why)

fn _stream_error(s: mut Session, sid: int, code: int):
    s.ctl += _rst(sid, code)
    s.streams.remove(sid)

# our first frames: SETTINGS, and the connection window
fn _hello(s: mut Session):
    p = _setting(3, s.o.max_streams) + _setting(4, s.o.stream_window) + _setting(5, s.o.max_frame) + _setting(6, s.o.max_header_list)
    s.ctl += frame(F_SETTINGS, 0, 0, p)
    if s.o.conn_window > 65535:
        s.ctl += _window(0, s.o.conn_window - 65535)

fn _run_call(h: fn(Call) Reply, c: Call, data: str, sid: int, out: chan[Out], enc: str, live: shared[int], inflight: shared[int]):
    r = h(Call(c.method, c.metadata, data[5..], c.encoding, c.conn))   # (the copy: in the call's task)
    out.send(_answer(sid, r, enc))
    live.update(_dec)
    inflight.update(_dec)

# the whole request is in: answer it (a handler, in a task) or refuse it
fn _finish(s: mut Session, sid: int):
    st = s.streams[sid]
    s.streams.remove(sid)
    if st.dead:
        return
    # every call gets exactly one answer (s.started counts them for the writer)
    s.started += 1
    d = st.data
    if len(d) < 5:
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(INTERNAL, "no request message"), s.accept_enc))
        return
    n = _be32(d, 1)
    if n != len(d) - 5:
        why = "more than one request message (streaming calls aren't supported)" if n < len(d) - 5 else "the request message is cut short"
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(INTERNAL if n > len(d) - 5 else UNIMPLEMENTED, why), s.accept_enc))
        return
    flag = d.byte(0)
    enc = ""
    if flag == 1:
        enc = st.encoding
        if enc == "" or enc == "identity" or not (enc in s.o.encodings):
            s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(UNIMPLEMENTED, "grpc-encoding " + (enc if enc != "" else "(none)") + " isn't supported"), s.accept_enc))
            return
    elif flag != 0:
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(INTERNAL, "bad message flag"), s.accept_enc))
        return
    c = Call(st.method, st.meta, "", enc, s.sock)
    s.live.update(_inc)
    s.inflight.update(_inc)
    handler = s.h
    out = s.out
    ae = s.accept_enc
    live = s.live
    inflight = s.inflight
    task.spawn(fn() _run_call(handler, c, d, sid, out, ae, live, inflight))  # (a captured `h` breaks the C: tern bug)

fn _bad_name(n: str) bool:
    for c in n:
        b = c.byte(0)
        if (b >= 65 and b <= 90) or b <= 32 or b >= 127 or b == 58:
            return true
    return false

fn _bad_value(v: str) bool:
    return v.contains("\r") or v.contains("\n") or v.contains("\0")

# a complete header block for stream sid
fn _headers(s: mut Session, sid: int, block: str, end: bool):
    hdrs: [str] = []
    size = 0
    if not hpack_decode(&s.hp, block, &hdrs, &size):
        why = s.hp.err
        _conn_error(&s, COMPRESSION_ERROR, why)
        return
    if sid in s.streams:                        # trailers (a client sends none for unary calls)
        if not end:
            _stream_error(&s, sid, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
        else:
            _finish(&s, sid)
        return
    if sid <= s.last or sid % 2 == 0:
        _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "stream id went back")
        return
    s.last = sid
    if s.err >= 0:
        return
    if size > s.o.max_header_list:
        s.ctl += _rst(sid, REFUSED_STREAM)      # (a stream error: the table is in step)
        s.started += 1
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, "headers too large"), s.accept_enc))
        return
    if len(s.streams) + s.live.get() >= s.o.max_streams:
        s.ctl += _rst(sid, REFUSED_STREAM)
        return
    st = Stream("", {}, "", s.o.stream_window, 0, false, "")
    method = ""
    ctype = ""
    regular = false
    malformed = false
    i = 0
    while i < len(hdrs):
        n = hdrs[i]
        v = hdrs[i + 1]
        i += 2
        if _bad_value(v):
            malformed = true
        if n.starts_with(":"):
            if regular:
                malformed = true
            match n:
                ":method":
                    method = v
                ":path":
                    st.method = v
                ":scheme" | ":authority":
                    pass
                _:
                    malformed = true
            continue
        regular = true
        if _bad_name(n) or n == "connection" or n == "keep-alive" or n == "transfer-encoding" or n == "upgrade" or n == "proxy-connection":
            malformed = true
            continue
        if n == "content-type":
            ctype = v
        elif n == "grpc-encoding":
            st.encoding = v
        if n in st.meta:
            st.meta[n] = st.meta[n] + ", " + v
        else:
            st.meta[n] = v
    if malformed or st.method == "":
        _stream_error(&s, sid, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
        return
    if method != "POST" or not ctype.starts_with("application/grpc"):
        s.started += 1
        s.out.send(_http_answer(sid, 405 if method != "POST" else 415))
        if not end:
            st.dead = true
            s.streams[sid] = st
        return
    s.streams[sid] = st
    if end:
        _finish(&s, sid)

fn _data(s: mut Session, sid: int, flags: int, p: int, n: int):
    # p: the payload's start in s.buf, n: its length (the whole frame counts for flow control)
    s.window -= n
    s.unacked += n
    if s.window < 0:
        _conn_error(&s, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, "sent past the connection window")
        return
    if s.unacked >= s.o.conn_window / 2:
        s.ctl += _window(0, s.unacked)
        s.window += s.unacked
        s.unacked = 0
    a = p
    b = p + n
    if flags & PADDED != 0:
        if n < 1:
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "padding")
            return
        pad = s.buf.byte(p)
        a += 1
        if pad > b - a:
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "padding longer than the frame")
            return
        b -= pad
    if not (sid in s.streams):
        if sid > s.last or sid == 0:
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "DATA on a stream that isn't open")
        return                                  # (a stream we answered or reset: dropped)
    s.streams[sid].window -= n
    if s.streams[sid].window < 0:
        _stream_error(&s, sid, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR)
        return
    if not s.streams[sid].dead:
        if len(s.streams[sid].data) + (b - a) > s.o.max_message + 5:
            s.streams[sid].dead = true
            s.streams[sid].data = ""
            s.started += 1
            s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, f"the request is larger than {s.o.max_message} bytes"), s.accept_enc))
            if flags & END_STREAM == 0:
                s.ctl += _rst(sid, NO_ERROR)      # (after the answer: the writer sends ctl first, see _flush)
        else:
            s.streams[sid].data += s.buf[a..b]
    if flags & END_STREAM != 0:
        _finish(&s, sid)
        return
    s.streams[sid].unacked += n
    if s.streams[sid].unacked >= s.o.stream_window / 2 and not s.streams[sid].dead:
        u = s.streams[sid].unacked
        s.ctl += _window(sid, u)
        s.streams[sid].window += u
        s.streams[sid].unacked = 0

fn _settings(s: mut Session, flags: int, p: int, n: int):
    if flags & ACK != 0:
        if n != 0:
            _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "SETTINGS ack with a payload")
        return
    if n % 6 != 0:
        _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "SETTINGS length")
        return
    win = -1
    fr = -1
    for k in 0..n / 6:
        id = (s.buf.byte(p + k * 6) << 8) | s.buf.byte(p + k * 6 + 1)
        v = _be32(s.buf, p + k * 6 + 2)
        match id:
            2:
                if v > 1:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "ENABLE_PUSH")
                    return
            4:
                if v > 2147483647:
                    _conn_error(&s, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, "INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE")
                    return
                win = v
            5:
                if v < 16384 or v > 16777215:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "MAX_FRAME_SIZE")
                    return
                fr = v
            _:
                pass                            # table size (our encoder has no table), limits
    s.out.send(Out.Settings(win, fr))           # the writer applies them, then acks

# Handles the complete frames in s.buf from s.at on. False once the connection is done.
fn process(s: mut Session) bool:
    while s.err < 0:
        have = len(s.buf) - s.at
        if have < 9:
            return true
        at = s.at
        n = (s.buf.byte(at) << 16) | (s.buf.byte(at + 1) << 8) | s.buf.byte(at + 2)
        typ = s.buf.byte(at + 3)
        flags = s.buf.byte(at + 4)
        sid = _be32(s.buf, at + 5) & 0x7fffffff
        if n > s.o.max_frame:
            _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "frame larger than MAX_FRAME_SIZE")
            return false
        if have < 9 + n:
            return true
        p = at + 9
        s.at = at + 9 + n
        if not s.seen_settings:
            if typ != F_SETTINGS or flags & ACK != 0:
                _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "expected SETTINGS first")
                return false
            s.seen_settings = true
        if s.cont != 0 and (typ != F_CONTINUATION or sid != s.cont):
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "expected CONTINUATION")
            return false
        match typ:
            0:
                if sid == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "DATA on stream 0")
                else:
                    _data(&s, sid, flags, p, n)
            1:
                if sid == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "HEADERS on stream 0")
                    return false
                a = p
                b = p + n
                if flags & PADDED != 0:
                    if n < 1:
                        _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "padding")
                        return false
                    pad = s.buf.byte(p)
                    a += 1
                    b -= pad
                if flags & PRIORITY_FLAG != 0:
                    a += 5
                if b < a:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "padding longer than the frame")
                    return false
                if b - a > s.o.max_header_list * 2 + 1024:
                    _conn_error(&s, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, "header block too large")
                    return false
                if flags & END_HEADERS != 0:
                    _headers(&s, sid, s.buf[a..b], flags & END_STREAM != 0)
                else:
                    s.cont = sid
                    s.block = s.buf[a..b]
                    s.block_end = flags & END_STREAM != 0
            9:
                if s.cont == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "CONTINUATION without HEADERS")
                    return false
                s.block += s.buf[p..p + n]
                if len(s.block) > s.o.max_header_list * 2 + 1024:
                    _conn_error(&s, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, "header block too large")
                    return false
                if flags & END_HEADERS != 0:
                    blk = s.block
                    s.block = ""
                    s.cont = 0
                    end = s.block_end
                    _headers(&s, sid, blk, end)
            2:
                if n != 5:
                    _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "PRIORITY length")
            3:
                if n != 4 or sid == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR if sid == 0 else FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "RST_STREAM")
                elif sid > s.last:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "RST_STREAM on an idle stream")
                else:
                    if sid in s.streams:
                        if s.streams[sid].dead:
                            s.streams.remove(sid)
                        else:
                            s.streams.remove(sid)
                    s.out.send(Out.Reset(sid))
            4:
                if sid != 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "SETTINGS on a stream")
                else:
                    _settings(&s, flags, p, n)
            5:
                _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "a client can't push")
            6:
                if n != 8 or sid != 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR if n != 8 else PROTOCOL_ERROR, "PING")
                elif flags & ACK == 0:
                    s.ctl += frame(F_PING, ACK, 0, s.buf[p..p + 8])
            7:
                if sid != 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "GOAWAY on a stream")
                # the client is leaving: answer what's open, then it closes
            8:
                if n != 4:
                    _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "WINDOW_UPDATE length")
                else:
                    inc = _be32(s.buf, p) & 0x7fffffff
                    if inc == 0:
                        if sid == 0:
                            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "zero WINDOW_UPDATE")
                        elif sid in s.streams:
                            _stream_error(&s, sid, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
                    elif sid > s.last and sid != 0:
                        _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "WINDOW_UPDATE on an idle stream")
                    else:
                        s.out.send(Out.Window(sid, inc))
            _:
                pass                            # unknown types are ignored
    return false

# sends the control frames gathered so far (before the reader waits)
fn _flush(s: mut Session):
    if s.ctl != "":
        s.out.send(Out.Raw(s.ctl))
        s.ctl = ""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the writer

struct Pending:
    sid: int
    body: str
    at: int                     # sent so far
    window: int
    trailers: str

fn _headers_frames(sid: int, block: str, end: bool, max_frame: int) str:
    fl = END_STREAM if end else 0
    if len(block) <= max_frame:
        return frame(F_HEADERS, fl | END_HEADERS, sid, block)
    out = frame(F_HEADERS, fl, sid, block[..max_frame])
    i = max_frame
    while i < len(block):
        j = min(i + max_frame, len(block))
        out += frame(F_CONTINUATION, END_HEADERS if j == len(block) else 0, sid, block[i..j])
        i = j
    return out

struct Writer:
    sock: net.Conn
    window: int                 # what we may still send on the connection
    initial: int                # the client's INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE
    max_frame: int
    deltas: {int: int}          # WINDOW_UPDATEs for streams not answered yet
    pending: [Pending]          # answers waiting on flow control
    out: str
    answers: int
    close_after: int            # -1 until the reader is done
    dead: bool

# as much of p as the windows allow; true when it's all out
fn _push(w: mut Writer, p: mut Pending) bool:
    while p.at < len(p.body):
        n = min(min(len(p.body) - p.at, w.max_frame), min(w.window, p.window))
        if n <= 0:
            return false
        w.out += frame(F_DATA, 0, p.sid, p.body[p.at..p.at + n])
        p.at += n
        w.window -= n
        p.window -= n
    w.out += _headers_frames(p.sid, p.trailers, true, w.max_frame)
    return true

fn _retry(w: mut Writer):
    if len(w.pending) == 0:
        return
    keep: [Pending] = []
    for i in 0..len(w.pending):
        p = w.pending[i]
        if not _push(&w, &p):
            keep.push(p)
    w.pending = keep

fn _write_item(w: mut Writer, it: Out):
    match it:
        Raw(b):
            w.out += b
        Answer(sid, head, body, trailers):
            w.answers += 1
            if head == "":
                w.out += _headers_frames(sid, trailers, true, w.max_frame)
                w.deltas.remove(sid)
                return
            w.out += _headers_frames(sid, head, false, w.max_frame)
            p = Pending(sid, body, 0, w.initial + w.deltas.get(sid, 0), trailers)
            w.deltas.remove(sid)
            if not _push(&w, &p):
                w.pending.push(p)
        Window(sid, inc):
            if sid == 0:
                w.window += inc
                if w.window > 2147483647:
                    w.out += _goaway(0, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, "window overflow")
                    w.dead = true
                    return
            else:
                found = false
                for i in 0..len(w.pending):
                    if w.pending[i].sid == sid:
                        w.pending[i].window += inc
                        found = true
                if not found:
                    if len(w.deltas) > 4096:
                        w.deltas = {}
                    w.deltas[sid] = w.deltas.get(sid, 0) + inc
            _retry(&w)
        Settings(win, fr):
            if win >= 0:
                for i in 0..len(w.pending):
                    w.pending[i].window += win - w.initial
                w.initial = win
            if fr >= 0:
                w.max_frame = fr
            w.out += frame(F_SETTINGS, ACK, 0, "")
            _retry(&w)
        Reset(sid):
            w.deltas.remove(sid)
            w.pending = w.pending.filter(fn(p) p.sid != sid)
        Close(n):
            w.close_after = n

fn _writer(sock: net.Conn, ch: chan[Out]):
    w = Writer(sock, 65535, 65535, 16384, {}, [], "", 0, -1, false)
    it = Out.Raw("")
    while true:
        if w.close_after >= 0 and (w.dead or (w.answers >= w.close_after and len(w.pending) == 0)):
            break
        got = false
        if w.close_after >= 0:
            got = ch.recv_timeout(&it, 30000)       # (a call that never answers: don't wait forever)
            if not got:
                break
        else:
            got = ch.next(&it)
            if not got:
                break
        _write_item(&w, it)
        while len(w.out) < 1 << 20 and ch.try_recv(&it):
            _write_item(&w, it)
        if w.out != "" and not w.dead:
            if not sock.write(w.out):
                w.dead = true
                w.pending = []
            w.out = ""
    sock.close()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- a connection

fn _serve_conn(srv: Server, c: net.Conn, handler: fn(Call) Reply, o: Options, t: Tables):
    out: chan[Out] = task.channel(0)
    fn add(m: mut {int: _Live}) int:
        m[c.fd] = _Live(c, out)
        return 0
    fn drop(m: mut {int: _Live}) int:
        m.remove(c.fd)
        return 0
    if srv.tls.ctx != 0 and not (tls.accept(c, srv.tls) and tls.alpn(c) == "h2"):
        c.close()                               # (not TLS, or no "h2": not a gRPC client)
        return
    s = new_session(c, out, o, t, handler, srv.inflight)
    # the preface
    while len(s.buf) < len(PREFACE):
        if c.refill(&s.buf, 0, 65536) <= 0:
            c.close()
            return
        if not PREFACE.starts_with(s.buf[..min(len(s.buf), len(PREFACE))]):
            if s.buf.starts_with("POST ") or s.buf.starts_with("GET ") or s.buf.starts_with("PUT "):
                msg = "this port speaks gRPC (HTTP/2); send OTLP/HTTP to the HTTP port\n"
                c.write(f"HTTP/1.1 505 HTTP Version Not Supported\r\ncontent-type: text/plain\r\ncontent-length: {len(msg)}\r\nconnection: close\r\n\r\n{msg}")
            c.close()
            return
    srv.conns.update(add)
    task.spawn(fn() _writer(c, out))
    s.at = len(PREFACE)
    _hello(&s)
    while process(&s):
        _flush(&s)
        while len(out) > 1024:                  # the client isn't reading (a PING flood?): wait
            task.sleep(2)
        if c.refill(&s.buf, s.at, 262144) <= 0:
            break
        s.at = 0
    _flush(&s)
    s.streams = {}
    out.send(Out.Close(s.started))
    srv.conns.update(drop)
```

## deps/openapi/openapi.tn

```tern
# openapi: describe a web API with Tern types; get an OpenAPI 3.1 document, Swagger UI, and a
# typed TypeScript client, all from the same routes you register.
#
#   import openapi
#   import roost
#
#   struct User:
#       id: int
#       name: str
#
#   fn main():
#       api = openapi.new("users", "1.0.0", "A small user service")
#       r = roost.router()
#       o = openapi.op("GET", "/users/{id}", "Get a user").returns[User]()
#       openapi.add(&api, &r, o, fn(req) roost.json(...))
#       openapi.serve(api, &r)                 # GET /openapi.json, GET /docs (Swagger UI)
#       roost.serve(r, 8080)
#
# Describing an operation (each returns the changed Op, so calls chain):
#   openapi.op(method, path, summary) Op     path params come from the path ("/users/{id}")
#   o.returns[T]()   o.accepts[T]()          the JSON response / request body is T
#   o.returns_text()                         a text/plain response
#   o.status(code)   o.describe(text)   o.tag(name)   o.id(operation_id)
#   o.query(name, type, description)         type: "string", "integer", "number", "boolean"
#   o.fails(code, description)               a documented error response (a 401 is added for
#                                            secured operations unless you give your own)
#   o.public()                               no key needed (default: the spec's security applies)
# Building and serving:
#   openapi.new(title, version, description) Spec
#   openapi.bearer(&spec, description)       every operation (but public ones) needs a bearer token
#   openapi.server(&spec, url)
#   openapi.add(&spec, &r, o, handler)       registers the route on r and records the operation
#   openapi.record(&spec, o)                 records an operation routed some other way (nested routers)
#   openapi.document(spec) str               the OpenAPI 3.1 JSON
#   openapi.typescript(spec) str             TypeScript types for every schema, and a fetch client
#   openapi.serve(spec, &r)                  GET /openapi.json and GET /docs (Swagger UI from
#                                            jsDelivr); call it after the last add
#
# Schemas come from json.schema[T](), so they always match what json.encode writes: every
# struct field is required, maps are objects with additionalProperties, int is int64.

import json
import roost

struct Param:
    name: str
    loc: str            # "path" or "query"
    ty: str             # JSON Schema type: string, integer, number, boolean
    required: bool
    description: str

struct Op:
    method: str
    path: str
    summary: str
    description: str
    tags: [str]
    op_id: str
    params: [Param]
    request: str        # JSON Schema text ("" for no body)
    response: str       # JSON Schema text ("" for no JSON body)
    text: bool          # the response is text/plain
    code: int
    open: bool          # no security requirement
    errors: [(int, str)]    # documented error responses: (status, description)

struct Spec:
    title: str
    version: str
    description: str
    servers: [str]
    bearer: str         # "" = no security scheme; else its description
    ops: [Op]

fn new(title: str, version: str, description: str) Spec:
    return Spec(title, version, description, [], "", [])

fn bearer(s: mut Spec, description: str):
    s.bearer = description

fn server(s: mut Spec, url: str):
    s.servers.push(copy(url))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- operations
fn _path_params(path: str) [Param]:
    out: [Param] = []
    rest = path
    i = rest.find("{")
    while i >= 0:
        j = rest.find("}")
        if j < i:
            break
        n = rest[i + 1..j]
        if n.starts_with("*"):
            n = n[1..]
        out.push(Param(n, "path", "string", true, ""))
        rest = rest[j + 1..]
        i = rest.find("{")
    return out

fn _op_id(method: str, path: str) str:
    out = method.lower()
    up = true
    for i in 0..len(path):
        ch = path[i]
        if ch == "/" or ch == "{" or ch == "}" or ch == "*" or ch == "-" or ch == "_" or ch == ".":
            up = true
        elif up:
            out += ch.upper()
            up = false
        else:
            out += ch
    return out

fn op(method: str, path: str, summary: str) Op:
    m = method.upper()
    return Op(m, path, summary, "", [], _op_id(m, path), _path_params(path), "", "", false, 200, false, [])

fn returns[T](o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.response = json.schema[T]()
    return out

fn accepts[T](o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.request = json.schema[T]()
    return out

fn returns_text(o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.text = true
    return out

fn status(o: Op, code: int) Op:
    out = o
    out.code = code
    return out

fn describe(o: Op, text: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.description = text
    return out

fn tag(o: Op, name: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.tags.push(copy(name))
    return out

fn id(o: Op, operation_id: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.op_id = operation_id
    return out

fn query(o: Op, name: str, ty: str, description: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.params.push(Param(name, "query", ty, false, description))
    return out

fn fails(o: Op, code: int, description: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.errors.push((code, copy(description)))
    return out

fn public(o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.open = true
    return out

fn add(s: mut Spec, r: mut roost.Router, o: Op, h: fn(roost.Request) roost.Response):
    r.route(o.method, o.path, h)
    s.ops.push(o)

# document an operation whose route is registered some other way (a nested router, a
# streaming handler, middleware in front of it)
fn record(s: mut Spec, o: Op):
    s.ops.push(o)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the document
# json.schema's output keeps its structs under a trailing "$defs"; the document moves them
# to components/schemas, shared by every operation
fn _split(schema: str, defs: mut {str: str}) str:
    k = schema.find(",\"$defs\":{")
    if k < 0:
        return schema
    root = schema[..k] + "}"
    body = schema[k + 10..len(schema) - 2]
    i = 0
    while i < len(body):
        e = body.find("\":")
        if body[i] != "\"" or e < 0:
            break
        rel = body[i..]
        q = rel.find("\":")
        name = rel[1..q]
        start = i + q + 2
        depth = 0
        j = start
        while j < len(body):
            ch = body.byte(j)
            if ch == 123:
                depth += 1
            elif ch == 125:
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    break
            j += 1
        defs[name] = _refs(body[start..j + 1])
        i = j + 2
    return _refs(root)

fn _refs(s: str) str:
    return s.replace("#/$defs/", "#/components/schemas/")

fn _short_names(defs: {str: str}) {str: str}:
    counts: {str: int} = {}
    for k in defs.keys():
        short = _ts_name(k, {})
        counts[short] = counts.get(short, 0) + 1
    names: {str: str} = {}
    for k in defs.keys():
        names[copy(k)] = _ts_name(k, counts)
    return names

fn _rename(s: str, names: {str: str}) str:
    out = s
    for k, v in names:
        if k != v:
            out = out.replace("#/components/schemas/" + k + "\"", "#/components/schemas/" + v + "\"")
    return out

fn _openapi_path(p: str) str:
    return p.replace("{*", "{")

fn _op_json(s: Spec, o: Op, defs: mut {str: str}) str:
    parts: [str] = ["\"operationId\":" + json_quote(o.op_id), "\"summary\":" + json_quote(o.summary)]
    if o.description != "":
        parts.push("\"description\":" + json_quote(o.description))
    if len(o.tags) > 0:
        parts.push("\"tags\":" + json.encode(o.tags))
    if len(o.params) > 0:
        ps: [str] = []
        for p in o.params:
            ps.push("{\"name\":" + json_quote(p.name) + ",\"in\":" + json_quote(p.loc) + ",\"required\":" + ("true" if p.required else "false") + ",\"schema\":{\"type\":" + json_quote(p.ty) + "}" + (",\"description\":" + json_quote(p.description) if p.description != "" else "") + "}")
        parts.push("\"parameters\":[" + ",".join(ps) + "]")
    if o.request != "":
        parts.push("\"requestBody\":{\"required\":true,\"content\":{\"application/json\":{\"schema\":" + _split(o.request, &defs) + "}}}")
    ok = "{\"description\":\"OK\"}"
    if o.response != "":
        ok = "{\"description\":\"OK\",\"content\":{\"application/json\":{\"schema\":" + _split(o.response, &defs) + "}}}"
    elif o.text:
        ok = "{\"description\":\"OK\",\"content\":{\"text/plain\":{\"schema\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}"
    resp = "\"" + str(o.code) + "\":" + ok
    has401 = false
    for e in o.errors:
        resp += ",\"" + str(e.0) + "\":{\"description\":" + json_quote(e.1) + "}"
        has401 = has401 or e.0 == 401
    if s.bearer != "" and not o.open and not has401:
        resp += ",\"401\":{\"description\":\"Missing or unknown credentials\"}"
    parts.push("\"responses\":{" + resp + "}")
    if o.open and s.bearer != "":
        parts.push("\"security\":[]")
    return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"

fn document(s: Spec) str:
    defs: {str: str} = {}
    paths: [str] = []
    by_path: {str: [str]} = {}
    for o in s.ops:
        p = _openapi_path(o.path)
        if not (p in by_path):
            by_path[copy(p)] = []
            paths.push(copy(p))
        by_path[p].push(json_quote(o.method.lower()) + ":" + _op_json(s, o, &defs))
    ps: [str] = []
    for p in paths:
        ps.push(json_quote(p) + ":{" + ",".join(by_path[p]) + "}")
    info = "{\"title\":" + json_quote(s.title) + ",\"version\":" + json_quote(s.version)
    if s.description != "":
        info += ",\"description\":" + json_quote(s.description)
    info += "}"
    out = "{\"openapi\":\"3.1.0\",\"info\":" + info
    sv: [str] = []
    for u in s.servers:
        sv.push("{\"url\":" + json_quote(u) + "}")
    if len(sv) == 0:
        sv.push("{\"url\":\"/\"}")                  # wherever the document is served from
    out += ",\"servers\":[" + ",".join(sv) + "]"
    out += ",\"paths\":{" + _rename(",".join(ps), _short_names(defs)) + "}"
    # short component names (User, not models.User) unless two would collide
    names = _short_names(defs)
    comps: [str] = []
    if len(defs) > 0:
        ds: [str] = []
        for k, v in defs:
            ds.push(json_quote(names[k]) + ":" + _rename(v, names))
        comps.push("\"schemas\":{" + ",".join(ds) + "}")
    if s.bearer != "":
        comps.push("\"securitySchemes\":{\"bearer\":{\"type\":\"http\",\"scheme\":\"bearer\",\"description\":" + json_quote(s.bearer) + "}}")
    if len(comps) > 0:
        out += ",\"components\":{" + ",".join(comps) + "}"
    if s.bearer != "":
        out += ",\"security\":[{\"bearer\":[]}]"
    return out + "}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- serving
const SWAGGER = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@5"

fn serve(s: Spec, r: mut roost.Router):
    doc = document(s)
    page = "<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset=utf-8><meta name=viewport content='width=device-width,initial-scale=1'><title>" + html_text(s.title) + " API</title><link rel=stylesheet href='" + SWAGGER + "/swagger-ui.css'></head><body><div id=swagger-ui></div><script src='" + SWAGGER + "/swagger-ui-bundle.js'></script><script src='/docs/init.js'></script></body></html>"
    init = "window.ui = SwaggerUIBundle({ url: '/openapi.json', dom_id: '#swagger-ui', deepLinking: true, persistAuthorization: true });"
    r.get("/openapi.json", fn(req) roost.json(doc))
    r.get("/docs", fn(req) roost.html(page))
    fn js(req: roost.Request) roost.Response:
        res = roost.text(init)
        res.content_type = "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"
        return res
    r.get("/docs/init.js", js)

fn html_text(s: str) str:
    return s.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;").replace(">", "&gt;").replace("'", "&#39;")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- TypeScript
# typescript(spec): a type for every schema, and createClient() with one typed method per
# operation (named by its operationId): path parameters, then the body, then the query.
# int64 becomes number: exact up to 2^53.

fn _ts_name(def: str, taken: {str: int}) str:
    short = def
    d = def.find(".")
    while d >= 0:
        short = short[d + 1..]
        d = short.find(".")
    if taken.get(short, 0) > 1:                 # store.Stats and forward.Stats: StoreStats, ForwardStats
        out = ""
        for part in def.split("."):
            if len(part) > 0:
                out += part[0].upper() + part[1..]
        return out
    return short

fn _ts_type(v: json.Value, names: {str: str}) str:
    ref = v.field("$ref").str_or("")
    if ref != "":
        n = ref[ref.find("/schemas/") + 9..]
        if ref.starts_with("#/$defs/"):
            n = ref[8..]
        return names.get(n, "unknown")
    alts = v.field("anyOf").elems()                 # Option[T]: T or null
    if len(alts) == 0:
        alts = v.field("oneOf").elems()             # an enum with payloads
    if len(alts) > 0:
        return " | ".join(alts.map(fn(a) _ts_type(a, names)))
    if v.field("const") is Str(c):                  # one variant's name
        return json_quote(c)
    labels = v.field("enum").elems()                # a string enum: "Active" | "Banned"
    if len(labels) > 0:
        return " | ".join(labels.map(fn(l) json_quote(l.str_or(""))))
    t = v.field("type").str_or("")
    if t == "null":
        return "null"
    if t == "integer" or t == "number":
        return "number"
    if t == "string":
        return "string"
    if t == "boolean":
        return "boolean"
    if t == "array":
        it = _ts_type(v.field("items"), names)
        if it.contains(" ") or it.contains("<"):
            return "Array<" + it + ">"
        return it + "[]"
    if t == "object":
        ap = v.field("additionalProperties")
        if ap is Obj(_, _):                           # (false: a closed object, not a map)
            return "Record<string, " + _ts_type(ap, names) + ">"
        props = v.field("properties")
        parts: [str] = []
        for k in props.fields():
            parts.push(_ts_key(k) + ": " + _ts_type(props.field(k), names))
        return "{ " + "; ".join(parts) + " }"
    return "unknown"

fn _ts_key(k: str) str:
    for i in 0..len(k):
        c = k.byte(i)
        if not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57 and i > 0) or c == 95 or c == 36):
            return json_quote(k)
    return k

fn _ts_schema(schema: str, names: {str: str}) str:
    match json.parse(schema):
        Ok(v):
            return _ts_type(v, names)
        Err(_):
            return "unknown"

fn _ts_param_type(ty: str) str:
    if ty == "integer" or ty == "number":
        return "number"
    if ty == "boolean":
        return "boolean"
    return "string"

fn typescript(s: Spec) str:
    defs: {str: str} = {}
    for o in s.ops:
        _split(o.request, &defs)
        _split(o.response, &defs)
    names = _short_names(defs)
    out = "// Generated from the " + s.title + " API (" + s.version + ") by Tern's openapi.typescript: don't edit.\n\n"
    for k, v in defs:
        out += "export type " + names[k] + " = " + _ts_schema(v, names) + ";\n"
    out += "\nexport class ApiError extends Error {\n  constructor(public status: number, public body: string) {\n    super(`${status}: ${body}`);\n  }\n}\n\n"
    out += "export type ClientOptions = { baseUrl?: string; token?: string; fetch?: typeof fetch; init?: RequestInit };\n\n"
    out += "export function createClient(opts: ClientOptions = {}) {\n"
    out += "  const base = opts.baseUrl ?? \"\";\n"
    out += "  async function call<T>(method: string, path: string, query: object | undefined, body: unknown, kind: \"json\" | \"text\" | \"none\"): Promise<T> {\n"
    out += "    let url = base + path;\n"
    out += "    if (query) {\n      const u = new URLSearchParams();\n      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(query)) if (v !== undefined && v !== null && v !== \"\") u.set(k, String(v));\n      const q = u.toString();\n      if (q) url += \"?\" + q;\n    }\n"
    out += "    const headers: Record<string, string> = { ...(opts.init?.headers as Record<string, string> | undefined) };\n"
    out += "    if (opts.token) headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${opts.token}`;\n"
    out += "    if (body !== undefined) headers[\"Content-Type\"] = \"application/json\";\n"
    out += "    const res = await (opts.fetch ?? fetch)(url, { credentials: \"same-origin\", ...opts.init, method, headers, body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body) });\n"
    out += "    if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(res.status, await res.text());\n"
    out += "    if (kind === \"none\") return undefined as T;\n"
    out += "    return (kind === \"text\" ? await res.text() : await res.json()) as T;\n  }\n"
    out += "  return {\n"
    for o in s.ops:
        args: [str] = []
        pp: [str] = []
        qp: [str] = []
        for p in o.params:
            if p.loc == "path":
                pp.push(_ts_key(p.name) + ": string")
            else:
                qp.push(_ts_key(p.name) + "?: " + _ts_param_type(p.ty))
        if len(pp) > 0:
            args.push("p: { " + "; ".join(pp) + " }")
        body = "undefined"
        if o.request != "":
            args.push("body: " + _ts_schema(_split(o.request, &defs), names))
            body = "body"
        query = "undefined"
        if len(qp) > 0:
            args.push("q: { " + "; ".join(qp) + " } = {}")
            query = "q"
        ret = "void"
        kind = "none"
        if o.response != "":
            ret = _ts_schema(_split(o.response, &defs), names)
            kind = "json"
        elif o.text:
            ret = "string"
            kind = "text"
        path = _openapi_path(o.path)
        for p in o.params:
            if p.loc == "path":
                path = path.replace("{" + p.name + "}", "${encodeURIComponent(p." + p.name + ")}")
        out += "    /** " + o.summary.replace("*/", "* /") + " */\n"
        out += "    " + o.op_id + ": (" + ", ".join(args) + ") => call<" + ret + ">(" + json_quote(o.method) + ", `" + path + "`, " + query + ", " + body + ", " + json_quote(kind) + "),\n"
    out += "  };\n}\n"
    return out
```

## deps/queue/queue.tn

```tern
# queue: a client for ternq, the message queue broker (examples/queue/).
#
#   import queue
#   c = queue.connect("127.0.0.1", 7070)          # check c.ok
#   c.publish("jobs", "hello")                     # true once the broker has it on disk
#   s = c.subscribe("jobs", "workers", 64)         # group "workers", up to 64 unacked at once
#   m = queue.empty_msg()
#   while s.next(&m):
#       print(m.body)
#       c.ack(m)                                   # or c.nack(m) to have it redelivered
#
# queue.connect(host: str, port: int) Client       one connection, shared by any number of tasks
# queue.connect_many(addrs: [str]) Client          several brokers ("host:port"); each queue lives
#                                                  on one, chosen by a hash of its name (sharding).
#                                                  An entry can list a primary and its followers,
#                                                  "h1:7070,h2:7070": the client moves to whichever
#                                                  of them is the primary (failover)
# queue.connect_auth(addrs: [str], token: str) Client   the same, for brokers started with --token
# c.shard_of(q: str) int                           which of them holds q
# queue.empty_msg() Msg                            a Msg to receive into
# c.ok bool                                        the first connect worked (it reconnects by itself later)
# c.publish(q: str, body: str) bool                waits for the broker's ack (false: client closed)
# c.publish_delayed(q: str, body: str, delay_ms: int) bool   deliver no sooner than delay_ms from now
# c.publish_batch(q: str, bodies: [str]) bool      one frame, one ack for all of them
# c.publish_async(q: str, body: str) chan[bool]    don't wait: recv() the result later (pipelining)
# c.subscribe(q: str, group: str, prefetch: int) Sub   each group gets every message; the
#                                                  consumers in a group share them. prefetch 0: pull only
# s.next(m: mut Msg) bool                          waits for the next message (false: client closed)
# s.next_timeout(m: mut Msg, ms: int) bool         false if none came within ms
# s.msgs chan[Msg]                                 the subscription's messages, as a channel
# c.fetch(s: Sub, max: int) [Msg]                  pull up to max messages now (any subscription)
# c.fetch_wait(s: Sub, max: int, ms: int) [Msg]    the same, but with none there, wait up to ms for some
# c.ack(m: Msg)   c.nack(m: Msg)                   acks are batched into one frame per burst
# c.unsubscribe(s: Sub)                            its unacked messages go back to the group
# c.stats(q: str) str                              JSON: depth, in-flight, rates, per group
# c.queues() str                                   JSON array of queue names
# c.shutdown_broker()                             ask the broker to stop gracefully (admin)
# c.close()
#
# Delivery is at least once: a message is redelivered if it isn't acked within the
# broker's visibility timeout, if it's nacked, or if its consumer disconnects. After a
# lost connection the client reconnects (with backoff), resends every publish that
# wasn't acked yet, and subscribes again, so a publish may arrive twice. With a failover
# list it tries the next address after a lost connection, and it tells every broker the
# highest epoch it has seen, so a replaced primary that is still running stops rather
# than taking writes (see examples/queue/README.md).
#
# Inside: one task owns the connection. Callers send it requests on a channel; it
# writes whatever has piled up with one write, and a reader task parses what the
# broker sends back (messages go straight to their subscription's channel).

import net
import task
import time

struct Msg:
    sid: int
    seq: int
    attempt: int
    body: str
    shard: int                                     # which broker (connect_many)

struct Client:
    ok: bool
    shards: [chan[Req]]                            # one connection task per broker

struct Sub:
    sid: int
    shard: int
    msgs: chan[Msg]

enum Req:
    Publish(queue: str, body: str, delay: int, reply: chan[bool])
    PublishBatch(queue: str, bodies: [str], reply: chan[bool])
    Subscribe(queue: str, group: str, prefetch: int, msgs: chan[Msg], reply: chan[int])
    Unsubscribe(sid: int)
    Ack(sid: int, seq: int, ok: bool)
    Fetch(sid: int, max: int, wait: int, reply: chan[int])
    Query(line: str, reply: chan[str])
    Raw(line: str)
    Close
    Reply(gen: int, id: int, ok: bool)            # from the reader
    Json(gen: int, id: int, text: str)
    Fetched(gen: int, sid: int, n: int)
    Lost(gen: int)
    Deliver(gen: int, m: Msg)
    Epoch(gen: int, epoch: int)

struct Pending:                                    # a request waiting for its reply
    frame: str
    ok: chan[bool]
    txt: chan[str]
    kind: int                                      # 0 publish, 1 query

struct SubInfo:
    queue: str
    group: str
    prefetch: int
    msgs: chan[Msg]

struct Addr:
    host: str
    port: int

struct State:
    addrs: [Addr]                                  # a primary and its followers
    cur: int                                       # the one we're connected to
    token: str
    epoch: int                                     # the highest the brokers told us
    shard: int
    conn: net.Conn
    gen: int
    next_id: int
    pend: {int: Pending}
    subs: {int: SubInfo}
    fetches: {int: [chan[int]]}
    out: str
    acks: {int: str}
    closed: bool
    up: bool

fn empty_msg() Msg:
    return Msg(0, 0, 0, "", 0)

fn connect(host: str, port: int) Client:
    return connect_many([f"{host}:{port}"])

fn connect_many(addrs: [str]) Client:
    return connect_auth(addrs, "")

# several brokers: each queue lives on one of them, picked by hashing its name
# (every client given the same list agrees on where each queue is)
fn connect_auth(addrs: [str], token: str) Client:
    shards: [chan[Req]] = []
    ok = len(addrs) > 0
    for i, entry in addrs:
        list = entry.split(",").map(fn(a) _addr(a.trim()))
        reqs: chan[Req] = task.channel(0)
        st = State(list, 0, token, 0, i, net.Conn(-1), 1, 1, {}, {}, {}, "", {}, false, true)
        if _dial(&st):
            task.spawn(fn() run(st, reqs))
        else:
            ok = false
        shards.push(reqs)
    return Client(ok, shards)

fn _addr(a: str) Addr:
    k = a.find(":")
    j = k
    while j >= 0:                                  # the last ":" ("[::1]:7070" works too)
        k = j
        rest = a[k + 1..]
        j = rest.find(":")
        if j >= 0:
            j += k + 1
    return Addr(a[..k].replace("[", "").replace("]", ""), a[k + 1..].to_int(7070))

# connect to the current address, or the next ones in turn: false if none answered
fn _dial(s: mut State) bool:
    for i in 0..len(s.addrs):
        a = s.addrs[s.cur]
        c = net.connect(a.host, a.port)
        if c.ok():
            s.conn = c
            if s.token != "" or len(s.addrs) > 1:
                c.write(f"I {s.epoch} {s.token}\n")
            return true
        s.cur = (s.cur + 1) % len(s.addrs)
    return false

# which broker holds queue q: the one scoring highest for it (rendezvous hashing, so
# adding a broker to the list moves only the queues that now score highest on it)
fn shard_of(c: Client, q: str) int:
    best = 0
    top = -1
    for i in 0..len(c.shards):
        h = i + 1
        for k in 0..len(q):
            h = (h * 31 + q.byte(k)) % 1000000007
        h = (h * 2654435761 + i * 40503) % 1000000007
        if h > top:
            top = h
            best = i
    return best

fn _to(c: Client, q: str) chan[Req]:
    return c.shards[shard_of(c, q)]

fn publish(c: Client, q: str, body: str) bool:
    return publish_async(c, q, body).recv()

fn publish_delayed(c: Client, q: str, body: str, delay_ms: int) bool:
    r: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Publish(q, body, delay_ms, r))
    return r.recv()

fn publish_async(c: Client, q: str, body: str) chan[bool]:
    r: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Publish(q, body, 0, r))
    return r

fn publish_batch(c: Client, q: str, bodies: [str]) bool:
    r: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.PublishBatch(q, bodies, r))
    return r.recv()

fn subscribe(c: Client, q: str, group: str, prefetch: int) Sub:
    msgs: chan[Msg] = task.channel(0)
    r: chan[int] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Subscribe(q, group, prefetch, msgs, r))
    return Sub(r.recv(), shard_of(c, q), msgs)

fn next(s: Sub, m: mut Msg) bool:
    return task.next(s.msgs, &m)

fn next_timeout(s: Sub, m: mut Msg, ms: int) bool:
    return s.msgs.recv_timeout(&m, ms)

fn fetch(c: Client, s: Sub, max: int) [Msg]:
    return fetch_wait(c, s, max, 0)

fn fetch_wait(c: Client, s: Sub, max: int, ms: int) [Msg]:
    r: chan[int] = task.channel(1)
    c.shards[s.shard].send(Req.Fetch(s.sid, max, ms, r))
    n = r.recv()
    out: [Msg] = []
    m = empty_msg()
    for i in 0..n:
        if not task.next(s.msgs, &m):
            break
        out.push(copy(m))
    return out

fn ack(c: Client, m: Msg):
    c.shards[m.shard].send(Req.Ack(m.sid, m.seq, true))

fn nack(c: Client, m: Msg):
    c.shards[m.shard].send(Req.Ack(m.sid, m.seq, false))

fn unsubscribe(c: Client, s: Sub):
    c.shards[s.shard].send(Req.Unsubscribe(s.sid))

fn stats(c: Client, q: str) str:
    r: chan[str] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Query("T {id} " + q, r))
    return r.recv()

fn queues(c: Client) str:
    out = ""
    for sh in c.shards:
        r: chan[str] = task.channel(1)
        sh.send(Req.Query("L {id}", r))
        txt = r.recv()
        if len(txt) > 2:
            if out != "":
                out += ","
            out += txt[1..len(txt) - 1]
    return "[" + out + "]"

fn shutdown_broker(c: Client):
    for sh in c.shards:
        sh.send(Req.Raw("X\n"))

fn close(c: Client):
    for sh in c.shards:
        sh.send(Req.Close)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the connection's task
fn run(st: State, reqs: chan[Req]):
    s = st
    g = s.gen
    cn = s.conn
    task.spawn(fn() reader(cn, g, reqs))
    r = Req.Close
    while not s.closed and task.next(reqs, &r):
        handle(&s, r, reqs)
        n = 0
        while n < 1024 and reqs.try_recv(&r):
            handle(&s, r, reqs)
            n += 1
        if not s.up and not s.closed:
            reconnect(&s, reqs)
        if s.closed:
            if s.up:
                s.conn.write(s.out + "Q\n")      # the broker closes the connection; the reader ends
            break
        send_out(&s)
    for id, p in s.pend:
        if p.kind == 0:
            p.ok.send(false)
        else:
            p.txt.send("")
    for sid, si in s.subs:
        task.close(si.msgs)
    for sid, fs in s.fetches:
        for f in fs:
            f.send(0)

fn send_out(s: mut State):
    out = s.out
    for sid, seqs in s.acks:
        out += seqs + "\n"
    s.acks = {}
    s.out = ""
    if out != "":
        s.conn.write(out)          # if this fails, the reader sees the end and we reconnect

fn handle(s: mut State, r: Req, reqs: chan[Req]):
    match r:
        Publish(q, body, delay, reply):
            id = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            f = f"P {id} {q} {delay} {len(body)}\n" + body
            _cat(&s.out, f)
            s.pend[id] = Pending(f, reply, dummy_txt(), 0)
        PublishBatch(q, bodies, reply):
            id = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            head = f"B {id} {q} 0 {len(bodies)}"
            for b in bodies:
                head += f" {len(b)}"
            f = head + "\n" + "".join(bodies)
            _cat(&s.out, f)
            s.pend[id] = Pending(f, reply, dummy_txt(), 0)
        Subscribe(q, group, prefetch, msgs, reply):
            sid = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            s.subs[sid] = SubInfo(q, group, prefetch, msgs)
            _cat(&s.out, f"S {sid} {q} {group} {prefetch}\n")
            reply.send(sid)
        Unsubscribe(sid):
            if sid in s.subs:
                task.close(s.subs[sid].msgs)
                s.subs.remove(sid)
                _cat(&s.out, f"U {sid}\n")
        Ack(sid, seq, ok):
            key = sid * 2
            tag = "A"
            if not ok:
                key += 1
                tag = "N"
            if key in s.acks:
                _cat(&s.acks[key], f" {seq}")
            else:
                s.acks[key] = f"{tag} {sid} {seq}"
        Fetch(sid, max, wait, reply):
            if not (sid in s.subs):
                reply.send(0)
            else:
                if not (sid in s.fetches):
                    s.fetches[sid] = []
                s.fetches[sid].push(reply)
                if wait > 0:
                    _cat(&s.out, f"F {sid} {max} {wait}\n")
                else:
                    _cat(&s.out, f"F {sid} {max}\n")
        Query(line, reply):
            id = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            f = line.replace("{id}", str(id)) + "\n"
            _cat(&s.out, f)
            s.pend[id] = Pending(f, dummy_ok(), reply, 1)
        Raw(line):
            _cat(&s.out, line)
        Close:
            s.closed = true
        Reply(gen, id, ok):
            if gen == s.gen and id in s.pend:
                p = s.pend[id]
                s.pend.remove(id)
                if p.kind == 0:
                    p.ok.send(ok)
                else:
                    p.txt.send("")
        Json(gen, id, text):
            if gen == s.gen and id in s.pend:
                p = s.pend[id]
                s.pend.remove(id)
                p.txt.send(text)
        Fetched(gen, sid, n):
            if gen == s.gen and sid in s.fetches and len(s.fetches[sid]) > 0:
                s.fetches[sid][0].send(n)
                s.fetches[sid] = s.fetches[sid][1..]
        Lost(gen):
            if gen == s.gen:
                s.up = false
        Epoch(gen, epoch):
            if epoch > s.epoch:
                s.epoch = epoch
        Deliver(gen, m):
            if gen == s.gen and m.sid in s.subs:
                mm = m
                mm.shard = s.shard
                s.subs[m.sid].msgs.send(mm)

fn dummy_ok() chan[bool]:
    c: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    return c

fn dummy_txt() chan[str]:
    c: chan[str] = task.channel(1)
    return c

# connect again (the next address of a failover list first, then backing off up to
# 2s), then resend what's pending and resubscribe. Requests keep being taken meanwhile
# (a publish waits in s.pend; a Close gives up).
fn reconnect(s: mut State, reqs: chan[Req]):
    wait = 50
    r = Req.Close
    s.cur = (s.cur + 1) % len(s.addrs)
    while true:
        if _dial(&s):
            break
        until = time.now_ms() + wait
        while not s.closed:
            left = until - time.now_ms()
            if left <= 0 or not reqs.recv_timeout(&r, left):
                break
            handle(&s, r, reqs)
        if s.closed:
            return
        wait = min(wait * 2, 2000)
    s.up = true
    s.gen += 1
    g = s.gen
    cn = s.conn
    task.spawn(fn() reader(cn, g, reqs))
    out = ""
    for sid, si in s.subs:
        out += f"S {sid} {si.queue} {si.group} {si.prefetch}\n"
    for id, p in s.pend:
        out += p.frame
    for sid, fs in s.fetches:
        for f in fs:
            f.send(0)
    s.fetches = {}
    s.acks = {}
    s.out = ""
    s.conn.write(out)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reading the broker's frames
fn reader(c: net.Conn, gen: int, reqs: chan[Req]):
    while true:
        line = c.read_line()
        if len(line) < 2 or not line.ends_with("\n"):
            break
        op = line.byte(0)
        pos = 1
        if op == 77:                                   # M sid seq attempt len
            sid = _int(line, &pos)
            seq = _int(line, &pos)
            att = _int(line, &pos)
            n = _int(line, &pos)
            body = _body(c, n)
            if len(body) < n:
                break
            reqs.send(Req.Deliver(gen, Msg(sid, seq, att, body, 0)))
        elif op == 75 or op == 69:                     # K id / E id msg
            id = _int(line, &pos)
            if id == 0 and op == 69:                   # this broker won't talk to us (unauthorized,
                break                                  # or replaced by a newer primary)
            reqs.send(Req.Reply(gen, id, op == 75))
        elif op == 86:                                 # V epoch
            reqs.send(Req.Epoch(gen, _int(line, &pos)))
        elif op == 74:                                 # J id len
            id = _int(line, &pos)
            n = _int(line, &pos)
            body = _body(c, n)
            if len(body) < n:
                break
            reqs.send(Req.Json(gen, id, body))
        elif op == 70:                                 # F sid n
            sid = _int(line, &pos)
            reqs.send(Req.Fetched(gen, sid, _int(line, &pos)))
    net.close(c)
    reqs.send(Req.Lost(gen))

fn _body(c: net.Conn, n: int) str:
    b = c.read(n)
    while len(b) < n:
        more = c.read(n - len(b))
        if more == "":
            return b
        b += more
    return b

fn _int(s: str, pos: mut int) int:
    n = len(s)
    while pos < n and s.byte(pos) == 32:
        pos += 1
    v = 0
    while pos < n:
        b = s.byte(pos)
        if b < 48 or b > 57:
            break
        v = v * 10 + (b - 48)
        pos += 1
    return v

# b += x in place (`s.field += x` would copy the whole string each time)
fn _cat(b: mut str, x: str):
    b += x
```

## deps/roost/check.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): input validation.

# Validating input: collect every problem, then answer 422 with all of them at once.
#   v = roost.check()
#   v.required("name", u.name)
#   v.max_len("name", u.name, 100)
#   v.email("email", u.email)
#   v.between("age", u.age, 0, 150)
#   if not v.valid():
#       return v.problems()        # 422 {"errors": {"name": "is required", ...}}
# Each field keeps its first problem.
struct Check:
    errors: {str: str}

fn check() Check:
    return Check({})

fn valid(v: Check) bool:
    return len(v.errors) == 0

fn fail(v: mut Check, field: str, message: str):
    if not (field in v.errors):
        v.errors[field] = message

fn required(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str):
    if value.trim() == "":
        fail(&v, field, "is required")

fn min_len(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str, n: int):
    if len(value) < n:
        fail(&v, field, f"must be at least {n} characters")

fn max_len(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str, n: int):
    if len(value) > n:
        fail(&v, field, f"must be at most {n} characters")

fn between(v: mut Check, field: str, value: int, lo: int, hi: int):
    if value < lo or value > hi:
        fail(&v, field, f"must be between {lo} and {hi}")

fn one_of(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str, options: [str]):
    if not (value in options):
        fail(&v, field, "must be one of " + ", ".join(options))

# a plausible address: one @, something before it, a dot in the domain, no spaces
fn email(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str):
    at = value.find("@")
    domain = ""
    if at > 0:
        domain = value[at + 1..]
    if at <= 0 or domain.find("@") >= 0 or domain.find(".") <= 0 or domain.ends_with(".") or value.contains(" "):
        fail(&v, field, "must be an email address")

# 422 Unprocessable Content with {"errors": {field: message, ...}}
fn problems(v: Check) Response:
    body = "{\"errors\":{"
    first = true
    for k, m in v.errors:
        if not first:
            body += ","
        first = false
        body += k.json_quote() + ":" + m.json_quote()
    return Response(422, "application/json", body + "}}", "", 0)
```

## deps/roost/middleware.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): middleware.

fn _fmt_us(us: int) str:
    if us < 1000:
        return str(us) + "us"
    if us < 1_000_000:
        return str(us / 1000) + "." + str(us / 100 % 10) + "ms"
    return str(us / 1_000_000) + "." + str(us / 100_000 % 10) + "s"

fn _log_mw(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) Response:
    t0 = http.now_us()
    res = inner(req)
    http.log(req.method + " " + req.path + " " + str(res.status) + " " + _fmt_us(http.now_us() - t0))
    return res

fn logger() fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return _log_mw

# Rate limiting: a token bucket per client IP (client_ip), refilled at per_second tokens a
# second up to burst. A request that finds its bucket empty gets 429 Too Many Requests with
# Retry-After. Buckets are shared by every thread; idle ones are forgotten.
fn rate_limit(per_second: float, burst: int) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    lim = http.limiter(per_second, burst)
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _limited(req, inner, lim, req.client_ip())

# the same, with your own key (an API key, a user id from the session, ...)
fn rate_limit_by(per_second: float, burst: int, key: fn(Request) str) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    lim = http.limiter(per_second, burst)
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _limited(req, inner, lim, key(req))

fn _limited(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, lim: http.Limiter, key: str) Response:
    wait = lim.consume(key)
    if wait <= 0.0:
        return inner(req)
    secs = int(wait) + 1
    return Response(429, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "too many requests", "Retry-After: " + str(secs) + "\r\n", 0)

fn _list_has(list: str, item: str) bool:
    for x in list.split(","):
        if x.trim() == item:
            return true
    return false

fn _cors(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, origins: str) Response:
    origin = req.header("origin")
    allow = ""
    if origins == "*":
        allow = "*"
    elif origin != "" and _list_has(origins, origin):
        allow = origin
```
